kingdom-of-lihyan.t: The Lihyanite kingdom of al-Ula, whose kings taxed the incense road through the Hejaz and carved monumental statues at Dedan.
kingdom-of-lihyan.o: Lihyan succeeded the [[s:kingdom-of-dedan|Kingdom of Dedan]] at the oasis of [[e:alula|al-Ula]], probably in the late 6th or 5th century BCE, after the Babylonian occupation of the [[s:kingdom-of-hejaz|Hejaz]] ended. Its kings ruled from Dedan and drew their wealth from caravans carrying [[e:incense|incense]] from south [[e:arabia|Arabia]] towards the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]].
kingdom-of-lihyan.r: Dadanitic inscriptions record a succession of Lihyanite kings, temple offerings and taxes paid to the god [[e:dhu-ghabat|Dhu Ghabat]]. Large sandstone statues of kings and nobles from the sanctuary at [[e:al-khuraybah|al-Khuraybah]] show contact with Egyptian and Hellenistic art. Minaean traders from the [[s:kingdom-of-main|Kingdom of Ma'in]] lived alongside the local population and kept their own officials.
kingdom-of-lihyan.e: Lihyan declined as the [[s:nabataean-kingdom|Nabataean Kingdom]] extended its control over the caravan trade and took [[e:hegra|Hegra]] (Mada'in [[s:salihids|Salih]]) to the north. By the 1st century BCE its independence had ended, though the dynasty's exact fate is uncertain. The Lion Tombs and statues at [[e:alula|al-Ula]] are among the region's best-known monuments.

kingdom-of-serbia.t: Serbian kingdom that doubled its territory in the Balkan Wars, endured the First World War and became the core of Yugoslavia.
kingdom-of-serbia.o: [[e:milan-i-of-serbia|Prince Milan Obrenović]] of the [[s:principality-of-serbia|Principality of Serbia]], independent since 1878, proclaimed himself king in 1882 with the support of [[e:austro-hungarian-empire|Austria-Hungary]]. His reign brought defeat by [[s:bulgaria|Bulgaria]] at [[e:battle-of-slivnitsa|Slivnitsa]] in 1885 and domestic unrest, and he abdicated in 1889 in favour of his son Alexander.
kingdom-of-serbia.r: The unpopular [[e:alexander-obrenovic|Alexander Obrenović]] was murdered with his queen by army officers in the [[e:may-coup-serbia|May Coup]] of 1903, and Peter I Karađorđević became king. Under the 1903 constitution and [[e:nikola-pasic|Nikola Pašić's]] [[e:peoples-radical-party|Radical Party]], [[s:serbia|Serbia]] became a parliamentary state, freed itself from Austrian economic control after the Pig War of 1906, and in the [[e:balkan-wars|Balkan Wars]] of 1912 to 1913 gained [[e:kosovo|Kosovo]] and [[e:vardar-macedonia|Vardar Macedonia]].
kingdom-of-serbia.e: After the [[e:sarajevo|Sarajevo]] assassination, [[e:austro-hungarian-empire|Austria-Hungary]] attacked [[s:serbia|Serbia]] in 1914. Overrun in 1915, its army retreated through [[s:albania|Albania]] to [[s:corcyra|Corfu]] and returned via the [[e:macedonian-front|Salonika front]] in 1918. On 1 December 1918 [[e:serbia|Serbia]] joined the [[s:kingdom-of-yugoslavia|Kingdom of Yugoslavia]], then called the Kingdom of [[e:serbs|Serbs]], [[e:croats|Croats]] and [[e:slovenes|Slovenes]].

kingdom-of-kasa.t: Bainuk kingdom of the lower Casamance river, whose king's title, Kasa Mansa, gave the region its name.
kingdom-of-kasa.o: Known mainly from Portuguese sources. When Portuguese traders reached the [[e:casamance|Casamance]] in the 15th century, they found a kingdom of the [[e:bainuk|Bainuk]] (Banyun) people on the south bank of the river, whose ruler was called the Kasa [[s:mansa-state|Mansa]], 'king of Kasa', a title shaped by [[e:mandinka|Mandinka]] usage.
kingdom-of-kasa.r: Kasa traded [[e:rice|rice]], wax, [[e:cotton|cotton]] cloth and slaves with Portuguese and [[e:luso-africans|Luso-African]] traders who settled at riverside ports. Its rulers dealt with merchants through local intermediaries, and the kingdom sat on the margins of the [[e:kaabu-empire|Kaabu Empire's]] sphere of influence.
kingdom-of-kasa.e: Kasa declined in the 17th century as [[e:mandinka|Mandinka]], [[e:balanta|Balanta]] and [[e:jola|Jola]] expansion and the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]] reshaped the region. Its name survives in the [[e:casamance|Casamance]] river and region of southern [[e:senegal|Senegal]].

kingdom-of-dawro.t: An Omotic kingdom of south-western Ethiopia, known for the great defensive stone wall attributed to its kings.
kingdom-of-dawro.o: Dawro, also called Kullo, lay west of [[s:kingdom-of-wolaita|Wolaita]] between the [[e:omo-river|Omo]] and [[e:gojeb-river|Gojeb]] rivers. Its royal dynasty is known from oral tradition, which places its consolidation in the 16th century, after the earlier Christian presence in the region had faded. The kingdom was closely related in language and culture to its neighbours Wolaita and Konta.
kingdom-of-dawro.r: The kawo (king) ruled with regional officials and clan leaders. Dawro is best known for the [[e:halala-kella|Halala Kella]], a stone wall running for well over 100 kilometres, attributed in tradition to King Halala and built to defend the realm. Its people farmed ensete and grain and traded with [[s:kingdom-of-kaffa|Kaffa]] and the [[e:gibe-river|Gibe]] kingdoms.
kingdom-of-dawro.e: In 1891 Dawro was conquered by the armies of [[e:menelik-ii|Menelik II]] and annexed to the [[s:ethiopian-empire|Ethiopian Empire]]. The [[e:dawro-zone|Dawro Zone]] today keeps the name, and the [[e:halala-kella|Halala Kella]] wall is a significant heritage site.

khanate-of-kalat.t: The Brahui-led khanate of Balochistan, the paramount power of the region for nearly three centuries until merged into Pakistan.
khanate-of-kalat.o: Around 1666 the Ahmadzai chief Mir Ahmad Khan I established a Brahui-led confederacy based at Kalat, in the highlands of central [[e:balochistan|Balochistan]], on the borderlands of Safavid [[e:persia|Persia]] and Mughal [[e:india|India]].
khanate-of-kalat.r: The Khan ruled through a tribal confederacy of Sarawan and Jhalawan chiefs. [[e:nasir-khan-i-of-kalat|Mir Nasir Khan I]], who reigned for much of the late 18th century, organised the army and administration and extended rule to the coast. In 1839 British troops stormed Kalat and killed [[e:mehrab-khan|Mehrab Khan]]; later treaties made it a British-protected state, with [[s:kharan-state|Kharan State]] and other chiefdoms as feudatories.
khanate-of-kalat.e: Khan [[e:ahmad-yar-khan|Ahmad Yar Khan]] declared independence in 1947 but acceded to [[s:islamic-republic-of-pakistan|Pakistan]] in March 1948. Kalat joined the [[s:baluchistan-states-union|Baluchistan States Union]] and was absorbed into [[e:west-pakistan|West Pakistan]] in 1955.

kishtwar-kingdom.t: A mountain kingdom on the upper Chenab, famed for saffron, whose Rajas converted to Islam in the 17th century before the Dogras of Jammu annexed it.
kishtwar-kingdom.o: Tradition holds that a [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] named Kahan Pal founded the dynasty around 1100. The kingdom occupied the high valleys of the upper [[e:chenab|Chenab]] between [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]] and the [[e:jammu|Jammu]] hills.
kishtwar-kingdom.r: Kishtwar exported saffron and lay on routes between [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]], [[s:chamba-state|Chamba]] and [[s:kingdom-of-ladakh|Ladakh]]. In the 17th century the [[e:sufism|Sufi]] saint Shah Farid-ud-din came to Kishtwar, and Raja [[e:kirat-singh-of-kishtwar|Kirat Singh]] converted to [[e:islam|Islam]], after which the dynasty and much of the population became Muslim. The Rajas were tributaries of the Mughal emperors.
kishtwar-kingdom.e: [[e:gulab-singh|Gulab Singh]], [[e:dogras|Dogra]] ruler of [[e:jammu|Jammu]] under the [[s:sikh-empire|Sikh Empire]], conquered Kishtwar in 1821. It became part of [[s:jammu-and-kashmir-princely-state|Jammu and Kashmir (princely state)]] in 1846 and is now a district of Jammu and [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]].

kingdom-of-marion.t: Cypriot kingdom on the north-west coast that grew rich on copper trade with Athens until Ptolemy I destroyed it in 312 BCE.
kingdom-of-marion.o: Marion grew near modern [[e:polis-chrysochous|Polis Chrysochous]] in north-west [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]], close to the [[e:copper|copper]] mines of Limni, in the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]]. It emerged as a city-kingdom in the Cypro-Archaic period, facing [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]] and the [[e:aegean|Aegean]] across the sea.
kingdom-of-marion.r: Marion exported [[e:copper|copper]] and imported large quantities of Athenian painted pottery, found in its cemeteries. Its kings, some with Greek names such as Stasioikos and others possibly Phoenician, issued coins in the 5th and 4th centuries BCE. Inscriptions use the Cypriot syllabary for Greek.
kingdom-of-marion.e: Its last king, [[e:stasioikos-ii|Stasioikos II]], sided with [[e:antigonus-i-monophthalmus|Antigonus]] against [[e:ptolemy-i-soter|Ptolemy I]], who destroyed Marion in 312 BCE and moved its people to [[s:kingdom-of-paphos|Paphos]]. [[e:ptolemy-ii-philadelphus|Ptolemy II]] refounded the site as Arsinoe c. 270 BCE, and the modern town of [[e:polis|Polis]] stands there today.

kingdom-of-lower-egypt.t: The predynastic Nile Delta, remembered by later Egyptians as a kingdom of the red crown centred on Buto before unification with the south.
kingdom-of-lower-egypt.o: Later Egyptian tradition held that before unification the Delta formed a kingdom of its own, with its capital at [[e:buto|Buto]] (Pe and Dep) and the red crown as its emblem. Archaeologically the region was home to the [[e:buto-maadi-culture|Buto-Maadi culture]] of the 4th millennium BCE, with settlements at Buto, Maadi and [[e:tell-el-farkha|Tell el-Farkha]].
kingdom-of-lower-egypt.r: Whether the Delta was ever a single kingdom is debated; many scholars see a cluster of chiefdoms and trading towns gradually absorbed by [[e:naqada|Naqada]] culture spreading from the south around 3400 to 3300 BCE. The [[e:palermo-stone|Palermo Stone]] lists names of early northern kings, but they cannot be checked. [[e:buto|Buto]] was home to the cobra goddess [[e:wadjet|Wadjet]], and Maadi traded [[e:copper|copper]], wine and oil with [[e:canaan|Canaan]].
kingdom-of-lower-egypt.e: The north was brought under southern rule around 3100 BCE, remembered as its conquest by [[e:narmer|Narmer]] or [[e:menes|Menes]] and the founding of [[s:early-dynastic-egypt|Early Dynastic Egypt]]. The red crown and [[e:wadjet|Wadjet]] survived as emblems of [[e:lower-egypt|Lower Egypt]] in royal regalia and titles for three thousand years.

kingdom-of-qataban.t: An incense kingdom of south Arabia centred on Wadi Bayhan and its capital Timna, rival of Saba and Hadramawt for five centuries.
kingdom-of-qataban.o: Qataban emerges in Sabaean inscriptions of the 7th century BCE as a junior ally of the [[s:kingdom-of-saba|Kingdom of Saba]]. As Sabaean power waned, its rulers asserted independence by the 5th or 4th century BCE, ruling from [[e:timna-yemen|Timna]] (modern Hajar Kuhlan) in [[e:wadi-bayhan|Wadi Bayhan]], at the start of the caravan route north.
kingdom-of-qataban.r: The kingdom taxed the [[e:incense|incense]] trade and built irrigation systems in [[e:wadi-bayhan|Wadi Bayhan]]. Its most famous text, a royal market law inscribed on a stele at [[e:timna-yemen|Timna]], regulated trade and taxes. Qatabanians worshipped the god Amm and wrote [[e:qatabanian-language|Qatabanic]]. At its height it reached the [[e:gulf-of-aden|Gulf of Aden]] coast and [[e:wadi-markha|Wadi Markha]].
kingdom-of-qataban.e: Qataban weakened in the 1st and 2nd centuries CE as sea trade grew. [[e:timna-yemen|Timna]] was burnt, and around 175 CE the [[s:kingdom-of-hadramawt|Kingdom of Hadramawt]] and the [[s:himyarite-kingdom|Himyarite Kingdom]] divided its lands. Excavations by American teams in the 1950s made Timna one of the best-known south Arabian sites.

kingdom-of-zazzau.t: Southernmost of the seven Hausa states, famed for the warrior queen Amina and for its role in raiding and trade toward the Niger and Benue.
kingdom-of-zazzau.o: Zazzau emerged by the 11th century among [[e:hausa|Hausa]] farming communities on the southern edge of [[s:hausa-kingdoms|Hausaland]] and is counted among the [[e:hausa-bakwai|Hausa Bakwai]]. Its early capital was Turunku. Tradition holds that [[e:zaria|Zaria]], the later capital, was founded in the 16th century by Queen Bakwa Turunku and named after one of her daughters.
kingdom-of-zazzau.r: Zazzau's position on the frontier made it the [[e:hausa|Hausa]] state of war captives and expansion: its rulers raided and taxed peoples to the south and controlled routes to the [[e:nupe-kingdom|Nupe]] and [[s:kwararafa|Kwararafa]] lands. [[e:queen-amina|Queen Amina]], remembered as a 16th century conqueror, is credited with walled camps across the region. [[e:islam|Islam]] spread among the ruling class from the 15th century.
kingdom-of-zazzau.e: In 1808 the jihadist [[e:mallam-musa|Malam Musa]] took [[e:zaria|Zaria]], which became the [[s:zaria-emirate|Zaria Emirate]] under the [[s:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto Caliphate]]. The [[e:hausa|Hausa]] royal house fled south and founded the [[s:abuja-emirate|Abuja Emirate]] at Zuba, today's [[e:suleja|Suleja]]. Zaria remains an [[e:emirate|emirate]] and a major city of northern [[e:nigeria|Nigeria]].

kalingga-kingdom.t: A Javanese kingdom on the north coast of Central Java, famed in Chinese records for the strict justice of its Queen Shima.
kalingga-kingdom.o: Chinese histories of the [[e:tang-dynasty|Tang dynasty]] describe a kingdom called Ho-ling on [[e:java|Java]] that sent envoys from the 7th century. Most historians place it on the north coast of [[e:central-java|Central Java]], near [[e:jepara|Jepara]]. Its beginnings are not recorded, and the register's dates are approximate.
kalingga-kingdom.r: The [[e:new-book-of-tang|New Book of Tang]] tells of [[e:queen-shima|Queen Shima]], chosen in 674, whose rule was so just that a bag of gold left in the road went untouched for three years until her own son touched it with his foot, for which she ordered his punishment. Ho-ling was also a Buddhist centre: the monk [[e:huining-monk|Huining]] worked there with the Javanese scholar Jnanabhadra in 664 to 665 to translate scriptures.
kalingga-kingdom.e: Kalingga's later history is obscure. Its people and court traditions are thought to have passed into the [[s:medang-kingdom|Medang Kingdom]], founded by [[e:sanjaya-of-mataram|Sanjaya]] in 732 in the interior of [[e:central-java|Central Java]]. The legend of [[e:queen-shima|Shima]] remains a popular story of good government in [[s:indonesia|Indonesia]].

kingdom-of-the-netherlands.t: The Dutch constitutional monarchy, shaped by the 1848 constitution, colonial empire, neutrality, war and post-war reconstruction into a founding EU member.
kingdom-of-the-netherlands.o: The Kingdom of the Netherlands took its present shape when William I accepted Belgian independence in the [[e:treaty-of-london-1839|Treaty of London]] of 1839. Constitutional revision in 1848, drafted under [[e:johan-rudolf-thorbecke|Johan Rudolf Thorbecke]], introduced ministerial responsibility and direct elections, establishing parliamentary government.
kingdom-of-the-netherlands.r: The colonial empire, above all the [[s:dutch-east-indies|Dutch East Indies]], brought wealth through the cultivation system, criticised in [[e:multatuli|Multatuli's]] [[e:max-havelaar|Max Havelaar]]. Society was organised in 'pillars' of Protestants, Catholics, socialists and liberals. The country stayed neutral in the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] but was occupied by [[e:germany|Germany]] from 1940 to 1945, while [[e:wilhelmina-of-the-netherlands|Queen Wilhelmina]] led the government from [[e:london|London]].
kingdom-of-the-netherlands.e: [[s:indonesia|Indonesia]] became independent in 1949. After the [[e:north-sea|North Sea]] flood of 1953 the Delta Works were built. The Netherlands co-founded [[e:nato|NATO]] and the [[e:european-communities|European Communities]], and since 1954 the Kingdom has included [[e:caribbean|Caribbean]] countries. [[e:willem-alexander-of-the-netherlands|Willem-Alexander]] became king in 2013.

kingdom-of-agbor.t: Ika kingdom west of the lower Niger, ruled by the Dein of Agbor and long within the sphere of the Benin Empire.
kingdom-of-agbor.o: Agbor lies in the forest between [[e:benin-city|Benin City]] and the [[e:niger-river|Niger]], among the [[e:ika-people|Ika]], an Igboid-speaking people with strong ties to the [[e:edo-people|Edo]]. Its kingship is believed to date from around the 15th century, when [[e:benin-empire|Benin]] influence spread east toward the river, and its traditions combine Edo and [[e:igbo-people|Igbo]] elements.
kingdom-of-agbor.r: The Dein of Agbor ruled with title-holding chiefs and age-grade associations over yam-farming villages. Agbor paid tribute to the [[e:oba-dynasty|Oba]] of the [[s:benin-empire|Benin Empire]] and adopted [[e:benin-empire|Benin]] titles and regalia, while keeping its own dynasty and local religious practices.
kingdom-of-agbor.e: After the British conquest of [[e:benin-empire|Benin]] in 1897, Agbor came under British control and was incorporated into [[s:protectorate-of-southern-nigeria|Southern Nigeria]]. The Dein of Agbor remains the traditional ruler of Agbor in Delta State.

kingdom-of-manu-a.t: The island realm of the Tuʻi Manuʻa in eastern Samoa, whose title was revered as the oldest and most sacred in Samoan tradition.
kingdom-of-manu-a.o: The [[e:manua-islands|Manuʻa]] group, the islands of [[e:tau-american-samoa|Taʻu]], Ofu and [[e:olosega|Olosega]], lies at the eastern end of the Samoan archipelago. Samoan tradition holds that the god [[e:tagaloa|Tagaloa]] created the islands and that the first Tuʻi Manuʻa was his descendant, so the title predates the great titles of [[e:upolu|Upolu]] and [[e:savaii|Savaiʻi]]. Its early history is known only from oral genealogies.
kingdom-of-manu-a.r: The Tuʻi [[e:manua-islands|Manuʻa]] lived on [[e:tau-american-samoa|Taʻu]] and was surrounded by strict taboos: commoners could not look on him directly, and a council of chiefs (fono) handled daily affairs. Villages lived from taro, breadfruit, coconut and fishing. Manuʻa stood somewhat apart from the wars over titles in western [[e:samoan-islands|Samoa]], and its prestige rested on ancestry and ritual rather than conquest. Christian missionaries arrived in the 1830s and most islanders converted.
kingdom-of-manu-a.e: After the Samoan islands were divided in 1899, [[e:tui-manua-elisala|Tuʻi Manuʻa Elisala]] signed a deed of cession to the [[s:united-states|United States]] in 1904, bringing [[e:manua-islands|Manuʻa]] into what became [[s:american-samoa|American Samoa]]. After his death in 1909 the American authorities discouraged the title, which fell into abeyance.

kingdom-of-israel.t: The northern Kingdom of Israel, a wealthy Iron Age state centred on Samaria, home of prophets Elijah and Amos, conquered by Assyria.
kingdom-of-israel.o: After [[e:solomon|Solomon's]] death c. 930 BCE, the northern tribes rejected his son and made [[e:jeroboam-i|Jeroboam I]] king, splitting the [[s:united-kingdom-of-israel|United Kingdom of Israel]]. Jeroboam set up shrines at [[e:bethel|Bethel]] and Dan to rival [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]]. [[e:omri|Omri]] founded a new capital at [[e:samaria|Samaria]] c. 880 BCE.
kingdom-of-israel.r: Israel was larger and richer than [[s:kingdom-of-judah|Judah]], with [[e:olive-oil|olive oil]], wine and trade links to [[s:tyre|Tyre]]. [[e:ahab|Ahab]] fielded 2,000 [[e:chariot|chariots]] at [[e:battle-of-qarqar|Qarqar]] in 853 BCE, and the Black [[e:obelisk|Obelisk]] shows [[e:jehu|Jehu]] paying tribute to [[e:shalmaneser-iii|Shalmaneser III]]. The prophets [[e:elijah|Elijah]], [[e:amos-prophet|Amos]] and [[e:hosea|Hosea]] condemned its kings' religious and social policies.
kingdom-of-israel.e: After a revolt against the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]], [[e:shalmaneser-v|Shalmaneser V]] besieged [[e:samaria|Samaria]], which fell in 722 BCE; [[e:sargon-ii|Sargon II]] deported over 27,000 people and made Israel a province. The exiles became the legend of the ten lost tribes, while the [[e:samaritans|Samaritans]] claim descent from those who remained.

kingdom-of-dhanyawadi.t: The first kingdom of Arakan in the Rakhine chronicles, remembered as the home of the Mahamuni image, the most revered Buddha statue in Myanmar.
kingdom-of-dhanyawadi.o: Rakhine chronicles place the founding of Dhanyawadi far back in antiquity, with a line of kings ruling from a walled city in the Kaladan valley. Historians date the excavated city, with its brick walls and palace site, to the early centuries CE, and the register's 1st to 4th century span follows the later chronicle chronology.
kingdom-of-dhanyawadi.r: Dhanyawadi was a [[e:rice|rice]]-growing and trading kingdom on the [[e:bay-of-bengal|Bay of Bengal]], open to Indian influence. Its fame rests on the [[e:mahamuni-buddha|Mahamuni Buddha]], which tradition says was cast in the Buddha's lifetime under King [[e:chandrasuriya|Chandrasuriya]]. [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] inscriptions and coins of the following Chandra kings show Indian-style kingship.
kingdom-of-dhanyawadi.e: According to the chronicles, power shifted south to the new city of [[s:kingdom-of-waithali|Waithali]] around 370. The Mahamuni image remained at Dhanyawadi until 1784, when the [[s:konbaung-dynasty|Konbaung dynasty]] carried it to [[e:amarapura|Amarapura]]; its temple, now within [[e:mandalay|Mandalay]], is still a major pilgrimage site.

kingdom-of-abkhazia.t: A western Georgian kingdom whose rulers, though Abkhaz in origin, built a Georgian church and culture and through Bagrat III united Georgia in 1008.
kingdom-of-abkhazia.o: Around 778 [[e:leon-ii-of-abkhazia|Leon II]], ruler of the [[s:principality-of-abasgia|Principality of Abasgia]], broke from the [[s:byzantine-empire|Byzantine Empire]] with [[e:khazar-khaganate|Khazar]] help, took the title king and joined Abasgia to [[s:kingdom-of-lazica|Egrisi]], the old lands of Lazica. He moved his capital to [[e:kutaisi|Kutaisi]], shifting the state's centre into the Georgian-speaking interior.
kingdom-of-abkhazia.r: Over the 9th century the kings replaced Greek with Georgian in church and government and separated the western Georgian church from [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]]. Under [[e:george-ii-of-abkhazia|George II]] and [[e:constantine-iii-of-abkhazia|Constantine III]] the kingdom expanded into [[s:kingdom-of-iberia|Kartli]] and fought the [[e:bagratuni-dynasty|Armenian Bagratids]]. Churches such as [[e:mokvi-cathedral|Mokvi]] and [[e:bedia-cathedral|Bedia]] show its wealth, and the kingdom controlled the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] coast and Rioni valley.
kingdom-of-abkhazia.e: In 978 the throne passed to [[e:bagrat-iii-of-georgia|Bagrat III]], son of the Bagratid Gurgen and an Abkhazian princess. In 1008 he inherited [[s:kingdom-of-iberia|Kartli]] as well, founding the united [[s:kingdom-of-georgia|Kingdom of Georgia]].

krivichs.t: A large East Slavic tribal union on the upper Dnieper, Dvina and Volga, whose towns became Smolensk and Polotsk.
krivichs.o: The Krivichs settled the forested watershed between the [[e:dnieper|Dnieper]], the [[e:western-dvina|Western Dvina]] and the upper [[e:volga|Volga]] between the 6th and 8th centuries, mixing with the Baltic and [[e:finnic-peoples|Finnic peoples]] already there. Archaeologists link them with the culture of long burial mounds. The [[e:primary-chronicle|Primary Chronicle]] names their towns [[e:smolensk|Smolensk]], [[e:polotsk|Polotsk]] and [[e:izborsk|Izborsk]].
krivichs.r: They were organised in clans and districts around fortified centres, governed by elders and tribal assemblies. Their lands lay on the river route from the Baltic to the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]], so trade with Scandinavians brought [[e:silver|silver]] and goods. According to the chronicle, the Krivichs joined the [[s:ilmen-slavs|Ilmen Slavs]] and Finnic tribes in inviting [[e:rurik|Rurik]] and his [[e:varangians|Varangians]] to rule them.
krivichs.e: In 882 [[e:oleg-of-novgorod|Prince Oleg]] took [[e:smolensk|Smolensk]] on his way south to [[e:kyiv|Kiev]], and the Krivichs were drawn into [[s:kievan-rus|Kievan Rus']], paying tribute and serving in its armies. Their territory later formed the [[s:principality-of-polotsk|Principality of Polotsk]] and the [[s:principality-of-smolensk|Principality of Smolensk]], and their name survives in Latvian as the word for Russians, krievi.

kanjuruhan-kingdom.t: A small Hindu kingdom near modern Malang in East Java, known from a single Sanskrit inscription of 760 and the temple of Badut.
kanjuruhan-kingdom.o: Kanjuruhan is known almost entirely from the [[e:dinoyo-inscription|Dinoyo inscription]] of 760, found near [[e:malang|Malang]]. It tells how King [[e:gajayana|Gajayana]], son of Dewasimha, built a temple to the sage [[e:agastya|Agastya]] and replaced an old wooden image with one of black stone. It is the oldest known kingdom of [[e:east-java|East Java]].
kanjuruhan-kingdom.r: The inscription shows a Shaivite court with [[e:brahmins|Brahmin]] priests, gifts of land and [[e:cattle|cattle]], and a cult of [[e:agastya|Agastya]] brought from southern [[e:india|India]]. [[e:candi-badut|Candi Badut]], one of the oldest temples in [[e:east-java|East Java]], is thought to be the shrine it describes.
kanjuruhan-kingdom.e: No later record names Kanjuruhan as an independent kingdom. In the 9th and 10th centuries inscriptions mention a Rakai Kanuruhan as a title within the [[s:medang-kingdom|Medang Kingdom]], suggesting the area had been absorbed and its rulers became regional lords.

kingdom-of-upper-mesopotamia.t: The short-lived realm of the Amorite king Shamshi-Adad I, who united northern Mesopotamia from the Zagros to the Euphrates and ruled through his sons.
kingdom-of-upper-mesopotamia.o: [[e:shamshi-adad-i|Shamshi-Adad]], an Amorite chief, seized Ekallatum on the [[e:tigris|Tigris]] and then the city of [[e:assur|Assur]] around 1808 BCE. He went on to take [[s:mari|Mari]] on the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]] and the [[e:khabur-river|Khabur]] plains, creating the first state to unify [[e:upper-mesopotamia|Upper Mesopotamia]], with its capital at [[s:apum|Shubat-Enlil]] ([[e:tell-leilan|Tell Leilan]]).
kingdom-of-upper-mesopotamia.r: [[e:shamshi-adad-i|Shamshi-Adad]] ruled as 'king of the universe', placing his elder son [[e:ishme-dagan-i|Ishme-Dagan]] at Ekallatum and his younger son [[e:yasmah-addu|Yasmah-Addu]] at [[s:mari|Mari]]. The [[e:mari|Mari]] archives preserve his letters, in which he scolds Yasmah-Addu for idleness and directs campaigns, [[e:census|censuses]] and harvests. The kingdom was a network of fortified cities, tribal allies and [[e:vassal|vassals]], held together by the king's personal energy. Later Assyrian tradition counted him among the kings of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]].
kingdom-of-upper-mesopotamia.e: After [[e:shamshi-adad-i|Shamshi-Adad]] died around 1776 BCE, the kingdom fell apart. [[e:zimri-lim|Zimri-Lim]] recovered [[s:mari|Mari]], local kings rose at [[s:kingdom-of-andarig|Andarig]], [[s:kingdom-of-karana|Karana]] and [[s:kingdom-of-kurda|Kurda]], and [[e:ishme-dagan-i|Ishme-Dagan]] kept only the core around Ekallatum and [[e:assur|Assur]].

khanate-of-tabriz.t: The khanate of the great city of Tabriz in the turbulent half-century after Nader Shah, ruled for much of it by the Kurdish Donboli family.
khanate-of-tabriz.o: [[e:tabriz|Tabriz]], the chief city of [[s:azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]], came under local khans after the death of [[e:nader-shah|Nader Shah]] in 1747, as rivals including [[e:azad-khan-afghan|Azad Khan Afghan]] and [[e:fath-ali-khan-afshar|Fath Ali Khan Afshar]] fought over the region. Under [[e:karim-khan-zand|Karim Khan]] of the [[s:zand-empire|Zand Empire]], [[e:najaf-qoli-khan-donboli|Najaf Qoli Khan]] of the Donboli family was confirmed as governor and ruled largely independently.
khanate-of-tabriz.r: [[e:najaf-qoli-khan-donboli|Najaf Qoli Khan]] rebuilt [[e:tabriz|Tabriz]] after the devastating earthquake of 1780, constructing new walls and gates. The city remained a major centre of trade between [[e:iran|Iran]], the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]] and [[e:russia|Russia]], famous for its bazaar and crafts. The khans balanced between the [[e:zand-dynasty|Zands]], the Donbolis of [[e:khoy|Khoy]] and other neighbours.
khanate-of-tabriz.e: [[e:agha-mohammad-khan-qajar|Agha Mohammad Khan]]'s [[s:qajar-iran|Qajar Iran]] took [[e:tabriz|Tabriz]] in the 1790s, and from 1799 the city became the seat of the [[e:qajar-dynasty|Qajar]] crown prince, notably [[e:abbas-mirza|Abbas Mirza]], as governor of [[s:azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]].

kel-gres.t: A Tuareg confederation pushed south from Aïr that settled on the borderlands of Hausaland, mixing pastoral and agricultural life.
kel-gres.o: The Kel Gres lived in the [[e:air-mountains|Aïr]] mountains in the early modern period, with ties to the [[s:sultanate-of-agadez|Sultanate of Agadez]]. Pressure from the [[s:kel-ewey|Kel Ewey]] drove them south, and by the 18th century they had settled in the region between [[e:tahoua|Tahoua]] and [[e:madaoua|Madaoua]] on the northern edge of the [[s:hausa-kingdoms|Hausa kingdoms]].
kel-gres.r: The Kel Gres combined [[e:camel|camel]] and [[e:cattle|cattle]] herding with control over farming villages worked by dependent and servile groups. They traded in salt and livestock and were drawn into the wars of the [[s:kingdom-of-gobir|Kingdom of Gobir]] and its neighbours, and later into rivalries with the [[s:iwellemmeden-kel-dinnik|Iwellemmeden Kel Dinnik]]. Muslim scholarly lineages had high prestige.
kel-gres.e: The French conquered the region around 1900, and [[e:tuareg|Tuareg]] resistance during the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] was suppressed by 1917. The Kel Gres are today part of [[e:niger-river|Niger's]] Tuareg population.

karafuto-prefecture.t: Japan's colony on the southern half of Sakhalin island, won from Russia in 1905 and lost to the Soviet Union in 1945.
karafuto-prefecture.o: The [[e:treaty-of-portsmouth|Treaty of Portsmouth]] that ended the [[e:russo-japanese-war|Russo-Japanese War]] in 1905 gave [[e:japan|Japan]] [[e:sakhalin|Sakhalin]] south of the 50th parallel. Japan set up the Karafuto Agency in 1907 at [[e:korsakov-sakhalin|Otomari]], moving its seat in 1908 to [[e:yuzhno-sakhalinsk|Toyohara]], the former Russian settlement of Vladimirovka.
karafuto-prefecture.r: Karafuto was run by a governor under the home government. Japanese settlers came to fish herring and salmon, cut [[e:timber|timber]] and work in pulp and paper mills and [[e:coal|coal]] mines, and the population reached about 400,000 by the 1940s, including Korean labourers. [[e:ainu|Ainu]], [[e:nivkh-people|Nivkh]] and [[e:orok-people|Uilta]] communities were pressed to assimilate. In 1943 Karafuto was made part of [[e:japan|Japan]] proper.
karafuto-prefecture.e: Soviet forces invaded in August 1945 and occupied the territory, and the Japanese population was repatriated by 1949, though many [[e:koreans|Koreans]] were left behind. [[e:japan|Japan]] renounced its claim in 1951, and the area is now part of [[e:russia|Russia's]] [[e:sakhalin-oblast|Sakhalin Oblast]].

kingdom-of-pengwern.t: A shadowy British kingdom of the Shropshire borderlands, remembered in the Welsh poems lamenting Cynddylan and the ruin of his hall.
kingdom-of-pengwern.o: Pengwern is known almost entirely from Welsh poetry, notably the [[e:canu-heledd|Canu Heledd]], a 9th or 10th century cycle of poems lamenting [[e:cynddylan|Cynddylan]], a 7th century prince. Its centre is uncertain; later tradition placed it at [[e:shrewsbury|Shrewsbury]], while scholars have suggested [[e:viroconium-cornoviorum|Wroxeter]], [[e:baschurch|Baschurch]] or the [[e:the-wrekin|Wrekin]].
kingdom-of-pengwern.r: Nothing reliable is recorded of its government. The poems describe [[e:cynddylan|Cynddylan's]] empty hall, his grave at Eglwysau Bassa, perhaps [[e:baschurch|Baschurch]], and his wars against the English, and he may have been an ally of [[e:penda-of-mercia|Penda]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-mercia|Kingdom of Mercia]]. The kingdom was probably one of several successors to the [[s:cornovii|Cornovii]] tribal region.
kingdom-of-pengwern.e: Pengwern seems to have fallen to Mercian expansion in the mid 7th century; [[e:cynddylan|Cynddylan's]] death is lamented in the poems. Its lands became Mercian, while its memory survived in Welsh literature as a symbol of loss.

kingdom-of-saxony.t: Kingdom of the Albertine Wettins created under Napoleon, a German industrial heartland around Dresden, Leipzig and Chemnitz.
kingdom-of-saxony.o: Elector [[e:frederick-augustus-iii-of-saxony|Frederick Augustus III of Saxony]] changed sides after [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia's]] defeat at [[e:jena|Jena]] and joined the [[s:confederation-of-the-rhine|Confederation of the Rhine]] in December 1806, taking the title King [[e:frederick-augustus-i-of-saxony|Frederick Augustus I]]. [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] also made him Duke of [[e:warsaw|Warsaw]] in 1807.
kingdom-of-saxony.r: [[e:saxony|Saxony]] fought for [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] until [[e:leipzig|Leipzig]] in 1813, and at the [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] it lost about three-fifths of its territory to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]]. A constitution followed the unrest of 1830, and the May Uprising in [[e:dresden|Dresden]] in 1849 was crushed with Prussian help. Textiles, machine building and mining made Saxony one of [[e:germany|Germany's]] most industrialised regions, and Leipzig was a centre of publishing and music.
kingdom-of-saxony.e: [[e:saxony|Saxony]] sided with [[e:austria|Austria]] in 1866, then joined the [[s:north-german-confederation|North German Confederation]] and in 1871 the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]]. [[e:frederick-augustus-iii-of-saxony|King Frederick Augustus III]] abdicated in November 1918, and the state became the [[s:free-state-of-saxony|Free State of Saxony]].

kingdom-of-gandhara.t: An ancient kingdom of Taxila and the Peshawar valley, gateway between India and Iran, before it became a province of the Achaemenid Empire.
kingdom-of-gandhara.o: Gandhara, praised in the [[e:rigveda|Rigveda]] for its sheep's wool, became one of the sixteen mahajanapadas by the 7th and 6th centuries BCE. It covered the [[e:peshawar|Peshawar]] valley and the land across the [[e:indus|Indus]] around [[e:taxila|Taxila]], in modern [[s:islamic-republic-of-pakistan|Pakistan]] and eastern [[s:islamic-emirate-of-afghanistan-2021-present|Afghanistan]], and controlled the routes linking the [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges plain]] with [[s:greco-bactrian-kingdom|Bactria]] and [[e:iran|Iran]].
kingdom-of-gandhara.r: Buddhist texts record its king Pukkusati, said to have exchanged envoys and gifts with [[e:bimbisara|Bimbisara of Magadha]] and later to have become a monk. [[e:taxila|Taxila]] was already a centre of learning, where teachers taught the [[e:vedas|Vedas]], medicine and statecraft to students from across northern [[e:india|India]]. Excavations at the [[e:bhir-mound|Bhir Mound]] reveal the early city with its irregular streets.
kingdom-of-gandhara.e: Around 518 BCE Gandhara appears as a subject land in the [[e:behistun-inscription|Behistun inscription]] of [[e:darius-i|Darius I]], conquered by [[e:cyrus-the-great|Cyrus]] or Darius, and it paid tribute to the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]]. Under Persian rule the Kharoshthi script developed from [[e:aramaic|Aramaic]]. Local rule resurfaced later in the [[s:kingdom-of-taxila|Kingdom of Taxila]] that Alexander met.

korean-empire.t: Korea's last independent monarchy, proclaimed by King Gojong in 1897 to assert equality with China and Japan, and annexed by Japan in 1910.
korean-empire.o: After [[e:japan|Japan's]] victory over [[e:qing-empire|Qing China]] in 1895 ended [[e:korea|Korea's]] tributary ties, Japanese agents murdered Queen Min, and [[e:gojong-of-korea|King Gojong]] took refuge in the Russian legation in 1896. Returning to his palace in 1897, he proclaimed the Great Han Empire and took the title of emperor, choosing the era name Gwangmu.
korean-empire.r: The [[e:gwangmu-reform|Gwangmu reforms]] carried out land surveys, issued land titles and brought electricity, [[e:telegraph|telegraphs]], a tramway and the first railway to [[e:seoul|Seoul]], while strengthening imperial power. The emperor suppressed the reformist Independence Club in 1898. [[e:korea|Korea]] became a prize in rivalry between [[e:russia|Russia]] and [[e:japan|Japan]], and Japan's victory in the war of 1904 and 1905 left it exposed.
korean-empire.e: The [[e:japan-korea-treaty-of-1905|Eulsa Treaty]] of 1905 made [[e:korea|Korea]] a Japanese [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] under Resident-General [[e:ito-hirobumi|Ito Hirobumi]]. [[e:gojong-of-korea|Gojong]] sent secret envoys to [[e:the-hague|The Hague]] in 1907 and was forced to abdicate for his son [[e:sunjong-of-korea|Sunjong]]; the army was disbanded, and [[e:japan|Japan]] annexed Korea in 1910.

kingdom-of-ystrad-tywi.t: Early Welsh kingdom of the Tywi valley in Carmarthenshire, conquered around 730 by Ceredigion to form the realm of Seisyllwg.
kingdom-of-ystrad-tywi.o: Ystrad Tywi, 'the vale of the Tywi', covered the fertile river valley and surrounding uplands of what is now [[e:carmarthenshire|Carmarthenshire]], including the old Roman town of [[e:carmarthen|Moridunum]], Carmarthen. After Roman rule ended around 410 it seems to have emerged as a separate territory, sometimes held by the kings of the neighbouring [[s:kingdom-of-dyfed|Kingdom of Dyfed]].
kingdom-of-ystrad-tywi.r: Very little is known about its rulers or government, and no secure king list survives. The Tywi valley was among the best farmland in south-west [[e:wales|Wales]], with major church sites such as Llandeilo Fawr, home of the gospel book now known as the [[e:lichfield-gospels|Lichfield Gospels]] before it left Wales.
kingdom-of-ystrad-tywi.e: Around 730 [[e:seisyll-ap-clydog|Seisyll ap Clydog]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-ceredigion|Kingdom of Ceredigion]] conquered Ystrad Tywi, forming a larger kingdom named [[s:kingdom-of-seisyllwg|Seisyllwg]] after him. This passed in the 10th century to [[e:hywel-dda|Hywel Dda]] and became part of [[s:kingdom-of-deheubarth|Deheubarth]], whose later princes ruled from Dinefwr in the Tywi valley.

kingdom-of-kaan.t: The Snake Kingdom, the most powerful Classic Maya state, which from Dzibanche and later Calakmul built a network of allies to encircle Tikal.
kingdom-of-kaan.o: The snake-head emblem dynasty of Kaan is first firmly attested at [[e:dzibanche|Dzibanche]] in southern [[e:quintana-roo|Quintana Roo]] in the 5th and 6th centuries. Around 635 the dynasty moved its seat to Calakmul in [[e:campeche|Campeche]], a large city whose own earlier lords had used a different emblem.
kingdom-of-kaan.r: Kaan exercised power through hegemony rather than direct rule: subject kings at [[s:caracol|Caracol]], [[s:naranjo|Naranjo]], [[s:dos-pilas|Dos Pilas]], [[s:el-peru-waka|El Perú-Waka']], [[s:la-corona|La Corona]] and [[s:cancuen|Cancuén]] acknowledged its overlords. Under [[e:yuknoom-cheen-ii|Yuknoom Ch'een II]], who reigned from 636 to about 686, it reached its height, and Calakmul holds more stelae than any other Maya city. Its alliance defeated [[s:tikal|Tikal]] in 562.
kingdom-of-kaan.e: Tikal's victory over [[e:yuknoom-yichaak-kahk|Yuknoom Yich'aak K'ahk']] in 695 broke Kaan's dominance, and its network fragmented in the 8th century. Calakmul raised its last monuments around 900. The kingdom remained little known until its glyphs were deciphered in the 1990s.

kingdom-of-albania-medieval.t: Angevin kingdom on the Albanian coast created by Charles I of Anjou in 1272 as a base for his ambitions against Byzantium.
kingdom-of-albania-medieval.o: [[e:charles-i-of-anjou|Charles I of Anjou]], king of [[e:sicily|Sicily]], acquired claims to the Albanian coast through the Treaty of [[s:commune-of-viterbo|Viterbo]] of 1267. In 1272 Albanian nobles and the city of [[e:durres|Durrës]] accepted him, and he proclaimed himself King of [[s:albania|Albania]] (Regnum Albaniae).
kingdom-of-albania-medieval.r: The kingdom was governed by Angevin captains-general and marshals from [[e:durres|Durrës]], with Albanian nobles granted titles and privileges. It served as a bridgehead for Charles's planned attack on [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]], but the Angevin army was defeated at the siege of [[e:berat|Berat]] in 1281. Thereafter it was reduced mostly to Durrës and its surroundings, held by the princes of [[e:achaea|Achaea]] and [[s:principality-of-taranto|Taranto]].
kingdom-of-albania-medieval.e: Albanian lords and the [[s:serbian-empire|Serbian Empire]] took much of the land in the 14th century. In 1368 [[e:karl-thopia|Karl Thopia]] seized [[e:durres|Durrës]], ending Angevin rule and founding the [[s:principality-of-albania-medieval|Principality of Albania (medieval)]].

kowoj.t: A Maya group of the Petén lakes that claimed descent from Mayapan and rivalled the Itza until both fell to Spain in 1697.
kowoj.o: According to their own traditions, the Kowoj (Couoh) migrated south from [[s:league-of-mayapan|Mayapan]] to the [[e:peten|Petén]] lakes after its fall around 1441, arriving by about 1450. They settled the north-eastern shores of [[e:lake-peten-itza|Lake Petén Itzá]] and nearby lakes, with [[e:zacpeten|Zacpetén]] on [[e:lake-salpeten|Lake Salpetén]] as an important centre.
kowoj.r: The Kowoj were led by their own lords and at times allied with, and at times fought, the [[s:itza-kingdom-of-nojpeten|Itza kingdom]] of Nojpetén. Their towns show architecture modelled on [[s:league-of-mayapan|Mayapan]], with temple assemblages and colonnaded halls. Excavations at [[e:zacpeten|Zacpetén]] revealed ritual deposits and evidence of warfare. Kowoj leaders were involved in the [[e:itza-people|Itza]] succession struggles of the 1690s.
kowoj.e: The Spanish conquest of Nojpetén in 1697 ended Kowoj independence. Many fled into the forests, and the survivors were gathered into colonial mission towns around the lake.

kingdom-of-han-206-bc.t: The remote kingdom Xiang Yu gave Liu Bang in 206 BCE, from which Liu fought his way out to defeat Xiang Yu and found the Han dynasty.
kingdom-of-han-206-bc.o: [[e:liu-bang|Liu Bang]], a minor [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] official turned rebel, was first to enter the Qin heartland and accepted the surrender of [[e:ziying|Ziying]]. [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]], wary of him, made him King of Han in 206 BCE, ruling the isolated [[e:hanzhong|Hanzhong]], Ba and Shu regions from Nanzheng. Liu Bang burned the plank roads behind him to show he had no ambitions.
kingdom-of-han-206-bc.r: With the chancellor [[e:xiao-he|Xiao He]] managing supplies and the general [[e:han-xin|Han Xin]] commanding the army, the kingdom became a base for war. Xiao He kept the [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] records and grain stores, and [[e:sichuan|Sichuan's]] resources fed the campaigns.
kingdom-of-han-206-bc.e: In 206 BCE [[e:liu-bang|Liu Bang]] conquered the [[e:three-qins|Three Qins]], then fought [[s:western-chu|Western Chu]] for four years, losing at [[e:xuzhou|Pengcheng]] but recovering. After [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu's]] death at [[e:battle-of-gaixia|Gaixia]] in 202 BCE, Liu Bang took the title of emperor, and his kingdom gave its name to the [[s:han-dynasty|Han Dynasty]] and to the [[e:han-chinese|Han Chinese]].

khanate-of-gilan.t: A short-lived khanate on the Caspian coast whose ruler Hedayat-Allah Khan built up Rasht before falling to Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar.
khanate-of-gilan.o: [[e:hedayat-allah-khan|Hedayat-Allah Khan]], of a notable family from [[e:fuman|Fuman]], became governor of [[e:gilan|Gilan]] under [[e:karim-khan-zand|Karim Khan]] of the [[s:zand-empire|Zand Empire]] around 1762 and soon ruled the province as an autonomous khanate with its centre at [[e:rasht|Rasht]].
khanate-of-gilan.r: [[e:gilan|Gilan]] was rich from [[e:silk|silk]], [[e:rice|rice]] and Caspian trade with [[e:russia|Russia]], and [[e:hedayat-allah-khan|Hedayat-Allah Khan]] developed [[e:rasht|Rasht]] as a commercial town. He was caught between the [[e:zand-dynasty|Zands]], the rising [[e:qajar-dynasty|Qajar]] leader [[e:agha-mohammad-khan-qajar|Agha Mohammad Khan]] and Russia, whose navy and merchants were active on the Caspian; he invited Russian help and briefly lost and regained his province.
khanate-of-gilan.e: In 1786 [[e:agha-mohammad-khan-qajar|Agha Mohammad Khan]] invaded [[e:gilan|Gilan]]. [[e:hedayat-allah-khan|Hedayat-Allah Khan]] fled and was killed, and Gilan became part of the emerging [[s:qajar-iran|Qajar Iran]].

kingdom-of-gwent.t: Welsh kingdom between the Usk and the Wye, heir to the Roman town of Caerwent, which fell to the Normans after 1067.
kingdom-of-gwent.o: Gwent took its name from [[e:venta-silurum|Venta Silurum]], [[e:caerwent|Caerwent]], the Roman capital of the [[s:silures|Silures]]. After Roman rule ended a kingdom formed in the land between the [[e:river-usk|Usk]] and the [[e:river-wye|Wye]], with traditions of a founder named Caradog Freichfras. Its kings were often the same as those of the [[s:kingdom-of-glywysing|Kingdom of Glywysing]], the two realms passing between branches of one dynasty.
kingdom-of-gwent.r: The [[e:book-of-llandaff|Llandaff charters]] record grants by its kings to churches and show a landscape of royal estates and small monasteries. Brochfael ap Meurig submitted to [[e:alfred-the-great|Alfred of Wessex]], according to [[e:asser|Asser]]. The kingdom lay on the English border, and its rulers alternately fought and allied with the Mercians and later the English kings, while the fertile [[e:river-usk|Usk]] valley and coastal levels provided its wealth.
kingdom-of-gwent.e: [[e:gruffydd-ap-llywelyn|Gruffudd ap Llywelyn]] seized Gwent in the 1050s. After the [[e:norman-conquest|Norman Conquest]] [[e:william-fitzosbern|William FitzOsbern]] built [[e:chepstow-castle|Chepstow Castle]] from 1067 and pushed west. Its last king, [[e:caradog-ap-gruffydd|Caradog ap Gruffudd]], was killed at the battle of [[e:battle-of-mynydd-carn|Mynydd Carn]] in 1081, and Gwent became Norman marcher lordships, later [[e:monmouthshire|Monmouthshire]].

kingdom-of-allada.t: Aja kingdom of the Slave Coast, the leading slave-trading state of the area in the 17th century and the ancestral seat of Dahomey's kings.
kingdom-of-allada.o: [[e:allada|Allada]] was founded by [[e:aja-people|Aja]] migrants from Tado, west of the [[e:mono-river|Mono river]], traditionally in the 15th century. Tradition links its royal line, descended from the founding ancestor Agassu, to the later rulers of the [[s:kingdom-of-dahomey|Kingdom of Dahomey]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-porto-novo|Kingdom of Porto-Novo]], which branched off from Allada in the 17th century.
kingdom-of-allada.r: [[e:allada|Allada's]] king, known to Europeans as the king of Ardra, controlled the coast through the port of Offra and dealt with Portuguese, [[e:dutch|Dutch]], English and French traders, becoming a major source of enslaved people by the 1640s. In 1670 Allada sent an ambassador to the court of [[e:louis-xiv|Louis XIV]]. Vodun cults and royal ancestor worship underpinned kingship.
kingdom-of-allada.e: In 1724 [[e:agaja|Agaja]] of [[s:kingdom-of-dahomey|Dahomey]] conquered [[e:allada|Allada]], which was absorbed into his kingdom. The town remains a ritual centre, and the Allada dynasty is recognised as the ancestor of [[e:benin-empire|Benin's]] royal houses.

kingdom-of-bhutan.t: The Himalayan Buddhist monarchy of the Wangchuck dynasty, known for its policy of Gross National Happiness.
kingdom-of-bhutan.o: After decades of civil strife in [[s:zhabdrung-bhutan|Zhabdrung Bhutan]], [[e:ugyen-wangchuck|Ugyen Wangchuck]], penlop of [[e:trongsa|Trongsa]], defeated his rivals and gained British favour. In 1907 an assembly of monks, officials and nobles at [[e:punakha|Punakha]] elected him the first hereditary king, the [[e:druk-gyalpo|Druk Gyalpo]], ending the dual system of rule.
kingdom-of-bhutan.r: The [[e:treaty-of-punakha|Treaty of Punakha]] in 1910 placed foreign affairs under British guidance, a role later taken by [[e:india|India]] in 1949. [[e:jigme-dorji-wangchuck|Jigme Dorji Wangchuck]] created a national assembly in 1953 and began modernisation, and [[e:thimphu|Thimphu]] became the capital. [[e:jigme-singye-wangchuck|Jigme Singye Wangchuck]] promoted [[e:gross-national-happiness|Gross National Happiness]] and preserved traditional culture. The expulsion of many [[e:lhotshampa|Lhotshampa]] of Nepali descent in the early 1990s remains controversial.
kingdom-of-bhutan.e: [[e:jigme-singye-wangchuck|Jigme Singye Wangchuck]] devolved power and abdicated in 2006 in favour of his son [[e:jigme-khesar-namgyel-wangchuck|Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck]]. [[s:zhabdrung-bhutan|Bhutan]] held its first parliamentary elections and adopted a constitution in 2008, becoming a [[e:constitutional-monarchy|constitutional monarchy]].

cr.a: See File history below for details.

kirghiz-ssr.t: The Soviet republic of the Kyrgyz in the Tian Shan, the direct forerunner of today's Kyrgyzstan.
kirghiz-ssr.o: Under the Soviet constitution of December 1936 the [[s:kazakh-assr|Kirghiz ASSR]] was made a union republic, the Kirghiz SSR, with its capital at [[e:bishkek|Frunze]], the former Pishpek and today's Bishkek.
kirghiz-ssr.r: The republic was a land of mountain pastures, livestock farming, mining and some industry, with a large Russian population in [[e:bishkek|Frunze]] and the north and [[e:uzbeks|Uzbeks]] in the south around Osh. [[e:kyrgyz-people|Kyrgyz]] culture was promoted in Soviet form, including the epic of [[e:epic-of-manas|Manas]] and the novels of [[e:chingiz-aitmatov|Chingiz Aitmatov]]. [[e:turdakun-usubaliyev|Turdakun Usubaliyev]] led the party from 1961 to 1985. Ethnic clashes between Kyrgyz and Uzbeks in Osh in 1990 killed hundreds.
kirghiz-ssr.e: The physicist [[e:askar-akayev|Askar Akayev]] became president in 1990. After the failed [[e:moscow|Moscow]] coup, the republic declared independence on 31 August 1991 as the Republic of [[s:kyrgyzstan|Kyrgyzstan]].

kingdom-of-orleans.t: Short-lived Merovingian kingdom of Clovis' son Chlodomer, which vanished when he fell in battle in 524.
kingdom-of-orleans.o: In the division of 511 [[e:clovis-i|Clovis]]' second son [[e:chlodomer|Chlodomer]] received lands along the [[e:loire|Loire]], with [[e:orleans|Orléans]] as his capital, together with [[e:tours|Tours]], [[e:bourges|Bourges]] and part of [[s:duchy-of-aquitaine|Aquitaine]].
kingdom-of-orleans.r: [[e:chlodomer|Chlodomer]] ruled for only thirteen years. Little is known of his government beyond his wars against the [[s:kingdom-of-the-burgundians|Kingdom of the Burgundians]], during which he had the captured [[e:sigismund-of-burgundy|King Sigismund]] and his family killed in 524.
kingdom-of-orleans.e: [[e:chlodomer|Chlodomer]] was killed later in 524 at the [[e:battle-of-vezeronce|Battle of Vézeronce]]. His uncles [[e:childebert-i|Childebert I]] and [[e:chlothar-i|Chlothar I]] murdered two of his young sons and divided his kingdom. The third son, [[e:clodoald|Clodoald]], escaped and became a monk; the town of [[e:saint-cloud|Saint-Cloud]] near [[e:paris|Paris]] is named after him.

kotda-pitha-state.t: A minor Kathi chiefship of central Kathiawar, one of the clan estates under British supervision.
kotda-pitha-state.o: Kotda Pitha was a small estate in central [[e:kathiawar|Kathiawar]] held by a Kathi family from around 1700. Its founding is known mainly from local tradition.
kotda-pitha-state.r: The Darbar held a few villages and, after 1807, came under British supervision in the [[e:kathiawar-agency|Kathiawar Agency]]. Little else is recorded in standard works.
kotda-pitha-state.e: Kotda Pitha merged into the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960.

krusevo-republic.t: Ten-day revolutionary government in the mountain town of Kruševo during the Ilinden Uprising of 1903, celebrated in North Macedonia as a founding moment.
krusevo-republic.o: On 2 August 1903, the feast of Saint [[e:elijah|Elijah]], the [[e:internal-macedonian-revolutionary-organization|Internal Macedonian-Adrianople Revolutionary Organisation]] launched the [[e:ilinden-preobrazhenie-uprising|Ilinden Uprising]] against Ottoman rule in [[e:macedonia-region|Macedonia]]. Rebels under [[e:nikola-karev|Nikola Karev]] and [[e:pitu-guli|Pitu Guli]] seized [[e:krusevo|Kruševo]], a prosperous mountain town of Slav, Aromanian and Greek-oriented [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] families, and proclaimed a provisional government.
krusevo-republic.r: [[e:nikola-karev|Karev]] headed a council that included members of the different communities, and the town's administration, courts and supplies were reorganised for defence. The [[e:krusevo-manifesto|Kruševo Manifesto]], attributed to the rebels, called on the local Muslim population to join the struggle against tyranny rather than against neighbours. The republic lasted about ten days.
krusevo-republic.e: An Ottoman army retook [[e:krusevo|Kruševo]] around 12 August 1903; [[e:pitu-guli|Pitu Guli]] died defending the Mečkin Kamen position and much of the town was burnt. [[s:bulgaria|Bulgaria]] and [[e:north-macedonia|North Macedonia]] both claim the uprising, and the Ilinden memorial at Kruševo is a national symbol of North [[e:macedonia-region|Macedonia]].

koliya-republic.t: A small clan republic in the Himalayan foothills, home of the Buddha's mother and neighbour and kin of the Shakyas.
koliya-republic.o: The Koliyas lived east of the [[s:shakya-republic|Shakya republic]], across the Rohini river in the [[e:terai|Terai]] of modern [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Nepal]] and [[e:india|India]]. They emerged as a self-governing clan by the 7th or 6th century BCE, with their main town at [[e:ramagrama|Ramagrama]]. The two clans intermarried, and Buddhist tradition makes Maya, mother of [[e:gautama-buddha|the Buddha]], a Koliya princess.
koliya-republic.r: Like the [[s:shakya-republic|Shakyas]], the Koliyas were governed by an assembly of clan heads. They grew [[e:rice|rice]] on land watered by the Rohini, and Buddhist texts tell how a quarrel with the Shakyas over its water nearly led to war until [[e:gautama-buddha|the Buddha]] reconciled them. They were dependent on the larger [[s:kingdom-of-kosala|Kingdom of Kosala]].
koliya-republic.e: After [[e:gautama-buddha|the Buddha]]'s death the Koliyas received a share of his relics and built a stupa at [[e:ramagrama|Ramagrama]], which survives in [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Nepal]]. They were absorbed by [[s:kingdom-of-kosala|Kosala]] and then by [[s:kingdom-of-magadha|Magadha]] in the 5th century BCE.

kingdom-of-armenia-orontid.t: The first Armenian dynasty, the Orontids or Yervandunis, ruled Armenia as Persian satraps and then as kings for over three centuries before the Seleucids took over.
kingdom-of-armenia-orontid.o: After the fall of the [[s:kingdom-of-urartu|Kingdom of Urartu]], Armenian-speaking groups dominated the highlands. The [[e:orontid-dynasty|Orontid]] family appears as governors of the [[e:satrapy|satrapy]] of [[s:armenia|Armenia]] under the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]], and the [[e:behistun-inscription|Behistun inscription]] of [[e:darius-i|Darius I]] records fighting in [[e:armenia|Armenia]] in 521 BCE. The traditional start of the dynasty in the 6th century BCE is uncertain.
kingdom-of-armenia-orontid.r: The [[e:orontid-dynasty|Orontids]] ruled as [[e:satrapy|satraps]] closely tied to the Persian court, sending horses as tribute, while [[e:xenophon|Xenophon]] described the villages and wheat beer of [[s:armenia|Armenia]] in 401 BCE. After [[e:alexander-the-great|Alexander the Great]], they ruled as effectively independent kings from [[e:armavir-ancient-city|Armavir]] and then [[e:yervandashat|Yervandashat]]. Their culture blended Iranian religion and [[e:aramaic|Aramaic]] administration with local traditions.
kingdom-of-armenia-orontid.e: Around 200 BCE the [[e:seleucid-empire|Seleucid]] king [[e:antiochus-iii-the-great|Antiochus III]] defeated [[e:orontes-iv|Orontes IV]] and divided the land between his generals [[e:artaxias-i|Artaxias]] and [[e:zariadres|Zariadres]]. After the Seleucid defeat at [[e:battle-of-magnesia|Magnesia]] in 190 BCE, Artaxias founded the [[s:kingdom-of-armenia-artaxiad|Kingdom of Armenia (Artaxiad)]], which kept many [[e:orontid-dynasty|Orontid]] traditions.

kingdom-of-ngoyo.t: A small Kongo coastal kingdom around Cabinda whose port grew into one of the busiest Atlantic slave-trading harbours north of the Congo River.
kingdom-of-ngoyo.o: Ngoyo was one of three [[e:kongo-language|Kikongo]]-speaking kingdoms on the coast north of the [[e:congo-river|Congo]] estuary, alongside the [[s:kingdom-of-loango|Kingdom of Loango]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-kakongo|Kingdom of Kakongo]]. Its people, the [[e:woyo|Woyo]], recognised the seniority of Loango in early times but by the mid-16th century Ngoyo was ruled by its own king, the Mangoyo, from Mbanza Ngoyo.
kingdom-of-ngoyo.r: The king was a sacred figure who, by tradition, could not see the sea, and was elected by senior lineages. Royal officials managed trade at the port of [[s:portuguese-congo|Cabinda]], where [[e:dutch|Dutch]], English, French and Portuguese ships bought slaves, [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and [[e:copper|copper]] brought from the interior. The trade made local merchant families rich and weakened the crown.
kingdom-of-ngoyo.e: After the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|Atlantic slave trade]] ended, the kingdom declined. In 1885 local princes signed the [[e:treaty-of-simulambuco|Treaty of Simulambuco]], placing the area under Portuguese protection, and it became the [[s:portuguese-congo|Cabinda]] exclave of [[s:portuguese-angola|Portuguese Angola]].

kataghan-khanate.t: An Uzbek khanate of northern Afghanistan centred on Kunduz, a slave-raiding power under Murad Beg until absorbed by the Afghan Emirate.
kataghan-khanate.o: The Qataghan [[e:uzbeks|Uzbeks]] had settled in the region of [[e:kunduz|Kunduz]] in the 17th and 18th centuries. In the early 19th century their leader [[e:murad-beg-of-kunduz|Murad Beg]] built a powerful state from Kunduz, taking [[e:balkh|Balkh]], [[s:principality-of-badakhshan|Badakhshan]] and neighbouring [[e:tajiks|Tajik]] districts around 1815 to 1820.
kataghan-khanate.r: [[e:murad-beg-of-kunduz|Murad Beg]] ruled with an army of [[e:uzbeks|Uzbek]] horsemen and grew rich from raiding and slaving, deporting [[e:tajiks|Tajiks]] of [[s:principality-of-badakhshan|Badakhshan]] to the marshy [[e:kunduz|Kunduz]] plain. The British traveller [[e:alexander-burnes|Alexander Burnes]] and [[e:william-moorcroft|William Moorcroft]] described his court in the 1820s and 1830s. Successors were weaker and paid tribute to [[e:bukhara|Bukhara]] or [[e:kabul|Kabul]].
kataghan-khanate.e: After [[e:murad-beg-of-kunduz|Murad Beg]]'s death in the 1840s the khanate declined. In 1859 [[e:dost-mohammad-khan|Dost Mohammad Khan's]] son [[e:mohammad-afzal-khan|Muhammad Afzal Khan]] conquered [[e:kunduz|Kunduz]] for the [[s:emirate-of-afghanistan|Emirate of Afghanistan]], ending its independence.

kazakhstan.t: The world's largest landlocked country, a resource-rich steppe state that built a new capital at Astana and balances between Russia, China and the West.
kazakhstan.o: The [[s:kazakh-ssr|Kazakh SSR]] was the last Soviet republic to declare independence, on 16 December 1991, under [[e:nursultan-nazarbayev|Nursultan Nazarbayev]], who had led it since 1989. The new state inherited the [[e:semey|Semipalatinsk]] test site, which was closed, and a large nuclear arsenal, which it gave up by 1995.
kazakhstan.r: [[e:nursultan-nazarbayev|Nazarbayev]] ruled as president for nearly three decades, building a strong presidential system with little political competition. Oil from fields such as [[e:tengiz-field|Tengiz]] and [[e:kashagan-field|Kashagan]], gas, uranium and metals brought rapid growth. The capital moved from [[e:almaty|Almaty]] to [[e:astana|Astana]] in 1997. The state promoted [[e:kazakhs|Kazakh]] language and culture while keeping Russian widely used and managing a large ethnic Russian minority in the north.
kazakhstan.e: [[e:nursultan-nazarbayev|Nazarbayev]] resigned in 2019 in favour of [[e:kassym-jomart-tokayev|Kassym-Jomart Tokayev]] but kept influence until the January 2022 unrest, when protests over fuel prices turned violent and Russian-led troops were briefly deployed. Tokayev then curbed Nazarbayev's family and introduced constitutional changes.

kingdom-of-ormus.t: The island kingdom of Hormuz, which controlled the mouth of the Gulf and its horse and spice trade until Persia and England expelled the Portuguese.
kingdom-of-ormus.o: Arab and Persian traditions say the kingdom was founded in the 11th century on the mainland near modern [[e:minab|Minab]] by a ruler from [[e:oman|Oman]]. Around 1300, harried by Mongol-era raids, its king moved the capital to the barren island of [[e:hormuz|Jarun]], which took the name Hormuz.
kingdom-of-ormus.r: [[e:hormuz|Hormuz]] lived by trade, taxing ships between [[e:india|India]], [[e:persia|Persia]], [[e:arabia|Arabia]] and [[e:east-africa|East Africa]] and shipping Arabian horses to India. [[e:marco-polo|Marco Polo]] and [[e:ibn-battuta|Ibn Battuta]] visited it. Kings controlled ports on both sides of the [[e:persian-gulf|Gulf]], including [[e:qalhat|Qalhat]], [[e:muscat|Muscat]] and [[s:sheikhdom-of-bahrain|Bahrain]], and paid tribute to stronger mainland powers. Water and food had to be brought to the island.
kingdom-of-ormus.e: [[e:afonso-de-albuquerque|Afonso de Albuquerque]] attacked in 1507 and in 1515 made [[e:hormuz|Hormuz]] a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the [[s:portuguese-empire|Portuguese Empire]], which built a fortress and controlled its customs. In 1622 an Anglo-Persian force under [[e:abbas-i-of-persia|Shah Abbas I]] of the [[s:safavid-empire|Safavid Empire]] captured the island, ending the kingdom; trade moved to [[e:bandar-abbas|Bandar Abbas]].

kingdom-of-epirus.t: Kingdom of the Molossians in north-west Greece, whose Aeacid kings led the Epirote peoples and produced Pyrrhus, Rome's most famous Greek opponent.
kingdom-of-epirus.o: The Molossian kings claimed descent from [[e:neoptolemus|Neoptolemus]], son of [[e:achilles|Achilles]], and were called [[e:aeacidae|Aeacids]]. Their kingdom in the mountains of [[e:epirus|Epirus]] emerges into history in the 5th century BCE; King [[e:tharyps|Tharyps]], educated at [[s:athens|Athens]], introduced Greek institutions and letters. The [[e:molossians|Molossians]] gradually led the other Epirote tribes, the [[e:chaonians|Chaonians]] and [[e:thesprotians|Thesprotians]], in an alliance.
kingdom-of-epirus.r: Kings ruled alongside an assembly and annual magistrates, swearing to govern by law. The economy rested on [[e:pastoralism|pastoralism]], with [[e:dodona|Dodona's]] oracle of [[e:zeus|Zeus]] as the great religious centre. [[e:alexander-i-of-russia|Alexander I]], brother of [[e:olympias|Olympias]] and uncle of [[e:alexander-the-great|Alexander the Great]], campaigned in southern [[e:italy|Italy]] until his death in 331 BCE. [[e:pyrrhus-of-epirus|Pyrrhus]] (297-272 BCE) made [[s:ambracia|Ambracia]] his capital and won costly victories over [[e:rome|Rome]].
kingdom-of-epirus.e: After [[e:pyrrhus-of-epirus|Pyrrhus]] died at [[s:argos|Argos]] in 272 BCE, his successors struggled against [[e:kingdom-of-macedon|Macedon]] and the [[e:aetolians|Aetolians]]. The last of the royal line, [[e:deidamia-ii-of-epirus|Deidamia]], was killed around 232 BCE and the monarchy was replaced by the [[s:epirote-league|Epirote League]]. Pyrrhus survives in the phrase 'Pyrrhic victory'.

karystos.t: City of southern Euboea, forced into the Delian League by Athens and later famed for its green-veined Cipollino marble.
karystos.o: Karystos lay at the southern end of [[e:euboea|Euboea]], below [[e:mount-ochi|Mount Ochi]]. Greek tradition held that its people were [[e:dryopes|Dryopes]], later joined by Ionian settlers. It grew in the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] as a farming and seafaring community, controlling the channel between Euboea and [[s:andros|Andros]].
karystos.r: The [[e:persians|Persians]] forced Karystos to submit in 490 BCE, and it fought on their side in 480 BCE. [[s:athens|Athens]] then compelled it to join the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]] c. 472 BCE. In the 4th century BCE it produced the physician [[e:diocles-of-carystus|Diocles]], and later the writer [[e:antigonus-i-monophthalmus|Antigonus]]. Its green-veined marble, [[e:cipollino-marble|Cipollino]], was quarried heavily in Roman times.
karystos.e: Karystos passed between Macedonian kings and [[s:athens|Athens]] in the [[e:hellenistic-period|Hellenistic period]] and came under Roman control by 146 BCE. Its marble quarries remained important under the Empire, and the modern town keeps the ancient name.

kotharia-state.t: A small Jadeja Rajput estate near Rajkot in Kathiawar, a cadet branch of the Rajkot ruling house.
kotharia-state.o: Kotharia was held by a branch of the [[e:jadeja|Jadeja Rajputs]] of [[s:rajkot-state|Rajkot]], who granted lands to younger sons as their share. The register dates its separate existence to around 1700.
kotharia-state.r: The Thakor ruled a small group of villages and, after 1807, came under British supervision in the [[e:kathiawar-agency|Kathiawar Agency]] as a minor non-salute state. Little else is recorded in standard references.
kotharia-state.e: Kotharia merged into the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960. It is now a suburb area of [[s:rajkot-state|Rajkot]].

katosan-state.t: A minor chiefship of the Mahi Kantha country in northern Gujarat, one of its many small hereditary holdings.
katosan-state.o: Katosan was one of the petty estates of the [[e:mahi-kantha-agency|Mahi Kantha]] region whose rulers held a small group of villages from around 1600. Its origins are known mainly from local tradition and colonial gazetteers.
katosan-state.r: The Thakor paid tribute through the [[e:gaekwads|Gaekwads of Baroda]] and was supervised by the [[e:mahi-kantha-agency|British Mahi Kantha Agency]]. Standard references record little beyond its status as a minor non-salute state.
katosan-state.e: Katosan was merged into [[s:bombay-presidency|Bombay Province]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960, in present [[e:mehsana-district|Mehsana district]].

kingdom-of-murcia.t: A Castilian frontier kingdom in south-eastern Spain, formed after the reconquest of Murcia and kept as a historical unit until 1833.
kingdom-of-murcia.o: After the [[e:mudejar-revolt-of-1264-1266|Mudéjar revolt]] of 1264-1266, [[e:james-i-of-aragon|James I of Aragon]] conquered [[e:murcia|Murcia]] on behalf of his son-in-law [[e:alfonso-x-of-castile|Alfonso X of Castile]], ending the [[s:third-taifa-of-murcia|Third Taifa of Murcia]]. Alfonso X resettled the territory with Castilians and Catalans and kept it as a separate kingdom within the [[s:crown-of-castile|Crown of Castile]].
kingdom-of-murcia.r: [[e:murcia|Murcia]] was a frontier facing both the [[s:emirate-of-granada|Emirate of Granada]] and the [[s:crown-of-aragon|Crown of Aragon]], which took its northern districts by the [[e:treaty-of-torrellas|Treaty of Torrellas]] in 1304. The irrigated [[e:huerta|huertas]] produced [[e:silk|silk]], fruit and grain, the [[e:mudejar|Mudéjar]] population declined, and [[e:cartagena-colombia|Cartagena]] grew into the main naval base on the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]].
kingdom-of-murcia.e: The kingdom was a historical title and administrative unit rather than a self-governing state. In 1833 [[e:javier-de-burgos|Javier de Burgos's]] reform divided [[e:spain|Spain]] into provinces, splitting the old kingdom into the provinces of [[e:murcia|Murcia]] and [[e:province-of-albacete|Albacete]].

khandpara-state.t: A small Garhjat state on the Mahanadi in central Orissa, founded by a branch of the Nayagarh ruling family.
khandpara-state.o: Khandpara was established around 1599 when a younger member of the [[s:nayagarh-state|Nayagarh]] ruling house received the territory as his own principality. It lay south of the [[e:mahanadi|Mahanadi]], near the gorge where the river leaves the hills for the coastal plain.
khandpara-state.r: Its Rajas governed a small agrarian state of [[e:rice|rice]] villages and forest, with [[e:kondh|Khond]] and other tribal communities in the hills. After 1803 Khandpara was one of the [[e:orissa-tributary-states|Orissa Tributary Mahals]] under British paramountcy, later in the [[e:eastern-states-agency|Eastern States Agency]]. Little else of its internal history is widely recorded.
khandpara-state.e: Khandpara joined the province of [[e:odisha|Orissa]] on 1 January 1948, with the other [[e:garhjat-states|Garhjat states]]. Its territory lies in present-day [[s:nayagarh-state|Nayagarh]] district.

kingdom-of-tondo.t: A Tagalog trading polity on Manila Bay, named in the Laguna Copperplate Inscription of 900 and ruled by Lakandula when the Spanish arrived.
kingdom-of-tondo.o: The [[e:laguna-copperplate-inscription|Laguna Copperplate Inscription]], dated 900 and the oldest known document from the [[s:philippines|Philippines]], mentions a leader of Tundun, generally identified with Tondo. The settlement grew on the northern shore of the [[e:pasig-river|Pasig River]] delta, trading with Chinese merchants, who knew the region as Lusong.
kingdom-of-tondo.r: Tondo was ruled by a lakan or paramount chief over a society of maginoo nobles, maharlika warriors and dependants. It traded [[e:rice|rice]], [[e:cotton|cotton]] and gold for Chinese [[e:porcelain|porcelain]] and [[e:silk|silk]] and had close ties with [[s:brunei-sultanate|Brunei]]. By the 16th century parts of the elite had adopted [[e:islam|Islam]], while most people kept indigenous beliefs.
kingdom-of-tondo.e: After [[e:miguel-lopez-de-legazpi|Miguel Lopez de Legazpi]] took [[s:kingdom-of-maynila|Maynila]] in 1571, [[e:lakandula|Lakandula]] accepted Spanish rule and was baptised. In 1587 to 1588 his relatives led the Tondo conspiracy to expel the Spanish, which was discovered and its leaders executed or exiled. Tondo became a district of [[e:manila|Manila]] in the [[s:captaincy-general-of-the-philippines|Captaincy General of the Philippines]].

kingdom-of-buhweju.t: A small mountain kingdom of western Uganda, incorporated into Ankole by the British in 1901.
kingdom-of-buhweju.o: Buhweju occupied the hills north-west of [[e:mbarara|Mbarara]]. Its traditions link its rulers to the [[e:chwezi|Chwezi]] of the [[s:empire-of-kitara|Empire of Kitara]], and it emerged as a separate kingdom around the 17th century, remaining independent of its larger neighbours [[s:kingdom-of-ankole|Ankole]] and [[s:kingdom-of-bunyoro|Bunyoro]] for much of its history.
kingdom-of-buhweju.r: Buhweju was a small state of farmers and herders ruled by a king with clan leaders. It was known for iron working and for its rugged, defensible terrain. Little else is reliably recorded.
kingdom-of-buhweju.e: Under the [[e:ankole-agreement|Ankole Agreement]] of 1901 the British merged Buhweju into the [[s:kingdom-of-ankole|Kingdom of Ankole]]. It is now a district of western [[s:uganda|Uganda]].

kish.t: A powerful city of northern Sumer whose name became a title of supreme rule: to be 'king of Kish' meant to hold hegemony over Mesopotamia.
kish.o: Kish lay on the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]] in northern [[e:babylonia|Babylonia]], east of later [[e:babylon|Babylon]]. The [[e:sumerian-king-list|Sumerian King List]] names it as the seat of the first dynasty after the flood. [[e:enmebaragesi|Enmebaragesi]], who ruled around 2600 BCE, is the earliest king in the list confirmed by his own inscriptions.
kish.r: Kish had a mixed population, and its early texts show a strong Semitic element alongside Sumerian. Its kings exercised influence far beyond the city: [[e:mesalim-of-kish|Mesalim of Kish]] acted as arbiter in the border dispute between [[s:lagash|Lagash]] and [[s:umma|Umma]], and later rulers of other cities, including [[e:eannatum|Eannatum of Lagash]], adopted the title 'king of Kish' to claim wider authority. Its patron god was the warrior [[e:zababa|Zababa]].
kish.e: Under [[e:ur-zababa|Ur-Zababa]], the [[e:cupbearer|cupbearer]] [[e:sargon-of-akkad|Sargon]] rose to power and founded the [[s:akkadian-empire|Akkadian Empire]] around 2334 BCE, absorbing Kish. The city survived as a cult centre under later rulers, including [[e:hammurabi|Hammurabi]] and the Neo-Babylonian kings, and the prestige of its royal title outlasted it by centuries.

kingdom-of-tethba.t: A midland Irish kingdom spanning Longford and Westmeath, held by branches of the southern Ui Neill and later by the O'Farrells and O'Quinns.
kingdom-of-tethba.o: Tethba appears in the earliest Irish annals as a territory in the Irish midlands, divided by the [[e:river-inny|River Inny]] into northern and southern parts. Its rulers in the early [[e:middle-ages|medieval period]] came from Cairpre and [[s:county-of-maine|Maine]], sons of [[e:niall-of-the-nine-hostages|Niall of the Nine Hostages]], making it part of the southern [[e:ui-neill|Ui Neill]] world centred on Mide.
kingdom-of-tethba.r: Tethba was a small overkingship of several local peoples, often subordinate to the kings of Mide. Monasteries such as [[e:ardagh-county-longford|Ardagh]] and [[e:clonmacnoise|Clonmacnoise's]] daughter houses stood in or near its lands. In the 11th and 12th centuries local families, the Ui Cuinn and the Ui Fergail, rose to power in the northern part, later known as [[e:annaly|Annaly]].
kingdom-of-tethba.e: After the Norman invasion much of southern Tethba was granted to [[e:hugh-de-lacy-lord-of-meath|Hugh de Lacy]] within the [[s:lordship-of-meath|Lordship of Meath]]. [[e:annaly|Annaly]] survived under the [[e:ofarrell|O'Farrells]] until the 16th century, when it became [[e:county-longford|County Longford]].

kingdom-of-libya.t: Independent Libya under King Idris, a poor federal monarchy transformed by oil discoveries and overthrown by Gaddafi in 1969.
kingdom-of-libya.o: Under a UN resolution, [[e:libya|Libya]] became independent on 24 December 1951 as a federal kingdom uniting [[s:tripolitania|Tripolitania]], [[e:cyrenaica|Cyrenaica]] and the [[s:sultanate-of-fezzan|Fezzan]], with [[e:idris-of-libya|Idris al-Senussi]], ruler of the [[s:emirate-of-cyrenaica|Emirate of Cyrenaica]], as King Idris I.
kingdom-of-libya.r: At independence [[e:libya|Libya]] was among the poorest countries in the world, depending on foreign aid and rent from British and American bases such as [[e:wheelus-air-base|Wheelus Air Base]]. The discovery of oil in 1959 and exports from 1961 brought sudden wealth. In 1963 the federation was abolished in favour of a unitary state. The king ruled conservatively, relying on Cyrenaican tribes.
kingdom-of-libya.e: On 1 September 1969, while Idris was abroad, army officers led by [[e:muammar-gaddafi|Muammar Gaddafi]] seized power and declared a republic. Idris died in exile in [[e:egypt|Egypt]] in 1983, and his flag was revived by the rebels of 2011.
