kingdom-of-cambodia.t: Present-day Cambodia, a constitutional monarchy restored in 1993 after decades of war, dominated in practice by Hun Sen and the Cambodian People's Party.
kingdom-of-cambodia.o: After the UN-supervised elections of May 1993, a constituent assembly adopted a new constitution, and on 24 September 1993 [[e:norodom-sihanouk|Norodom Sihanouk]] returned to the throne of a restored [[s:kingdom-of-cambodia-1953-1970|Kingdom of Cambodia]]. [[e:norodom-ranariddh|Norodom Ranariddh]] and [[e:hun-sen|Hun Sen]] became joint prime ministers of a coalition government.
kingdom-of-cambodia.r: The king reigns as head of state with limited powers; [[e:norodom-sihanouk|Sihanouk]] abdicated in 2004 in favour of his son [[e:norodom-sihamoni|Norodom Sihamoni]]. [[e:hun-sen|Hun Sen]] ousted [[e:norodom-ranariddh|Ranariddh]] in fighting in 1997 and dominated politics for decades. The last [[e:khmer-rouge|Khmer Rouge]] forces surrendered in 1998. Garment exports, tourism to [[e:angkor|Angkor]] and Chinese investment drove growth, while the main opposition party was dissolved in 2017.
kingdom-of-cambodia.e: The kingdom continues today. In 2023 [[e:hun-sen|Hun Sen]] handed the premiership to his son [[e:hun-manet|Hun Manet]], and in 2024 became president of the Senate. [[s:kingdom-of-cambodia-1953-1970|Cambodia]] joined [[e:association-of-southeast-asian-nations|ASEAN]] in 1999.

kingdom-of-diarra.t: Soninke kingdom of the Sahel north of the Senegal and Niger headwaters that outlived the Ghana Empire by nearly seven centuries.
kingdom-of-diarra.o: Diarra, or Diara, arose in the Kingaga region around present-day [[e:nioro-du-sahel|Nioro du Sahel]] as the [[s:ghana-empire|Ghana Empire]] fragmented. Tradition dates it to 1076, the year associated with the [[e:almoravid-empire|Almoravid Empire's]] attack on Ghana. Its first ruling house was the Niakhate clan, later replaced by the [[e:diawara|Diawara]].
kingdom-of-diarra.r: Diarra's [[e:soninke|Soninke]] rulers governed a mixed population of farmers and herders and profited from the trade between the desert and the savanna. The kingdom was usually a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of a larger power, first of the [[s:mali-empire|Mali Empire]] and then of the [[s:songhai-empire|Songhai Empire]], while keeping its own dynasties.
kingdom-of-diarra.e: In the 18th century Diarra was overrun by the [[e:bambara-people|Bambara]] of [[s:kingdom-of-kaarta|Kaarta]], who took its lands in 1754, according to the register's dating. The [[e:diawara|Diawara]] remain a recognised [[e:soninke|Soninke]] clan in western [[e:mali|Mali]].

kingdom-of-biram.t: Hausa state east of Kano, traditionally the oldest of the seven Hausa kingdoms and seat of their legendary founder's eldest son.
kingdom-of-biram.o: Biram, centred on Garun Gabas, appears in the [[e:bayajidda|Bayajidda]] legend: the hero is said to have had a son named Biram by a [[e:bornu|Bornu]] princess before reaching [[s:kingdom-of-daura|Daura]], so the kingdom was counted first among the [[s:hausa-kingdoms|Hausa Bakwai]]. Its origins probably lie in the 11th century, on the borderland between the [[e:hausa|Hausa]] plains and the [[s:kanem-bornu-empire|Kanem-Bornu Empire]].
kingdom-of-biram.r: Tradition gives Biram the role of seat of government among the [[e:hausa|Hausa states]], but in practice it was small and strongly influenced by [[e:bornu|Bornu]], to which it paid tribute for long periods. Its records are sparse, and its rulers are known only from late lists.
kingdom-of-biram.e: [[e:fula|Fulani]] forces of the [[e:jihad|jihad]] overran Biram in the first decade of the 19th century, and its lands were incorporated into the [[s:hadejia-emirate|Hadejia Emirate]]. Garun Gabas survives as a town in [[e:jigawa-state|Jigawa State]].

kingdom-of-ndorwa.t: A kingdom of the highlands between Rwanda and Uganda, remembered for its queen Kitami and as the cradle of the Nyabingi spirit cult.
kingdom-of-ndorwa.o: Ndorwa lay in the hills of today's south-western [[s:uganda|Uganda]] and northern [[s:kingdom-of-rwanda|Rwanda]]. Traditions from the region describe it as a kingdom of the 17th century, linked by marriage and war with the Kingdom of Rwanda, the [[s:kingdom-of-mpororo|Kingdom of Mpororo]] and the states of [[s:kingdom-of-ankole|Ankole]]. Its history is known only from oral accounts.
kingdom-of-ndorwa.r: Little is known of its government. Traditions remember a queen, Kitami, whose spirit became [[e:nyabingi|Nyabingi]], the focus of a powerful healing and resistance cult that spread across the region and later inspired revolts against colonial rule in the early 20th century.
kingdom-of-ndorwa.e: Ndorwa broke up in the 18th century and was conquered by [[s:kingdom-of-rwanda|Rwanda]] around 1800. Its lands were later divided by the colonial border between Rwanda and Uganda's [[e:kigezi|Kigezi]] district.

khedivate-of-egypt.t: Egypt under the khedives, which opened the Suez Canal, fell into debt and came under British occupation in 1882 while remaining nominally Ottoman.
khedivate-of-egypt.o: In 1867 the Ottoman sultan granted [[e:isma-il-pasha|Ismail Pasha]], grandson of [[e:muhammad-ali-of-egypt|Muhammad Ali]], the title of khedive and greater autonomy, transforming [[s:egypt-under-muhammad-ali|Egypt under Muhammad Ali]] into the Khedivate. Ismail aimed to make [[e:egypt|Egypt]] part of [[e:europe|Europe]], rebuilding [[e:cairo|Cairo]] on Parisian lines.
khedivate-of-egypt.r: The [[e:suez-canal|Suez Canal]] opened in 1869, and the [[e:cotton|cotton]] boom funded railways and schools, but borrowing became ruinous. Ismail sold his canal shares to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in 1875 and accepted Anglo-French financial control before being deposed in 1879. [[e:ahmed-urabi|Ahmed Urabi's]] nationalist revolt led [[e:britain|Britain]] to invade in 1882, and [[e:evelyn-baring-1st-earl-of-cromer|Lord Cromer]] effectively governed [[e:egypt|Egypt]] from 1883 to 1907.
khedivate-of-egypt.e: When the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]] joined the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] in 1914, [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] deposed [[e:abbas-ii-of-egypt|Khedive Abbas II]], ended Ottoman [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] and declared a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]], creating the [[s:sultanate-of-egypt|Sultanate of Egypt]] under [[e:hussein-kamel-of-egypt|Hussein Kamel]].

kingdom-of-galicia.t: The north-western Iberian kingdom centred on Santiago de Compostela, sometimes ruled by its own kings but usually joined with León and Castile.
kingdom-of-galicia.o: When [[e:alfonso-iii-of-asturias|Alfonso III of Asturias]] was deposed in 910, his son [[e:ordono-ii-of-leon|Ordoño II]] took [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Galicia]] as his kingdom. [[e:galicia|Galicia]] had been the core of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-suebi|Kingdom of the Suebi]] and a part of the Asturian realm, and the cult of [[e:james-the-great|St James]] at [[e:santiago-de-compostela|Compostela]] had made it famous across [[e:europe|Europe]].
kingdom-of-galicia.r: [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Galicia]] was dominated by a powerful nobility and the church, above all the archbishops of [[s:spanish-jamaica|Santiago]] such as [[e:diego-gelmirez|Diego Gelmírez]]. It had its own kings at times, among them [[e:garcia-ii-of-galicia|García II]] from 1065 to 1071, and [[e:alfonso-vii-of-leon-and-castile|Alfonso VII]] was crowned king of [[e:galicia|Galicia]] at [[e:santiago|Santiago]] in 1111. [[e:galician-portuguese|Galician-Portuguese]] became a major literary language, used for the troubadour lyric and the [[e:cantigas-de-santa-maria|Cantigas de Santa Maria]].
kingdom-of-galicia.e: From 1230 [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Galicia]] was permanently part of the [[s:crown-of-castile|Crown of Castile]], though it kept the title of kingdom and from the 16th century its own Junta. The provincial reform of 1833 abolished it as an administrative unit, but [[e:galicia|Galicia]] today is an autonomous community.

kingdom-of-kiziba.t: The northernmost Haya kingdom west of Lake Victoria, ruled by a Bito dynasty linked to Bunyoro.
kingdom-of-kiziba.o: Kiziba lay on the [[e:kagera-river|Kagera river]] at the northern edge of today's [[s:tanzania|Tanzania]]. Its rulers belonged to the [[e:babiito-dynasty|Babito]] clan, which traditions link with the royal house of the [[s:kingdom-of-bunyoro|Kingdom of Bunyoro]], and it emerged as a separate kingdom by the 17th century.
kingdom-of-kiziba.r: The mukama governed a [[e:haya-people|Haya]] farming society growing bananas and [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]], which was chewed as a stimulant and used in rituals. Kiziba kept its independence among rival Haya states and had close contacts with [[s:kingdom-of-buganda|Buganda]] to the north. Its court and royal rituals resembled those of other [[e:great-lakes|Great Lakes]] kingdoms.
kingdom-of-kiziba.e: Kiziba became a subordinate chiefdom under [[s:german-east-africa|German East Africa]] and then [[e:tanganyika-territory|British Tanganyika Territory]], ruled through its kings as a native authority. It ceased to exist when [[s:tanganyika|Tanganyika]] abolished the chieftaincies in 1963.

kingdom-of-loango.t: The Vili kingdom of the Loango coast, a major Atlantic trading power known for its raffia cloth, copper and ivory and later for slaves.
kingdom-of-loango.o: Loango emerged among the [[e:vili-people|Vili]] north of the [[e:congo-river|Congo River]], probably by the 15th century, and by the mid-16th century had shaken off any dependence on the [[e:kingdom-of-kongo|Kingdom of Kongo]]. Its king, the [[e:maloango|Maloango]], ruled from [[e:mbanza-loango|Mbanza Loango]] (Buali) near [[e:loango-bay|Loango Bay]], the kingdom's main harbour.
kingdom-of-loango.r: The [[e:maloango|Maloango]] was a sacred ruler chosen from princes of the royal matrilineage, assisted by ministers responsible for trade, war and the coast. Loango exported fine [[e:raffia-cloth|raffia cloth]], used as currency in the region, together with [[e:copper|copper]] from the Mindouli mines, [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and dyewood. From the 17th century [[e:dutch|Dutch]], English and French ships bought slaves at [[e:loango-bay|Loango Bay]] in large numbers.
kingdom-of-loango.e: The end of the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]] and long interregnums left the crown weak in the 19th century. In 1883 the coast came under French protection, and the area became part of the [[s:french-congo|French Congo]]. The [[e:maloango|Maloango]] title survives as a traditional office.

kingdom-of-gonja.t: A savanna kingdom in northern Ghana founded by Mande horsemen, whose divisional chiefs rotated the paramount title and whose Muslim scholars wrote its chronicle.
kingdom-of-gonja.o: Gonja tradition credits its foundation to [[e:ndewura-jakpa|Ndewura Jakpa]], leader of [[e:mande-peoples|Mande]] cavalry from the [[e:niger-river|Niger]] region, who conquered the lands between the Black and [[e:white-volta|White Volta]] rivers in the mid-17th century. The invaders, the [[e:ngbanya|Ngbanya]], ruled over many older peoples, and Jakpa divided the conquests among his sons, creating the divisions that formed the kingdom.
kingdom-of-gonja.r: The paramount chief, the Yagbumwura, was chosen in rotation from the ruling divisions and resided at Nyanga (Yagbum). Society was layered into the ruling estate, Muslim scholars of [[e:mande-peoples|Mande]] origin and commoners. Gonja controlled the kola trade of [[e:salaga|Salaga]] and Kafaba, linking the [[s:ashanti-empire|Ashanti Empire]] with [[e:hausa|Hausa]] traders. Muslim clerics wrote the [[e:kitab-ghanja|Kitab Ghanja]], an 18th-century chronicle of the state.
kingdom-of-gonja.e: The [[s:ashanti-empire|Ashanti Empire]] defeated Gonja in 1751-1752 and took tribute until 1874, when [[e:salaga|Salaga]] revolted. In the 1890s [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and [[e:germany|Germany]] divided the area, and most of Gonja became part of the [[s:northern-territories-of-the-gold-coast|Northern Territories of the Gold Coast]]. The Yagbumwura still heads the traditional state in [[e:ghana|Ghana]].

kingdom-of-waterford.t: A Norse town-kingdom at the mouth of the Suir, often called Ireland's oldest city, until its storming by the Anglo-Normans in 1170.
kingdom-of-waterford.o: [[e:vikings|Vikings]] raided the south-east in the 9th century, and in 914 a large fleet under [[e:ragnall-ua-imair|Ragnall]] established a base at [[e:waterford|Waterford]], Vedrafjordr. The settlement grew into a fortified trading town ruled by Norse kings or jarls, sometimes linked to the [[s:kingdom-of-dublin|Kingdom of Dublin]].
kingdom-of-waterford.r: [[e:waterford|Waterford]] traded wine, slaves and goods across the [[e:irish-sea|Irish Sea]] and to [[e:france|France]]. Its rulers became Christian and accepted [[e:bishop|bishops]] consecrated at [[e:canterbury|Canterbury]] from 1096. Irish overkings of [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Munster]], especially the [[e:obrien-dynasty|O'Briens]], often controlled the town, and [[e:reginalds-tower|Reginald's Tower]] recalls its Norse defences.
kingdom-of-waterford.e: In 1170 [[e:richard-de-clare-2nd-earl-of-pembroke|Strongbow]] and [[e:raymond-fitzgerald|Raymond le Gros]] stormed the town, and Strongbow married [[e:aoife-macmurrough|Aoife]], daughter of [[e:diarmait-mac-murchada|Diarmait Mac Murchada]], there. [[e:henry-ii-of-england|Henry II]] landed at [[e:waterford|Waterford]] in 1171 and made it a royal city in the [[s:lordship-of-ireland|Lordship of Ireland]].

kanker-state.t: A small Gond-country princely state in the hills of present-day Chhattisgarh, ruled from Kanker until 1948.
kanker-state.o: Kanker has inscriptions of local Somavanshi rulers from the 12th and 13th centuries; tradition dates the later ruling family to 1385. Its early history is only partly known.
kanker-state.r: Kanker was a forested state with a mainly [[e:gond-people|Gond]] population. In the 18th century it came under the [[e:bhonsles|Bhonsles]] of the [[s:nagpur-kingdom|Nagpur Kingdom]], passing under British control in 1853 and becoming one of the [[e:chhattisgarh-feudatory-states|Chhattisgarh Feudatory States]].
kanker-state.e: Kanker merged into the [[e:central-provinces|Central Provinces]], later [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]], in 1948 and is now a district of [[e:chhattisgarh|Chhattisgarh]].

kumul-khanate.t: A semi-autonomous Uyghur principality at Hami, loyal to the Qing for over two centuries, whose abolition in 1930 set off a major revolt in Xinjiang.
kumul-khanate.o: The Muslim ruling family of the [[e:hami|Hami]] oasis, threatened by the [[s:dzungar-khanate|Dzungar Khanate]], submitted to the [[e:kangxi-emperor|Kangxi Emperor]] in 1696 and helped Qing armies against the [[e:dzungars|Dzungars]]. Its leader [[e:abd-allah-beg|Abd Allah Beg]] was rewarded with a hereditary rank, and his descendants became princes (wang) of Hami under the [[s:qing-empire|Qing Empire]].
kumul-khanate.r: The khans governed the Turkic Muslim inhabitants of the oasis through their own begs, collected taxes in kind and [[e:corvee-labour|corvée]] from their subjects, and supplied the Qing with troops and provisions. They kept their position through the Qing conquest of [[e:xinjiang|Xinjiang]] in 1759 and the turmoil of [[s:yettishar|Yettishar]], and were regarded as one of the most loyal frontier houses.
kumul-khanate.e: After the death of the last khan, [[e:maqsud-shah|Maqsud Shah]], in 1930, the [[e:xinjiang|Xinjiang]] governor [[e:jin-shuren|Jin Shuren]] abolished the khanate and imposed direct rule and new taxes. The resulting [[e:hami|Kumul]] rebellion of 1931 drew in the Hui warlord [[e:ma-zhongying|Ma Zhongying]] and helped spark the [[s:first-east-turkestan-republic|First East Turkestan Republic]].

kingdom-of-lamjung.t: A hill kingdom of central Nepal from whose ruling house the Shah kings of Gorkha, and thus of Nepal, descended.
kingdom-of-lamjung.o: Lamjung emerged around 1500 in the hills of the Marsyangdi valley, ruled by a dynasty that claimed [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] descent. Its kings gained prominence among the [[e:chaubise-rajya|Chaubise Rajya]], the twenty-four principalities of central [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Nepal]]. In 1559 [[e:drabya-shah|Drabya Shah]], a younger son of the Lamjung ruler, founded the [[s:gorkha-kingdom|Gorkha Kingdom]] to the east.
kingdom-of-lamjung.r: Lamjung was a small agricultural state of terraced fields with a [[e:gurung|Gurung]] population and a [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] ruling family. Its kings competed with their [[s:gorkha-kingdom|Gorkha]] kinsmen for influence and allied at times with the [[s:kingdom-of-tanahun|Kingdom of Tanahun]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-palpa|Kingdom of Palpa]] against Gorkha expansion. Few detailed records survive.
kingdom-of-lamjung.e: After [[e:prithvi-narayan-shah|Prithvi Narayan Shah's]] conquests, Lamjung was annexed by the [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Kingdom of Nepal]] in 1782. It is now Lamjung district.

kingdom-of-iarmumu.t: The early medieval kingdom of West Munster around Killarney's lakes, ruled by the Eoganacht Locha Lein, rivals of the Munster kings at Cashel.
kingdom-of-iarmumu.o: Iarmumu took shape in south-west Ireland by the 6th century, when the [[e:eoganachta|Eoganacht]] Locha Lein, a branch of the dynasties ruling [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Munster]], established themselves around [[e:lough-leane|Loch Lein]], the Lower Lake at [[e:killarney|Killarney]]. Their territory covered much of later [[s:ciarraige-luachra|Kerry]] and west [[e:county-cork|Cork]], and they ruled over earlier peoples such as the [[e:corcu-duibne|Corcu Duibne]].
kingdom-of-iarmumu.r: The kings of Iarmumu sometimes claimed the kingship of all [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Munster]], but were usually excluded from the rotation of Cashel's [[e:eoganachta|Eoganacht]] branches. [[e:inisfallen|Inisfallen]] on [[e:lough-leane|Loch Lein]] became an important monastery, later home of the [[e:annals-of-inisfallen|Annals of Inisfallen]]. [[e:cattle|Cattle]] wealth and client peoples supported the dynasty.
kingdom-of-iarmumu.e: The dynasty declined from the 8th century, and in the 11th and 12th centuries the Ui Donnchada, a branch of the [[e:eoganacht-raithlind|Eoganacht Raithlind]] driven west from [[e:county-cork|Cork]], took over the lands around [[e:lough-leane|Loch Lein]]. The area then fell within the [[s:kingdom-of-desmond|Kingdom of Desmond]] under the [[e:charles-maccarthy|MacCarthys]], with the O'Donoghues as local lords around [[e:killarney|Killarney]].

kachari-kingdom.t: The kingdom of the Dimasa people of Assam, which moved from Dimapur to Maibang and finally Khaspur in the Barak valley.
kachari-kingdom.o: The [[e:dimasa-people|Dimasa Kacharis]] ruled the Dhansiri valley from [[e:dimapur|Dimapur]], whose carved stone pillars survive, by the 13th century. Repeated wars with the [[s:ahom-kingdom|Ahom kingdom]], which sacked Dimapur in 1536, pushed the kings south to [[e:maibang|Maibang]] in the [[e:dima-hasao|North Cachar]] hills, and in the 18th century to [[e:khaspur|Khaspur]] in the plains of [[e:cachar|Cachar]].
kachari-kingdom.r: The kings ruled a [[e:dimasa-people|Dimasa]] society organised in clans and gradually adopted [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] kingship; in 1790 Krishnachandra and his brother [[e:govinda-chandra-narayan|Govinda Chandra]] were formally admitted to Hindu [[e:kshatriya|Kshatriya]] status, and the kingdom was styled Heramba. Courts and land records came to use Bengali. The kingdom alternated between tribute to the [[e:ahom-people|Ahoms]] and independence, and fought [[s:kingdom-of-manipur|Manipur]] and the Jaintia kingdom.
kachari-kingdom.e: Burmese invasions in the 1810s and 1820s ravaged [[e:cachar|Cachar]]. After [[e:govinda-chandra-narayan|Govinda Chandra]], the last king, was assassinated in 1830 without an heir, the [[e:east-india-company|British East India Company]] annexed the plains in 1832. The hill areas followed later, and the region is now part of [[e:assam|Assam]].

kingdom-of-khotan.t: The jade-rich Buddhist kingdom of the southern Silk Road, whose Saka-speaking kings lasted more than a thousand years until the Kara-Khanid conquest.
kingdom-of-khotan.o: Khotan, Yutian in Chinese, grew in the oasis watered by rivers from the [[e:kunlun-mountains|Kunlun Mountains]] on the southern edge of the Taklamakan. Its own legends trace the founding to Indian and Chinese settlers, including a son of the emperor [[e:ashoka|Ashoka]]. It appears in Han records from the 2nd century BCE, already trading the white and green jade of its rivers.
kingdom-of-khotan.r: Khotan's people spoke Khotanese, an Eastern Iranian [[s:saka|Saka]] language preserved in many Buddhist texts. Its kings, of the Visa dynasty, made it a major centre of [[e:mahayana-buddhism|Mahayana Buddhism]], and tradition says a Chinese princess smuggled silkworm eggs to it in her headdress. Under the [[s:tang-dynasty|Tang Dynasty]] it was one of the [[e:four-garrisons-of-anxi|Four Garrisons of Anxi]]; in the 10th century King [[e:li-shengtian|Li Shengtian]] kept close ties with [[e:dunhuang|Dunhuang]].
kingdom-of-khotan.e: After a long war, the Muslim [[s:kara-khanid-khanate|Kara-Khanid Khanate]] conquered Khotan around 1006. Its Buddhist culture was replaced by [[e:islam|Islam]] and the Turkic language, but [[e:manuscript|manuscripts]] from Khotan and [[e:dunhuang|Dunhuang]] preserve Khotanese literature.

kingdom-of-rhufoniog.t: Small early Welsh kingdom between the Conwy and Clwyd valleys, named in legend after a son of Cunedda, later a cantref of Gwynedd.
kingdom-of-rhufoniog.o: Welsh tradition, preserved in genealogies written down centuries later, says the district took its name from Rhufon, one of the sons of [[e:cunedda|Cunedda]] who came from the north to settle north [[e:wales|Wales]] in the 5th century. The story is a later origin legend, but Rhufoniog existed as a distinct territory in the uplands of what is now [[e:denbighshire|Denbighshire]].
kingdom-of-rhufoniog.r: Very little is known of its rulers or government. It was one of several small early kingdoms of north [[e:wales|Wales]] whose local dynasties appear in medieval genealogies, and its territory included the hills around [[e:denbigh|Denbigh]]. Farming and [[e:cattle|cattle]]-rearing were the mainstay of a thinly settled land.
kingdom-of-rhufoniog.e: By the 9th century Rhufoniog had been absorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-gwynedd|Kingdom of Gwynedd]] and later formed one of the cantrefi of the [[e:perfeddwlad|Perfeddwlad]], the borderland between Gwynedd and [[e:england|England]] contested by Welsh princes and English kings until 1283.

kingdom-of-janjero.t: A small kingdom of the Yem people in south-western Ethiopia, known for its sacred kingship and its position between Kaffa, Ennarea and the Gibe states.
kingdom-of-janjero.o: Janjero, the kingdom of the Yem people, lay in the valley of the [[e:omo-river|Omo]] and [[e:gibe-river|Gibe]] rivers. It appears in Ethiopian chronicles from the 16th century as a tributary of the emperors, and [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] writers of the 17th century describe its rulers. Its own traditions are poorly recorded.
kingdom-of-janjero.r: Janjero was ruled by a sacred king whose person was surrounded by taboos, and European travellers reported elaborate royal rituals, including stories of sacrifice that may be exaggerated. Its people farmed ensete and grain and traded with neighbouring [[e:oromo|Oromo]] kingdoms and [[s:kingdom-of-kaffa|Kaffa]]. It spoke [[e:yemsa-language|Yemsa]], an Omotic language.
kingdom-of-janjero.e: In 1894 Janjero submitted to [[e:menelik-ii|Menelik II]], partly through the intervention of [[e:abba-jifar-ii|Abba Jifar II]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-jimma|Kingdom of Jimma]], and it was incorporated into the [[s:ethiopian-empire|Ethiopian Empire]]. The Yem people today have their own administrative unit in south-western [[s:federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia|Ethiopia]].

kingdom-of-altava.t: A Christian Berber kingdom of western Algeria whose king Kusaila killed the Arab conqueror Uqba ibn Nafi.
kingdom-of-altava.o: After the death of [[e:garmul|Garmul]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-moors-and-romans|Kingdom of the Moors and Romans]] in 578, [[e:berbers|Berber]] rulers continued to hold the region of [[e:altava|Altava]] and the plains of western [[e:algeria|Algeria]]. By the 7th century the dominant group was the [[e:awraba|Awraba]], a Berber confederation whose leader [[e:kusaila|Kusaila]] (Kasila) was Christian.
kingdom-of-altava.r: Almost nothing is known of the kingdom between 578 and the 680s. Arab writers say [[e:kusaila|Kusaila]] was captured by the commander [[e:abu-al-muhajir-dinar|Abu al-Muhajir]], converted to [[e:islam|Islam]] and accompanied the Arab army, but was humiliated by [[e:uqba-ibn-nafi|Uqba ibn Nafi]]. In 682 or 683 he ambushed and killed Uqba at [[e:battle-of-vescera|Tahuda]] near [[e:biskra|Biskra]], then took [[e:kairouan|Kairouan]] and ruled [[e:ifriqiya|Ifriqiya]] for several years.
kingdom-of-altava.e: [[e:kusaila|Kusaila]] was killed around 688 to 690 in battle against [[e:zuhayr-ibn-qays|Zuhayr ibn Qays]], and the [[s:umayyad-caliphate|Umayyad Caliphate]] subdued the region by 708. The [[e:awraba|Awraba]] converted to [[e:islam|Islam]] and later welcomed Idris I at [[e:volubilis|Volubilis]], helping found the [[s:idrisid-dynasty|Idrisid dynasty]].

kingdom-of-bundu.t: A Muslim clerical state between the Senegal and Faleme rivers, among the earliest of its kind in West Africa and a forerunner of the later Fulbe imamates.
kingdom-of-bundu.o: Bundu was founded around 1690 by [[e:malik-sy|Malik Sy]], a [[e:toroodbe|Torodbe]] cleric from [[s:imamate-of-futa-toro|Futa Toro]], who obtained land from the ruler of the [[s:kingdom-of-gajaaga|Kingdom of Gajaaga]] and drew settlers to his community. He is remembered by the clerical title eliman; his descendants, the [[e:sisibe|Sisibe]], ruled after him and later took the title almamy. Its creation came a generation before the [[e:jihad|jihads]] of [[s:imamate-of-futa-jallon|Futa Jallon]] and [[e:futa-toro|Futa Toro]].
kingdom-of-bundu.r: Bundu was governed by almamys of the [[e:sisibe|Sisibe]] lineage, whose succession was often contested between rival branches. Its towns, [[e:boulebane|Boulebane]] and Koussan among them, were centres of Islamic learning. Lying near the [[e:bambuk|Bambuk]] goldfields and on the routes from the upper [[e:senegal|Senegal]] to the [[e:the-gambia|Gambia]], it profited from caravans of gold, slaves, cloth and salt, and it warred repeatedly with [[s:kingdom-of-kaarta|Kaarta]], [[s:kingdom-of-khasso|Khasso]] and [[s:kingdom-of-gajaaga|Gajaaga]].
kingdom-of-bundu.e: In the 1850s Bundu was caught between [[e:el-hadj-umar-tall|Umar Tall]] and the French. Almamy [[e:bokar-saada|Bokar Saada]] sided with [[e:france|France]], and Bundu became a French [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] in the 1880s before being absorbed into [[s:french-senegal|French Senegal]], its almamys reduced to local chiefs by about 1905.

kingdom-of-great-britain.t: The kingdom created by the union of England and Scotland in 1707, which became Europe's leading maritime and commercial power in the 18th century.
kingdom-of-great-britain.o: The [[e:acts-of-union-1707|Acts of Union]] of 1707, passed by the [[s:kingdom-of-england|Kingdom of England]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-scotland|Kingdom of Scotland]], merged them into one kingdom with a single Parliament at [[e:palace-of-westminster|Westminster]], while [[e:scotland|Scotland]] kept its own law, church and education. The two countries had shared a monarch since 1603.
kingdom-of-great-britain.r: Great Britain developed cabinet government under [[e:robert-walpole|Robert Walpole]] and the Hanoverian kings from 1714. It defeated Jacobite risings in 1715 and 1745. Trade, the [[e:bank-of-england|Bank of England]] and naval power built an empire in [[e:north-america|North America]], the [[e:caribbean|Caribbean]] and [[e:india|India]], and the [[e:seven-years-war|Seven Years' War]] brought [[s:province-of-canada|Canada]]. The American colonies were lost in 1783, while the [[e:industrial-revolution|Industrial Revolution]] began.
kingdom-of-great-britain.e: The Acts of Union of 1800 joined Great Britain with the [[s:kingdom-of-ireland|Kingdom of Ireland]] to form the [[s:united-kingdom-of-great-britain-and-ireland|United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland]] on 1 January 1801.
kingdom-of-great-britain.re: Christianity; Church of England, Church of Scotland

kingdom-of-saloum.t: Serer and Wolof kingdom of the Saloum delta in Senegal, rich from salt and trade, ruled by the Guelowar dynasty from Kahone.
kingdom-of-saloum.o: Saloum was founded around 1494 by [[e:mbegan-ndour|Mbegan Ndour]], a [[e:serer|Serer]] warrior linked through his mother to the [[e:guelowar|Guelowar]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-sine|Kingdom of Sine]], who according to tradition killed Eli [[e:banabhatta|Bana]], the Muslim cleric then ruling the region. The capital was set at [[e:kahone|Kahone]], near present-day [[e:kaolack|Kaolack]], and the kingdom broke free of the [[s:jolof-empire|Jolof Empire]] in the following decades.
kingdom-of-saloum.r: The Buur Saloum ruled with a council of great titled chiefs and the Lingeer, a royal woman of high rank. Saloum controlled salt pans in the delta and trade routes to the [[e:the-gambia|Gambia]] river, and became the most extensive Serer-[[e:wolof|Wolof]] state. In the 1860s the jihadist [[e:maba-diakhou-ba|Maba Diakhou Ba]] conquered much of it, spreading [[e:islam|Islam]].
kingdom-of-saloum.e: [[e:france|France]] made Saloum a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] and absorbed it into the colony of [[s:french-senegal|French Senegal]] in 1891. Its kings served as colonial chiefs until the monarchy lapsed in the 20th century. [[e:kaolack|Kaolack]] became a centre of the groundnut trade.

kingdom-of-meirionnydd.t: Early Welsh kingdom between the Mawddach and the Dyfi, named after a grandson of Cunedda, which gave its name to the later county of Merioneth.
kingdom-of-meirionnydd.o: According to Welsh genealogical tradition, Meirionnydd took its name from Meirion, a grandson of [[e:cunedda|Cunedda]], who was granted the land between the rivers [[e:afon-mawddach|Mawddach]] and [[e:river-dyfi|Dyfi]] in the 5th century. Like other Cunedda stories, this is a later legend, but a separate royal line for Meirionnydd is recorded in medieval genealogies.
kingdom-of-meirionnydd.r: Little is recorded of its government. The kingdom covered a mountainous coastal region including [[e:cadair-idris|Cadair Idris]], with farming on the valley floors and the coast, and its people were linked by sea with the rest of [[e:cardigan-bay|Cardigan Bay]]. Its kings appear to have been subordinate to the more powerful rulers of the [[s:kingdom-of-gwynedd|Kingdom of Gwynedd]] for much of their history.
kingdom-of-meirionnydd.e: Meirionnydd was absorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-gwynedd|Kingdom of Gwynedd]], probably by the 10th century, becoming one of its cantrefi. After the English conquest of 1283 it formed the core of the county of [[e:merionethshire|Merioneth]], and the name survives in the region of Meirionnydd today.

kingdom-of-poland-1385-1569.t: Jagiellonian Poland, which with Lithuania defeated the Teutonic Knights, built a powerful noble democracy and enjoyed a Renaissance golden age.
kingdom-of-poland-1385-1569.o: In 1385 the [[e:union-of-krewo|Union of Krewo]] arranged the marriage of [[e:jadwiga-of-poland|Queen Jadwiga]] to [[e:w-adys-aw-ii-jagie-o|Jogaila]], grand duke of [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]], who was baptised and crowned in 1386 as Wladyslaw II Jagiello. His dynasty linked the Polish Crown to the [[e:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Grand Duchy of Lithuania]] and for a time also ruled [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]] and [[e:hungary|Hungary]].
kingdom-of-poland-1385-1569.r: Together, [[e:poland|Poland]] and [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] crushed the [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Knights]] at [[e:battle-of-grunwald|Grunwald]] in 1410, and the [[e:second-peace-of-thorn|Second Peace of Thorn]] in 1466 brought [[s:royal-prussia|Royal Prussia]] and the port of Gdansk under the Crown. The nobility won growing privileges, and the 1505 statute [[e:nihil-novi|Nihil novi]] required the consent of the [[e:sejm|Sejm]] for new laws. [[e:krakow|Krakow]] became a [[e:renaissance|Renaissance]] centre, home to [[e:nicolaus-copernicus|Copernicus]] and to Italian builders at [[e:wawel-hill|Wawel]] castle.
kingdom-of-poland-1385-1569.e: [[e:sigismund-ii-augustus|Sigismund II Augustus]], last of the male [[e:jagiellonian-dynasty|Jagiellons]], had no heir. To preserve the union, the [[e:union-of-lublin|Union of Lublin]] in 1569 merged the kingdom with [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] into the [[s:polish-lithuanian-commonwealth|Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth]], with a common elected king and [[e:sejm|Sejm]].

kingdom-of-buellt.t: Small Welsh kingdom around Builth Wells, ruled by a dynasty claiming descent from Vortigern, and later the place where Llywelyn ap Gruffudd was killed.
kingdom-of-buellt.o: Buellt lay in the middle [[e:river-wye|Wye]] and [[e:river-irfon|Irfon]] valleys around modern Builth [[e:well|Wells]]. The [[e:historia-brittonum|Historia Brittonum]] of about 829 says [[e:ambrosius-aurelianus|Ambrosius]] granted Buellt and [[s:kingdom-of-gwrtheyrnion|Gwrtheyrnion]] to Pascent, son of [[e:vortigern|Vortigern]], and names [[e:fernmail|Fernmail]] as the ruler of both in the author's own day. Among its wonders it lists Carn Cabal, a cairn said to bear the footprint of Arthur's hound.
kingdom-of-buellt.r: Little is recorded of its government. It was a small upland kingdom of river valleys and hill grazing, generally ruled together with the [[s:kingdom-of-gwrtheyrnion|Kingdom of Gwrtheyrnion]] and lying between the larger realms of the [[s:kingdom-of-powys|Kingdom of Powys]], the [[s:kingdom-of-brycheiniog|Kingdom of Brycheiniog]] and the south-western kingdoms.
kingdom-of-buellt.e: Buellt was absorbed by larger Welsh kingdoms in the 10th century and later became a cantref contested between Welsh princes and Norman lords, with a castle at Builth. In 1282 [[e:llywelyn-ap-gruffudd|Llywelyn ap Gruffudd]], last native [[e:prince-of-wales|Prince of Wales]], was killed near [[e:cilmeri|Cilmeri]] in Buellt.

kingdom-of-buleleng.t: North Balinese kingdom founded by the warrior Panji Sakti, whose defeat in 1849 began the Dutch conquest of Bali.
kingdom-of-buleleng.o: Buleleng was founded around 1660 by [[e:gusti-panji-sakti|Gusti Panji Sakti]], a noble of the [[s:kingdom-of-gelgel|Gelgel]] court who built a power base on the north coast of [[e:bali|Bali]]. He made [[e:singaraja|Singaraja]] his capital and extended his rule across the strait to [[s:blambangan-kingdom|Blambangan]] in eastern [[e:java|Java]] in 1697, making Buleleng briefly the leading Balinese state.
kingdom-of-buleleng.r: The kingdom looked outward through its north-coast harbours, trading [[e:rice|rice]], [[e:cattle|cattle]] and slaves with [[e:bugis|Bugis]], Chinese and European merchants. It was ruled by a [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] raja and his noble kin, with [[e:brahmins|Brahmana]] priests at court. In the 18th century it passed for a time under the control of the [[s:kingdom-of-karangasem|Kingdom of Karangasem]].
kingdom-of-buleleng.e: Disputes over the plunder of shipwrecks led the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] to attack in 1846 and 1848, when the patih [[e:gusti-ketut-jelantik|Gusti Ketut Jelantik]] defeated them at [[e:battle-of-jagaraga|Jagaraga]]. A third expedition in 1849 conquered Buleleng, and [[e:singaraja|Singaraja]] became the Dutch administrative centre for [[e:bali|Bali]] and [[e:lombok|Lombok]].

kingdom-of-mukish.t: Mukish, the kingdom of Alalakh in the Amuq plain, best known for King Idrimi, whose statue tells the story of an exiled prince who won back a throne.
kingdom-of-mukish.o: [[e:alalakh|Alalakh]], at Tell Atchana near [[e:antioch|Antakya]], was a town of the fertile [[e:amuq-valley|Amuq plain]] by the early 2nd millennium BCE. In the 18th century BCE [[e:abba-el-i|Abba-El]] of [[s:yamhad|Yamhad]] granted it to his brother [[e:yarim-lim-of-alalakh|Yarim-Lim]], making it a dependent kingdom of [[e:aleppo|Aleppo]]. [[e:leonard-woolley|Leonard Woolley's]] excavations from 1937 recovered palaces and archives from this period.
kingdom-of-mukish.r: [[e:alalakh|Alalakh's]] palace archives record a society of nobles who owned [[e:chariot|chariots]], free farmers and dependent labourers, written in Akkadian with many Hurrian names. After a Hittite destruction c. 1600 BCE, [[e:idrimi|Idrimi]], a refugee prince from [[e:aleppo|Aleppo]], took the city and ruled Mukish as a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the [[s:mitanni-empire|Mitanni Empire]], as his inscribed statue relates.
kingdom-of-mukish.e: [[e:suppiluliuma-i|Suppiluliuma I]] of the [[s:hittite-empire|Hittite Empire]] conquered Mukish in the 14th century BCE and gave some of its land to [[s:kingdom-of-ugarit|Ugarit]]. [[e:alalakh|Alalakh]] was abandoned around 1200 BCE, during the collapse of the [[e:late-bronze-age|Late Bronze Age]], and its region later formed part of [[s:patina|Patina]].

kingdom-of-kianja.t: A Haya kingdom near Bukoba, split from Kyamutwara around 1800, whose king Kahigi became a leading ally of German rule.
kingdom-of-kianja.o: Kianja was formed around 1800 when succession disputes divided the [[s:kingdom-of-kyamutwara|Kingdom of Kyamutwara]] in the [[e:kagera-region|Kagera region]] west of [[e:lake-victoria|Lake Victoria]]. A branch of the [[e:hinda-dynasty|Hinda dynasty]] took control of the new kingdom, which became one of the largest of the [[e:haya-people|Haya]] states.
kingdom-of-kianja.r: The mukama ruled over a dense population of banana and [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]] farmers through chiefs drawn from royal and noble lineages. In the 1890s King Kahigi II welcomed the Germans and used their support to extend his power over neighbouring [[e:haya-people|Haya]] states, a policy that made Kianja the most favoured native authority in the region.
kingdom-of-kianja.e: Kianja remained a native authority under [[s:german-east-africa|German East Africa]] and [[e:tanganyika-territory|British Tanganyika Territory]]. It ceased to exist in 1963, when independent [[s:tanganyika|Tanganyika]] abolished the chieftaincies.

kingdom-of-buna.t: Kingdom of north-eastern Ivory Coast, founded by a Dagomba-linked dynasty over the Kulango and known for its Muslim scholarly community.
kingdom-of-buna.o: Buna traditions say the kingdom was founded around 1600 by Bunkani, a prince linked to the [[s:kingdom-of-dagbon|Kingdom of Dagbon]], who imposed his rule over the [[e:kulango|Kulango]] farmers of the upper [[e:comoe-river|Comoe]] and [[e:black-volta|Black Volta]] region. The town of Bouna became its capital.
kingdom-of-buna.r: The king ruled over [[e:kulango|Kulango]] villages whose earth-priests kept their religious role. Muslim [[e:wangara|Dyula]] traders and scholars settled in Bouna, which became a centre of Islamic learning on the routes between the [[e:niger-bend|Niger bend]] and the [[e:akan|Akan]] goldfields. Buna was at times a tributary of the [[s:ashanti-empire|Ashanti Empire]].
kingdom-of-buna.e: In 1896 the forces of [[e:samori-ture|Samori Ture]] sacked Bouna. The French took control shortly afterwards, and Buna became part of [[s:french-ivory-coast|French Ivory Coast]]. A king of Bouna remains a traditional ruler.

kingdom-of-serbia-medieval.t: Nemanjić Serbia as a kingdom, which gained its own church, grew rich on silver mines and expanded south to become the Balkans' leading power.
kingdom-of-serbia-medieval.o: Stefan, son of [[e:stefan-nemanja|Stefan Nemanja]] and ruler of the [[s:grand-principality-of-serbia|Grand Principality of Serbia]], was crowned king in 1217 with a crown sent by [[e:pope-honorius-iii|Pope Honorius III]], earning the name [[e:stefan-the-first-crowned|Stefan the First-Crowned]]. In 1219 his brother [[e:sava|Sava]] obtained an autocephalous Serbian archbishopric from the Patriarch at [[e:nicaea|Nicaea]].
kingdom-of-serbia-medieval.r: The king ruled through royal courts that moved between residences, with nobles holding land in return for service. [[e:stefan-uros-i|Uroš I]] invited [[e:saxons|Saxon]] miners, opening the [[e:silver|silver]] mine at [[e:brskovo|Brskovo]]; later mines such as [[e:novo-brdo|Novo Brdo]] made [[s:serbia|Serbia]] rich and supplied Ragusa's trade. Royal foundations such as [[e:mileseva-monastery|Mileševa]], [[e:sopocani-monastery|Sopoćani]] and [[e:gracanica-monastery|Gračanica]] have celebrated frescoes. [[e:stefan-milutin|Milutin]] (1282–1321) took northern [[e:macedonia-region|Macedonia]] from [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]], and [[e:stefan-decanski|Stefan Dečanski]] crushed [[s:bulgaria|Bulgaria]] at [[e:battle-of-velbazhd|Velbazhd]] in 1330.
kingdom-of-serbia-medieval.e: [[e:stefan-dusan|Stefan Dušan]], who took the throne in 1331, conquered much of Byzantine [[e:macedonia-region|Macedonia]], [[s:albania|Albania]] and [[e:epirus|Epirus]] and in 1346 was crowned emperor at [[e:skopje|Skopje]], turning the kingdom into the [[s:serbian-empire|Serbian Empire]].

kolathunadu.t: The kingdom of the Kolathiri rajas of northern Kerala, heirs of the ancient Mushika line and rivals of the Zamorins of Calicut.
kolathunadu.o: Kolathunadu emerged as an independent chiefdom in northern [[e:malabar-coast|Malabar]] after the decline of the [[e:chera-dynasty|Chera]] kingdom of [[e:mahodayapuram|Mahodayapuram]] in the early 12th century. Its Kolathiri rulers claimed descent from the earlier [[e:mushika-dynasty|Mushika dynasty]] of [[e:ezhimala|Ezhimala]] and controlled the coast around [[e:kannur|Cannanore]] and the [[e:pepper|pepper]]-growing hinterland.
kolathunadu.r: Power was shared within a large matrilineal royal family whose branches held separate seats, and [[e:nair|Nair]] warriors formed the backbone of society. The kingdom traded [[e:pepper|pepper]] and [[e:spice-trade|spices]] with Arab merchants, and later with the Portuguese, who built [[e:st-angelo-fort|Fort St Angelo]] at [[e:kannur|Cannanore]] in 1505. The Ali Rajas of the [[s:arakkal-kingdom|Arakkal kingdom]] began as Muslim ministers and admirals of the Kolathiris.
kolathunadu.e: Internal division split the realm into several branch seats, with Chirakkal the senior one. [[e:hyder-ali|Hyder Ali]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-mysore-1399-1799|Kingdom of Mysore]] overran [[e:malabar-coast|Malabar]] in 1766, and in 1792 the region passed to the [[e:east-india-company|British East India Company]]. The Chirakkal family survived as pensioned landholders.

kingdom-of-bithynia.t: Bithynia, a Hellenistic kingdom of north-western Anatolia that invited the Galatians in, sheltered Hannibal and was bequeathed to Rome.
kingdom-of-bithynia.o: The Bithynians, a people of Thracian origin, lived south of the [[s:bosporan-kingdom|Bosporus]] and the [[e:sea-of-marmara|Sea of Marmara]]. Their dynast [[e:zipoetes-i-of-bithynia|Zipoetes I]] resisted [[e:lysimachus|Lysimachus]] and the [[s:seleucid-empire|Seleucid Empire]], and in 297 BCE he took the title king, founding a dynasty that lasted over two centuries.
kingdom-of-bithynia.r: [[e:nicomedes-i-of-bithynia|Nicomedes I]] founded [[e:nicomedia|Nicomedia]] as his capital in 264 BCE and invited Celtic warriors into Asia, who settled in [[s:galatia|Galatia]]. [[e:prusias-i-of-bithynia|Prusias I]] expanded the kingdom, founded [[e:bursa|Prusa]] and sheltered [[e:hannibal|Hannibal]], who took poison at [[e:libyssa|Libyssa]] in 183 BCE rather than be handed to [[e:rome|Rome]]. The kings promoted Greek city life.
kingdom-of-bithynia.e: [[e:nicomedes-iv|Nicomedes IV]], restored to his throne by [[e:rome|Rome]], left [[e:bithynia|Bithynia]] to the [[s:roman-republic|Roman Republic]] in his will in 74 BCE. The bequest provoked the [[e:third-mithridatic-war|Third Mithridatic War]] with the [[s:kingdom-of-pontus|Kingdom of Pontus]], and Bithynia became a Roman province.

kingdom-of-jibei.t: A fragment of the old state of Qi given to Tian An in 206 BCE, destroyed within months when Tian Rong reunited Qi by force.
kingdom-of-jibei.o: [[e:tian-an|Tian An]], a grandson of King Jian, the last king of the [[s:state-of-qi|State of Qi]], captured several towns north of the Ji River during the war against the [[s:qin-dynasty|Qin dynasty]] and followed [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]] to [[e:battle-of-julu|Julu]]. In 206 BCE Xiang Yu made him King of Jibei, with his capital at Boyang in central [[e:shandong|Shandong]].
kingdom-of-jibei.r: Jibei was one of three kingdoms into which [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]] split Qi, alongside the [[s:kingdom-of-jiaodong|Kingdom of Jiaodong]] and Qi (206 BC), to weaken the powerful [[e:tian|Tian]] clan. It lasted too short a time for any government to take shape.
kingdom-of-jibei.e: [[e:tian-rong|Tian Rong]], the Qi strongman excluded from [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu's]] settlement, attacked the three kingdoms in 206 BCE, killed [[e:tian-an|Tian An]] and reunited Qi under himself, provoking Xiang Yu's invasion of Qi.

kingdom-of-sonbai.t: Atoni kingdom of West Timor whose rulers held a ritual supremacy over the interior and were courted in turn by the Portuguese and the Dutch.
kingdom-of-sonbai.o: Sonbai grew out of the [[e:atoni|Atoni]] (Meto) chiefdoms of the [[e:west-timor|West Timor]] highlands, where its lords were recognised as senior ritual rulers over neighbouring domains such as Mollo and [[e:amanuban|Amanuban]]. By the 17th century it was drawn into the rivalry between the Portuguese-allied [[e:topasses|Topasses]] of [[e:lifau|Lifau]] and the [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] at [[e:kupang|Kupang]], and in the 1650s it split in two.
kingdom-of-sonbai.r: A branch known as Small Sonbai moved near [[e:kupang|Kupang]] and became a Company ally, while Great Sonbai remained in the mountains. Power rested on [[e:sacred-kingship|sacred kingship]], alliances of lineages and tribute in kind, and the realm supplied sandalwood and beeswax to foreign traders. Most people followed the indigenous [[e:atoni|Atoni]] religion centred on ancestors and the earth.
kingdom-of-sonbai.e: Small Sonbai was absorbed into [[e:dutch|Dutch]] administration around [[e:kupang|Kupang]], and Great Sonbai kept its independence in the interior until the Dutch campaign of 1906 captured its last ruler, [[e:sobe-sonbai-iii|Sobe Sonbai III]], who died in exile. The name survives as a symbol of Timorese resistance.

kingdom-of-sai.t: One of the three kingdoms carved from the Qin heartland in 206 BCE, held by the former Qin officer Sima Xin, which fell to Liu Bang within months.
kingdom-of-sai.o: [[e:sima-xin|Sima Xin]] had been chief clerk under the [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] general [[e:zhang-han|Zhang Han]] and surrendered with him to [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]] in 207 BCE. Xiang Yu divided the [[e:guanzhong|Guanzhong]] region among three former Qin commanders to block [[e:liu-bang|Liu Bang]], giving Sima Xin the kingdom of Sai east of [[e:xianyang|Xianyang]], with its capital at Yueyang.
kingdom-of-sai.r: Sai's population resented its new king, since [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]] had massacred some 200,000 surrendered [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] soldiers at Xin'an while sparing their commanders. The kingdom had no time to develop any administration of its own.
kingdom-of-sai.e: When [[e:liu-bang|Liu Bang]] broke out of [[e:hanzhong|Hanzhong]] in 206 BCE, [[e:sima-xin|Sima Xin]] surrendered and his land became Han territory. He later fled back to [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]] and killed himself after a Chu defeat at [[e:battle-of-chenggao|Chenggao]] in 203 BCE.

kantora.t: Mandinka kingdom of the upper Gambia river, whose riverside market was the furthest point reached by Portuguese ships in the 15th century.
kantora.o: Kantora was one of the [[e:mandinka|Mandinka]] states established along the [[e:the-gambia|Gambia]] as the [[s:mali-empire|Mali Empire]] extended its influence west. It occupied the south bank of the upper river around present-day Fatoto and [[e:basse-santa-su|Basse]]. The Portuguese explorer [[e:diogo-gomes|Diogo Gomes]] reached its market, which he called Cantor, around 1456.
kantora.r: Kantora's rulers controlled the highest navigable point on the river, where caravans from the upper [[e:niger-river|Niger]] and [[e:bambuk|Bambuk]] brought gold, [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and slaves to trade for salt, cloth and European goods. It later fell within the orbit of the [[s:kaabu-empire|Kaabu Empire]], and Muslim traders settled in its towns.
kantora.e: In the 1860s and 1870s Kantora was conquered by the [[e:fula|Fula]] leader [[e:alfa-molo-balde|Alfa Molo]] and his son [[e:musa-molo|Musa Molo]], becoming part of [[s:fuladu|Fuladu]]. The area was divided between [[s:gambia-colony-and-protectorate|British Gambia]] and [[s:french-senegal|French Senegal]] by the boundary of 1889.

kingdom-of-yong.t: The kingdom of Zhang Han, the Qin general turned king, who guarded the western Wei valley against Liu Bang until his capital was flooded in 205 BCE.
kingdom-of-yong.o: [[e:zhang-han|Zhang Han]] was the [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] general who crushed [[e:chen-sheng|Chen Sheng's]] rising, then surrendered to [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]] after the defeat of Qin forces at [[e:battle-of-julu|Julu]]. In 206 BCE Xiang Yu made him King of Yong, ruling the western [[e:guanzhong|Guanzhong]] region from Feiqiu, west of [[e:xianyang|Xianyang]], as the main barrier against [[e:liu-bang|Liu Bang]] in [[e:hanzhong|Hanzhong]].
kingdom-of-yong.r: Yong was one of the [[e:three-qins|Three Qins]], with the [[s:kingdom-of-sai|Kingdom of Sai]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-di-206-bc|Kingdom of Di]] (206 BC). Like them, it lacked local loyalty because [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]] had slaughtered the [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] soldiers [[e:zhang-han|Zhang Han]] had led.
kingdom-of-yong.e: Later in 206 BCE [[e:liu-bang|Liu Bang's]] general [[e:han-xin|Han Xin]] crossed the mountains by the [[e:chencang|Chencang]] route and defeated [[e:zhang-han|Zhang Han]]. Besieged in Feiqiu, Zhang held out until 205 BCE, when the Han army flooded the city and he killed himself.

khanate-of-ardabil.t: One of the semi-independent khanates of Azerbaijan after Nader Shah's death, ruled by Shahsevan chiefs from the Safavid holy city of Ardabil.
khanate-of-ardabil.o: When [[e:assassination-of-nader-shah|Nader Shah was assassinated]] in 1747, the [[s:afsharid-empire|Afsharid Empire]] broke apart and local khans took power across the [[e:caucasus|Caucasus]] and [[s:azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]]. In [[e:ardabil|Ardabil]], home of the shrine of Sheikh Safi al-Din, ancestor of the [[e:safavid-empire|Safavids]], chiefs of the Shahsevan tribal confederation established a khanate.
khanate-of-ardabil.r: The khans relied on Shahsevan nomadic cavalry from the Moghan steppe and the Sabalan mountains. [[e:nazar-ali-khan-shahsevan|Nazar Ali Khan Shahsevan]] was the leading figure of the later 18th century. The khanate was drawn into the conflicts of its neighbours, notably the [[e:quba|Quba]] khanate, the [[s:talysh-khanate|Talysh Khanate]] and the [[s:karabakh-khanate|Karabakh Khanate]], and was briefly occupied by [[e:fatali-khan-of-quba|Fath Ali Khan of Quba]].
khanate-of-ardabil.e: [[e:agha-mohammad-khan-qajar|Agha Mohammad Khan]]'s [[s:qajar-iran|Qajar Iran]] imposed control over [[s:azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]] in the 1790s, and by 1808 the khanate had been fully absorbed into the [[e:qajar-dynasty|Qajar]] state as a governorate.

kutai-kartanegara-sultanate.t: A Malay-Dayak sultanate on the Mahakam River in East Kalimantan, which absorbed ancient Kutai Martadipura and ruled until 1960.
kutai-kartanegara-sultanate.o: According to the Salasilah [[s:kingdom-of-kutai|Kutai]] chronicle, the kingdom was founded around 1300 at Kutai Lama near the mouth of the [[e:mahakam-river|Mahakam River]] by [[e:aji-batara-agung-dewa-sakti|Aji Batara Agung Dewa Sakti]]. It was at first a [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] state that looked to [[e:majapahit-empire|Majapahit]], while upriver lay the old Kingdom of Kutai, known as Martadipura.
kutai-kartanegara-sultanate.r: [[e:islam|Islam]] was adopted around 1575. In 1635 [[e:aji-pangeran-sinum-panji-mendapa|Aji Pangeran Sinum Panji Mendapa]] conquered Martadipura and joined the two names. The sultans traded rattan, gold and birds' nests from the interior with [[e:bugis|Bugis]] merchants, and in 1782 moved their capital upriver to [[e:tenggarong|Tenggarong]]. In the colonial era [[e:coal|coal]] and oil brought new wealth.
kutai-kartanegara-sultanate.e: After a clash with British adventurer [[e:james-erskine-murray|James Erskine Murray]], the sultan accepted [[e:dutch|Dutch]] overlordship in 1844. The sultanate became part of [[s:indonesia|Indonesia]] and was abolished in 1960 under [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Aji Muhammad Parikesit. It was revived as a cultural institution in 2001, and its palace is now a museum.

khorezm-peoples-soviet-republic.t: The short-lived Soviet-backed republic that replaced the Khanate of Khiva in 1920 before being divided among the new national republics.
khorezm-peoples-soviet-republic.o: In early 1920 the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] and the reformist [[e:young-khivans|Young Khivans]] overthrew the [[s:khanate-of-khiva|Khanate of Khiva]], then dominated by the [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] warlord [[e:junaid-khan|Junaid Khan]]. In April 1920 the Khorezm People's Soviet Republic was proclaimed, with [[e:khiva|Khiva]] as capital.
khorezm-peoples-soviet-republic.r: Officially independent and allied with [[s:russian-sfsr|Soviet Russia]], it was governed by [[e:young-khivans|Young Khivans]] and later communists, under strong influence from [[e:moscow|Moscow]]. It nationalised the khan's estates, opened schools and fought [[e:junaid-khan|Junaid Khan's]] [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] forces. Purges in 1921 and 1922 removed many of the original leaders, and it became the Khorezm Soviet Socialist Republic in 1923.
khorezm-peoples-soviet-republic.e: In the national delimitation of 1924 the republic was divided among the [[s:uzbek-ssr|Uzbek SSR]], the [[s:turkmen-ssr|Turkmen SSR]] and the new [[e:karakalpak-autonomous-oblast|Karakalpak Autonomous Oblast]], later [[s:karakalpakstan|Karakalpakstan]]. [[e:khiva|Khiva's]] walled inner town, [[e:itchan-kala|Itchan Kala]], survived and is now a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]].

kingdom-of-jimma.t: The richest of the Oromo kingdoms of the Gibe region, famous for its coffee and markets, which kept autonomy within Ethiopia until 1932.
kingdom-of-jimma.o: Jimma, also called Jimma Abba Jifar, emerged around 1790 when [[e:oromo|Oromo]] groups in the [[e:gibe-river|Gibe]] valley, who had settled there during the migrations of earlier centuries, formed a monarchy under [[e:abba-magal|Abba Magal]]. It grew by absorbing neighbours, and under Abba Jifar I (r. 1830 to 1855) the dynasty adopted [[e:islam|Islam]].
kingdom-of-jimma.r: The king ruled through appointed governors and officials, a departure from the egalitarian [[e:oromo|Oromo]] gadaa system. Jimma's markets, especially at Hirmata near the capital Jiren, traded [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]], [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]], civet, gold and slaves. [[e:abba-jifar-ii|Abba Jifar II]] (r. 1878 to 1932) submitted to [[e:menelik-ii|Menelik II]] in 1882 and paid tribute in return for internal autonomy.
kingdom-of-jimma.e: After [[e:abba-jifar-ii|Abba Jifar II's]] death in 1932 [[e:haile-selassie|Haile Selassie]] ended Jimma's autonomy and made it a province of the [[s:ethiopian-empire|Ethiopian Empire]]. Abba Jifar's palace at Jiren is preserved, and Jimma is now one of [[e:ethiopia|Ethiopia's]] main [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]] towns.

kingdom-of-ankole.t: A cattle kingdom of south-western Uganda, famous for its long-horned Ankole cattle, which grew by absorbing its neighbours in the colonial era.
kingdom-of-ankole.o: Traditions trace Nkore, later Ankole, to the [[e:hinda-dynasty|Hinda dynasty]], founded by [[e:ruhinda|Ruhinda]], who is said to have inherited part of the [[s:empire-of-kitara|Empire of Kitara]] around the 15th century. For centuries it was a small state east of [[e:lake-edward|Lake Edward]], often raided by [[s:kingdom-of-bunyoro|Bunyoro]] and [[s:kingdom-of-rwanda|Rwanda]], before it began to expand under rulers such as [[e:ntare-iv-of-ankole|Ntare IV]].
kingdom-of-ankole.r: The mugabe (king) presided over a society divided between the [[e:cattle|cattle]]-owning [[e:bahima|Bahima]] and the farming [[e:bairu|Bairu]], with power and prestige tied to herds of long-horned cattle. The royal drum [[e:bagyendanwa|Bagyendanwa]] embodied the kingship. Rule was loose, relying on chiefs and the king's cattle camps. Under [[e:ntare-v|Ntare V]] in the late 19th century Ankole extended its influence over neighbouring states.
kingdom-of-ankole.e: The [[e:ankole-agreement|Ankole Agreement]] of 1901 made it a kingdom of the [[s:uganda-protectorate|Uganda Protectorate]] and added the [[s:kingdom-of-mpororo|Kingdom of Mpororo]], the [[s:kingdom-of-igara|Kingdom of Igara]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-buhweju|Kingdom of Buhweju]] to its territory. The monarchy was abolished in 1967 and, unlike its neighbours, was not restored in the 1990s.

kassite-babylonia.t: The longest-ruling dynasty in Babylonian history: Kassite kings from the Zagros who reunited Babylonia and made it a great power of the Amarna age.
kassite-babylonia.o: The [[e:kassites|Kassites]], a people from the [[e:zagros-mountains|Zagros]] with their own language and gods, had settled in [[e:mesopotamia|Mesopotamia]] in the 18th century BCE. After the Hittite king [[e:mursili-i|Mursili I]] sacked [[e:babylon|Babylon]] in 1595 BCE, Kassite rulers took over the city, perhaps first under [[e:agum-ii|Agum II]], and around 1460 BCE [[e:ulamburiash|Ulamburiash]] conquered the [[s:sealand-dynasty|Sealand dynasty]], uniting all [[e:babylonia|Babylonia]], called Karduniash.
kassite-babylonia.r: The Kassite kings adopted Babylonian language, religion and court culture, promoting [[e:marduk|Marduk]] of [[e:babylon|Babylon]]. [[e:kurigalzu-i|Kurigalzu I]] built a new royal city, [[e:dur-kurigalzu|Dur-Kurigalzu]], with a [[e:ziggurat|ziggurat]]. In the 14th century kings such as [[e:kadashman-enlil-i|Kadashman-Enlil I]] and [[e:burna-buriash-ii|Burna-Buriash II]] exchanged letters, gold and princesses with [[e:egypt|Egypt]] in the [[e:akhetaten|Amarna]] correspondence. Land grants were recorded on carved boundary stones (kudurrus), horses and [[e:chariot|chariots]] were prized, and scribes standardised literary works such as the [[e:epic-of-gilgamesh|Epic of Gilgamesh]].
kassite-babylonia.e: [[e:tukulti-ninurta-i|Tukulti-Ninurta I]] of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]] sacked [[e:babylon|Babylon]] around 1225 BCE. In 1158 BCE the Elamite [[e:shutruk-nahhunte|Shutruk-Nahhunte]] invaded, and around 1155 BCE the last Kassite king, [[e:enlil-nadin-ahi|Enlil-nadin-ahi]], was carried off, after which the [[s:second-dynasty-of-isin|Second Dynasty of Isin]] took power.

kingdom-of-powys.t: Kingdom of mid and north-east Wales and the Marches that long faced Mercia across Offa's Dyke, until it split into two lordships after 1160.
kingdom-of-powys.o: Powys arose in the territory of the [[s:cornovii|Cornovii]] after Roman rule ended around 410, its name perhaps from the [[e:latin|Latin]] pagenses, country people. Its early kings claimed descent from Cadell Ddyrnllug and, according to the [[e:pillar-of-eliseg|Pillar of Eliseg]], from [[e:vortigern|Vortigern]] and [[e:magnus-maximus|Magnus Maximus]]. Its first centre may have been at [[e:viroconium-cornoviorum|Wroxeter]] or [[s:kingdom-of-pengwern|Pengwern]] before the English advance pushed it westward.
kingdom-of-powys.r: Powys bordered the Mercians and suffered heavily from their expansion; [[e:selyf-ap-cynan|Selyf ap Cynan]] fell at the [[e:battle-of-chester|battle of Chester]] around 615, and [[e:offa-of-mercia|Offa]] built his dyke along the frontier in the 8th century. [[e:cyngen-ap-cadell|Cyngen ap Cadell]] raised the [[e:pillar-of-eliseg|Pillar of Eliseg]] near [[e:llangollen|Llangollen]] to honour an ancestor who won back land from the English. Later kings ruled from [[e:mathrafal|Mathrafal]], and its society rested on [[e:cattle|cattle]] and kin-based law.
kingdom-of-powys.e: Cyngen died on pilgrimage to [[e:rome|Rome]] in 854, and Powys passed to [[e:rhodri-the-great|Rhodri the Great]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-gwynedd|Kingdom of Gwynedd]]. A native dynasty returned under [[e:bleddyn-ap-cynfyn|Bleddyn ap Cynfyn]] in the 1060s, but after [[e:madog-ap-maredudd|Madog ap Maredudd]] died in 1160 the kingdom split into [[s:powys-fadog|Powys Fadog]] and [[s:powys-wenwynwyn|Powys Wenwynwyn]].

kingdom-of-commagene.t: Commagene, a small kingdom on the upper Euphrates whose king Antiochus I built the colossal god-statues on the summit of Nemrut Dağı.
kingdom-of-commagene.o: Commagene, the former [[s:kummuh|Kummuh]], lay between the [[e:taurus-mountains|Taurus]] mountains and the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]]. Its governor [[e:ptolemaeus-of-commagene|Ptolemaeus]] broke away from the [[s:seleucid-empire|Seleucid Empire]] c. 163 BCE. His successor [[e:mithridates-i-callinicus|Mithridates I Callinicus]] married a [[e:seleucid-empire|Seleucid]] princess, uniting Persian and Macedonian royal lines.
kingdom-of-commagene.r: [[e:antiochus-i-theos-of-commagene|Antiochus I Theos]] ruled from [[e:samosata|Samosata]] and devised a royal cult in which Greek and Persian gods were merged. On [[e:mount-nemrut|Nemrut Dağı]] he built a burial mound flanked by giant statues of himself with Zeus-Oromasdes, Apollo-[[e:mithra|Mithras]] and Heracles-Artagnes. Commagene grew rich from its fertile valleys and river crossings.
kingdom-of-commagene.e: [[e:rome|Rome]] annexed Commagene in 17 CE, restored it to [[e:antiochus-iv-epiphanes|Antiochus IV]] in 38 CE, and finally absorbed it into the province of [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] in 72 CE under Vespasian.
