kingdom-of-tungning.t: The Ming loyalist kingdom of Koxinga and his heirs on Taiwan, which drove out the Dutch and became the first Han Chinese state on the island.
kingdom-of-tungning.o: [[e:koxinga|Koxinga]] ([[s:zheng-wang-shichong|Zheng]] Chenggong), son of the merchant-admiral [[e:zheng-zhilong|Zheng Zhilong]], led Ming loyalist forces on the [[e:fujian|Fujian]] coast after 1646. After a failed attack on [[e:nanjing|Nanjing]] in 1659 he sought a new base, invaded [[s:dutch-formosa|Dutch Formosa]] in 1661 and took [[e:fort-zeelandia-taiwan|Fort Zeelandia]] in 1662, but died a few months later.
kingdom-of-tungning.r: His son [[e:zheng-jing|Zheng Jing]] and the minister [[e:chen-yonghua|Chen Yonghua]] built a Chinese-style administration at Tungning ([[e:tainan|Tainan]]), founded the first Confucian temple and schools on [[s:republic-of-china|Taiwan]] in 1666, settled soldiers on farmland and traded with [[e:japan|Japan]], South-east Asia and the [[e:east-india-company|English East India Company]]. [[s:zheng-wang-shichong|Zheng]] Jing joined the [[e:revolt-of-the-three-feudatories|Revolt of the Three Feudatories]] in 1674 and occupied coastal [[e:fujian|Fujian]] for a time.
kingdom-of-tungning.e: After [[e:zheng-jing|Zheng Jing's]] death in 1681, court factions placed his young son [[e:zheng-keshuang|Zheng Keshuang]] on the throne. In 1683 the Qing admiral [[e:shi-lang|Shi Lang]] destroyed the [[s:zheng-wang-shichong|Zheng]] fleet at [[e:penghu|Penghu]], and Zheng Keshuang surrendered. [[s:republic-of-china|Taiwan]] became a prefecture of [[e:fujian|Fujian]] under the [[s:qing-empire|Qing Empire]].

kingdom-of-the-swedes.t: Early kingdom of the Svear around Lake Mälaren and Uppsala, whose kings ruled the trading town of Birka and later united the Swedish lands.
kingdom-of-the-swedes.o: [[e:tacitus|Tacitus]] wrote of the [[e:svear|Suiones]] in the 1st century, and by the 6th century the Svear had a power centre at [[e:gamla-uppsala|Old Uppsala]], where great royal mounds were raised. Rich boat graves at [[e:vendel|Vendel]] and [[e:valsgarde|Valsgärde]] show a wealthy warrior elite. Later sagas trace the kings to the legendary [[e:ynglings|Yngling dynasty]].
kingdom-of-the-swedes.r: Kingship was tied to the pagan cult at [[e:uppsala|Uppsala]], described by [[e:adam-of-bremen|Adam of Bremen]], and to assemblies of free men at the thing. [[e:birka|Birka]], founded in the 8th century on [[e:lake-malaren|Lake Mälaren]], linked the kingdom to trade routes east to Rus' and the Byzantine and Abbasid worlds. [[e:rimbert|Rimbert's]] life of [[e:ansgar|Ansgar]] records King Björn receiving the Frankish missionary around 830 and King Olof receiving him again around 852.
kingdom-of-the-swedes.e: [[e:eric-the-victorious|Eric the Victorious]], who defeated a rival at [[e:battle-of-fyrisvellir|Fýrisvellir]] in the 980s, and his son [[e:olof-skotkonung|Olof Skötkonung]] extended [[e:svear|Svear]] rule over the [[e:geats|Geats]]. This union of the Svear and Götar is regarded as the start of the medieval [[s:kingdom-of-sweden|Kingdom of Sweden]], and the [[e:uppsala|Uppsala]] kingship gave [[e:sweden|Sweden]] its name.

kingdom-of-the-gepids.t: East Germanic kingdom in the Tisza plain and Transylvania that rose after Attila's empire collapsed and was destroyed by Lombards and Avars in 567.
kingdom-of-the-gepids.o: The [[e:gepids|Gepids]], a Gothic-related people, were subjects of [[e:attila|Attila's]] [[e:huns|Huns]]. In 454 their king [[e:ardaric|Ardaric]] led the revolt that crushed Attila's sons at the [[e:battle-of-nedao|River Nedao]], and the Gepids took over the lands east of the [[e:danube|Danube]] in the [[e:tisza|Tisza]] plain and [[s:principality-of-transylvania|Transylvania]].
kingdom-of-the-gepids.r: Gepid kings ruled a mixed population of Germanic, Sarmatian and local peoples, and adopted Arian [[e:christianity|Christianity]]. Rich princely graves such as those at [[e:apahida|Apahida]] show their wealth. They seized [[e:sirmium|Sirmium]] (Sremska Mitrovica) on the [[e:sava|Sava]], a key city, and competed with the [[e:ostrogoths|Ostrogoths]], [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] and the [[e:lombards|Lombards]] for the middle [[e:danube|Danube]]. Kings [[e:thurisind|Thurisind]] and [[e:cunimund|Cunimund]] fought the [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombards]] in the 550s and 560s.
kingdom-of-the-gepids.e: In 567 the [[e:lombards|Lombards]] under [[e:alboin|Alboin]], allied with the newly arrived [[e:avars|Avars]], destroyed the kingdom; [[e:cunimund|Cunimund]] was killed and Alboin made his skull into a drinking cup. The Gepid lands passed to the [[s:avar-khaganate|Avar Khaganate]].

kingdom-of-lithuania.t: The only crowned kingdom in Lithuanian history, created when Mindaugas accepted Catholic baptism and a royal crown from the Pope.
kingdom-of-lithuania.o: [[e:mindaugas|Mindaugas]] had united the Lithuanian lands by the 1240s but faced a coalition of rivals backed by the [[s:livonian-order|Livonian Order]]. To split his enemies he accepted baptism in 1251, and [[e:pope-innocent-iv|Pope Innocent IV]] authorised his coronation, which took place in July 1253, probably in [[e:vilnius|Vilnius]].
kingdom-of-lithuania.r: As king, [[e:mindaugas|Mindaugas]] ruled a mainly pagan land with a small Catholic church and a [[e:bishop|bishop]] appointed for [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]]. He granted lands, including parts of [[e:samogitia|Samogitia]], to the [[s:livonian-order|Livonian Order]] in return for its support. The kingdom brought [[e:lithuania|Lithuania]] into the diplomatic world of [[e:latin|Latin]] [[e:europe|Europe]] while Mindaugas extended his power over [[e:black-ruthenia|Black Ruthenia]].
kingdom-of-lithuania.e: After the [[e:samogitians|Samogitians]] crushed the [[s:livonian-order|Livonian Order]] at [[e:battle-of-durbe|Durbe]] in 1260, [[e:mindaugas|Mindaugas]] broke with the order and seems to have abandoned [[e:christianity|Christianity]]. He was murdered in 1263 by his nephew [[e:treniota|Treniota]] and [[e:daumantas-of-pskov|Daumantas]], and the royal title lapsed. The state continued as the [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Grand Duchy of Lithuania]]; his coronation is marked by a Lithuanian national holiday.

kadambas-of-goa.t: A Kadamba dynasty that ruled Goa for nearly four centuries, made rich by Arab trade through the port of Gopakapattana.
kadambas-of-goa.o: The [[e:goa|Goa]] [[s:kadamba-dynasty|Kadambas]] claimed descent from the earlier Kadamba dynasty of [[e:banavasi|Banavasi]]. Shashthadeva I established them in the Goa region around 960, at first as feudatories of the [[s:western-chalukya-empire|Western Chalukya Empire]], with the capital at [[e:chandor|Chandrapura]], modern Chandor.
kadambas-of-goa.r: [[e:jayakeshi-i|Jayakeshi I]] moved the capital to the port of [[e:goa-velha|Gopakapattana]] on the Zuari river, modern [[e:goa|Goa]] Velha, which became a busy harbour trading with [[e:arabia|Arabia]], [[e:east-africa|East Africa]] and [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]]; the [[s:kadamba-dynasty|Kadambas]] welcomed Arab merchants and allowed a mosque to be built. They issued gold coins and fought the [[e:silahara-dynasty|Silaharas]] for control of the [[e:konkan-coast|Konkan coast]]. The Mahadeva temple at [[e:tambdi-surla-mahadeva-temple|Tambdi Surla]], built of basalt, survives from their period.
kadambas-of-goa.e: In the 13th century the [[s:kadamba-dynasty|Kadambas]] came under the [[e:seuna-yadava-dynasty|Yadavas]], and in the 14th century [[e:goa|Goa]] was raided by the armies of the [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]]. Around 1345 their rule collapsed, and Goa later passed to the [[s:vijayanagara-empire|Vijayanagara Empire]] and the [[s:bahmani-sultanate|Bahmani Sultanate]].

kingdom-of-the-isle-of-wight.t: A tiny Jutish kingdom on the Isle of Wight, the last part of England to accept Christianity, ended by the violent conquest of Caedwalla in 686.
kingdom-of-the-isle-of-wight.o: [[e:bede|Bede]] reports that the [[e:isle-of-wight|Isle of Wight]], like Kent and part of [[e:hampshire|Hampshire]], was settled by [[e:jutes|Jutes]]. The [[e:anglo-saxon-chronicle|Anglo-Saxon Chronicle]] claims that [[e:cerdic|Cerdic]] and [[e:cynric|Cynric]] took the island in 530 and gave it to their kinsmen Stuf and Wihtgar, but the story is largely legendary.
kingdom-of-the-isle-of-wight.r: The Wihtwara lived from farming and the sea under their own kings, sometimes dependents of greater neighbours. In 661 [[e:wulfhere-of-mercia|Wulfhere]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-mercia|Kingdom of Mercia]] gave the island to the South [[e:saxons|Saxon]] king [[e:aethelwealh-of-sussex|Aethelwealh]]. The island was still pagan in the 680s.
kingdom-of-the-isle-of-wight.e: In 686 [[e:caedwalla|Caedwalla]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-wessex|Kingdom of Wessex]] conquered the island, killed King [[e:arwald|Arwald]] and had his two young brothers executed after baptism, as [[e:bede|Bede]] recounts. The island became part of [[e:wessex|Wessex]] and was converted by [[e:wilfrid|Wilfrid's]] clergy.

kwantung-oblast.t: Russia's leased territory at the tip of the Liaodong peninsula, home of the Port Arthur naval base, lost to Japan in the Russo-Japanese War.
kwantung-oblast.o: After the [[e:triple-intervention|Triple Intervention]] forced [[e:japan|Japan]] to give up the [[e:liaodong|Liaodong]] peninsula in 1895, the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] obtained a twenty-five-year lease of its southern tip from the [[s:qing-empire|Qing Empire]] in 1898. [[e:russia|Russia]] fortified [[e:lushunkou|Port Arthur]] as an ice-free Pacific naval base and built a commercial port at [[e:dalian|Dalny]].
kwantung-oblast.r: The territory was linked to [[e:harbin|Harbin]] by the southern branch of the Chinese Eastern Railway. It was governed by military officers, and in 1903 Admiral [[e:yevgeny-alekseyev|Yevgeny Alekseyev]], based at [[e:lushunkou|Port Arthur]], became [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]] of the [[e:russian-far-east|Russian Far East]]. Russian advance in [[e:manchuria|Manchuria]] alarmed [[e:japan|Japan]] and [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and led directly to war.
kwantung-oblast.e: [[e:japan|Japan]] attacked [[e:lushunkou|Port Arthur]] in February 1904. After a costly siege, the fortress commander [[e:anatoly-stessel|Anatoly Stessel]] surrendered in January 1905. The [[e:treaty-of-portsmouth|Treaty of Portsmouth]] transferred the lease to Japan, which renamed it the [[s:kwantung-leased-territory|Kwantung Leased Territory]].

kingdom-of-tambora.t: Small kingdom on the slopes of Mount Tambora in Sumbawa, wiped out by the largest volcanic eruption in recorded history.
kingdom-of-tambora.o: Little is known of its origins. Tambora was one of several small realms on [[e:sumbawa|Sumbawa]], alongside the [[s:bima-sultanate|Bima Sultanate]], Dompu, Sanggar and the [[s:sumbawa-sultanate|Sumbawa Sultanate]], and from the 17th century it came under Makassarese and then [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] influence through treaties with Sumbawan rulers.
kingdom-of-tambora.r: Its people grew [[e:rice|rice]] and traded horses, honey, sappanwood and sandalwood. Tambora was ruled by a Muslim raja. Its language, recorded in a short wordlist gathered for [[e:stamford-raffles|Thomas Stamford Raffles]], appears unrelated to the Austronesian languages around it and may have been a non-Austronesian isolate.
kingdom-of-tambora.e: The eruption of [[e:mount-tambora|Mount Tambora]] in April 1815 buried the kingdom and neighbouring Pekat under ash and pyroclastic flows, killing nearly all its inhabitants. The ensuing global cooling caused the Year Without a Summer in 1816. Excavations since 2004 have uncovered houses, pottery and remains, earning Tambora the name the [[e:pompeii|Pompeii]] of the East.

kingdom-of-araucania-and-patagonia.t: A kingdom proclaimed among the Mapuche by a French adventurer in 1860, which never won recognition but survives as a claim of French pretenders.
kingdom-of-araucania-and-patagonia.o: [[e:orelie-antoine-de-tounens|Orélie-Antoine de Tounens]], a lawyer from the [[e:dordogne|Dordogne]] in [[e:france|France]], travelled to [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]] in 1858 and went to [[s:araucania|Araucanía]], the independent [[e:mapuche|Mapuche]] lands south of the [[e:biobio-river|Biobío]]. In November 1860 he proclaimed himself King Orélie-Antoine I of Araucanía and, days later, added [[e:patagonia|Patagonia]], claiming support from Mapuche chiefs.
kingdom-of-araucania-and-patagonia.r: The kingdom existed largely on paper. [[e:orelie-antoine-de-tounens|Orélie-Antoine]] issued a constitution, a flag and decrees, and some [[s:araucania|Mapuche]] leaders, such as Quilapán, seem to have seen him as a potential ally against Chilean expansion. He had no army, administration or international recognition, and [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]] regarded the scheme as a threat to its [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]].
kingdom-of-araucania-and-patagonia.e: Chilean authorities arrested him in January 1862, declared him insane and deported him to [[e:france|France]]. He returned several times without success and died in France in 1878. [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]] carried out the [[e:occupation-of-araucania|Occupation of Araucanía]] by 1883. French claimants still use his title.

kingdom-of-ndongo.t: The Mbundu kingdom of the Ngola, whose title gave Angola its name and whose queen Njinga fought the Portuguese for decades.
kingdom-of-ndongo.o: Ndongo was formed by [[e:mbundu|Mbundu]] chiefdoms between the [[e:kwanza-river|Kwanza]] and [[e:lucala-river|Lukala]] rivers in the late 15th century under a ruler titled the Ngola. Initially a tributary of the [[e:kingdom-of-kongo|Kingdom of Kongo]], it asserted independence in the 1550s, and a Portuguese embassy reached its capital [[e:kabasa|Kabasa]] in 1560.
kingdom-of-ndongo.r: The Ngola ruled through regional lords (sobas) who paid tribute in [[e:cattle|cattle]], salt, cloth and slaves. From 1575, when [[e:paulo-dias-de-novais|Paulo Dias de Novais]] founded [[e:luanda|Luanda]], Ndongo faced constant war with [[s:portuguese-angola|Portuguese Angola]] and its [[e:imbangala|Imbangala]] allies, who sought slaves for the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|Atlantic trade]]. [[e:njinga-of-ndongo-and-matamba|Njinga Mbande]], who became ruler in 1624, negotiated, converted, fought and allied with the [[e:dutch|Dutch]], later ruling from the [[s:kingdom-of-matamba|Kingdom of Matamba]].
kingdom-of-ndongo.e: Ndongo was split between [[e:njinga-of-ndongo-and-matamba|Njinga]]'s party and a Portuguese-backed puppet king, [[e:ngola-hari|Ngola Hari]]. When his successor rebelled, the Portuguese stormed the fortress of [[e:pungo-andongo|Pungo Andongo]] in 1671, ending the kingdom. The Ngola title gave [[s:portuguese-angola|Angola]] its name, and Njinga is a national heroine.

kingdom-of-greece.t: The Greek monarchy from 1832 to 1973, which more than doubled Greece's territory and lived through the National Schism, occupation, civil war and dictatorship.
kingdom-of-greece.o: Under the [[e:london-conference-of-1832|London Conference of 1832]], [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], [[e:france|France]] and [[e:russia|Russia]] made [[e:otto-of-greece|Otto of Bavaria]] king of independent [[e:greece|Greece]], replacing the [[s:first-hellenic-republic|First Hellenic Republic]]. He arrived at [[e:nafplio|Nauplia]] in 1833 with Bavarian regents, and [[s:athens|Athens]] became the capital in 1834. A revolt in September 1843 forced him to grant a constitution.
kingdom-of-greece.r: Otto was deposed in 1862 and replaced by [[e:george-i-of-greece|George I]], whose long reign added the [[s:united-states-of-the-ionian-islands|Ionian Islands]] (1864), [[e:thessaly|Thessaly]] (1881) and, through the Balkan Wars, Macedonia, [[e:epirus|Epirus]] and [[e:crete|Crete]]. Politics were shaped by the [[e:megali-idea|Great Idea]] of uniting [[e:greeks|Greeks]] and by the clash between [[e:eleftherios-venizelos|Eleftherios Venizelos]] and [[e:constantine-i-of-greece|King Constantine I]]. Defeat in [[e:asia-minor|Asia Minor]] in 1922 brought a population exchange with [[e:turkey|Turkey]].
kingdom-of-greece.e: The monarchy was replaced by the [[s:second-hellenic-republic|Second Hellenic Republic]] in 1924 and restored in 1935, followed by the [[e:ioannis-metaxas|Metaxas]] dictatorship, [[e:axis-powers|Axis]] occupation and civil war. After the 1967 coup, [[e:constantine-ii-of-greece|Constantine II]] went into exile; the junta abolished the monarchy in 1973, confirmed by referendum in 1974.

kingdom-of-yugoslavia.t: First united state of the South Slavs, a monarchy torn by rivalry between Serbs and Croats and destroyed by the Axis invasion of 1941.
kingdom-of-yugoslavia.o: As [[e:austro-hungarian-empire|Austria-Hungary]] collapsed, the [[s:state-of-slovenes-croats-and-serbs|State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs]] joined the [[s:kingdom-of-serbia|Kingdom of Serbia]] and [[s:montenegro|Montenegro]] to form the Kingdom of [[e:serbs|Serbs]], [[e:croats|Croats]] and [[e:slovenes|Slovenes]], proclaimed in [[e:belgrade|Belgrade]] on 1 December 1918 under the [[e:karadordevic-dynasty|Karađorđević dynasty]]. Its borders, confirmed by the post-war treaties, joined lands with very different histories, faiths and economies.
kingdom-of-yugoslavia.r: The centralist [[e:vidovdan-constitution|Vidovdan Constitution]] of 1921 favoured Serbian dominance and was opposed by [[e:stjepan-radic|Stjepan Radić's]] [[e:croatian-peasant-party|Croatian Peasant Party]]. After Radić was shot in parliament in 1928, King Alexander imposed a dictatorship in 1929 and renamed the country [[e:yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]]. He was assassinated in [[s:massalia|Marseille]] in 1934, and Prince Paul's regency created the [[s:banovina-of-croatia|Banovina of Croatia]] in 1939.
kingdom-of-yugoslavia.e: In March 1941 the government signed the [[e:tripartite-pact|Tripartite Pact]], but officers overthrew it two days later. [[e:germany|Germany]] and its allies invaded on 6 April 1941 and the army capitulated within eleven days. King [[e:peter-ii-of-yugoslavia|Peter II]] went into exile, and the country was partitioned among the [[s:independent-state-of-croatia|Independent State of Croatia]] and occupying powers.
kingdom-of-yugoslavia.re: Serbian Orthodox and Catholic Christianity, Sunni Islam

kingdom-of-gajaaga.t: Soninke kingdom of the upper Senegal river, called Galam by the French, a hub of the gum, gold and slave trades.
kingdom-of-gajaaga.o: Gajaaga was founded by the Bacili clan of [[e:soninke|Soninke]] on the upper [[e:senegal|Senegal]] around the junction with the [[e:faleme-river|Faleme]] river, an area rich in gold from nearby [[e:bambuk|Bambuk]]. It emerged as an independent kingdom in the 17th century as larger [[e:sahel|Sahel]] empires declined.
kingdom-of-gajaaga.r: The ruler, the Tunka, was chosen from the Bacili lineages and ruled from Maxanna and other river towns. The French built Fort Saint-Joseph nearby around 1700 and later [[e:bakel|Bakel]], and Gajaaga traded slaves, gum arabic, gold and grain down the river to [[e:saint-louis-senegal|Saint-Louis]]. [[e:soninke|Soninke]] merchants and clerics were active traders across the region.
kingdom-of-gajaaga.e: Civil wars in the 18th and 19th centuries left Gajaaga divided into two parts, Goye and Kammera. The French extended their control and placed the area under a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] in 1858, and it became part of [[s:french-senegal|French Senegal]].

keos.t: Cycladic island state of four small cities nearest to Attica, home of the poets Simonides and Bacchylides.
keos.o: Keos lies off the tip of [[e:attica|Attica]] and had a major [[e:bronze-age|Bronze Age]] town at [[e:ayia-irini-kea|Ayia Irini]]. In the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] [[e:ionia|Ionian Greeks]] settled it, and the island was organised as a tetrapolis of four cities, Ioulis, [[e:karthaia|Karthaia]], [[e:koressia|Koressia]] and [[e:poiessa|Poiessa]], which sometimes acted together as one state.
keos.r: Keos was famous for its poets: [[e:simonides-of-ceos|Simonides]] and his nephew [[e:bacchylides|Bacchylides]], both from Ioulis, wrote for patrons across [[e:greece|Greece]] in the 6th and 5th centuries BCE. [[e:strabo|Strabo]] records a Keian law said to require citizens over sixty to drink hemlock. The island exported ruddle, a red earth pigment, and paid tribute in the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]].
keos.e: Keos joined the [[s:second-athenian-league|Second Athenian League]] but revolted in the 360s BCE and was subdued. In the 3rd century BCE [[e:koressia|Koressia]] became a Ptolemaic naval base renamed [[s:kingdom-of-marion|Arsinoe]]. The island passed under Roman control by 146 BCE.

kingdom-of-nri.t: Igbo sacred kingdom whose priest-king, the Eze Nri, held ritual rather than military authority over a wide area of south-eastern Nigeria for nearly a thousand years.
kingdom-of-nri.o: Nri traditions trace the kingdom to Eri, a culture hero said to have come down from the sky near the [[e:anambra-river|Anambra]] river, and to his descendant Ifikuanim, remembered as the first [[e:eze-nri|Eze Nri]]. The traditional founding date of 948 rests on genealogical reckoning. The famous 9th and 10th century bronzes from nearby [[e:igbo-ukwu|Igbo-Ukwu]] are often linked to Nri ritual culture.
kingdom-of-nri.r: The [[e:eze-nri|Eze Nri]] was a ritual ruler chosen after an interregnum and secluded in his palace. Nri did not rule by force: its titled priests, marked with ichi facial scars, travelled across [[e:igboland|Igboland]] to cleanse abominations, crown local title-holders, settle disputes and proclaim peace. The Ozo title system and a network of yam and agricultural rites spread from Nri.
kingdom-of-nri.e: Nri's influence waned from the 18th century as the [[s:aro-confederacy|Aro Confederacy]] and slave trading reshaped [[e:igboland|Igboland]]. In 1911 British colonial officials forced the [[e:eze-nri|Eze Nri]] to renounce his ritual powers. The title survives as a traditional office in [[e:anambra-state|Anambra State]], and Nri is remembered as a cradle of [[e:igbo-people|Igbo]] culture.

kingdom-of-bamum.t: Grassfields kingdom of western Cameroon whose king Ibrahim Njoya invented a script, a religion and a palace culture still admired today.
kingdom-of-bamum.o: Bamum tradition traces the dynasty to [[e:nchare-yen|Nchare Yen]], a [[e:tikar-people|Tikar]] prince who conquered the area around [[e:foumban|Foumban]] and became its first Mfon, traditionally in 1394. The kingdom remained small until the late 18th or early 19th century, when Mbuembue expanded it greatly and fortified the capital with a deep ditch.
kingdom-of-bamum.r: The Mfon ruled from a large palace at [[e:foumban|Foumban]] with titled palace servants and councils of nobles. Bamum was famous for brass casting, beadwork and carved thrones. King [[e:ibrahim-njoya|Ibrahim Njoya]], who came to the throne in the late 1880s, created the Bamum script, a [[e:printing-press|printing]] press, maps and a syncretic religion blending [[e:islam|Islam]], [[e:christianity|Christianity]] and local belief.
kingdom-of-bamum.e: Bamum came under [[s:kamerun|German Kamerun]] around 1902 and then [[s:french-cameroon|French Cameroon]] after the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]]. The French curtailed [[e:ibrahim-njoya|Njoya]]'s power in the 1920s and exiled him in 1931. The dynasty survives as a sultanate at [[e:foumban|Foumban]], whose palace houses a renowned museum.

kadi-burhan-al-din-state.t: The sultanate of a judge and poet who seized the Eretnid throne and held central Anatolia against the Ottomans, Mamluks and Turkmen.
kadi-burhan-al-din-state.o: [[e:kadi-burhan-al-din|Kadi Burhan al-Din]] Ahmad was a jurist from [[e:kayseri|Kayseri]] who served the [[s:eretnids|Eretnids]] as judge and [[e:vizier|vizier]]. As the dynasty weakened he became the real power, and in 1381, after the death of [[e:ala-al-din-ali|Ala al-Din Ali]], he declared himself sultan in [[e:sivas|Sivas]].
kadi-burhan-al-din-state.r: He spent his reign fighting: against the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]], whom he defeated at [[e:battle-of-kirkdilim|Kirkdilim]] in 1392, against the [[e:mamluk|Mamluks]], the [[s:aq-qoyunlu|Aq Qoyunlu]], [[e:mutahharten|Mutahharten of Erzincan]] and the beys of [[e:amasya|Amasya]]. He was also a poet whose divan of Turkish verse is one of the earliest in [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]], and his court historian Astarabadi wrote the [[e:bazm-u-razm|Bazm u Razm]], a chronicle of his reign in Persian.
kadi-burhan-al-din-state.e: In 1398 he was killed by the [[s:aq-qoyunlu|Aq Qoyunlu]] chief [[e:qara-yuluk-osman|Qara Yuluk Osman]]. [[e:sivas|Sivas]] surrendered to [[e:bayezid-i|Bayezid I]], but [[e:timur|Timur]] destroyed it in 1400.

kingdom-of-gumma.t: A Gibe Oromo kingdom of south-western Ethiopia, known for its fervent Islam and for resisting incorporation into Menelik's empire.
kingdom-of-gumma.o: Gumma emerged around 1810 west of the [[e:didessa-river|Didessa]], as [[e:oromo|Oromo]] groups of the region formed hereditary monarchies. It was one of five [[e:gibe-river|Gibe]] kingdoms, alongside the [[s:kingdom-of-jimma|Kingdom of Jimma]], [[s:limmu-ennarea|Limmu-Ennarea]], the [[s:kingdom-of-gomma|Kingdom of Gomma]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-gera|Kingdom of Gera]].
kingdom-of-gumma.r: Gumma's kings governed through appointed officials and drew revenue from farming and trade in [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]], [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and slaves. The kingdom became known as a centre of militant [[e:islam|Islam]], and its rulers waged campaigns against non-Muslim neighbours. Little else is recorded in detail.
kingdom-of-gumma.e: Gumma was subjected to the [[s:ethiopian-empire|Ethiopian Empire]] in the 1880s, and after a revolt it was finally conquered and annexed in 1902.

kingdom-of-lydia.t: Lydia, the western Anatolian kingdom of Sardis, where the first coins were struck and Croesus became a byword for wealth.
kingdom-of-lydia.o: Greek tradition traced a Heraclid dynasty in [[e:lydia|Lydia]], then called Maeonia, back to c. 1200 BCE, but the kingdom becomes historical with [[e:gyges-of-lydia|Gyges]], who seized the throne c. 680 BCE and founded the [[e:mermnad-dynasty|Mermnad dynasty]]. He fought the [[s:cimmerians|Cimmerians]] and sent gifts to [[s:delphi|Delphi]].
kingdom-of-lydia.r: From [[e:sardis|Sardis]] the [[e:mermnad-dynasty|Mermnad]] kings ruled the [[e:gediz-river|Hermus]] valley and subdued most Greek cities of [[e:ionia|Ionia]]. Electrum from the river [[e:pactolus|Pactolus]] underpinned the first coinage in the late 7th century BCE, and [[e:croesus|Croesus]] introduced separate gold and [[e:silver|silver]] coins. The huge burial mound of [[e:alyattes|Alyattes]] stands at [[e:bin-tepe|Bin Tepe]].
kingdom-of-lydia.e: After a war with the [[s:median-empire|Median Empire]] ended by the eclipse of 585 BCE, [[e:croesus|Croesus]] attacked [[e:persia|Persia]] and was defeated by [[e:cyrus-the-great|Cyrus]], who took [[e:sardis|Sardis]] c. 546 BCE. [[e:lydia|Lydia]] became a [[e:satrapy|satrapy]] of the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]], and Sardis its western capital.

kingdom-of-argyll-and-the-isles.t: The short-lived sea realm of Somerled, who seized the southern Hebrides from the kings of Man and founded the dynasty of the Lords of the Isles.
kingdom-of-argyll-and-the-isles.o: [[e:somerled|Somerled]], a Norse-Gaelic warlord of [[e:argyll|Argyll]] married to a daughter of Olaf I of Man, challenged his brother-in-law [[e:godred-olafsson|Godred]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-isles|Kingdom of the Isles]]. After a sea battle in 1156 the [[e:hebrides|Hebrides]] were divided, and in 1158 Somerled drove Godred from Man, ruling Argyll, [[e:kintyre|Kintyre]] and the southern isles.
kingdom-of-argyll-and-the-isles.r: [[e:somerled|Somerled's]] power rested on galley fleets and the loyalty of Gaelic and Norse-Gaelic kindreds. He acted as an independent ruler, sometimes allied with and sometimes against the Scottish king, and is linked with the founding of [[e:saddell-abbey|Saddell Abbey]] in [[e:kintyre|Kintyre]].
kingdom-of-argyll-and-the-isles.e: [[e:somerled|Somerled]] was killed in 1164 at [[e:battle-of-renfrew|Renfrew]] while invading the [[s:kingdom-of-scotland|Kingdom of Scotland]]. His realm was divided among his sons, ancestors of the [[e:clan-macdougall|MacDougalls]], [[e:clan-donald|MacDonalds]] and [[e:clann-ruaidhri|MacRuairis]], whose descendants later formed the [[s:lordship-of-the-isles|Lordship of the Isles]].

kingdom-of-nso.t: The largest kingdom of Cameroon's Bamenda Grassfields, ruled by the Fon of Nso from Kumbo.
kingdom-of-nso.o: Nso tradition names [[e:ngonnso|Ngonnso]], a [[e:tikar-people|Tikar]] princess who left her home with followers, as the founder of the kingdom, traditionally around the late 14th century. The early capital moved several times before settling at [[e:kumbo|Kumbo]], and Nso expanded by absorbing neighbouring chiefdoms in the 18th and 19th centuries.
kingdom-of-nso.r: The [[e:fon-title|Fon]] ruled as a sacred king with regulatory societies, the Ngwerong and Ngiri, which enforced his decisions, kept royal rituals and managed succession. Lineage heads held land and titles. Nso fought long wars with the [[s:kingdom-of-bamum|Kingdom of Bamum]], and craftsmen produced carved masks, stools and beaded regalia.
kingdom-of-nso.e: German forces occupied [[e:kumbo|Kumbo]] in the first years of the 20th century, and Nso became part of [[s:kamerun|German Kamerun]] and later [[s:british-cameroons|British Cameroons]]. The [[e:fon-title|Fon]] of Nso still reigns. In 2022 [[e:berlin|Berlin's]] museums agreed to return a statue of [[e:ngonnso|Ngonnso]] taken by a German officer.

kingdom-of-magadha.t: The kingdom of south Bihar that conquered its rivals one by one and became the core of the Nanda and Maurya empires.
kingdom-of-magadha.o: [[e:magadha|Magadha]] lay south of the [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges]] in modern [[e:bihar|Bihar]], around the hill-ringed capital of [[e:rajgir|Rajagriha]]. Vedic texts regarded it as a land on the edge of orthodox society. Its rise began in the mid-6th century BCE under [[e:bimbisara|Bimbisara]] of the [[e:haryanka-dynasty|Haryanka dynasty]], who conquered the [[s:kingdom-of-anga|Kingdom of Anga]] and won [[s:kingdom-of-kashi|Kashi]] territory by marriage alliance.
kingdom-of-magadha.r: [[e:magadha|Magadha's]] kings built a strong army, helped by fertile [[e:rice|rice]] land, iron ore from the hills and forests that supplied [[e:war-elephant|war elephants]]. [[e:bimbisara|Bimbisara]] and his son [[e:ajatashatru|Ajatashatru]] were patrons of the Buddha and [[e:mahavira|Mahavira]], and the First Buddhist Council met at [[e:rajgir|Rajagriha]]. Ajatashatru conquered the [[s:vajji|Vajji]] league and [[s:kingdom-of-kosala|Kosala]], his successor [[e:udayin|Udayin]] founded [[e:pataliputra|Pataliputra]], and the [[e:shishunaga-dynasty|Shishunaga dynasty]] later conquered [[s:kingdom-of-avanti|Avanti]].
kingdom-of-magadha.e: Around 345 BCE [[e:mahapadma-nanda|Mahapadma Nanda]] overthrew the last [[e:shishunaga-dynasty|Shishunaga]] king and founded the [[s:nanda-empire|Nanda Empire]], which ruled from [[e:pataliputra|Pataliputra]] over most of the [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges]] valley. [[e:magadha|Magadha]] remained the heart of the [[s:maurya-empire|Maurya Empire]] and, centuries later, of the [[s:gupta-empire|Gupta Empire]].

keraite-khanate.t: A powerful Christian steppe khanate in central Mongolia, whose ruler Toghrul was Genghis Khan's patron and rival, and later the model for legends of Prester John.
keraite-khanate.o: The [[e:keraites|Keraites]] were a large tribal union living along the [[e:orkhon-river|Orkhon]] and [[e:tuul-river|Tuul]] rivers in central [[s:mongolia|Mongolia]], probably of Mongolic speech with strong Turkic influences. [[e:syriac|Syriac]] sources record that their ruler converted to the [[e:church-of-the-east|Church of the East]] around 1007, together with many of his people.
keraite-khanate.r: The khanate was a confederation of clans under a ruling family, with Christian priests and Nestorian practices alongside steppe customs. Its rulers, among them [[e:marghuz-buyruk|Marghuz Buyruk]], fought the [[e:tatars|Tatars]], [[s:naiman-khanate|Naimans]] and [[s:merkit-confederation|Merkits]]. [[e:ong-khan|Toghrul]], sworn brother of [[e:genghis-khan|Temüjin's]] father, became the most powerful khan of central [[s:mongolia|Mongolia]] and received the title Ong Khan from the [[s:jin-dynasty-1115-1234|Jin dynasty]] (1115-1234) in 1196 after the campaign against the Tatars.
keraite-khanate.e: [[e:ong-khan|Toghrul]] helped the young [[e:genghis-khan|Temüjin]] rise but turned against him; in 1203 Temüjin defeated the [[e:keraites|Keraites]], and Toghrul was killed by [[s:naiman-khanate|Naimans]] while fleeing. The Keraites joined the [[s:mongol-empire|Mongol Empire]]; the Keraite princess [[e:sorghaghtani-beki|Sorghaghtani Beki]] was mother of [[e:mongke|Möngke]], [[e:kublai-khan|Kublai]] and [[e:hulagu-khan|Hülegü]].

kingdom-of-italy-medieval.t: The medieval Kingdom of Italy, contested by Italian magnates after 888 and then held by the German emperors, whose authority waned as the cities grew.
kingdom-of-italy-medieval.o: When the [[s:carolingian-empire|Carolingian Empire]] broke up in 888, Italian nobles elected [[e:berengar-i-of-italy|Berengar of Friuli]] as King of [[e:italy|Italy]]. For seventy years rival [[e:magnates|magnates]] and outsiders, among them Guy and [[e:lambert-of-italy|Lambert of Spoleto]], [[e:louis-the-blind|Louis of Provence]], Rudolf of [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Burgundy]] and [[e:hugh-of-arles|Hugh of Arles]], fought for the crown, which was traditionally received at [[s:commune-of-pavia|Pavia]].
kingdom-of-italy-medieval.r: In 951 [[e:otto-i|Otto I]] of [[e:germany|Germany]] took the title, and from his imperial coronation in 962 the crown was tied to the German emperors, often crowned with the [[e:iron-crown-of-lombardy|Iron Crown of Lombardy]]. [[e:arduin-of-ivrea|Arduin of Ivrea]] was the last native king (1002–1014). Imperial rule relied on [[e:bishop|bishops]] and counts, but the communes grew independent; the [[s:lombard-league|Lombard League]] defeated [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]] at [[e:battle-of-legnano|Legnano]] in 1176, and the [[e:peace-of-constance|Peace of Constance]] in 1183 recognised their self-government.
kingdom-of-italy-medieval.e: After the 13th century the kingdom survived mainly as a legal framework of imperial fiefs. [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]] was the last emperor crowned King of [[e:italy|Italy]], at [[s:republic-of-bologna|Bologna]] in 1530. Imperial claims in Italy ended with the [[e:french-revolutionary-wars|French Revolutionary Wars]] and the [[e:treaty-of-luneville|Treaty of Lunéville]] in 1801.

kingdom-of-baol.t: Wolof and Serer kingdom of central Senegal, often united with Cayor, where Amadou Bamba later founded the holy city of Touba.
kingdom-of-baol.o: [[e:baol|Baol]] was a province of the [[s:jolof-empire|Jolof Empire]] that broke away in the mid-16th century, following [[e:cayor|Cayor's]] victory at [[e:battle-of-danki|Danki]] in 1549. Its ruler, the Teigne, was chosen from royal lineages with ties to both [[e:wolof|Wolof]] and [[e:serer|Serer]] families, and the capital was at Lambaye.
kingdom-of-baol.r: The Teigne ruled with titled chiefs and a slave soldiery over a mixed population of [[e:wolof|Wolof]] and [[e:serer|Serer]] farmers growing [[e:millet|millet]] and later [[e:groundnut|groundnuts]]. [[e:baol|Baol]] was frequently united with [[s:cayor|Cayor]] under one ruler; [[e:lat-sukaabe-fall|Lat Sukaabe Fall]] held both thrones around 1700. Baol's coastal towns traded with the French and Portuguese.
kingdom-of-baol.e: [[e:france|France]] established control over [[e:baol|Baol]] in the 1880s and 1890s and absorbed it into [[s:french-senegal|French Senegal]]. In 1887 the [[e:sufism|Sufi]] leader [[e:amadou-bamba|Amadou Bamba]] founded [[e:touba|Touba]] in Baol, and the region became the heartland of the [[e:mouride-brotherhood|Mouride brotherhood]].

kara-khanid-khanate.t: The first Turkic dynasty to adopt Islam as a state religion, which brought Transoxiana under Turkic rule and produced classic works of Turkic literature.
kara-khanid-khanate.o: The Kara-Khanid dynasty emerged in the mid-9th century among the [[s:karluk-yabgu|Karluk Yabgu]], [[e:chigils|Chigil]] and [[e:yaghma|Yagma]] tribes after the fall of the [[s:uyghur-khaganate|Uyghur Khaganate]], with centres at [[e:balasagun|Balasagun]] and [[s:kingdom-of-shule|Kashgar]]. Around 934 the ruler [[e:satuq-bughra-khan|Satuq Bughra Khan]] converted to [[e:islam|Islam]], and his successors made it the religion of the state.
kara-khanid-khanate.r: The khanate had a dual structure, with a senior [[e:khagan|khagan]] and a junior co-ruler, and [[e:appanage|appanages]] held by members of the royal clan. In 999 it took [[e:bukhara|Bukhara]] from the [[s:samanid-empire|Samanid Empire]], bringing [[e:transoxiana|Transoxiana]] under Turkic rule. The Kara-Khanids built mosques and [[e:madrasa|madrasas]], and Turkic Islamic literature grew up under them, culminating after the split in [[e:yusuf-balasaguni|Yusuf Balasaguni's]] [[e:kutadgu-bilig|Kutadgu Bilig]] and the dictionary of Turkic languages that the Kara-Khanid prince Mahmud al-Kashgari compiled in [[e:baghdad|Baghdad]].
kara-khanid-khanate.e: Dynastic rivalry split the khanate around 1042 into the [[s:eastern-kara-khanid-khanate|Eastern Kara-Khanid Khanate]] and the [[s:western-kara-khanid-khanate|Western Kara-Khanid Khanate]], which became [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[e:seljuk-empire|Seljuks]] and the [[s:qara-khitai|Qara Khitai]].

kingdom-of-navarre.t: The Basque Pyrenean kingdom of Pamplona, which under Sancho III dominated Christian Spain and survived in part until 1841.
kingdom-of-navarre.o: Around 824, after the [[e:basques|Basques]] defeated a Frankish army at the second Battle of [[e:battle-of-roncevaux-pass|Roncevaux]], [[e:inigo-arista|Íñigo Arista]] became ruler of [[e:pamplona|Pamplona]], allied with his kinsmen the [[s:banu-qasi|Banu Qasi]]. In 905 [[e:sancho-garces-i-of-pamplona|Sancho Garcés]] I founded the [[e:jimenez-dynasty|Jimena dynasty]] and pushed south into the [[e:ebro-river|Ebro]] valley and [[e:la-rioja-spain|La Rioja]].
kingdom-of-navarre.r: [[e:sancho-iii-of-navarre|Sancho III the Great]], from 1004 to 1035, controlled Aragon, [[s:kingdom-of-castile|Castile]] and the Pyrenean counties, the dominant power of Christian [[e:iberia|Iberia]]. After a period of partition between 1076 and 1134, the kingdom revived. [[e:sancho-vii-of-navarre|Sancho VII]] fought at [[e:battle-of-las-navas-de-tolosa|Las Navas de Tolosa]] in 1212. French dynasties ruled from 1234, and [[e:charles-iii-of-navarre|Charles III the Noble]] built the palace of [[e:olite|Olite]]. Basque, Romance and [[e:latin|Latin]] were spoken, and the kingdom kept its own fueros and cortes.
kingdom-of-navarre.e: In 1512 [[e:ferdinand-ii-of-aragon|Ferdinand the Catholic]] conquered [[e:upper-navarre|Upper Navarre]], joined to [[s:kingdom-of-castile|Castile]] in 1515, while [[s:lower-navarre|Lower Navarre]] north of the [[e:pyrenees|Pyrenees]] remained with the [[e:house-of-albret|Albret]] family. Its kings became kings of [[e:france|France]] in 1589. Spanish Navarre kept its own institutions until the law of 1841 made it a province.

khanate-of-kokand.t: An Uzbek khanate of the Ferghana valley that grew to rule Tashkent and the Kyrgyz and Kazakh steppes before Russia annexed it in 1876.
khanate-of-kokand.o: Around 1709 [[e:shahrukh-bi|Shahrukh Bi]], leader of the [[e:ming-empire|Ming]] [[e:uzbeks|Uzbek]] tribe, broke away from the [[s:khanate-of-bukhara|Khanate of Bukhara]] and established a separate state in the eastern [[s:principality-of-ferghana|Ferghana]] valley. His successors built [[e:kokand|Kokand]] as their capital, and Narbuta Bi strengthened the state in the late 18th century.
khanate-of-kokand.r: [[e:alim-khan-of-kokand|Alim Khan]], who took the title khan around 1800, created a standing army and conquered [[e:tashkent|Tashkent]] in 1809. His brother and successor [[e:umar-khan-of-kokand|Umar Khan]] was a patron of poetry whose wife [[e:nodira|Nodira]] was a celebrated poet. The khanate controlled the trade routes to [[s:kingdom-of-shule|Kashgar]] and dominated [[e:kyrgyz-people|Kyrgyz]] and [[e:kazakhs|Kazakh]] nomads, building forts such as [[e:kyzylorda|Ak-Mechet]] on the [[e:syr-darya|Syr Darya]]. Rivalry between settled [[e:sarts|Sarts]] and nomadic [[e:kipchaks|Kipchaks]] caused civil wars.
khanate-of-kokand.e: [[e:russia|Russia]] took [[e:kyzylorda|Ak-Mechet]] in 1853 and [[e:tashkent|Tashkent]] in 1865. After a revolt against the pro-Russian [[e:khudayar-khan|Khudayar Khan]] in 1875, General [[e:mikhail-skobelev|Skobelev]] crushed resistance and Russia annexed the khanate in 1876 as the [[s:principality-of-ferghana|Ferghana]] Oblast of the [[s:turkestan-governorate-general|Turkestan Governorate-General]].

kingdom-of-ui-failge.t: Irish midland kingdom of the O'Connor Faly, which resisted English expansion from its bogland strongholds until the plantation of Offaly in 1556.
kingdom-of-ui-failge.o: The Uí Failge, 'descendants of Failge', claimed descent from Rus Failge, a son of the legendary [[s:kingdom-of-leinster|Leinster]] king [[e:cathair-mor|Cathair Mór]]. From the early [[e:middle-ages|medieval period]] they held a kingdom in the north-west of the Kingdom of Leinster, in what is now [[e:county-offaly|County Offaly]], which takes its name from them. From the 11th century their rulers were the [[e:oconnor-faly|Ua Conchobair Failge]], O'Connor Faly.
kingdom-of-ui-failge.r: Their territory of bog, esker and woodland was hard for invaders to penetrate. After the [[e:anglo-norman-invasion-of-ireland|Anglo-Norman invasion]] the [[e:fitzgeralds-of-kildare|FitzGeralds of Kildare]] took their eastern lands, but the [[e:oconnor-faly|O'Connors Faly]] held the rest, raiding the [[e:the-pale|Pale]] and taking protection payments known as black rent. Their stronghold at [[e:daingean|Daingean]], set among bogs, was their main fortress in the 16th century.
kingdom-of-ui-failge.e: After [[e:brian-oconnor-faly|Brian O'Connor Faly]] rebelled and surrendered in the 1540s, the English took [[e:daingean|Daingean]]. In 1556 the government of [[e:mary-i-of-england|Mary I]] shired the kingdom as [[e:county-offaly|King's County]], with Daingean renamed Philipstown, and planted it with English settlers, ending the kingdom.
kingdom-of-ui-failge.la: Old Irish, later Middle and Early Modern Irish

kingdom-of-croatia-925-1102.t: Medieval Croatian kingdom of the Trpimirović dynasty, which reached from the Drava to the Adriatic before passing to the Hungarian crown.
kingdom-of-croatia-925-1102.o: Around 925 [[e:tomislav-of-croatia|Tomislav]], ruler of the [[s:duchy-of-croatia|Duchy of Croatia]], also held the [[s:duchy-of-pannonian-croatia|Duchy of Pannonian Croatia]] and was addressed as king in papal letters. He had defeated [[e:hungarian-invasions-of-europe|Hungarian raids]] and the army of [[e:simeon-i-of-bulgaria|Simeon I of Bulgaria]], uniting the [[e:croats|Croats]] in one kingdom.
kingdom-of-croatia-925-1102.r: Kings ruled with a council of nobles and bans, from royal seats such as [[e:knin|Knin]], [[e:biograd-na-moru|Biograd na Moru]] and Nin. [[e:petar-kresimir-iv|Petar Krešimir IV]] (1058–1074) brought the Byzantine Dalmatian towns under his control, and [[e:demetrius-zvonimir|Demetrius Zvonimir]] was crowned by a papal legate in 1076, tying [[e:croatia|Croatia]] to the Reformed [[e:papacy|papacy]]. The [[e:baska-tablet|Baška tablet]] records Zvonimir's gift in Glagolitic script.
kingdom-of-croatia-925-1102.e: After [[e:demetrius-zvonimir|Zvonimir]] died without heirs, [[e:ladislaus-i-of-hungary|Ladislaus I of Hungary]] claimed the throne. The last king, [[e:petar-snacic|Petar Snačić]], fell at [[e:battle-of-gvozd-mountain|Gvozd]] in 1097, and in 1102 Coloman was crowned king of [[e:croatia|Croatia]], beginning the [[s:kingdom-of-croatia-1102-1526|Kingdom of Croatia]] (1102-1526) in union with [[e:hungary|Hungary]].

kingdom-of-kucha.t: The largest oasis kingdom of the northern Tarim Basin, a Buddhist centre famous for its music, the Kizil caves and the great translator Kumarajiva.
kingdom-of-kucha.o: Kucha, Qiuci in Chinese, was an Indo-European-speaking oasis state between the [[e:tian-shan|Tianshan]] Mountains and the Taklamakan desert, recorded from the 2nd century BCE among the kingdoms of the [[e:western-regions|Western Regions]]. Its rulers, later known in Chinese by the surname Bai, balanced between the [[e:xiongnu-empire|Xiongnu]], the [[s:han-dynasty|Han Dynasty]] and later steppe powers.
kingdom-of-kucha.r: Kuchean, now called Tocharian B, was written in Brahmi script. Kucha's monasteries, including the painted caves at [[e:kizil-caves|Kizil]], made it a leading centre of [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]], and the translator [[e:kumarajiva|Kumarajiva]] was born there in 344; in 384 the [[s:former-qin|Former Qin]] general [[e:lu-guang|Lü Guang]] took the city and carried him east. Kuchean musicians and instruments shaped the court music of the [[e:sui-dynasty|Sui]] and the [[s:tang-dynasty|Tang Dynasty]].
kingdom-of-kucha.e: The [[s:later-tang|Tang]] conquered Kucha in 648 and made it the seat of the [[e:anxi-protectorate|Anxi Protectorate]]. When Tang control collapsed in the late 8th century, [[e:uyghurs|Uyghurs]] moved in, and after 840 Kucha became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-qocho|Kingdom of Qocho]] and was gradually Turkicised.

kingdom-of-gododdin.t: British kingdom of Lothian centred on Edinburgh, celebrated in the early Welsh poem Y Gododdin, which fell to Northumbria in the 7th century.
kingdom-of-gododdin.o: Gododdin was the post-Roman kingdom of the [[s:votadini|Votadini]], whose name became Guotodin and then Gododdin in Welsh. Its centre was [[e:din-eidyn|Din Eidyn]], the rock of [[e:edinburgh|Edinburgh]], and it stretched across [[e:lothian|Lothian]] and the eastern Borders. Welsh tradition also linked the district of [[e:manaw-gododdin|Manaw Gododdin]], around the head of the [[e:firth-of-forth|Forth]], with [[e:cunedda|Cunedda]], legendary founder of the [[s:kingdom-of-gwynedd|Kingdom of Gwynedd]].
kingdom-of-gododdin.r: The kingdom is best known from Y Gododdin, attributed to the poet [[e:aneirin|Aneirin]], which mourns a war band feasted for a year by [[e:mynyddog-mwynfawr|Mynyddog Mwynfawr]] at [[e:din-eidyn|Din Eidyn]] and then slaughtered at [[e:battle-of-catraeth|Catraeth]], usually identified as [[e:catterick|Catterick]], around 600. The poem portrays an aristocratic warrior society bound by loyalty, mead and gifts. Hillforts such as [[e:traprain-law|Traprain Law]] and [[e:castle-rock-edinburgh|Edinburgh Castle Rock]] were key centres.
kingdom-of-gododdin.e: The Anglian kingdom of [[s:kingdom-of-bernicia|Bernicia]], later [[s:kingdom-of-northumbria|Northumbria]], expanded northward in the 7th century. Irish annals record the siege of Etin in 638, generally taken as the Northumbrian capture of [[e:edinburgh|Edinburgh]]. [[e:lothian|Lothian]] remained English until it passed to the Scottish kings in the 10th and 11th centuries.

kingdom-of-kazembe.t: The eastern Lunda kingdom of the Luapula valley, a wealthy trading state visited by Portuguese explorers and David Livingstone.
kingdom-of-kazembe.o: Around 1740 a [[e:lunda-empire|Lunda]] general sent east by the [[e:mwata-yamvo|Mwata Yamvo]] of the [[s:lunda-empire|Lunda Empire]] conquered the [[e:luapula-river|Luapula]] valley south of [[e:lake-mweru|Lake Mweru]]. His successors, bearing the title Mwata [[e:kazembe|Kazembe]], built an independent kingdom that still paid tribute to the Lunda court.
kingdom-of-kazembe.r: The [[e:kazembe|Kazembe]] ruled from a large capital through [[e:lunda-empire|Lunda]] aristocrats who governed local chiefs. The kingdom traded [[e:copper|copper]] from [[e:katanga|Katanga]], [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and slaves with Portuguese from [[e:tete|Tete]] and Swahili-Arab merchants from the east coast. The Portuguese explorer [[e:francisco-de-lacerda-e-almeida|Francisco de Lacerda]] died there in 1798, and [[e:david-livingstone|Livingstone]] visited in 1867–68. The annual [[e:mutomboko|Mutomboko ceremony]] commemorates the conquest.
kingdom-of-kazembe.e: In the late 19th century [[e:msiri|Msiri's]] Yeke state took [[e:katanga|Katanga]] and Swahili-Arab traders eroded [[e:kazembe|Kazembe's]] power. [[e:british-south-africa-company|British South Africa Company]] forces occupied the capital in 1899, and the kingdom was absorbed into [[s:northern-rhodesia|Northern Rhodesia]]. The Mwata Kazembe remains a traditional ruler in [[e:zambia|Zambia]].

kingdom-of-germany.t: The German kingdom at the heart of the Holy Roman Empire, an elective monarchy whose kings claimed the imperial crown for more than eight centuries.
kingdom-of-germany.o: The kingdom grew out of [[s:east-francia|East Francia]]. Its kings, from [[e:henry-the-fowler|Henry the Fowler]] in 919, were elected by the great nobles. When [[e:otto-i|Otto I]] was crowned emperor in [[e:rome|Rome]] in 962, the German crown became joined with the imperial title and with kingship of [[e:italy|Italy]] and later [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Burgundy]], a link that defined the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]].
kingdom-of-germany.r: German kings were elected, from 1356 by the seven prince-[[e:prince-elector|electors]] under the [[e:golden-bull-of-1356|Golden Bull]], and crowned at [[s:free-imperial-city-of-aachen|Aachen]]. Royal power weakened during the Investiture Controversy and after the fall of the [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]], while princes, [[e:bishop|bishops]] and [[e:free-imperial-city|free cities]] gained autonomy. From 1438 the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] held the crown almost without break, governing with the [[e:imperial-diet|Imperial Diet]].
kingdom-of-germany.e: The [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] and [[e:thirty-tyrants|the Thirty]] Years' War, ended by the [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] in 1648, left [[e:germany|Germany]] a federation of nearly sovereign states. Under Napoleonic pressure, [[e:francis-ii|Francis II]] abdicated on 6 August 1806, dissolving the Empire and the German kingdom with it.
kingdom-of-germany.re: Catholic Christianity, Lutheranism and Calvinism after 1517

kingdom-of-hawaii.t: The island kingdom united by Kamehameha I, which became an internationally recognised constitutional monarchy before American businessmen overthrew it in 1893.
kingdom-of-hawaii.o: [[e:hawaii|Hawaii]] was divided among rival chiefdoms, including the [[s:chiefdom-of-hawaii-island|Chiefdom of Hawaii Island]], the [[s:chiefdom-of-maui|Chiefdom of Maui]] and the [[s:chiefdom-of-oahu|Chiefdom of Oahu]]. [[e:kamehameha-i|Kamehameha]], a chief from Hawaii Island armed with Western guns and advisers, conquered [[e:maui|Maui]] and won the [[e:battle-of-nuuanu|Battle of Nuʻuanu]] on [[e:oahu|Oahu]] in 1795. [[e:kauai|Kauaʻi]] accepted his overlordship peacefully in 1810, completing unification.
kingdom-of-hawaii.r: After [[e:kamehameha-i|Kamehameha]]'s death the kapu system was abolished in 1819, and American Protestant missionaries arrived in 1820. [[e:kamehameha-iii|Kamehameha III]] granted the first constitution in 1840 and the [[e:great-mahele|Great Māhele]] of 1848 created private land ownership, much of it soon held by foreigners. Sandalwood, whaling and then [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] drove the economy, and plantation labour brought Chinese, Japanese and Portuguese migrants. [[e:honolulu|Honolulu]] became the capital in 1845.
kingdom-of-hawaii.e: [[e:sugar-plantation|Sugar]] planters forced the [[e:bayonet-constitution|Bayonet Constitution]] on King [[e:kalakaua|Kalākaua]] in 1887. When Queen Liliʻuokalani sought a new constitution, a committee backed by [[e:united-states-marine-corps|US Marines]] overthrew her in January 1893 and set up the [[s:provisional-government-of-hawaii|Provisional Government of Hawaii]].

kamakura-shogunate.t: Japan's first warrior government, which ruled from Kamakura alongside the imperial court and twice repelled Mongol invasions.
kamakura-shogunate.o: After victory in the [[e:genpei-war|Genpei War]], [[e:minamoto-no-yoritomo|Minamoto no Yoritomo]] won the right in 1185 to appoint military governors (shugo) and estate stewards (jito) across [[e:japan|Japan]], creating a warrior administration based at [[e:kamakura|Kamakura]]. The court named him [[e:shogun|shogun]] in 1192.
kamakura-shogunate.r: After [[e:minamoto-no-yoritomo|Yoritomo's]] death power passed to the [[e:hojo-clan|Hojo]] family, who ruled as regents (shikken) for puppet [[e:shogun|shoguns]]. They defeated the retired emperor [[e:emperor-go-toba|Go-Toba]] in the [[e:jokyu-war|Jokyu War]] of 1221 and issued the Goseibai shikimoku law code in 1232 for warriors. Under [[e:hojo-tokimune|Hojo Tokimune]] the shogunate resisted Mongol invasions in 1274 and 1281. New Buddhist movements of [[e:honen|Honen]], [[e:shinran|Shinran]], [[e:nichiren|Nichiren]] and Zen spread widely.
kamakura-shogunate.e: The cost of the Mongol defence left warriors unrewarded and resentful. [[e:emperor-go-daigo|Emperor Go-Daigo]] rose against the [[e:hojo-clan|Hojo]], and in 1333 [[e:ashikaga-takauji|Ashikaga Takauji]] took [[e:kyoto|Kyoto]] while [[e:nitta-yoshisada|Nitta Yoshisada]] stormed [[e:kamakura|Kamakura]], ending the regime and opening the [[s:kenmu-restoration|Kenmu Restoration]].

kingdom-of-ulaid.t: The ancient over-kingdom of Ulster, linked in legend with Emain Macha and the Ulster Cycle, which shrank to Antrim and Down before the Anglo-Normans.
kingdom-of-ulaid.o: The Ulaid, probably Ptolemy's [[s:voluntii|Voluntii]], gave their name to [[s:northern-ireland|Ulster]]. Irish tradition remembers them as rulers of the whole north from [[e:emain-macha|Emain Macha]], Navan Fort near [[e:armagh|Armagh]], the setting of the [[e:ulster-cycle|Ulster Cycle]] tales of [[e:conchobar-mac-nessa|Conchobar mac Nessa]] and [[e:cu-chulainn|Cú Chulainn]]. In the 5th century, according to tradition, the [[e:three-collas|Three Collas]] and the [[e:ui-neill|Uí Néill]] drove them east of the [[e:river-bann|River Bann]].
kingdom-of-ulaid.r: In historic times the kingdom was an over-kingship shared between the [[s:dal-fiatach|Dal Fiatach]] of Down and the [[s:dal-naraidi|Dal nAraidi]] of [[e:county-antrim|Antrim]]. Kings such as [[e:baetan-mac-cairill|Báetán mac Cairill]] and [[e:congal-caech|Congal Cáech]] challenged the [[e:ui-neill|Uí Néill]], but defeat at [[e:battle-of-moira|Mag Rath]] in 637 ended their hopes of wider supremacy. The kingdom's monasteries, including [[e:bangor-abbey|Bangor]], [[e:movilla-abbey|Movilla]] and [[e:nendrum-monastery|Nendrum]], were among the great centres of early Irish learning.
kingdom-of-ulaid.e: [[e:vikings|Viking]] raids and [[e:ui-neill|Uí Néill]] pressure confined the Ulaid to [[e:county-antrim|Antrim]] and Down. In 1177 [[e:john-de-courcy|John de Courcy]] captured [[e:downpatrick|Downpatrick]] and defeated [[e:ruaidri-mac-duinn-sleibe|Ruaidrí Mac Duinn Sléibe]], and the Ulaid lands became the [[e:anglo-normans|Anglo-Norman]] [[s:earldom-of-ulster|Earldom of Ulster]].

kingdom-of-kartli.t: The central Georgian kingdom around Tbilisi, a Persian vassal for much of its history, which produced Georgia's first printing press and a famous law code.
kingdom-of-kartli.o: [[s:kingdom-of-iberia|Kartli]], the historic core of eastern [[s:georgia|Georgia]], emerged as a separate kingdom during the break-up of the [[s:kingdom-of-georgia|Kingdom of Georgia]] in the late 15th century. [[e:constantine-ii-of-georgia|Constantine II]], the last king to claim all [[e:georgia|Georgia]], was left by about 1490 with Kartli alone, and his descendants ruled it from [[e:tbilisi|Tbilisi]].
kingdom-of-kartli.r: [[s:kingdom-of-iberia|Kartli]] lay on the front line between the Ottoman and Safavid empires and was usually a Safavid [[e:vassal|vassal]]; several kings, such as [[e:rostom-of-kartli|Rostom]], converted to [[e:islam|Islam]] to hold the throne. [[e:simon-i-of-kartli|Simon I]] fought both empires and died an Ottoman captive. [[e:vakhtang-vi-of-kartli|Vakhtang VI]], regent and king in the early 18th century, compiled a law code, edited the Georgian chronicles and set up a [[e:printing-press|printing]] press in [[e:tbilisi|Tbilisi]] in 1709.
kingdom-of-kartli.e: After [[e:vakhtang-vi-of-kartli|Vakhtang VI]] sought Russian help and fled to [[e:russia|Russia]] in 1724, the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] occupied [[s:kingdom-of-iberia|Kartli]] until 1735. [[e:teimuraz-ii-of-kakheti|Teimuraz II]] regained the throne in 1744, and on his death in 1762 his son [[e:erekle-ii|Erekle II]] united Kartli with [[s:kingdom-of-kakheti|Kakheti]].

kingdom-of-mercia.t: The great midland kingdom that dominated England in the 8th century under Aethelbald and Offa, whose Dyke still marks the Welsh border.
kingdom-of-mercia.o: Mercia, the 'border people', arose among [[e:angles|Angles]] in the upper [[e:river-trent|Trent]] valley. Later genealogies place its first kings, [[e:icel|Icel]] and [[e:creoda-of-mercia|Creoda]], in the 6th century, but the first well-attested ruler is the pagan [[e:penda-of-mercia|Penda]], who fought [[s:kingdom-of-northumbria|Northumbria]] and [[s:kingdom-of-east-anglia|East Anglia]] from the 620s to his death at the [[e:battle-of-the-winwaed|Winwaed]] in 655.
kingdom-of-mercia.r: Mercian kings ruled from [[e:tamworth|Tamworth]], with a bishopric at [[e:lichfield|Lichfield]], and dominated client kingdoms such as the [[s:kingdom-of-the-hwicce|Hwicce]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-the-magonsaete|Magonsaete]]. [[e:offa-of-mercia|Offa]] took the title king of the English, issued a reformed [[e:silver|silver]] penny, corresponded with [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]] and built [[e:offas-dyke|Offa's Dyke]]. He briefly created an archbishopric at Lichfield.
kingdom-of-mercia.e: Defeat by [[s:kingdom-of-wessex|Wessex]] at [[e:battle-of-ellendun|Ellendun]] in 825 and the [[e:vikings|Viking]] conquests of the 870s split Mercia. Its western half, under [[e:aethelred-lord-of-the-mercians|Aethelred]] and [[e:aethelflaed|Aethelflaed]], the Lady of the Mercians, allied with [[e:wessex|Wessex]]. After Aethelflaed's death in 918 it was absorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-the-anglo-saxons|Kingdom of the Anglo-Saxons]].

kingdom-of-finland-1918.t: The short-lived attempt to make independent Finland a monarchy under a German prince, abandoned when Germany lost the First World War.
kingdom-of-finland-1918.o: After the civil war, conservative politicians wanted a strong monarchy tied to [[e:germany|Germany]], whose troops had helped the Whites win. On 9 October 1918 a rump parliament, without the Social Democrats, elected [[e:prince-frederick-charles-of-hesse|Prince Frederick Charles of Hesse]] as king of [[s:republic-of-finland|Finland]]. [[e:pehr-evind-svinhufvud|Pehr Evind Svinhufvud]] served as regent.
kingdom-of-finland-1918.r: The kingdom existed largely on paper. [[e:prince-frederick-charles-of-hesse|Frederick Charles]] never came to [[s:republic-of-finland|Finland]], and no coronation took place. German influence over the army and the economy was strong, and the monarchists hoped the throne would secure German protection against [[s:russian-sfsr|Soviet Russia]].
kingdom-of-finland-1918.e: [[e:germany|Germany's]] defeat in November 1918 made a German king impossible. [[e:prince-frederick-charles-of-hesse|Frederick Charles]] renounced the throne on 14 December 1918, and [[e:carl-gustaf-emil-mannerheim|Mannerheim]] replaced [[e:pehr-evind-svinhufvud|Svinhufvud]] as regent. The constitution of 1919 created the [[s:republic-of-finland|Republic of Finland]], and the monarchy project was abandoned.

katsina-emirate.t: The emirate that replaced the Hausa kingdom of Katsina after the jihad, ruled by Fulani emirs while the old dynasty carried on at Maradi.
katsina-emirate.o: In 1807 the [[e:fula|Fulani]] scholar [[e:umaru-dallaji|Umaru Dallaji]], a follower of [[e:usman-dan-fodio|Usman dan Fodio]], captured [[s:katsina-kingdom|Katsina]] from the [[e:hausa|Hausa]] ruler, who fled north and eventually founded the [[s:sultanate-of-maradi|Sultanate of Maradi]]. Dallaji became the first emir and founded the dynasty that ruled until the colonial period.
katsina-emirate.r: [[s:katsina-kingdom|Katsina]] had been the leading commercial and scholarly city of [[s:hausa-kingdoms|Hausaland]], but war with [[s:sultanate-of-maradi|Maradi]] and the rise of [[e:kano|Kano]] drew trade away during the 19th century. The emir governed with titled officials, many offices inherited from the Katsina Kingdom, and the [[e:emirate|emirate]] remained a frontier power, constantly raided by the [[e:hausa|Hausa]] exiles to the north. Islamic scholarship continued in its mosques and schools.
katsina-emirate.e: British forces occupied [[s:katsina-kingdom|Katsina]] in 1903. In 1906 the British deposed the emir and appointed [[e:muhammadu-dikko|Muhammadu Dikko]], founder of the Sullubawa dynasty, which still reigns. The northern part of the old kingdom lies in [[e:niger-river|Niger]].

kingdom-of-ouagadougou.t: The leading Mossi kingdom, whose ruler the Mogho Naaba still holds court in the capital of Burkina Faso.
kingdom-of-ouagadougou.o: [[e:mossi|Mossi]] tradition credits Oubri, a grandson of [[e:ouedraogo|Ouedraogo]], with founding the kingdom of Ouagadougou around 1495 by subduing the local farming peoples of the [[e:white-volta|White Volta]] basin. Successive rulers extended its authority, and it became the largest of the Mossi states alongside the [[s:kingdom-of-yatenga|Kingdom of Yatenga]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-tenkodogo|Kingdom of Tenkodogo]].
kingdom-of-ouagadougou.r: The [[e:mogho-naba|Mogho Naaba]], 'ruler of the world', governed through ministers, provincial chiefs and a court of pages and royal servants. [[e:mossi|Mossi]] cavalry resisted the [[s:mali-empire|Mali Empire]] and the [[s:songhai-empire|Songhai Empire]], whose ruler [[e:askia-muhammad|Askia Muhammad]] attacked them in 1497. Mossi religion and earth-priests remained strong, and [[e:islam|Islam]] made only limited progress before the 19th century.
kingdom-of-ouagadougou.e: In 1896 French forces took Ouagadougou, and [[e:mogho-naaba-wobgo|Mogho Naaba Wobgo]] fled. The kingdom became part of [[s:french-west-africa|French West Africa]], and Ouagadougou the capital of [[s:french-upper-volta|French Upper Volta]] and later [[e:burkina-faso|Burkina Faso]]. The [[e:mogho-naba|Mogho Naaba]] still reigns as a respected traditional ruler.

kingdom-of-koki.t: A small kingdom west of Lake Victoria, founded by a prince of Bunyoro and absorbed into Buganda in 1896.
kingdom-of-koki.o: Tradition says Koki was founded around 1740 by Bwohe, a prince of the [[s:kingdom-of-bunyoro|Kingdom of Bunyoro]], who settled in the lands west of [[e:lake-victoria|Lake Victoria]] in today's Rakai district. It lay between [[s:kingdom-of-buganda|Buganda]], [[s:kingdom-of-ankole|Ankole]] and the [[e:haya-people|Haya]] kingdoms.
kingdom-of-koki.r: Koki was a small farming and [[e:cattle|cattle]]-keeping kingdom, ruled by a king, or kamuswaga, through chiefs. From around 1800 it paid tribute to the [[s:kingdom-of-buganda|Kingdom of Buganda]] while keeping its own dynasty, and it took part in the trade in [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and iron goods around the lake.
kingdom-of-koki.e: In 1896 Koki's ruler agreed to incorporation into [[s:kingdom-of-buganda|Buganda]], and it became a county of the kingdom under the [[s:uganda-protectorate|Uganda Protectorate]], its ruler keeping the title kamuswaga. It remains part of the Buganda region today.

kingdom-of-raiatea.t: The sacred island kingdom of the Society Islands, home of the great marae of Taputapuatea, whose people fought French annexation until 1897.
kingdom-of-raiatea.o: Raiatea, called Havaiʻi in older traditions, was a religious and voyaging centre of eastern [[e:polynesia|Polynesia]], and its marae of [[e:taputapuatea|Taputapuatea]] at Opoa drew chiefs from across the region. The cult of the war god [[e:oro|ʻOro]] spread from there. By the 18th century the high chiefs of the Tamatoa line ruled Raiatea and neighbouring [[e:tahaa|Tahaʻa]], though warriors from [[e:bora-bora|Bora Bora]] conquered the island around the 1760s.
kingdom-of-raiatea.r: Kings ruled through a chiefly hierarchy, with priests of [[e:oro|ʻOro]] wielding great influence. The priest-navigator [[e:tupaia|Tupaia]], who sailed with [[e:james-cook|James Cook]] in 1769, came from Raiatea. Missionaries of the [[e:london-missionary-society|London Missionary Society]] arrived in 1818, [[e:christianity|Christianity]] spread quickly, and the kingdom adopted written law codes. Breadfruit, coconut and fishing sustained the islanders, and Raiatea traded with visiting ships.
kingdom-of-raiatea.e: The [[e:jarnac-convention|Jarnac Convention]] of 1847 between [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and [[e:france|France]] guaranteed the independence of the [[e:leeward-islands-society-islands|Leeward Islands]]. France annexed Raiatea in 1888, but a resistance led by the chief [[e:teraupoo|Teraupoʻo]] lasted until 1897. The island became part of [[s:french-polynesia|French Polynesia]], and [[e:taputapuatea|Taputapuatea]] is a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]].

kingdom-of-lindsey.t: A small Anglian kingdom in north Lincolnshire centred on Roman Lincoln, briefly fought over by Northumbria and Mercia before Mercian absorption.
kingdom-of-lindsey.o: Lindsey took its name from the Roman [[e:lindum-colonia|Lindum]] ([[e:lincoln-england|Lincoln]]), and Anglian settlers established a kingdom there in the late 5th or 6th century. A list of its kings survives in a collection of royal genealogies, tracing them to [[e:woden|Woden]], ending with [[e:aldfrith-of-lindsey|Aldfrith]] in the late 8th century.
kingdom-of-lindsey.r: The kingdom lay between the [[e:humber|Humber]] and the [[e:river-witham|Witham]], bounded by fen and sea, and was too small to stand alone. [[e:paulinus-of-york|Paulinus]] preached at [[e:lincoln-england|Lincoln]] around 628 under Northumbrian protection, building a stone church. A separate bishopric of Lindsey was founded in 678.
kingdom-of-lindsey.e: [[s:kingdom-of-northumbria|Northumbria]] and [[s:kingdom-of-mercia|Mercia]] contested Lindsey until the [[e:battle-of-the-trent|Battle of the Trent]] in 679 left it permanently Mercian. Its kings faded into dependent rulers and disappeared by about 800. The district was later settled by [[e:danes|Danes]] and formed part of [[e:lincolnshire|Lincolnshire]].

khandesh-sultanate.t: A small sultanate of the Tapti valley ruled by the Faruqi dynasty from Burhanpur and the great fortress of Asirgarh.
khandesh-sultanate.o: [[e:malik-raja-faruqi|Malik Raja Faruqi]], a noble granted lands in the Tapti valley by [[e:firuz-shah-tughluq|Firuz Shah Tughluq]] of the [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]], became effectively independent around 1382 as [[e:delhi|Delhi's]] authority collapsed. His son [[e:nasir-khan-faruqi|Nasir Khan]] took the fortress of [[e:asirgarh-fort|Asirgarh]] and founded the city of [[e:burhanpur|Burhanpur]], which became the capital of the Faruqi kingdom.
khandesh-sultanate.r: [[e:khandesh|Khandesh]] was a buffer state between the larger [[s:gujarat-sultanate|Gujarat Sultanate]], [[s:malwa-sultanate|Malwa Sultanate]] and the [[e:deccan-sultanates|Deccan sultanates]], and its rulers survived by shifting alliances and marriages. [[e:burhanpur|Burhanpur]] grew into a busy centre of [[e:cotton|cotton]] textiles and trade on the route between north [[e:india|India]] and the [[e:deccan|Deccan]]. The Faruqis built mosques, including the [[e:jama-masjid-burhanpur|Jama Masjid of Burhanpur]].
khandesh-sultanate.e: [[e:akbar|Akbar]] of the [[s:mughal-empire|Mughal Empire]] demanded submission, and when [[e:bahadur-shah-faruqi|Bahadur Shah Faruqi]] resisted, Mughal armies besieged [[e:asirgarh-fort|Asirgarh]], which surrendered in 1601. [[e:khandesh|Khandesh]] became a Mughal province, and [[e:burhanpur|Burhanpur]] served as a base for Mughal campaigns in the [[e:deccan|Deccan]].

kingdom-of-paeonia.t: Ancient kingdom of the Axios (Vardar) valley north of Macedon, whose kings minted fine silver coins before falling under Macedonian control.
kingdom-of-paeonia.o: The Paeonians held the [[e:vardar|Axios]] and [[e:struma|Strymon]] valleys from early times; [[e:homer|Homer]] lists them as allies of [[e:troy|Troy]]. In 511 BCE the Persian general [[e:megabazus|Megabazus]] deported many of them to Asia. A kingdom with its own coinage emerged in the 4th century BCE, centred on [[e:bylazora|Bylazora]] and [[e:stip|Astibos]] (Štip).
kingdom-of-paeonia.r: Kings such as [[e:lyppeios|Lyppeios]], [[e:patraos|Patraos]] and [[e:audoleon|Audoleon]] issued [[e:silver|silver]] coins showing [[e:apollo|Apollo]] and horsemen, and Audoleon was honoured at [[s:athens|Athens]]. The economy rested on herding, farming and the trade route along the [[e:vardar|Axios]]. The Paeonians worshipped the sun and a [[e:dionysus|Dionysus]] called Dyalos, and were famed riders. [[e:philip-ii-of-macedon|Philip II of Macedon]] forced them into dependency after 358 BCE, and they served in Alexander's army.
kingdom-of-paeonia.e: Celtic invasions in 279 BCE weakened the kingdom. In 217 BCE [[e:philip-v-of-macedon|Philip V of Macedon]] took [[e:bylazora|Bylazora]], ending its independence, and after 168 BCE Paeonia became part of [[e:macedonia-roman-province|Roman Macedonia]].

kingdom-of-hejaz.t: The Hashemite kingdom proclaimed by Sharif Hussein during the Arab Revolt, which held Mecca and Medina until conquered by Ibn Saud.
kingdom-of-hejaz.o: In June 1916 [[e:hussein-bin-ali-king-of-hejaz|Hussein ibn Ali]], head of the [[s:sharifate-of-mecca|Sharifate of Mecca]], launched the Arab Revolt against the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]] with British support, encouraged by the [[e:mcmahon-hussein-correspondence|Hussein-McMahon correspondence]]. He proclaimed himself King of the Arab Lands; the [[e:allies|Allies]] recognised him as King of the [[e:hejaz|Hejaz]]. His sons Faisal and Abdullah led Arab forces north.
kingdom-of-hejaz.r: The kingdom controlled the [[e:hejaz|Hejaz]], its holy cities, the pilgrimage and the port of [[e:jeddah|Jeddah]], financed largely by British [[e:subsidy|subsidies]] and pilgrim fees. [[e:hussein-bin-ali-king-of-hejaz|Hussein]] refused to accept the post-war [[e:league-of-nations-mandate|mandates]] in [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]], [[e:palestine|Palestine]] and [[e:iraq|Iraq]], quarrelled with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and declined to sign the [[e:treaty-of-versailles|Treaty of Versailles]]. In March 1924, after [[e:turkey|Turkey]] abolished the [[e:caliphate|caliphate]], he declared himself caliph.
kingdom-of-hejaz.e: [[e:ibn-saud|Ibn Saud's]] Ikhwan took [[e:taif|Ta'if]] and then [[e:mecca|Mecca]] in late 1924. [[e:hussein-bin-ali-king-of-hejaz|Hussein]] abdicated in favour of his son Ali, who surrendered [[e:jeddah|Jeddah]] in December 1925. The [[e:hejaz|Hejaz]] became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-hejaz-and-nejd|Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd]], while Hussein's sons ruled the [[s:kingdom-of-iraq|Kingdom of Iraq]] and the [[s:emirate-of-transjordan|Emirate of Transjordan]].

kingdom-of-kurdistan.t: A short-lived Kurdish kingdom proclaimed at Sulaymaniyah by Sheikh Mahmud Barzanji in defiance of British plans for Iraq.
kingdom-of-kurdistan.o: [[e:mahmud-barzanji|Sheikh Mahmud Barzanji]], a [[e:sufism|Sufi]] leader of the Qadiri order and notable of [[e:sulaymaniyah|Sulaymaniyah]], was appointed governor by the British in 1918. He rebelled in 1919, was defeated and exiled to [[e:india|India]]. In 1922, with Turkish forces threatening the [[e:mosul|Mosul]] region, the British brought him back to restore order, and in November 1922 he proclaimed himself King of [[e:kurdistan|Kurdistan]].
kingdom-of-kurdistan.r: The kingdom had a cabinet, issued stamps and a newspaper, and claimed authority over the Kurdish districts around [[e:sulaymaniyah|Sulaymaniyah]], but its administration was rudimentary and depended on tribal support. Mahmud negotiated with [[e:turkey|Turkey]] while the British sought to include the region in the new Iraqi state. The [[e:royal-air-force|Royal Air Force]] bombed Sulaymaniyah in 1923, one of the first uses of air power to police a colonial territory.
kingdom-of-kurdistan.e: British and Iraqi forces took [[e:sulaymaniyah|Sulaymaniyah]] in 1924, and the region was incorporated into [[s:mandatory-iraq|Mandatory Iraq]]. Sheikh Mahmud led further revolts until 1931 and remains a symbol of Kurdish nationalism.

kingdom-of-hengshan.t: Wu Rui's kingdom in the middle Yangtze, created by Xiang Yu in 206 BCE, whose ruler switched to Liu Bang and became the first King of Changsha.
kingdom-of-hengshan.o: [[e:wu-rui|Wu Rui]], a [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] magistrate of Po county who was popular with the Yue peoples, joined the rebellion against the [[s:qin-dynasty|Qin dynasty]] and sent troops with his son-in-law [[e:ying-bu|Ying Bu]]. In 206 BCE [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]] made him King of Hengshan, with his capital at Zhu near modern [[e:huanggang|Huanggang]] in [[e:hubei|Hubei]].
kingdom-of-hengshan.r: Hengshan straddled the [[e:yangtze-river|Yangtze]] east of the [[s:kingdom-of-linjiang|Kingdom of Linjiang]], controlling [[e:rice|rice]] lands and river trade. [[e:wu-rui|Wu Rui's]] support among the [[e:baiyue|Baiyue]] peoples of the south gave him a following beyond the Chinese population.
kingdom-of-hengshan.e: [[e:wu-rui|Wu Rui]] supported [[e:liu-bang|Liu Bang]] against [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]], and after the Han victory in 202 BCE he was moved to become King of [[e:changsha|Changsha]]. His family held Changsha until 157 BCE, one of the few non-Liu kingdoms to survive under the [[s:han-dynasty|Han Dynasty]].

kingdom-of-cilicia.t: Cilicia, a vassal kingdom of the Syennesis dynasty at Tarsus that kept its own kings under Persia until 401 BCE.
kingdom-of-cilicia.o: After the fall of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]], local rulers in the Cilician plain and [[s:hilakku|Rough Cilicia]] formed a kingdom with [[e:tarsus|Tarsus]] as its capital, drawing on the lands of Que and Hilakku. Babylonian records call part of it Pirindu, and [[e:neriglissar|Neriglissar]] of the [[s:chaldean-empire|Chaldean Empire]] fought its king [[e:appuashu|Appuashu]] in 557 BCE.
kingdom-of-cilicia.r: Its kings bore the title or name [[e:syennesis|Syennesis]]. One Syennesis mediated, with a Babylonian envoy, the peace between [[s:kingdom-of-lydia|Lydia]] and the [[s:median-empire|Median Empire]] after the eclipse battle of 585 BCE. Under the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]] the kingdom kept its own rulers, paid tribute in [[e:silver|silver]] and white horses and supplied ships to the Persian fleet.
kingdom-of-cilicia.e: In 401 BCE [[e:syennesis|Syennesis]] and his wife [[e:epyaxa|Epyaxa]] supported [[e:cyrus-the-younger|Cyrus the Younger]] in his revolt. After its failure the [[e:persians|Persians]] abolished the kingship and turned [[e:cilicia|Cilicia]] into an ordinary [[e:satrapy|satrapy]].

kingdom-of-gampola.t: The Sinhalese kingdom of the central hills, under which Buddhist temple architecture flourished and the Alakeshvara family rose to power.
kingdom-of-gampola.o: [[e:bhuvanaikabahu-iv|Bhuvanaikabahu IV]] moved the royal seat from [[e:kurunegala|Kurunegala]] to Gampola, on the Mahaweli river in the central highlands, around 1341. The move followed the drift of Sinhalese power away from the northern plains after the fall of the [[s:kingdom-of-dambadeniya|Kingdom of Dambadeniya]] and the pressure of the [[s:jaffna-kingdom|Jaffna Kingdom]].
kingdom-of-gampola.r: The Gampola kings were weak, and real power lay with ministers, above all the [[e:alagakkonara-family|Alakeshvara]] family, who built a fortress at [[s:kingdom-of-kotte|Kotte]] near [[e:colombo|Colombo]] and resisted [[e:jaffna|Jaffna's]] expansion. The period produced fine Buddhist monuments, notably the [[e:gadaladeniya-vihara|Gadaladeniya]] and [[e:lankatilaka-vihara|Lankatilaka]] temples, which blend Sinhalese and south Indian styles. Contacts with the [[s:vijayanagara-empire|Vijayanagara Empire]] increased.
kingdom-of-gampola.e: In 1411 the Chinese admiral [[e:zheng-he|Zheng He]] fought and captured the ruler [[e:vira-alakeshvara|Vira Alakeshvara]] and took him to [[e:china|China]]. Soon afterwards [[e:parakramabahu-vi|Parakramabahu VI]] took power and moved the capital to [[s:kingdom-of-kotte|Kotte]], founding the Kingdom of [[e:sri-jayawardenepura-kotte|Kotte]] in 1412.
