kingdom-of-castile.t: The medieval kingdom of Castile, which took Toledo, crushed the Almohads at Las Navas de Tolosa and became the dominant power of Christian Iberia.
kingdom-of-castile.o: Ferdinand I, count of Castile and from 1037 king of León, is traditionally counted as the first king of Castile. At his death in 1065 he divided his realms, leaving Castile to his eldest son [[e:sancho-ii-of-castile|Sancho II]]. After Sancho's murder in 1072 his brother [[e:alfonso-vi-of-castile|Alfonso VI]] reunited [[s:crown-of-castile|Castile and León]].
kingdom-of-castile.r: Castile was a frontier society of free settlers, town councils with their own fueros and mounted warriors, later organised in military orders such as [[e:order-of-calatrava|Calatrava]] and [[s:spanish-jamaica|Santiago]]. [[e:alfonso-vi-of-castile|Alfonso VI]] took [[e:toledo|Toledo]] in 1085. [[e:alfonso-viii|Alfonso VIII]], defeated at [[e:battle-of-alarcos|Alarcos]] in 1195, led the coalition that destroyed the [[e:almohad-caliphate|Almohad]] army at [[e:battle-of-las-navas-de-tolosa|Las Navas de Tolosa]] in 1212. [[e:burgos|Burgos]], on the pilgrim road to [[e:santiago|Santiago]], prospered on trade and wool.
kingdom-of-castile.e: [[s:crown-of-castile|Castile and León]] were separated again from 1157, but in 1230 Ferdinand III, already king of Castile, inherited León, creating the lasting union known as the Crown of Castile, which absorbed most of [[e:al-andalus|al-Andalus]] within a generation.

karamanli-tripoli.t: The hereditary Karamanli pashas of Tripoli, a corsair dynasty best known for fighting the United States in the First Barbary War.
karamanli-tripoli.o: In 1711 [[e:ahmed-karamanli|Ahmed Karamanli]], a cavalry officer of mixed Turkish and local descent, seized power in [[s:county-of-tripoli|Tripoli]], massacred his [[e:janissaries|Janissary]] rivals and founded a dynasty. The Ottoman sultan recognised him as pasha, and [[s:ottoman-tripolitania|Ottoman Tripolitania]] became a hereditary, largely autonomous state.
karamanli-tripoli.r: The Karamanli pashas lived from corsairing, tribute from European powers and the trans-Saharan trade through the [[s:sultanate-of-fezzan|Fezzan]], which [[e:yusuf-karamanli|Yusuf Karamanli]] annexed in 1812. Yusuf, who ruled from 1795, declared war on the [[s:united-states|United States]] in 1801; the frigate [[e:philadelphia|Philadelphia]] was captured, and American forces took [[e:derna|Derna]] in 1805 before a peace treaty.
karamanli-tripoli.e: After European pressure ended corsairing and tribute, debts mounted and civil war broke out in 1832. In 1835 the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] sent a fleet, deposed the last Karamanli and restored direct rule as the [[s:tripolitania-vilayet|Tripolitania Vilayet]].

khanate-of-maku.t: The longest-lived of the Azerbaijani khanates: a mountain domain on the Ottoman and Russian borders whose khans kept local power until 1922.
khanate-of-maku.o: [[e:maku|Maku]], a town built under a cliff in the far north-west of [[e:iran|Iran]] near [[e:mount-ararat|Mount Ararat]], came under the hereditary khans of the Turkic [[e:bayat-tribe|Bayat]] clan after the death of [[e:nader-shah|Nader Shah]] in 1747. Its strategic position on the routes to the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]] and the [[e:caucasus|Caucasus]] gave it importance beyond its size.
khanate-of-maku.r: Unlike most khanates of [[s:azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]], [[e:maku|Maku]] kept its own khans under [[s:qajar-iran|Qajar Iran]], which treated them as hereditary governors of a frontier district. They controlled tribes, customs posts and border trade. In the early 20th century Morteza Qoli Khan, known as Eqbal al-Saltaneh, was one of the richest and most powerful men in north-western [[e:iran|Iran]], opposing the constitutionalists of [[e:tabriz|Tabriz]].
khanate-of-maku.e: After the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]], [[e:reza-shah|Reza Khan's]] government reasserted central control, and in 1922 Eqbal al-Saltaneh lost his position; he died in detention soon after. [[e:maku|Maku]] was integrated into the provincial system of [[s:pahlavi-iran|Pahlavi Iran]].

kingdom-of-palpa.t: A Sen hill kingdom of western Nepal ruled from Tansen, once the most powerful of the Chaubise Rajya before falling to Gorkha.
kingdom-of-palpa.o: The Sen dynasty, claiming [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] descent, established itself in the hills of Palpa in the late 15th century; [[e:mukunda-sen|Mukunda Sen]] is the best-known early ruler. He is said to have campaigned as far as the [[e:kathmandu-valley|Kathmandu Valley]], and his realm, centred on [[e:tansen-nepal|Tansen]], was later divided among his sons into Palpa, the [[s:kingdom-of-makwanpur|Kingdom of Makwanpur]] and other states.
kingdom-of-palpa.r: Palpa was the leading state of the [[e:chaubise-rajya|Chaubise Rajya]], the twenty-four hill principalities of central [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Nepal]], and controlled trade routes from the Gangetic plain into the hills. Its kings intermarried with the [[s:gorkha-kingdom|Gorkha]] and [[s:kingdom-of-tanahun|Tanahun]] royal families, and the town of [[e:tansen-nepal|Tansen]] developed [[e:newar-people|Newar]] trading communities and temples.
kingdom-of-palpa.e: Palpa resisted the [[s:gorkha-kingdom|Gorkha]] unification for decades, relying on marriage alliances with the Gorkha court and on its hill fortresses. It was finally annexed by the [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Kingdom of Nepal]] in 1806, and its last king, [[e:prithvipal-sen|Prithvipal Sen]], was killed in [[e:kathmandu|Kathmandu]].

kyrgyzstan.t: A mountainous Central Asian republic, once called an 'island of democracy', whose politics have been shaped by three popular revolutions.
kyrgyzstan.o: The [[s:kirghiz-ssr|Kirghiz SSR]] declared independence on 31 August 1991 under [[e:askar-akayev|Askar Akayev]], a physicist and reformer who had been elected president in 1990. The new state adopted a constitution in 1993 and its own currency, the som.
kyrgyzstan.r: [[e:askar-akayev|Akayev]]'s early liberal reforms gave way to corruption and family rule. The economy relies on the [[e:kumtor-gold-mine|Kumtor]] gold mine, agriculture and remittances from migrants in [[e:russia|Russia]]. Divisions between the north and the south around Osh and [[e:jalal-abad|Jalal-Abad]] have shaped politics, and in 2010 ethnic violence between [[e:kyrgyz-people|Kyrgyz]] and [[e:uzbeks|Uzbeks]] in Osh killed hundreds. Russia kept an airbase at [[e:kant-kyrgyzstan|Kant]], while a US base at Manas operated until 2014.
kyrgyzstan.e: Protests overthrew [[e:askar-akayev|Akayev]] in the [[e:tulip-revolution|Tulip Revolution]] of 2005 and his successor [[e:kurmanbek-bakiyev|Kurmanbek Bakiyev]] in 2010, after which a parliamentary system was briefly adopted. After unrest in 2020 [[e:sadyr-japarov|Sadyr Japarov]] became president and restored strong presidential rule by referendum in 2021.

katsina-kingdom.t: Hausa kingdom that became the leading commercial and scholarly city of Hausaland in the 17th and 18th centuries.
katsina-kingdom.o: Katsina was one of the [[s:hausa-kingdoms|Hausa Bakwai]], the seven core [[e:hausa|Hausa states]]. Tradition says [[e:muhammadu-korau|Korau]], a wrestler and newcomer, killed Sanau, the last ruler of the earlier Durbawa line, and founded a new dynasty in the 14th century. Muhammadu Korau, remembered as the first Muslim king and dated to the second half of the 15th century, is often identified with this founder, so the early chronology is uncertain.
katsina-kingdom.r: Katsina stood at the southern end of a major trans-Saharan route through [[s:sultanate-of-agadez|Agadez]] and became a centre of trade in cloth, leather, slaves and kola, and of Islamic learning, with scholars teaching at the [[e:gobarau-minaret|Gobarau]] mosque. It fought long wars with [[e:kano|Kano]] and acknowledged at times the [[s:kanem-bornu-empire|Kanem-Bornu Empire]] and the [[s:songhai-empire|Songhai Empire]].
katsina-kingdom.e: In 1807 the [[e:fula|Fulani]] jihadist [[e:umaru-dallaji|Umaru Dallaji]] captured the city, and Katsina became the [[s:katsina-emirate|Katsina Emirate]] within the [[s:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto Caliphate]]. The [[e:hausa|Hausa]] royal family withdrew north and founded the [[s:sultanate-of-maradi|Sultanate of Maradi]], now in [[e:niger-river|Niger]].

kingdom-of-zamfara.t: Hausa kingdom of the north-western plains that rose to power in the 16th and 17th centuries before being destroyed by its rival Gobir.
kingdom-of-zamfara.o: Zamfara was counted among the [[e:banza-bakwai|Banza Bakwai]], the 'illegitimate' [[e:hausa|Hausa states]] outside the core seven. Its people occupied the fertile valley of the Zamfara river west of [[s:katsina-kingdom|Katsina]]. Tradition dates its first rulers to around 1200, though the kingdom becomes visible in records only in the 16th century.
kingdom-of-zamfara.r: From its capital at [[e:birnin-zamfara|Birnin Zamfara]] the kingdom expanded in the 17th century, raiding as far as [[e:kano|Kano]] and controlling routes between [[s:hausa-kingdoms|Hausaland]] and the [[e:niger-river|Niger]]. Its rulers combined [[e:islam|Islam]] with [[e:hausa|Hausa]] royal rites, and the state's power rested on cavalry and slave labour on its farms.
kingdom-of-zamfara.e: In 1762 [[s:kingdom-of-gobir|Gobir]] under Babari sacked [[e:birnin-zamfara|Birnin Zamfara]] and occupied much of its land. The surviving Zamfara state, based at Anka, was conquered in the [[e:fulani-war|Fulani jihad]] around 1808 and came under the [[s:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto Caliphate]]. Its name lives on in [[e:zamfara-state|Zamfara State]], [[e:nigeria|Nigeria]].

kingdom-of-pergamon.t: Hellenistic kingdom of the Attalid dynasty in western Anatolia, a great centre of art and learning that was bequeathed to Rome in 133 BCE.
kingdom-of-pergamon.o: [[e:philetaerus|Philetaerus]], an officer guarding [[e:lysimachus|Lysimachus]]' treasure of 9,000 [[e:talent|talents]] at the citadel of [[e:pergamon|Pergamon]], changed sides to [[e:seleucus-i-nicator|Seleucus I]] in 282 BCE and kept the fortress and money. His nephew [[e:eumenes-i|Eumenes I]] asserted independence from the [[e:seleucid-empire|Seleucids]]. [[e:attalus-i|Attalus I]] took the title of king around 238 BCE after defeating the [[s:galatia|Galatians]].
kingdom-of-pergamon.r: The [[e:attalid-dynasty|Attalids]] built [[e:pergamon|Pergamon]] into a showpiece capital of terraces, temples and [[e:theatre|theatre]], with a library second only to [[e:alexandria|Alexandria's]], traditionally linked to the development of parchment. The [[e:pergamon-altar|Great Altar of Zeus]] celebrated victory over the [[s:galatia|Galatians]]. Loyal alliance with [[e:rome|Rome]] brought [[e:eumenes-ii|Eumenes II]] wide lands in [[e:asia-minor|Asia Minor]] after the [[e:treaty-of-apamea|Peace of Apamea]] in 188 BCE.
kingdom-of-pergamon.e: [[e:attalus-iii|Attalus III]] died in 133 BCE leaving his kingdom to [[e:rome|Rome]]. [[e:aristonicus|Aristonicus]], claiming to be a royal son, led a revolt that was crushed by 129 BCE, and the kingdom became the Roman province of Asia. The [[e:pergamon-altar|Pergamon Altar]] is now in [[e:berlin|Berlin]].

kingdom-of-italy-napoleonic.t: Napoleon's Kingdom of Italy, ruled from Milan by his stepson Eugène de Beauharnais, which gave northern Italians a modern state and a common army.
kingdom-of-italy-napoleonic.o: When [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] became emperor of the French, the [[s:italian-republic-1802-1805|Italian Republic]] (1802–1805) was turned into a kingdom. On 26 May 1805 Napoleon crowned himself king of [[e:italy|Italy]] in [[e:milan-cathedral|Milan Cathedral]] with the [[e:iron-crown-of-lombardy|Iron Crown of Lombardy]], and appointed his stepson [[e:eugene-de-beauharnais|Eugène de Beauharnais]] as [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]].
kingdom-of-italy-napoleonic.r: The kingdom grew to include [[e:venetia|Venetia]] in 1806, the [[e:marche|Marche]] in 1808 and [[e:south-tyrol|South Tyrol]] in 1810, and for a time [[s:histria|Istria]] and [[e:dalmatia|Dalmatia]], which passed to the [[s:illyrian-provinces|Illyrian Provinces]] in 1809. It had [[e:departement|departments]] and [[e:prefect|prefects]] on the French model, the [[e:napoleonic-code|Napoleonic Code]], public schools and an efficient tax system. Its [[e:conscription|conscript]] army fought in [[e:spain|Spain]] and [[e:russia|Russia]], where tens of thousands died in 1812.
kingdom-of-italy-napoleonic.e: After [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] defeats, [[e:eugene-de-beauharnais|Eugène]] signed an armistice in April 1814. A riot in [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]] killed the finance minister [[e:giuseppe-prina|Giuseppe Prina]], and Austrian troops took over; the territory became the [[s:kingdom-of-lombardy-venetia|Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia]] and other restored states.

kingdom-of-main.t: The Minaean kingdom of al-Jawf, whose merchants ran the incense trade from Yemen to Egypt and even the Greek island of Delos.
kingdom-of-main.o: Ma'in arose in the al-[[e:al-jawf-yemen|Jawf]] valley north of [[e:marib|Marib]], in a region of city-states once subject to the [[s:kingdom-of-saba|Kingdom of Saba]]. By the 6th or 5th century BCE it was independent, its kings ruling from [[e:qarnawu|Qarnawu]] with [[e:baraqish|Yathill]] (Baraqish) as a second major city.
kingdom-of-main.r: Ma'in was above all a trading state. Minaean merchants organised [[e:incense|incense]] caravans to [[s:gaza|Gaza]] and [[e:egypt|Egypt]], kept a colony at [[s:kingdom-of-dedan|Dedan]] in the [[s:kingdom-of-hejaz|Hejaz]], and left inscriptions as far away as [[s:delos|Delos]]. Inscriptions list Minaean men marrying foreign wives from Gaza and Egypt. The main god was [[e:wadd|Wadd]], and the kings governed with councils drawn from leading families. The language was [[e:minaic-language|Minaic]].
kingdom-of-main.e: Ma'in depended on caravan trade and lost importance as Ptolemaic and Roman shipping in the [[e:red-sea|Red Sea]] grew. Around 100 BCE it was absorbed by the [[s:kingdom-of-saba|Kingdom of Saba]]. The walls of [[e:baraqish|Baraqish]] still stand in al-[[e:al-jawf-yemen|Jawf]].

kingdom-of-gyaman.t: An Abron kingdom around the Muslim trading town of Bondoukou, long a reluctant tributary of the Ashanti Empire on the border of modern Ghana and Ivory Coast.
kingdom-of-gyaman.o: Gyaman was founded in the late 17th century by [[e:bono-people|Abron]] (Bono) migrants under their leader [[e:tan-date|Tan Date]], who moved west from the Bono area to escape the rising power of the [[s:ashanti-empire|Ashanti Empire]]. They settled around [[e:bondoukou|Bondoukou]], an old town of [[e:wangara|Dyula]] Muslim traders on the route between the goldfields and the middle [[e:niger-river|Niger]], and ruled the local peoples.
kingdom-of-gyaman.r: [[e:bono-people|Abron]] kings, chosen from a royal matrilineage on the [[e:akan|Akan]] model, held court at sites near [[e:bondoukou|Bondoukou]], while [[e:wangara|Dyula]] scholars and merchants ran the trade in gold, kola and cloth. [[e:ashanti-empire|Asante]] armies conquered Gyaman around 1740 and imposed tribute. King [[e:kofi-adinkra|Kofi Adinkra]] revolted and was killed in 1818; Akan tradition links the adinkra cloth symbols to his name.
kingdom-of-gyaman.e: Gyaman regained autonomy after [[e:ashanti-empire|Ashanti]] defeats in the 1870s, but in the 1890s [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and [[e:france|France]] divided it, and [[e:samori-ture|Samori Toure]] occupied it in 1895-1897. Its western part went to the [[s:french-ivory-coast|French Ivory Coast]] and the east to the [[s:gold-coast-colony|Gold Coast]].
kingdom-of-gyaman.re: Akan traditional religion, Sunni Islam among traders

khasa-malla-kingdom.t: A Himalayan kingdom of the Khasa people that ruled western Nepal and parts of western Tibet from Sinja, with a court that patronised both Buddhism and Hinduism.
khasa-malla-kingdom.o: The Khasa Mallas emerged in the Karnali basin of western [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Nepal]] around the 12th century. Under Nagaraja they made [[e:sinja|Sinja]], in the [[s:kingdom-of-jumla|Jumla]] valley, their capital and expanded north into the [[s:guge|Guge]] and [[e:purang|Purang]] regions of western [[s:tibet-1912-1951|Tibet]] and south and east across the western Himalayan foothills.
khasa-malla-kingdom.r: Inscriptions and stone pillars, some in early Nepali written in [[e:devanagari|Devanagari]], record the kings and their donations. Ripumalla and Prithvimalla were among the most powerful rulers; Ripumalla left an inscription on the Ashokan pillar at [[e:lumbini|Lumbini]] in 1312. The court supported Buddhist monasteries in [[s:tibet-1912-1951|Tibet]] and [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] shrines in [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Nepal]], and the kingdom grew rich on trans-Himalayan trade in salt, wool and grain. The Dullu inscription of Prithvimalla is a key source for its history.
khasa-malla-kingdom.e: By the late 14th century the kingdom fragmented into small principalities later known as the [[e:baise-rajya|Baise Rajya]], the twenty-two kingdoms of the Karnali region, among them the [[s:kingdom-of-jumla|Kingdom of Jumla]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-doti|Kingdom of Doti]]. The language of its inscriptions is an ancestor of modern Nepali.

kingdom-of-saba.t: Biblical Sheba: the incense kingdom of Marib whose great dam, temples and caravans made it the leading power of ancient south Arabia.
kingdom-of-saba.o: Sabaean inscriptions begin around the 8th century BCE, when rulers titled mukarrib governed from [[e:marib|Marib]] in the Yemeni desert margin. The early [[e:marib-dam|Marib Dam]] captured seasonal floods to irrigate two vast oases. In the 7th century BCE [[e:karibil-watar|Karib'il Watar]] conquered the [[s:kingdom-of-awsan|Kingdom of Awsan]] and imposed Sabaean supremacy over much of south-western [[e:arabia|Arabia]].
kingdom-of-saba.r: Saba grew rich on frankincense and [[e:myrrh|myrrh]] carried north along the [[e:caravan-trade|caravan routes]] to [[s:gaza|Gaza]] and [[e:mesopotamia|Mesopotamia]]. Society was organised in tribes and communes bound to the king; the national god [[e:almaqah|Almaqah]] was worshipped at the [[e:awwam-temple|Awwam]] temple near [[e:marib|Marib]]. Sabaic, written in the Ancient [[e:south-arabia|South Arabian]] script, became the region's prestige language. Its fame gave rise to the story of the [[e:queen-of-sheba|Queen of Sheba]].
kingdom-of-saba.e: From the 1st century BCE Saba lost ground as sea trade bypassed the caravans and the [[s:himyarite-kingdom|Himyarite Kingdom]] rose in the highlands. After centuries of rivalry, [[e:shammar-yahrish|Shammar Yahrish]] of Himyar absorbed Saba around 275 CE, keeping the title King of Saba and [[e:dhu-raydan|Dhu Raydan]]. The [[e:marib-dam|Marib Dam]] finally failed in the 6th century.

kingdom-of-mataram-lombok.t: Balinese Hindu kingdom that ruled the Muslim Sasak people of Lombok until the bloody Dutch intervention of 1894.
kingdom-of-mataram-lombok.o: Princes from the [[s:kingdom-of-karangasem|Kingdom of Karangasem]] had established Balinese rule in western [[e:lombok|Lombok]] by the late 17th century, displacing Makassarese influence. Several rival Balinese courts emerged on the island, and around 1740 [[s:mataram-sultanate|Mataram]] became the leading one; in 1838 to 1839 it defeated its rivals, uniting Lombok under a single Balinese dynasty based at Mataram and Cakranegara.
kingdom-of-mataram-lombok.r: A [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] Balinese elite ruled a majority of Muslim [[e:sasak-people|Sasak]] farmers, taxing their [[e:rice|rice]] and controlling their aristocrats. The kingdom grew rich exporting rice and became powerful enough to rule [[s:kingdom-of-karangasem|Karangasem]] on [[e:bali|Bali]] after 1849. Its Balinese princes built the [[e:pura-meru|Pura Meru]] temple and the Mayura water palace in Cakranegara.
kingdom-of-mataram-lombok.e: [[e:sasak-people|Sasak]] nobles rebelled and appealed to the [[e:dutch|Dutch]], who sent an expedition in 1894. After a surprise night attack destroyed part of the Dutch force, reinforcements stormed Cakranegara, where members of the royal house died in a puputan; the aged raja surrendered and died in exile in [[e:batavia|Batavia]]. The [[e:lombok-treasure|Lombok Treasure]] was taken to the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]], and the island joined the [[s:dutch-east-indies|Dutch East Indies]].

kingdom-of-munster.t: Southern Irish over-kingdom ruled from the Rock of Cashel by the Eóganachta and later by the Dál Cais of Brian Bóruma, until it split in two in 1118.
kingdom-of-munster.o: Munster, Mumu in Irish, was one of the ancient provinces of Ireland. From around the 5th century the [[e:eoganachta|Eóganachta]] dynasties, tracing descent from [[e:conall-corc|Conall Corc]], the legendary founder of [[e:rock-of-cashel|Cashel]], established an over-kingship over the province, displacing earlier [[s:iverni|Érainn]] peoples such as the [[s:corcu-loigde|Corcu Loigde]].
kingdom-of-munster.r: Kings ruled from [[e:rock-of-cashel|Cashel]] through a confederation of [[e:eoganachta|Eóganacht]] branches, collecting tribute from many subject peoples. Several were also churchmen or patrons of learning, such as [[e:feidlimid-mac-crimthainn|Feidlimid mac Crimthainn]], king and abbot, who died in 847. [[e:cathal-mac-finguine|Cathal mac Finguine]], who died in 742, challenged the [[e:ui-neill|Uí Néill]] for supremacy. In the 10th century the [[e:dal-cais|Dál Cais of Thomond]] took the kingship, and [[e:brian-boru|Brian Bóruma]], king of Munster from 978, became [[e:high-king-of-ireland|High King of Ireland]] in 1002.
kingdom-of-munster.e: In 1101 [[e:muirchertach-ua-briain|Muirchertach Ua Briain]] gave the [[e:rock-of-cashel|Rock of Cashel]] to the Church. In 1118 [[e:toirdelbach-ua-conchobair|Toirdelbach Ua Conchobair]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-connacht|Kingdom of Connacht]] divided Munster by the [[e:treaty-of-glanmire|Treaty of Glanmire]] into Desmond, under the [[e:charles-maccarthy|MacCarthys]], and Thomond, under the [[e:obrien-dynasty|O'Briens]].

kingdom-of-manyika.t: A Shona kingdom of the eastern highlands, ruled by the Mutasa, whose goldfields drew Portuguese traders and later British and Portuguese rivals.
kingdom-of-manyika.o: Manyika emerged around 1490 in the highlands that now straddle the [[e:zimbabwe|Zimbabwe]]–[[s:portuguese-mozambique|Mozambique]] border, as a tributary state on the edge of the [[e:mutapa-empire|Mutapa]] realm. Its rulers, who bore the title [[e:mutasa|Mutasa]], soon became effectively independent, controlling the alluvial gold of the region and the routes to the coast.
kingdom-of-manyika.r: The [[e:mutasa|Mutasa]] ruled through a network of chiefs and kin, and rainmaking and ancestral [[e:spirit-medium|spirit mediums]] supported royal authority. Gold was traded at Portuguese fairs such as [[e:manica-mozambique|Masekesa]], and the kingdom was a frequent target of Portuguese, [[s:kingdom-of-barwe|Barwe]] and Uteve ambitions. In the 19th century it suffered raids from the [[e:gaza-empire|Gaza Nguni]].
kingdom-of-manyika.e: In 1890 [[e:mutasa|Mutasa]] signed an agreement with the [[e:british-south-africa-company|British South Africa Company]], which clashed with the Portuguese claim. Fighting at [[e:manica-mozambique|Macequece]] in 1891 and the [[e:anglo-portuguese-treaty-of-1891|Anglo-Portuguese treaty]] that year split Manyika between [[s:southern-rhodesia|Southern Rhodesia]] and [[s:portuguese-mozambique|Portuguese Mozambique]]. Manyika remains a [[e:shona|Shona]] dialect and regional identity.

kummuh.t: Kummuh, a Neo-Hittite kingdom on the upper Euphrates around Samosata, forerunner of later Commagene.
kummuh.o: Kummuh arose after the Hittite collapse c. 1180 BCE in the land on the right bank of the upper [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]] around [[e:samosata|Samosata]], modern [[e:samsat|Samsat]]. Assyrian texts mention it from the time of [[e:tiglath-pileser-i|Tiglath-Pileser I]], c. 1100 BCE, when it was a target of raids.
kummuh.r: Its kings ruled a farming land of river valleys and wrote inscriptions in Luwian hieroglyphs. Placed between the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-urartu|Kingdom of Urartu]], they usually paid tribute to [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyria]]; Kushtashpi joined an Urartian alliance against Tiglath-Pileser III and then submitted again.
kummuh.e: In 708 BCE [[e:sargon-ii|Sargon II]] deposed King Muwatalli for conspiring with [[s:kingdom-of-urartu|Urartu]], deported its people and made Kummuh an Assyrian province. The name survived as [[s:kingdom-of-commagene|Commagene]], later the Kingdom of Commagene.

kingdom-of-mysore-1399-1799.t: The south Indian kingdom of the Wodeyars that became a formidable military power under Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan.
kingdom-of-mysore-1399-1799.o: According to tradition [[e:yaduraya|Yaduraya]] founded the [[e:wadiyar-dynasty|Wodeyar]] line at [[e:mysore|Mysore]] in 1399. The kingdom was a small [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the [[s:vijayanagara-empire|Vijayanagara Empire]] until Raja Wodeyar I seized [[e:srirangapatna|Srirangapatna]] in 1610 after Vijayanagara's decline, making it his capital and the base of an expanding state in southern [[e:karnataka|Karnataka]].
kingdom-of-mysore-1399-1799.r: [[e:chikka-devaraja-wodeyar|Chikka Devaraja Wodeyar]] built a centralised administration with regular revenue [[e:departement|departments]] in the late 17th century. From 1761 the commander [[e:hyder-ali|Hyder Ali]] took real power, and his son [[e:tipu-sultan|Tipu Sultan]] ruled as sultan from 1782. They built a modern army with French help, used iron-cased rockets, promoted [[e:sericulture|sericulture]] and trade, and fought four wars against the [[e:east-india-company|British East India Company]].
kingdom-of-mysore-1399-1799.e: [[e:tipu-sultan|Tipu Sultan]] was killed when British forces stormed [[e:srirangapatna|Srirangapatna]] in 1799, ending the [[e:fourth-anglo-mysore-war|Fourth Anglo-Mysore War]]. The British restored a child [[e:wadiyar-dynasty|Wodeyar]], [[e:krishnaraja-wodeyar-iii|Krishnaraja Wodeyar III]], as ruler of a reduced princely state of [[e:mysore|Mysore]], which joined the [[s:dominion-of-india|Dominion of India]] in 1947.
kingdom-of-mysore-1399-1799.re: Hinduism; Islam under Hyder Ali and Tipu

kingdom-of-imereti.t: The western Georgian kingdom centred on Kutaisi that endured Ottoman pressure for centuries until the Russian Empire annexed it in 1810.
kingdom-of-imereti.o: In 1259-1260 [[e:david-vi-narin|David VI Narin]], a co-king of the [[s:kingdom-of-georgia|Kingdom of Georgia]], rebelled against the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] and withdrew to [[e:kutaisi|Kutaisi]], creating a separate western kingdom. [[e:george-v|George V]] the Brilliant reunited it with the rest of [[s:georgia|Georgia]] in 1330, but it broke away again in the 1380s and was finally independent after the division of 1490.
kingdom-of-imereti.r: The kings ruled from [[e:kutaisi|Kutaisi]] with the Gelati monastery as a royal shrine, but powerful [[e:vassal|vassals]], the [[e:house-of-dadiani|Dadiani of Mingrelia]], the [[e:house-of-gurieli|Gurieli]] of [[s:principality-of-guria|Guria]] and the dukes of [[s:duchy-of-racha|Racha]], often defied them. From 1555 Imereti was tributary to the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]], and the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]] with Ottoman ports was a scourge. [[e:solomon|Solomon]] I defeated the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] at [[e:battle-of-chikhori-1757|Chikhori]] in 1757 and banned the slave trade.
kingdom-of-imereti.e: [[e:solomon-ii-of-imereti|Solomon II]] accepted a Russian [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] in 1804 but resisted direct rule, and in 1810 the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] deposed him and annexed Imereti. He died in exile at [[e:trabzon|Trabzon]] in 1815.

kingdom-of-east-anglia.t: The kingdom of the East Angles in Norfolk and Suffolk, famed for the Sutton Hoo ship burial and for its martyred last king, Edmund.
kingdom-of-east-anglia.o: [[e:angles|Angles]] settled [[e:norfolk|Norfolk]] and [[e:suffolk|Suffolk]] in the 5th century, and the Wuffingas dynasty, named after [[e:wuffa|Wuffa]], ruled by the 6th century. Its royal centre lay at [[e:rendlesham|Rendlesham]] in the [[e:river-deben|Deben]] valley, close to the burial ground at [[e:sutton-hoo|Sutton Hoo]].
kingdom-of-east-anglia.r: [[e:raedwald-of-east-anglia|Raedwald]], overlord of the southern English around 616, probably lies in the [[e:sutton-hoo|Sutton Hoo]] ship burial, with its gold and Byzantine [[e:silver|silver]]. He kept both a Christian altar and a pagan one. Later kings founded the bishopric of [[e:dommoc|Dommoc]], traditionally [[e:dunwich|Dunwich]], under [[e:felix-of-burgundy|Felix]], and [[e:anna-of-east-anglia|Anna]]'s daughter [[e:aethelthryth|Aethelthryth]] founded the monastery at [[e:ely-cambridgeshire|Ely]]. [[e:ipswich|Ipswich]] became one of the first post-Roman towns.
kingdom-of-east-anglia.e: East Anglia was often under Mercian overlordship in the 8th century. The [[e:great-heathen-army|Great Heathen Army]] killed [[e:edmund-the-martyr|King Edmund]] in 869 and the [[e:danes|Danes]] later settled the land as the [[s:danish-kingdom-of-east-anglia|Danish Kingdom of East Anglia]]. Edmund's cult grew at [[e:bury-st-edmunds|Bury St Edmunds]].

kingdom-of-shule.t: The oasis kingdom of Kashgar at the western end of the Tarim Basin, a crossroads where the Silk Roads met before climbing the Pamirs.
kingdom-of-shule.o: Shule, the Chinese name for [[e:kashgar|Kashgar]], was a city-state at the foot of the [[e:pamir-mountains|Pamirs]], recorded by Han sources from the 2nd century BCE. Its people spoke an Eastern Iranian language related to [[s:saka|Saka]], and it controlled the routes west to [[s:principality-of-ferghana|Ferghana]] and [[s:greco-bactrian-kingdom|Bactria]] and south towards [[e:india|India]].
kingdom-of-shule.r: Shule was ruled by local kings who switched allegiance between the [[e:xiongnu-empire|Xiongnu]], Kushan, Han and later Turkic powers. In the 70s CE the Han general [[e:ban-chao|Ban Chao]] used it as his base for reconquering the [[e:western-regions|Western Regions]]. [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] was strong, and the city's markets traded [[e:silk|silk]], horses and jade. Under the [[s:tang-dynasty|Tang Dynasty]] its kings of the Pei family ruled as one of the [[e:four-garrisons-of-anxi|Four Garrisons of Anxi]].
kingdom-of-shule.e: The [[s:tibetan-empire|Tibetan Empire]] took the [[e:tarim-basin|Tarim]] garrisons around 790, ending [[s:later-tang|Tang]] authority. In the 10th century [[e:kashgar|Kashgar]] became the capital of the [[s:kara-khanid-khanate|Kara-Khanid Khanate]], whose rulers converted to [[e:islam|Islam]] and turned the city into a centre of Turkic Muslim culture.

kagal-senior.t: A Maratha jagir under Kolhapur held by the Ghatge family, which gave Kolhapur its reforming Maharaja, Shahu.
kagal-senior.o: Kagal was the seat of the Ghatge family, [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] chiefs with a long record of service under the [[e:bijapur|Bijapur]] sultanate and the Maratha kings. By around 1700 they held Kagal as a [[e:jagir|jagir]], later divided into senior and junior branches, as feudatories of [[s:kolhapur-state|Kolhapur State]].
kagal-senior.r: The chiefs governed a small territory south of [[s:kolhapur-state|Kolhapur]] under its overlordship. The family was closely tied to the Kolhapur court, and in 1884 [[e:shahu-of-kolhapur|Yeshwantrao Ghatge]], son of the chief of Kagal Senior, was adopted into the Kolhapur royal house, becoming the reforming [[e:maharaja|Maharaja]] Shahu.
kagal-senior.e: Kagal merged with [[s:kolhapur-state|Kolhapur]] into [[s:bombay-presidency|Bombay Province]] in 1949 and became part of [[e:maharashtra|Maharashtra]] in 1960. It is now a town in Kolhapur district.

kingdom-of-colchis.t: The land of the Golden Fleece on the eastern Black Sea, an early Georgian kingdom whose gold, timber and Greek trading ports made it a bridge between the Caucasus and the Greek world.
kingdom-of-colchis.o: Colchis appears as Qulha in Urartian inscriptions of the 8th century BCE, when it emerged in the lowlands of the Rioni and its foothills, in part inheriting the lands of [[s:diauehi|Diauehi]]. Greek colonists from [[s:miletus|Miletus]] founded ports such as [[e:phasis-town|Phasis]] and [[e:dioscurias|Dioscurias]] in the 6th century BCE, and the [[e:argonauts|Argonaut]] legend fixed its fame.
kingdom-of-colchis.r: Power was held by kings and local sceptre-bearing chiefs ruling from towns such as [[e:vani|Vani]], whose rich burials hold fine gold jewellery. Colchians traded linen, [[e:timber|timber]], honey and slaves with the [[e:greeks|Greeks]] and, according to [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]], sent regular gifts to the Achaemenid court. They spoke a Kartvelian language, and local coins called Colchian tetri circulated widely.
kingdom-of-colchis.e: In the 2nd century BCE the kingdom fragmented under local rulers, and about 101 BCE [[e:mithridates-vi-of-pontus|Mithridates VI]] annexed it to the [[s:kingdom-of-pontus|Kingdom of Pontus]]. After Pontus fell to [[e:rome|Rome]], the coast passed under Roman influence and the western Georgian kingdom of [[s:kingdom-of-lazica|Lazica]] later grew in the same lands.

khairagarh-state.t: A Nagvanshi-ruled state of Chhattisgarh whose last rulers gave their palace for India's first university of music and fine arts.
khairagarh-state.o: Khairagarh was ruled by a Nagvanshi family that had held land in the area since earlier times. It became a distinct feudatory state in the 19th century under the [[e:bhonsles|Bhonsles]] of the [[s:nagpur-kingdom|Nagpur Kingdom]] and then the British.
khairagarh-state.r: The state was one of the [[e:chhattisgarh|Chhattisgarh]] feudatory states, ruled by a Raja over [[e:rice|rice]]-growing plains and forested hills. Its rulers were patrons of music, and Raja Birendra Bahadur Singh and [[s:rani|Rani]] [[e:pawaya|Padmavati]] later gave their palace to found the [[e:indira-kala-sangeet-vishwavidyalaya|Indira Kala Sangeet Vishwavidyalaya]] in 1956.
khairagarh-state.e: Khairagarh acceded to [[e:india|India]] and on 1 January 1948 was merged into the [[e:central-provinces|Central Provinces and Berar]]. The town is now in [[e:chhattisgarh|Chhattisgarh]].

kingdom-of-westphalia.t: Napoleonic kingdom ruled by his brother Jérôme, Germany's first state with a written constitution and equal rights for Jews.
kingdom-of-westphalia.o: After defeating [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] created the Kingdom of [[e:westphalia|Westphalia]] in 1807 by the [[e:treaties-of-tilsit|Peace of Tilsit]], combining [[s:electorate-of-hesse|Hesse-Kassel]], [[s:principality-of-wolfenbuttel|Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel]], Prussian lands west of the [[e:elbe|Elbe]] such as [[e:magdeburg|Magdeburg]] and [[e:halberstadt|Halberstadt]], and parts of [[e:hanover|Hanover]]. He gave it to his youngest brother [[e:jerome-bonaparte|Jérôme Bonaparte]], with [[e:kassel|Kassel]] as capital.
kingdom-of-westphalia.r: The constitution of November 1807, the first in [[e:germany|Germany]], abolished [[e:serfdom|serfdom]] and [[e:guild|guild]] privileges, introduced the [[e:napoleonic-code|Napoleonic Code]] and granted equal rights to [[e:jews|Jews]]. A parliament of estates met. But heavy taxes, French demands for soldiers and losses in [[e:russia|Russia]] made the regime unpopular, and [[e:jerome-bonaparte|Jérôme]]'s court was known for extravagance. Revolts broke out in 1809.
kingdom-of-westphalia.e: After the battle of [[e:leipzig|Leipzig]] in 1813 Russian troops took [[e:kassel|Kassel]] and [[e:jerome-bonaparte|Jérôme]] fled. The old rulers returned to [[s:electorate-of-hesse|Hesse-Kassel]], [[e:brunswick|Brunswick]] and [[e:hanover|Hanover]], while [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] recovered its lands.

kingdom-of-mapungubwe.t: Southern Africa's first class-divided kingdom, ruled from a hilltop above the Limpopo and famed for its golden rhinoceros.
kingdom-of-mapungubwe.o: The kingdom grew out of the earlier settlement at K2 ([[e:bambandyanalo|Bambandyanalo]]) near the confluence of the [[e:shashe-river|Shashe]] and [[e:limpopo|Limpopo]] rivers. The ruling group later moved onto [[e:mapungubwe-hill|Mapungubwe Hill]], separating itself physically from commoners below. Wealth came from [[e:cattle|cattle]], farming on the floodplain and a growing trade in [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and gold with [[e:swahili|Swahili merchants]] on the [[e:indian-ocean|Indian Ocean]] coast.
kingdom-of-mapungubwe.r: Archaeology is the only source. The elite lived and were buried on the hilltop with gold-foil objects, including the famous golden rhinoceros, while ordinary people lived in the valley. [[e:gla|Glass]] [[e:bead|beads]] from [[e:india|India]] and the [[e:middle-east|Middle East]], Chinese celadon and locally worked gold show a link through coastal ports such as [[e:sofala|Sofala]] to the wider [[e:indian-ocean|Indian Ocean]] economy. Sacred leadership and rainmaking probably underpinned royal authority.
kingdom-of-mapungubwe.e: Dates differ between chronologies: older ones place the kingdom between about 1075 and 1220, while more recent research dates the hilltop capital to about 1220-1290. Mapungubwe was then abandoned, possibly as a cooler, drier climate undermined floodplain farming. Power and trade shifted north to the [[s:kingdom-of-zimbabwe|Kingdom of Zimbabwe]], which inherited many of its institutions. The site is now a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage]] landscape in [[s:republic-of-south-africa|South Africa]].

kingdom-of-characene.t: A trading kingdom at the head of the Gulf, centred on Charax Spasinou, that linked Parthian Mesopotamia with India, Arabia and Palmyra.
kingdom-of-characene.o: [[e:hyspaosines|Hyspaosines]], a [[e:seleucid-empire|Seleucid]] governor of the head of the Gulf, refounded the flooded city of [[e:alexandria|Alexandria]] on the [[e:tigris|Tigris]] as [[e:charax-spasinou|Charax Spasinou]] and declared independence around 141 BCE as Seleucid power collapsed. He briefly held [[e:babylon|Babylon]] in 127 BCE before becoming a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the [[s:parthian-empire|Parthian Empire]].
kingdom-of-characene.r: Characene, also called Mesene, prospered from long-distance trade: ships from [[e:india|India]] and the Gulf unloaded at [[e:charax-spasinou|Charax]], and Palmyrene merchants organised caravans from there to the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]], as inscriptions at [[s:palmyrene-empire|Palmyra]] show. Kings minted [[e:silver|silver]] tetradrachms with Greek legends. Its population included [[e:babylonians|Babylonians]], [[e:arabs|Arabs]], [[e:greeks|Greeks]] and Iranians, and the geographer [[e:isidore-of-charax|Isidore of Charax]] came from the city. The Roman emperor [[e:trajan|Trajan]] visited King [[e:attambelos-vii|Attambelos VII]] in 116 CE.
kingdom-of-characene.e: [[e:ardashir-i|Ardashir I]] conquered Characene around 222 CE, and it became the Sasanian province of [[e:meshan|Meshan]]. [[e:charax-spasinou|Charax]] declined as rivers shifted, its role later taken by [[e:basra|Basra]].

kingdom-of-etruria.t: A Napoleonic kingdom created in Tuscany for a Spanish Bourbon prince in 1801, abolished six years later.
kingdom-of-etruria.o: By agreements between [[e:france|France]] and [[e:spain|Spain]] in 1800–1801, including the [[e:treaty-of-aranjuez-1801|Treaty of Aranjuez]], the [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Grand Duchy of Tuscany]] was taken from its Habsburg-[[e:lorraine|Lorraine]] ruler and turned into the Kingdom of [[e:etruria|Etruria]] for [[e:louis-i-of-etruria|Louis of Bourbon-Parma]], in exchange for the [[s:ile-bourbon|Bourbon]] claim to the [[s:duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza|Duchy of Parma and Piacenza]].
kingdom-of-etruria.r: Louis I, in poor health, ruled from [[s:duchy-of-florence|Florence]] under strong French influence; the [[s:state-of-the-presidi|State of the Presidi]] was added. After his death in 1803 his widow [[e:maria-luisa-duchess-of-lucca|Maria Luisa of Spain]] governed as regent for their young son [[e:charles-ii-duke-of-parma|Charles Louis]]. The court was conservative and pious, and the kingdom paid heavily to support French troops.
kingdom-of-etruria.e: In 1807 [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] dissolved the kingdom under the [[e:treaty-of-fontainebleau-1807|Treaty of Fontainebleau]] and annexed [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Tuscany]] to [[e:france|France]] in 1808. In 1809 he made his sister [[e:elisa-bonaparte|Elisa]] grand duchess. [[e:maria-luisa-duchess-of-lucca|Maria Luisa]] later received the [[s:duchy-of-lucca|Duchy of Lucca]].

kakuyid-dynasty.t: A Daylamite dynasty that ruled Isfahan and Hamadan in the early 11th century, in whose service the philosopher Avicenna wrote some of his major works.
kakuyid-dynasty.o: [[e:ala-al-dawla-muhammad|Ala al-Dawla Muhammad]], called Ibn Kakuya because he was the maternal uncle (kaku) of the [[e:buyid-dynasty|Buyid]] regent [[e:sayyida-shirin|Sayyida]], was appointed governor of [[e:isfahan|Isfahan]] around 1008. As Buyid authority fragmented, he made himself an independent ruler and took [[e:hamadan|Hamadan]] from the [[s:buyid-dynasty|Buyids]] in the 1020s.
kakuyid-dynasty.r: Ala al-Dawla held a court at [[e:isfahan|Isfahan]] where [[e:avicenna|Ibn Sina]] (Avicenna) served as physician and adviser from about 1024 to his death in 1037, completing works such as the [[e:danishnama-yi-alai|Danishnama-yi Ala'i]], written in Persian and named after his patron. The [[e:kakuyids|Kakuyids]] fought the [[s:ghaznavid-empire|Ghaznavid Empire]], which occupied Isfahan more than once. They patronised building in Isfahan, including works at the [[e:jameh-mosque-of-isfahan|Friday Mosque]].
kakuyid-dynasty.e: Ala al-Dawla's son [[e:faramurz|Faramurz]] surrendered [[e:isfahan|Isfahan]] to the Seljuk sultan [[e:tughril|Tughril]] in 1051 and received [[e:yazd|Yazd]] and [[e:abarkuh|Abarquh]] instead. The [[e:kakuyids|Kakuyids]] ruled there as Seljuk [[e:vassal|vassals]] until about 1141, when power passed to the [[s:atabegs-of-yazd|Atabegs of Yazd]].

kingdom-of-the-thuringians.t: A Germanic kingdom in central Germany, briefly one of the great powers of the post-Roman west until the Franks destroyed it in 531.
kingdom-of-the-thuringians.o: The Thuringians appear around 400 in a Roman veterinary text that praises their horses. They likely descended in part from the [[s:hermunduri|Hermunduri]] and [[e:angles|Angles]], and formed a kingdom centred on the Thuringian basin, extending at its height from the [[e:harz|Harz]] to the [[e:danube|Danube]] and from the [[e:werra|Werra]] to the [[e:elbe|Elbe]].
kingdom-of-the-thuringians.r: In the early 6th century King [[e:herminafrid|Herminafrid]] married [[e:amalaberga|Amalaberga]], niece of the Ostrogothic king [[e:theodoric-the-great|Theodoric the Great]], linking [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]] to the Ostrogothic alliance system. Rich graves, horse burials and the trade in horses show an aristocratic warrior society. Little is known of its institutions, as it left no written records of its own.
kingdom-of-the-thuringians.e: After [[e:theodoric-the-great|Theodoric]]'s death removed Ostrogothic protection, the Frankish kings [[e:theuderic-i|Theuderic I]] and [[e:chlothar-i|Chlothar I]] defeated the Thuringians on the [[e:unstrut|Unstrut]] in 531; [[e:herminafrid|Herminafrid]] was killed soon after at [[e:zulpich|Zülpich]]. The north went to [[e:saxons|Saxon]] allies, the rest to the [[s:franks|Franks]], later forming the [[s:duchy-of-thuringia|Duchy of Thuringia]].

kedatuan-of-madja-as.t: A confederation of Visayan settlements on Panay, known from the legend of ten Bornean datus who bought the island from the Ati people.
kedatuan-of-madja-as.o: The story of Madja-as comes from the [[e:maragtas|Maragtas]], published by [[e:pedro-monteclaro|Pedro Monteclaro]] in 1907 from oral tradition. It tells of ten datus fleeing a tyrant in [[e:borneo|Borneo]], led by [[e:datu-puti|Datu Puti]], who bought the lowlands of Panay from the Ati chief [[e:marikudo|Marikudo]] for a golden salakot, a native hat, and a long gold necklace. Historians such as [[e:william-henry-scott|William Henry Scott]] regard the account as folklore, not history.
kedatuan-of-madja-as.r: Panay's real 16th-century society, described by the Spanish, was made up of independent coastal communities led by datus, with nobles, freemen and dependants. They grew [[e:rice|rice]], traded with Chinese and Bornean merchants and practised ancestor worship.
kedatuan-of-madja-as.e: [[e:miguel-lopez-de-legazpi|Miguel Lopez de Legazpi]] moved his base to Panay in 1569 and Spanish rule followed. The Madja-as legend is now celebrated in the [[e:ati-atihan-festival|Ati-Atihan]] and Binirayan festivals and remains part of Visayan identity.

kingdom-of-wessex.t: The kingdom of the West Saxons, which survived the Viking onslaught under Alfred the Great and grew into the Kingdom of England.
kingdom-of-wessex.o: The [[e:anglo-saxon-chronicle|Anglo-Saxon Chronicle]] traces [[e:wessex|Wessex]] to [[e:cerdic|Cerdic]] and [[e:cynric|Cynric]], said to have landed in 495 and taken the kingship in 519. Early kings of the Gewisse operated in the upper [[e:river-thames|Thames]] valley before expanding west and south. Archaeology suggests more complex origins than the Chronicle's story.
kingdom-of-wessex.r: [[e:wessex|Wessex]] was divided into shires under ealdormen, with royal estates, law codes from [[e:ine-of-wessex|Ine]] around 694, and bishoprics at [[e:winchester|Winchester]] and [[e:sherborne|Sherborne]]. [[e:christianity|Christianity]] arrived with [[e:birinus|Birinus]] in 635. Victory over [[s:kingdom-of-mercia|Mercia]] at [[e:battle-of-ellendun|Ellendun]] in 825 made [[e:egbert-of-wessex|Ecgberht]] the leading southern king. Alfred built a network of fortified burhs, a navy and a revival of learning in English.
kingdom-of-wessex.e: Alfred defeated [[e:guthrum|Guthrum]] at [[e:battle-of-edington|Edington]] in 878 and his successors reconquered the [[e:danelaw|Danelaw]]. From 886 [[e:wessex|Wessex]] merged into the [[s:kingdom-of-the-anglo-saxons|Kingdom of the Anglo-Saxons]], and under Aethelstan in 927 it became the core of the [[s:kingdom-of-england|Kingdom of England]], with [[e:winchester|Winchester]] its royal centre.

karelo-finnish-soviet-socialist-republic.t: Soviet union republic created after the Winter War from Karelia and lands taken from Finland, downgraded to an autonomous republic in 1956.
karelo-finnish-soviet-socialist-republic.o: After the [[e:winter-war|Winter War]], the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] in March 1940 combined the [[e:karelian-assr|Karelian Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic]] with most of the territory ceded by [[s:republic-of-finland|Finland]], creating a full union republic with [[e:petrozavodsk|Petrozavodsk]] as capital. [[e:otto-wille-kuusinen|Otto Wille Kuusinen]], former head of the [[s:finnish-democratic-republic|Finnish Democratic Republic]], became its head of state.
karelo-finnish-soviet-socialist-republic.r: Its status as a union republic was partly intended as a framework for absorbing [[s:republic-of-finland|Finland]]. Finnish was promoted alongside Russian, though [[e:finns|Finns]] and [[s:karelians|Karelians]] were a minority among Russians. The republic depended on forestry, mining and fishing. Finnish forces occupied much of it, including [[e:petrozavodsk|Petrozavodsk]], during the [[e:continuation-war|Continuation War]] of 1941-1944.
karelo-finnish-soviet-socialist-republic.e: After the war [[s:republic-of-finland|Finland]] was clearly not to be annexed, and the republic's role faded. In 1956 it was downgraded to the [[e:karelian-assr|Karelian Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic]] within the [[s:russian-sfsr|Russian SFSR]]. Today it is the Republic of [[s:karelians|Karelia]] in [[e:russia|Russia]].

kingdom-of-tir-chonaill.t: The Gaelic lordship of north-west Ulster, ruled from the 13th century by the O'Donnells, whose flight in 1607 ended independent Gaelic rule in Ulster.
kingdom-of-tir-chonaill.o: Tir Chonaill, the land of Conall, was named after [[e:conall-gulban|Conall Gulban]], a son of [[e:niall-of-the-nine-hostages|Niall of the Nine Hostages]]. His descendants, the [[e:cenel-conaill|Cenel Conaill]], formed one branch of the northern [[e:ui-neill|Ui Neill]] and held much of present-day [[e:county-donegal|County Donegal]]. [[e:columba|Columba of Iona]] belonged to this kindred, which also shared the high kingship in the early centuries.
kingdom-of-tir-chonaill.r: [[e:cenel-conaill|Cenel Conaill]] kings alternated the northern overkingship with Cenel nEogain until the 8th century. From the 13th century the [[e:odonnell-dynasty|O'Donnell]] family ruled the territory, based from 1474 at [[e:donegal-castle|Donegal Castle]], with a strong fleet, Scottish [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]] and learned bardic families such as the [[e:o-cleirigh|O'Clerys]]. The Franciscan [[e:donegal-friary|Donegal Friary]], founded in 1474 by [[e:red-hugh-odonnell|Hugh Roe O'Donnell]] and his wife Nuala, was a key patron foundation.
kingdom-of-tir-chonaill.e: [[e:red-hugh-odonnell|Red Hugh O'Donnell]] joined [[e:hugh-oneill-earl-of-tyrone|Hugh O'Neill]] in the [[e:nine-years-war-ireland|Nine Years' War]] against [[e:england|England]]. After defeat, [[e:rory-odonnell-1st-earl-of-tyrconnell|Rory O'Donnell]], Earl of Tyrconnell, left Ireland in the Flight of the Earls in 1607, and his lands were confiscated for the [[e:plantation-of-ulster|Plantation of Ulster]] under the [[s:kingdom-of-ireland|Kingdom of Ireland]].

karelians.t: Finnic people around Lake Ladoga and their stronghold of Korela, allies of Novgorod whose land was divided between Sweden and Rus' in 1323.
karelians.o: The Karelians emerged in the late [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] on the north-western shores of [[e:lake-ladoga|Lake Ladoga]] and the Karelian Isthmus. Their wealth came from the [[e:fur-trade|fur trade]], and by the 12th century they were closely tied to [[e:veliky-novgorod|Novgorod]], joining its campaigns against the [[e:finns|Finns]] and Swedes.
karelians.r: Karelian society was led by local chiefs and wealthy families who controlled fur collection from the north. Rich graves with [[e:silver|silver]] ornaments and swords show a prosperous elite. In 1227 Prince [[e:yaroslav-ii-of-vladimir|Yaroslav Vsevolodovich]] of [[e:veliky-novgorod|Novgorod]] had many Karelians baptised into [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox Christianity]], and Korela became their main fortified centre.
karelians.e: In 1278 [[e:veliky-novgorod|Novgorod]] campaigned against the Karelians and tightened its control over them. [[e:sweden|Sweden]] pressed from the west and founded [[e:vyborg|Vyborg]] in 1293. The [[e:treaty-of-noteborg|Treaty of Nöteborg]] in 1323 divided [[e:karelia|Karelia]] between Sweden and Novgorod, a border that shaped the later divide between Lutheran [[s:grand-duchy-of-finland|Finland]] and [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] [[e:russia|Russia]].
