kingitanga.t: The Māori King Movement, created in 1858 to unite tribes under a monarch and halt land sales, which fought British forces and held the King Country for two decades.
kingitanga.o: In the 1850s many Māori, alarmed at the loss of land to settlers in the [[s:colony-of-new-zealand|Colony of New Zealand]], sought a king to stand equal to [[e:queen-victoria|Queen Victoria]] and to protect land under a single authority. After long debate, [[e:waikato|Waikato]] tribes and their allies chose the Waikato chief [[e:potatau-te-wherowhero|Pōtatau Te Wherowhero]], crowned at [[e:ngaruawahia|Ngāruawāhia]] in 1858, with [[e:wiremu-tamihana|Wiremu Tāmihana]] as the leading organiser.
kingitanga.r: The movement set up councils, courts, a newspaper and a flag, and refused to sell land. Governor [[e:george-grey|George Grey]] saw it as a challenge to [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] and invaded the [[e:waikato|Waikato]] in 1863. After defeats at [[e:battle-of-rangiriri|Rangiriri]] and [[e:battle-of-orakau|Ōrākau]], about 1.2 million acres were confiscated. King [[e:tawhiao|Tāwhiao]] withdrew south into the [[e:king-country|Rohe Pōtae]], the King Country, which remained closed to Europeans behind a boundary called the aukati.
kingitanga.e: [[e:tawhiao|Tāwhiao]] made peace in 1881, and in 1883 the [[e:king-country|King Country]] was opened to surveys for the [[e:north-island-main-trunk|North Island Main Trunk railway]]. The movement survives, with its monarch based at [[e:turangawaewae|Tūrangawaewae]] in [[e:ngaruawahia|Ngāruawāhia]].

kingdom-of-uteve.t: A Shona kingdom behind the port of Sofala whose rulers, the Sachiteve, charged the Portuguese for passage to the gold fairs of the interior.
kingdom-of-uteve.o: Uteve emerged in the late 15th century when a branch of the ruling house in the [[e:mutapa-empire|Mutapa]] lands broke away and established itself between the [[e:zimbabwean-plateau|Zimbabwe plateau]] and the coast. Its position astride the routes from [[e:sofala|Sofala]] to the inland goldfields made it a key intermediary for [[e:swahili|Swahili]] and then Portuguese traders.
kingdom-of-uteve.r: The king, called the Sachiteve (Quiteve to the Portuguese), was a sacred ruler bound by strict ritual; the [[e:dominican-order|Dominican friar]] [[e:joao-dos-santos|Joao dos Santos]], who lived at [[e:sofala|Sofala]] in the 1590s, described royal ceremonies and the custom by which a king who became infirm or blemished was expected to take poison. [[e:spirit-medium|Spirit mediums]] and ancestor cults were central. The Portuguese paid regular tribute, the curva, for the right to trade through the kingdom.
kingdom-of-uteve.e: Uteve was weakened by succession disputes and in the 19th century fell under the domination of the [[e:gaza-empire|Gaza Nguni]]. By around 1890 its lands were included in the territory of the [[s:mozambique-company|Mozambique Company]] within [[s:portuguese-mozambique|Portuguese Mozambique]].

kalmyk-khanate.t: A khanate of Oirat Mongols who migrated to the Volga steppe, the westernmost Buddhist state in Europe.
kalmyk-khanate.o: In the early 17th century the [[e:torghut|Torghut]], an [[e:oirats|Oirat]] Mongol tribe, under their leader [[e:kho-orluk|Kho Orluk]], migrated west from [[s:dzungar-khanate|Dzungaria]] across the [[e:kazakhs|Kazakh]] steppe, reaching the lower [[e:volga|Volga]] by about 1630 and driving out the [[s:nogai-horde|Nogai Horde]]. [[e:ayuka-khan|Ayuka Khan]] later received the title of khan from the [[e:dalai-lama|Dalai Lama]].
kalmyk-khanate.r: The [[e:kalmyks|Kalmyks]] were pastoral nomads following [[e:tibetan-buddhism|Tibetan Buddhism]], with monasteries and a code of law based on the [[e:mongol-oirat-code|Mongol-Oirat Code]] of 1640. As allies of [[e:russia|Russia]] they guarded its southern frontier, fighting the [[s:crimean-khanate|Crimean Khanate]], the [[s:kazakh-khanate|Kazakh Khanate]] and Ottoman forces. [[e:ayuka-khan|Ayuka Khan]], ruling from 1669 to 1724, was the khanate's most powerful leader.
kalmyk-khanate.e: Russian settlement and controls on the steppe pushed many [[e:kalmyks|Kalmyks]] to return east. In 1771 [[e:ubashi-khan|Ubashi Khan]] led some 150,000 across the steppe to [[s:dzungar-khanate|Dzungaria]], losing many on the way. [[e:catherine-the-great|Catherine the Great]] abolished the khanate, and those left on the [[e:volga|Volga]] are the ancestors of today's Kalmyks.

cr.a: naturalearthdata.com, offered to the Public Domain per Terms of Use

kingdom-of-chiang-mai.t: The restored Lan Na principality of Chiang Mai under Siamese overlordship, ruled by Kawila's descendants until absorbed into Siam's provinces.
kingdom-of-chiang-mai.o: After [[e:kawila|Kawila]] of [[s:principality-of-lampang|Lampang]] helped expel the Burmese from [[s:lan-na|Lan Na]], he rebuilt the depopulated city of Chiang Mai from 1796, bringing in war captives from the Shan and [[e:tai-lu-people|Tai Lue]] regions. In 1802 the [[s:rattanakosin-kingdom|Rattanakosin Kingdom]] recognised him as king of Chiang Mai, a [[e:vassal|vassal]] state.
kingdom-of-chiang-mai.r: [[e:kawila|Kawila]] and his successors of the [[e:chet-ton-dynasty|Chet Ton dynasty]] governed Chiang Mai, [[e:lamphun|Lamphun]] and [[s:principality-of-lampang|Lampang]] as related principalities, sending tribute and troops to [[e:bangkok|Bangkok]]. Chiang Mai prospered on [[e:rice|rice]] and teak, and in the late 19th century British firms from [[s:myanmar|Burma]] operated large logging concessions, which led to disputes and Siamese intervention.
kingdom-of-chiang-mai.e: From the 1870s [[e:bangkok|Bangkok]] placed commissioners in Chiang Mai, and the Chiang Mai treaties with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] strengthened Siamese control. In 1899 [[s:lan-na|Lan Na]] was turned into a regular monthon. The princely title lapsed with the death of [[e:kaew-nawarat|Kaew Nawarat]] in 1939, and Chiang Mai is now [[e:thailand|Thailand's]] main northern city.

kingdom-of-odoacer.t: Kingdom of the barbarian general Odoacer, who deposed the last western emperor, Romulus Augustulus, in 476 and ruled Italy until 493.
kingdom-of-odoacer.o: [[e:odoacer|Odoacer]], an officer of Germanic origin in the Roman army in [[e:italy|Italy]], led a mutiny of soldiers demanding land. In 476 he defeated the general [[e:orestes-roman-general|Orestes]] and deposed his son, the young emperor [[e:romulus-augustulus|Romulus Augustulus]], sending the imperial regalia to [[e:zeno-emperor|Zeno]] in [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]]. His soldiers proclaimed him king.
kingdom-of-odoacer.r: [[e:odoacer|Odoacer]] ruled from [[s:lordship-of-ravenna|Ravenna]] as king while nominally recognising the eastern emperor. He kept the Roman administration and the Senate, appointing Roman consuls and officials, and gave his soldiers land, traditionally a third of estates. An Arian Christian, he tolerated the Catholic Church. He gained [[e:sicily|Sicily]] from the [[e:vandals|Vandals]] by treaty, took [[e:dalmatia|Dalmatia]] and destroyed the Rugian kingdom on the [[e:danube|Danube]] in 487.
kingdom-of-odoacer.e: [[e:zeno-emperor|Zeno]] sent [[e:theodoric-the-great|Theodoric]] and the [[e:ostrogoths|Ostrogoths]] against [[e:odoacer|Odoacer]] in 489. After defeats on the [[e:soca|Isonzo]] and at [[s:commune-of-verona|Verona]], Odoacer held out in [[s:lordship-of-ravenna|Ravenna]] for three years. He agreed to share power in 493 but was killed by Theodoric at a banquet days later, and the [[s:ostrogothic-kingdom|Ostrogothic Kingdom]] replaced his.

konbaung-dynasty.t: The last Burmese royal dynasty, which conquered Ayutthaya, Arakan and Manipur, fought China and Britain, and fell to British annexation in 1885.
konbaung-dynasty.o: In 1752 [[e:alaungpaya|Alaungpaya]], headman of [[e:shwebo|Moksobo]], now Shwebo, rose against the [[s:restored-hanthawaddy-kingdom|Restored Hanthawaddy Kingdom]], reunited [[s:myanmar|Burma]] by 1757 and founded [[e:yangon|Rangoon]]. His sons extended the empire: [[e:hsinbyushin|Hsinbyushin]] sacked [[s:ayutthaya-kingdom|Ayutthaya]] in 1767 and repelled four Qing invasions between 1765 and 1769.
konbaung-dynasty.r: Konbaung kings ruled through royal service groups and provincial governors, holding the Shan states and [[s:kingdom-of-manipur|Manipur]] as tributaries. [[e:bodawpaya|Bodawpaya]] conquered [[s:mrauk-u-kingdom|Arakan]] in 1785. Capitals moved between [[e:shwebo|Shwebo]], Ava, [[e:amarapura|Amarapura]] and finally [[e:mandalay|Mandalay]], built by [[e:mindon-min|Mindon]] in 1857. Mindon promoted the Fifth Buddhist Council, [[e:telegraph|telegraphs]] and modern administration, but the kingdom shrank after wars with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in 1824 to 1826 and 1852.
konbaung-dynasty.e: After disputes over trade and teak concessions, [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] invaded in the [[e:third-anglo-burmese-war|Third Anglo-Burmese War]] and captured [[e:mandalay|Mandalay]] in November 1885. [[e:thibaw-min|King Thibaw]] was exiled to [[e:india|India]], and [[s:myanmar|Burma]] was annexed to [[s:british-burma|British Burma]] on 1 January 1886.

kingdom-of-bernicia.t: The northern Anglian kingdom based on the fortress of Bamburgh, whose kings united with Deira to create Northumbria.
kingdom-of-bernicia.o: The [[e:anglo-saxon-chronicle|Anglo-Saxon Chronicle]] dates Bernicia to 547, when [[e:ida-of-bernicia|Ida]] took the kingship and built [[s:earldom-of-bamburgh|Bamburgh]]. Its people were [[e:angles|Angles]] who settled the coast between the [[e:river-tees|Tees]] and the [[e:firth-of-forth|Forth]] among the British population. The British name Bryneich suggests the kingdom took over an earlier British territory.
kingdom-of-bernicia.r: Bernicia's kings were warriors whose power rested on tribute and plunder. [[e:aethelfrith-of-northumbria|Aethelfrith]] defeated Aedan of [[s:dal-riata|Dal Riata]] at [[e:battle-of-degsastan|Degsastan]] in 603 and the [[e:britons-celtic-people|Britons]] at [[e:battle-of-chester|Chester]], then seized [[s:kingdom-of-deira|Deira]]. His son [[e:oswald-of-northumbria|Oswald]] brought Aidan from [[e:iona|Iona]], who founded [[e:lindisfarne|Lindisfarne]] in 635, and royal sites such as [[e:yeavering|Yeavering]] show grand halls.
kingdom-of-bernicia.e: Under [[e:oswiu|Oswiu]], Bernicia and the [[s:kingdom-of-deira|Kingdom of Deira]] were joined permanently after 654, forming the [[s:kingdom-of-northumbria|Kingdom of Northumbria]]. [[s:earldom-of-bamburgh|Bamburgh]] remained a royal fortress and later the seat of the Earldom of Bamburgh.

kingdom-of-raigama.t: A minor Sinhalese kingdom of south-western Sri Lanka created by the division of Kotte in 1521 and reabsorbed less than two decades later.
kingdom-of-raigama.o: Raigama was formed in 1521, when the [[s:kingdom-of-kotte|Kingdom of Kotte]] was split among the three sons of [[e:vijayabahu-vi|Vijayabahu VI]] after they killed him. [[e:raigam-bandara|Pararajasinghe]], also called Raigam Bandara, received the Raigama district south of [[e:sri-jayawardenepura-kotte|Kotte]], while his brothers took Kotte itself and the [[s:kingdom-of-sitawaka|Kingdom of Sitawaka]].
kingdom-of-raigama.r: Very little is known about government in Raigama. It was a small territory of [[e:rice|rice]] and [[e:cinnamon|cinnamon]] land between [[s:kingdom-of-kotte|Kotte]] and [[s:kingdom-of-sitawaka|Sitawaka]], and its ruler was overshadowed by his more powerful brothers.
kingdom-of-raigama.e: On [[e:raigam-bandara|Raigam Bandara's]] death in 1538 the territory was taken by [[e:mayadunne|Mayadunne]] of [[s:kingdom-of-sitawaka|Sitawaka]], and the kingdom ceased to exist.

cr.a: Original: Sri Lanka Vectorization: Zscout370, Mike Rohsopht

kingdom-of-rano.t: One of the seven original Hausa states, a small kingdom south of Kano remembered in tradition as a centre of indigo dyeing.
kingdom-of-rano.o: Little is known beyond [[e:hausa|Hausa]] tradition. Rano is counted among the [[s:hausa-kingdoms|Hausa Bakwai]], the seven states said to descend from Bawo, son of the hero [[e:bayajidda|Bayajidda]] and the queen of [[s:kingdom-of-daura|Daura]]. It occupied the plain south of [[e:kano|Kano]] and is thought to have emerged around the same time as its neighbours, by the 11th century.
kingdom-of-rano.r: In the traditional division of roles among the [[e:hausa|Hausa states]], Rano and [[e:kano|Kano]] were the 'chiefs of [[e:indigo|indigo]]', known for dyed cloth. The [[e:kano-chronicle|Kano Chronicle]] shows Rano frequently overshadowed by Kano, whose rulers at times treated it as a dependency, and its own king list is poorly recorded.
kingdom-of-rano.e: During the [[e:fulani-war|Fulani jihad]] Rano was absorbed into the [[s:kano-emirate|Kano Emirate]] around 1807, and its town became a district seat under [[e:kano|Kano]]. A separate Rano [[e:emirate|Emirate]] was created by [[e:kano-state|Kano State]] in 2019, reviving the old name.

karasids.t: A beylik on the Sea of Marmara and Aegean whose annexation gave the Ottomans the soldiers and ships to cross into Europe.
karasids.o: Around the end of the 13th century the [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] leader [[e:karesi-bey|Karesi Bey]] took the former Byzantine region of [[e:mysia|Mysia]], with [[e:balikesir|Balikesir]] and [[e:pergamon|Pergamon]], as Byzantine defences in western [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]] collapsed.
karasids.r: The Karasids raided across the [[e:hellespont|Dardanelles]] into [[e:thrace|Thrace]] and the [[e:aegean|Aegean]], sometimes as allies of Byzantine factions. [[e:ibn-battuta|Ibn Battuta]] met the ruler of [[e:pergamon|Pergamon]], [[e:yakhshi-bey|Yakhshi Bey]], in the 1330s. After [[e:karesi-bey|Karesi Bey's]] death his sons, Demirhan and Yakhshi, divided the lands and quarrelled, opening the way to Ottoman intervention. The [[e:beylik|beylik]]'s warriors and commanders, such as [[e:haci-ilbey|Haci Ilbey]] and [[e:evrenos-bey|Evrenos Bey]], later served the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]].
karasids.e: [[e:orhan|Orhan]] annexed the [[e:beylik|beylik]], a process usually dated to around 1345, though resistance continued for some years. Its manpower and [[e:hellespont|Dardanelles]] coast enabled the Ottoman crossing to [[e:gallipoli|Gallipoli]] in 1354.

kingdom-of-ihangiro.t: One of the Haya kingdoms on the western shore of Lake Victoria, ruled by a Hinda dynasty until chieftaincies were abolished in 1963.
kingdom-of-ihangiro.o: Ihangiro emerged around the 17th century in the [[e:kagera-region|Kagera region]] of north-western [[s:tanzania|Tanzania]], one of several small kingdoms of the [[e:haya-people|Haya people]]. Its royal line belonged to the [[e:hinda-dynasty|Hinda dynasty]], related to that of the [[s:kingdom-of-karagwe|Kingdom of Karagwe]], from which it is said to have broken away.
kingdom-of-ihangiro.r: The mukama (king) ruled with chiefs and clan heads over a dense farming population growing bananas, [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]] and beans on the fertile shores of [[e:lake-victoria|Lake Victoria]]. Like other [[e:haya-people|Haya]] states it had [[e:sacred-kingship|sacred kingship]] with royal drums and was active in regional trade in iron goods, coffee and barkcloth.
kingdom-of-ihangiro.e: Ihangiro came under [[s:german-east-africa|German East Africa]] in the 1890s and continued as a native authority under [[e:tanganyika-territory|British Tanganyika Territory]]. The government of independent [[s:tanganyika|Tanganyika]] abolished the chieftaincies in 1963.

kuban-cossack-host.t: The Cossack community of the Kuban, descended largely from the Zaporozhian Cossacks, which garrisoned the north-western Caucasus for Russia.
kuban-cossack-host.o: The Kuban [[e:cossacks|Cossack]] Host was formed in 1860 by merging the [[s:black-sea-cossack-host|Black Sea Cossack Host]], made up of former [[e:zaporozhian-cossacks|Zaporozhian Cossacks]] resettled on the Kuban in 1792, with part of the [[e:caucasus-line-cossack-host|Caucasus Line Cossack Host]]. It was centred on [[e:krasnodar|Yekaterinodar]], modern Krasnodar.
kuban-cossack-host.r: [[e:cossacks|Cossacks]] held land in stanitsas in return for military service, electing village atamans while the host's chief ataman was appointed by the tsar. They provided cavalry and the plastun scout units and settled lands cleared of [[e:circassians|Circassians]] after 1864. Many spoke a Ukrainian dialect, and the Kuban grew rich on grain. Their choir and traditions survive.
kuban-cossack-host.e: After 1917 the [[e:kuban-rada|Kuban Rada]] declared autonomy and allied with the [[e:white-movement|Whites]]. The [[s:russian-sfsr|Russian SFSR]] conquered the region in 1920, abolished the host and persecuted [[e:cossacks|Cossacks]]. The host was revived as a cultural and service organisation in the 1990s.

knossos.t: Leading city-state of Iron Age Crete on the site of the great Minoan palace, rival of Gortyn until the Roman conquest of 67 BCE.
knossos.o: [[s:palace-state-of-knossos|Knossos]] survived the fall of its [[e:bronze-age|Bronze Age]] palace as a town and grew again in the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]]. By the 7th century BCE it was a Dorian-speaking polis and, with [[s:gortyn|Gortyn]], one of the two strongest cities of [[e:crete|Crete]]. The Minoan past was remembered in myths of [[e:minos|Minos]] and the [[e:labyrinth|Labyrinth]].
knossos.r: Like other Cretan cities, [[s:palace-state-of-knossos|Knossos]] was ruled by annual magistrates called [[e:kosmoi|kosmoi]], with men's messes and citizen training. The seer [[e:epimenides|Epimenides]] was said to come from Knossos. Its coins showed the [[e:labyrinth|Labyrinth]] and the [[e:minotaur|Minotaur]]. In the [[e:hellenistic-period|Hellenistic period]] Knossos fought [[s:gortyn|Gortyn]] and [[s:lyttos|Lyttos]], destroying Lyttos in 220 BCE, and took part in the [[s:cretan-koinon|Cretan Koinon]].
knossos.e: [[e:rome|Rome]] conquered [[e:crete|Crete]] under [[e:quintus-caecilius-metellus-creticus|Quintus Caecilius Metellus]] between 69 and 67 BCE. [[s:gortyn|Gortyn]] became the provincial capital, while [[s:palace-state-of-knossos|Knossos]] was refounded as a Roman colony under Augustus. The Palace State of Knossos is described separately.

kazakh-assr.t: The autonomous Soviet republic of the Kazakhs within Russia, whose collectivisation brought a famine that killed over a third of the Kazakh people.
kazakh-assr.o: In August 1920 the Soviet government created the [[s:kirghiz-assr|Kirghiz ASSR]], as [[e:kazakhs|Kazakhs]] were then called by Russians, within the [[s:russian-sfsr|Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic]], with [[e:orenburg|Orenburg]] as capital, absorbing the territory of the [[s:alash-autonomy|Alash Autonomy]]. In 1925 it was renamed the Kazakh ASSR, the capital moved to [[e:kyzylorda|Kyzylorda]], and in 1929 to [[e:almaty|Alma-Ata]].
kazakh-assr.r: The republic's leaders, such as First Secretary [[e:filipp-goloshchekin|Filipp Goloshchekin]] from 1925, imposed Soviet rule on a mainly nomadic population. Collectivisation and forced settlement of nomads from 1929, combined with grain and livestock requisitioning, caused the famine of 1930 to 1933, the [[e:kazakh-famine-of-1930-1933|Asharshylyk]], in which about 1.5 million people died and many fled to [[e:china|China]] and [[e:central-asia|Central Asia]].
kazakh-assr.e: Under the 1936 Soviet constitution the republic was raised to the status of a union republic, becoming the [[s:kazakh-ssr|Kazakh SSR]].

kingdom-of-sikkim.t: A Buddhist Himalayan kingdom ruled by the Namgyal Chogyals for over three centuries until it became a state of India in 1975.
kingdom-of-sikkim.o: In 1642 three Tibetan lamas consecrated [[e:phuntsog-namgyal|Phuntsog Namgyal]] as the first Chogyal at [[e:yuksom|Yuksom]], founding a Buddhist monarchy over the [[e:bhutia|Bhutia]] and [[e:lepcha|Lepcha]] peoples. Later capitals included [[e:rabdentse|Rabdentse]] and [[e:tumlong|Tumlong]].
kingdom-of-sikkim.r: The Chogyals ruled through [[e:bhutia|Bhutia]] nobles and monasteries such as [[e:pemayangtse-monastery|Pemayangtse]], with [[e:tibetan-buddhism|Tibetan Buddhism]] as state religion. Sikkim lost territory to [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Nepal]] and [[s:zhabdrung-bhutan|Bhutan]], and in 1861 a treaty with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] made it a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]]; the capital moved to [[e:gangtok|Gangtok]] in 1894. Nepali settlers came to form a majority of the population.
kingdom-of-sikkim.e: After 1947 Sikkim became an Indian [[e:protectorate|protectorate]]. Agitation against [[e:palden-thondup-namgyal|Palden Thondup Namgyal]] in the 1970s led to a 1975 referendum that abolished the monarchy, and Sikkim became [[e:india|India's]] 22nd state.

kingdom-of-khasso.t: A Fulbe-ruled kingdom on the upper Senegal river around Medine, a key ally of the French during the siege of 1857.
kingdom-of-khasso.o: Khasso arose in the late 17th century when [[e:fula|Fulbe]] herders who had settled among [[e:mandinka|Malinke]] farmers on the upper [[e:senegal|Senegal]] created a kingdom. Its rulers came from the Diallo clan, and the population, known as the [[e:khassonke|Khassonke]], mixed Fulbe and [[e:mande-peoples|Mande]] culture and language. It lay between more powerful neighbours: [[s:kingdom-of-bundu|Bundu]] to the west and the [[s:kingdom-of-kaarta|Kingdom of Kaarta]] to the east.
kingdom-of-khasso.r: Khasso was a loose kingdom of related chiefdoms, often weakened by succession disputes. Its position on the river, by the [[e:felou-falls|Felou]] falls just above [[e:medine-mali|Medine]] at the head of navigation, made it a stage on the trade route between the coast and the upper [[e:niger-river|Niger]], and its rulers dealt with French traders from [[e:saint-louis-senegal|Saint-Louis]]. Most of the population kept traditional religion alongside a Muslim minority.
kingdom-of-khasso.e: In 1855 the French built a fort at [[e:medine-mali|Medine]] with the support of King [[e:juka-sambala|Juka Sambala]]. [[e:el-hadj-umar-tall|Umar Tall]] besieged it in 1857, but [[e:paul-holle|Paul Holl]] and Sambala held out until [[e:louis-faidherbe|Faidherbe]] arrived. Khasso became a French [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] around 1880 and was absorbed into [[s:french-sudan|French Sudan]].

cr.a: ? localisation en jaune par Ji-Elle 15:18, 28 March 2008 (UTC)

kingdom-of-loigis.t: Irish midland kingdom of the O'Mores, centred on the Rock of Dunamase, which fought the English until the plantation of Laois in 1556.
kingdom-of-loigis.o: The Loígis were a people of the Irish midlands in what is now [[e:county-laois|County Laois]], which takes its name from them. Tradition claimed they had won their lands as warriors serving the kings of the [[s:kingdom-of-leinster|Kingdom of Leinster]], and they formed a subject kingdom of Leinster from the early [[e:middle-ages|medieval period]]. From the 11th century their ruling family was the [[e:omore|Uí Mórda]], O'More.
kingdom-of-loigis.r: The kingdom was a land of bog, woodland and pasture, defended by its terrain. The [[e:rock-of-dunamase|Rock of Dunamase]] was a royal stronghold before the [[e:anglo-normans|Anglo-Normans]] took it in the late 12th century and built a castle there. From the 14th century the [[e:omore|O'Mores]] regained much of their territory, raiding the [[e:the-pale|English Pale]] and living by [[e:cattle|cattle]] and the tribute of their followers.
kingdom-of-loigis.e: Under [[e:mary-i-of-england|Mary I]] the English government confiscated Laois and [[s:kingdom-of-ui-failge|Offaly]] and in 1556 created [[e:county-laois|Queen's County]], planted with English settlers around [[e:portlaoise|Maryborough]], today Portlaoise. The [[e:omore|O'Mores]] resisted for decades, notably under [[e:rory-og-omore|Rory Óg O'More]], but their kingdom was ended.
kingdom-of-loigis.la: Old Irish, later Middle and Early Modern Irish

kamata-kingdom.t: A kingdom of western Assam and northern Bengal that grew out of ancient Kamarupa and was destroyed by the Bengal Sultanate in 1498.
kamata-kingdom.o: Kamata emerged in the 13th century from the western remains of the [[s:kamarupa|Kamarupa]] kingdom. Sandhya, a ruler based at Kamarupanagara, moved his capital west to Kamatapur after Turkic attacks around 1257, giving the kingdom its name. It then held the land between the [[e:karatoya-river|Karatoya]] and the [[e:brahmaputra|Brahmaputra]] rivers.
kamata-kingdom.r: Little is documented about government under the early kings. In the 15th century the Khen dynasty ruled from Kamatapur, near modern [[s:cooch-behar-state|Cooch Behar]], where extensive earthen ramparts survive. Its last king, [[e:nilambar|Nilambar]], controlled a large territory and defended it against the [[s:bengal-sultanate|Bengal Sultanate]]. [[e:shaktism|Shakta]] [[e:hinduism|Hinduism]] and local cults dominated.
kamata-kingdom.e: Around 1498 [[e:alauddin-husain-shah|Alauddin Husain Shah]] of the [[s:bengal-sultanate|Bengal Sultanate]] captured Kamatapur by a ruse and ended Khen rule. [[e:bengal|Bengal's]] hold proved short, and the region was soon taken by the Koch dynasty, whose kingdom later split into [[s:cooch-behar-state|Koch Bihar]] and [[s:koch-hajo|Koch Hajo]].

kingdom-of-athamania.t: Small mountain kingdom on the borders of Epirus and Thessaly whose king Amynander played the Roman, Macedonian and Seleucid powers off against each other.
kingdom-of-athamania.o: The [[e:athamanians|Athamanians]] were a people of the [[e:pindus|Pindus]] mountains around the upper Achelous, between [[e:epirus|Epirus]], [[e:thessaly|Thessaly]] and [[e:aetolia|Aetolia]]. Little is known of their early history. Under Macedonian and Epirote dominance they had their own kings, and the kingdom became visible in the later 3rd century BCE, with its royal seat at Argithea.
kingdom-of-athamania.r: Athamania was a pastoral highland realm of villages and fortified hilltop towns. Its importance came from its position on routes between [[e:thessaly|Thessaly]] and western [[e:greece|Greece]]. King [[e:amynander|Amynander]] joined [[e:rome|Rome]] against [[e:philip-v-of-macedon|Philip V of Macedon]] in 200-197 BCE and acted as an intermediary, then sided with [[e:antiochus-iii-the-great|Antiochus III]] in 191 BCE.
kingdom-of-athamania.e: Philip V overran Athamania in 191 BCE and [[e:amynander|Amynander]] fled to [[s:ambracia|Ambracia]]. With Aetolian help he recovered his kingdom in 189 BCE, but it disappears from the record soon after and was absorbed into its neighbours. Knowledge of it comes almost entirely from [[e:polybius|Polybius]] and [[e:livy|Livy]].

kel-ajjer.t: The Tuareg confederation of the Tassili n'Ajjer, based around the oasis of Ghat, which controlled caravan routes between Libya and the Sahel.
kel-ajjer.o: The Kel Ajjer emerged as a distinct confederation of the eastern [[e:tuareg|Tuareg]], occupying the [[e:tassili-najjer|Tassili n'Ajjer]] plateau and the oases of [[e:ghat|Ghat]] and [[e:djanet|Djanet]] in present-day south-eastern [[e:algeria|Algeria]] and south-western [[e:libya|Libya]]. Their organisation took shape by the 17th century.
kel-ajjer.r: The confederation was led by an amenokal from a noble lineage, presiding over noble warriors, [[e:vassal|vassal]] herders and dependent oasis farmers. [[e:ghat|Ghat]] was a key stop on the caravan route from [[s:county-of-tripoli|Tripoli]] to [[e:kano|Kano]], and the Kel Ajjer taxed and protected caravans. They fought a long war with the [[s:kel-ahaggar|Kel Ahaggar]] in the 1870s.
kel-ajjer.e: The [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] garrisoned [[e:ghat|Ghat]] from 1875, and later [[s:italian-libya|Italian Libya]] claimed it, while [[e:france|France]] took [[e:djanet|Djanet]] in 1911. Many Kel Ajjer joined the [[s:senussi-order|Senussi Order]]'s revolt against the French in 1916, which was suppressed, dividing the confederation between French and Italian rule.

kingdom-of-fortriu.t: The leading Pictish kingdom, whose kings dominated northern Britain in the 7th to 9th centuries and whose heartland is now placed around Moray.
kingdom-of-fortriu.o: Fortriu takes its name from the Verturiones, listed by [[e:ammianus-marcellinus|Ammianus Marcellinus]] in the 360s as one of the two main peoples of the [[e:picts|Picts]]. In early Irish annals 'king of Fortriu' became the title of the most powerful Pictish rulers. Long located in [[e:strathearn|Strathearn]], it is now usually placed around [[s:kingdom-of-moray|Moray]] and [[e:easter-ross|Easter Ross]], following work by Alex Woolf.
kingdom-of-fortriu.r: Kings of Fortriu built an over-kingship across [[s:kingdom-of-the-picts|Pictland]]. [[e:bridei-son-of-beli|Bridei son of Beli]] destroyed the Northumbrian army at [[e:battle-of-dun-nechtain|Dun Nechtain]] in 685, ending English dominance in the north. [[e:oengus-i-of-the-picts|Óengus son of Fergus]], from 729 to 761, defeated rivals and even campaigned against [[s:dal-riata|Dál Riata]] and Strathclyde. Major centres included the fortress of [[e:burghead|Burghead]] and the monastery of [[e:portmahomack|Portmahomack]]. Later kings such as [[e:caustantin-mac-fergusa|Constantín son of Fergus]] also ruled [[e:dal-riata|Dál Riata]].
kingdom-of-fortriu.e: In 839 a [[e:vikings|Viking]] army killed the king of Fortriu, [[e:eoganan-mac-oengusa|Eóganán]], with many nobles. In the aftermath [[e:kenneth-macalpin|Cináed mac Ailpín]] seized power, and Fortriu merged into the Gaelic kingdom of Alba around 900. The region later re-emerged as the province of [[s:kingdom-of-moray|Moray]].

cr.a: Users Angusmclellan, Angusmclellan, Angusmclellan on en.wikipedia

kingdom-of-holland.t: Napoleon's client kingdom for his brother Louis, who tried to rule as a Dutch king and was removed for defending his subjects.
kingdom-of-holland.o: In 1806 [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] replaced the [[s:batavian-republic|Batavian Republic]] with a kingdom and installed his brother [[e:louis-bonaparte|Louis Bonaparte]] as king. Louis learned [[e:dutch|Dutch]], made [[e:amsterdam|Amsterdam]] the capital and turned its town hall into a royal palace.
kingdom-of-holland.r: Louis founded the [[e:royal-netherlands-academy-of-arts-and-sciences|Royal Institute]] and a national museum, introduced a civil code and took a sympathetic line toward [[e:dutch|Dutch]] interests. He resisted conscription and enforced the [[e:continental-system|Continental System]] only loosely, which allowed smuggling with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]]. The economy suffered nonetheless, and the British landed on [[e:walcheren|Walcheren]] in 1809.
kingdom-of-holland.e: [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]], angry at Louis's independence, forced him to abdicate in July 1810, and the kingdom was annexed to the [[s:french-empire|French Empire]]. French rule ended in 1813, leading to the [[s:sovereign-principality-of-the-united-netherlands|Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands]].

kingdom-of-armenia-arsacid.t: Armenia under a branch of the Parthian Arsacid dynasty, which in the early 4th century made Christianity its state religion and later created the Armenian alphabet.
kingdom-of-armenia-arsacid.o: After the [[e:artaxiad-dynasty|Artaxiad]] line ended, [[s:armenia|Armenia]] passed through years of rival kings installed by [[e:rome|Rome]] and [[e:parthia|Parthia]]. The Arsacid branch took hold when [[e:tiridates-i-of-armenia|Tiridates I]], brother of the Parthian king, was crowned by [[e:nero|Nero]] in Rome in 66 CE, a compromise that followed the Roman defeat at [[e:battle-of-rhandeia|Rhandeia]] and let both empires claim a stake.
kingdom-of-armenia-arsacid.r: Kings ruled from [[e:artaxata|Artaxata]] and later [[e:vagharshapat|Vagharshapat]] over powerful hereditary noble houses such as the [[e:mamikonian-dynasty|Mamikonians]] and [[e:bagratuni-dynasty|Bagratunis]]. [[e:tiridates-iii-of-armenia|Tiridates III]] adopted [[e:christianity|Christianity]] around 301 through [[e:gregory-the-illuminator|Gregory the Illuminator]], and [[e:etchmiadzin-cathedral|Etchmiadzin]] cathedral was founded. Around 405 [[e:mesrop-mashtots|Mesrop Mashtots]] created the Armenian alphabet, launching a translation literature. [[s:armenia|Armenia]] was a battleground between the [[s:roman-empire|Roman Empire]] and the [[s:sasanian-empire|Sasanian Empire]].
kingdom-of-armenia-arsacid.e: In 387 [[e:rome|Rome]] and [[e:persia|Persia]] partitioned [[s:armenia|Armenia]], leaving most of it as a Sasanian client. In 428 Armenian nobles asked the Persian king to remove [[e:artaxias-iv|Artaxias IV]], and the monarchy was abolished; the east became [[s:persarmenia|Persarmenia]].

kingdom-of-wurttemberg.t: South German kingdom raised by Napoleon, which grew from a Protestant duchy into a constitutional monarchy of industry and engineering.
kingdom-of-wurttemberg.o: Elector [[e:frederick-i-of-wurttemberg|Frederick of Württemberg]] allied with [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] and was rewarded with territory and the title of king, which he proclaimed on 1 January 1806. The new kingdom doubled in size with Catholic [[e:upper-swabia|Upper Swabia]], former imperial cities and church lands.
kingdom-of-wurttemberg.r: [[e:frederick-i-of-wurttemberg|Frederick I]] ruled autocratically, but his son [[e:william-i-of-wurttemberg|William I]] granted a constitution in 1819 and promoted agriculture, founding the [[e:university-of-hohenheim|Hohenheim academy]] and the [[e:cannstatter-wasen|Cannstatter Wasen]] festival. Württemberg had a strong tradition of skilled crafts, and by the late 19th century [[e:stuttgart|Stuttgart]] was a centre of engineering, with [[e:gottlieb-daimler|Gottlieb Daimler]] and [[e:robert-bosch|Robert Bosch]]. It kept its own army and postal service in the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]].
kingdom-of-wurttemberg.e: Württemberg sided with [[e:austria|Austria]] in 1866 but joined the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]] in 1871. In November 1918 [[e:william-ii-of-wurttemberg|King William II]] abdicated, and the state became the [[s:free-peoples-state-of-wurttemberg|Free People's State of Württemberg]].

kingdom-of-arles.t: The united kingdom of Burgundy and Provence, stretching from Basel to the Mediterranean, that became the third crown of the Holy Roman emperors.
kingdom-of-arles.o: Around 933 [[e:rudolf-ii-of-burgundy|Rudolf II of Upper Burgundy]] acquired the [[s:kingdom-of-lower-burgundy|Kingdom of Lower Burgundy]] from [[e:hugh-of-arles|Hugh of Arles]], uniting the lands between the [[e:jura-mountains|Jura]] and the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]]. His son [[e:conrad-i-of-burgundy|Conrad the Peaceful]] ruled from 937 to 993 under the protection of Otto I, who had taken the young king to his court.
kingdom-of-arles.r: Royal power was weak: counts, archbishops of [[e:lyon|Lyon]], [[e:vienne|Vienne]] and [[e:arles|Arles]], and later lords such as the dauphins of [[s:dauphine-of-viennois|Viennois]] and counts of [[s:county-of-provence|Provence]] held real authority. When the childless [[e:rudolf-iii-of-burgundy|Rudolf III]] died in 1032, the kingdom passed to [[e:conrad-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Conrad II]]. [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]] was crowned at Arles in 1178 and Charles IV in 1365.
kingdom-of-arles.e: French influence grew steadily along the [[e:rhone|Rhône]]. In 1378 Charles IV made the [[e:dauphin-of-france|French Dauphin]], the future [[e:charles-vi-of-france|Charles VI]], imperial vicar of the kingdom for life, effectively ending imperial rule there. Its lands were gradually absorbed by the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]] and [[s:county-of-savoy|Savoy]].

cr.a: Blank map of Europe.svg: maix¿? derivative work: Alphathon

kingdom-of-sardinia.t: An island kingdom created for Aragon in the 14th century that passed to Savoy in 1720 and became the core of the Kingdom of Italy.
kingdom-of-sardinia.o: In 1297 [[e:pope-boniface-viii|Pope Boniface VIII]] created a Kingdom of [[e:sardinia|Sardinia]] and [[s:corsican-republic|Corsica]] for [[e:james-ii-of-aragon|James II]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-aragon|Kingdom of Aragon]]. His son Alfonso conquered the Pisan parts of the island in 1323–1324, founding the kingdom in fact.
kingdom-of-sardinia.r: Aragonese rule met long resistance from the [[s:judicate-of-arborea|Judicate of Arborea]], whose [[e:eleanor-of-arborea|Eleonora]] issued the [[e:carta-de-logu|Carta de Logu]] law code; Arborea fell in 1420. [[e:sardinia|Sardinia]] was then governed by [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroys]] at [[e:cagliari|Cagliari]], under [[e:kingdom-of-aragon|Aragon]] and [[s:habsburg-spain|Habsburg Spain]], with its own parliament. [[e:austria|Austria]] took it in 1708, and in 1720 the [[e:treaty-of-the-hague-1720|Treaty of The Hague]] gave it to [[e:victor-amadeus-ii|Victor Amadeus II]] of the [[s:duchy-of-savoy|Duchy of Savoy]], who ruled from [[e:turin|Turin]].
kingdom-of-sardinia.e: The [[s:duchy-of-savoy|Savoy]] kingdom joined [[e:piedmont|Piedmont]], Savoy and [[e:nice|Nice]]; the Perfect Fusion of 1847 unified it, and [[e:charles-albert-of-sardinia|Charles Albert]] granted the [[e:statuto-albertino|Statuto]] in 1848. Under [[e:victor-emmanuel-ii|Victor Emmanuel II]] and [[e:camillo-benso-count-of-cavour|Cavour]] it led [[e:italian-unification|Italian unification]], becoming the [[s:kingdom-of-italy|Kingdom of Italy]] in 1861.

kingdom-of-waithali.t: The second great kingdom of Arakan, whose Chandra kings left Sanskrit inscriptions and coins showing a Buddhist realm linked to Bengal and India.
kingdom-of-waithali.o: Rakhine chronicles say the capital moved from [[s:kingdom-of-dhanyawadi|Dhanyawadi]] to Waithali, a new city a short distance to the south, around 370 under King Mahataing Chandra. Its walled site near [[e:kyauktaw|Kyauktaw]] has been excavated, and the [[e:anandachandra-inscription|Anandachandra inscription]] of the early 8th century lists the kings of the dynasty.
kingdom-of-waithali.r: Waithali's rulers, known as the [[s:chandra-dynasty|Chandra dynasty]], used [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] and Indian royal styles and issued [[e:silver|silver]] coins bearing the conch and the trident-like srivatsa symbol. The kingdom traded across the [[e:bay-of-bengal|Bay of Bengal]] and patronised [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]], with [[e:mahayana-buddhism|Mahayana]] and [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] elements. The [[e:anandachandra-inscription|Anandachandra inscription]] records the king's donations to monks and [[e:brahmins|Brahmins]].
kingdom-of-waithali.e: The chronicles say Waithali declined in the 8th and 9th centuries, and in 818 power passed to a new line in the [[e:lemro-river|Lemro]] valley, opening the Lemro period of the [[s:mrauk-u-kingdom|Kingdom of Arakan]]. Waithali's ruins, with their brick walls and a large seated Buddha, survive near [[e:kyauktaw|Kyauktaw]].

kingdom-of-kampuchea-1945.t: Cambodia's first brief independence, declared by King Norodom Sihanouk under Japanese sponsorship in March 1945.
kingdom-of-kampuchea-1945.o: Following the Japanese coup against French rule in [[e:indochina|Indochina]] on 9 March 1945, [[e:norodom-sihanouk|King Norodom Sihanouk]] on 13 March annulled the treaties with [[e:france|France]] and proclaimed the independence of [[s:kingdom-of-cambodia-1953-1970|Cambodia]], renamed [[s:kingdom-of-cambodia|Kampuchea]], the [[e:khmer-empire|Khmer]] name for the country.
kingdom-of-kampuchea-1945.r: The new government abolished the French romanised script for [[e:khmer-empire|Khmer]] that had been introduced in 1943 and restored the Buddhist lunar calendar. In August 1945 the nationalist [[e:son-ngoc-thanh|Son Ngoc Thanh]], returning from [[e:japan|Japan]], became prime minister after a palace coup by his supporters and tried to resist the return of [[e:france|France]].
kingdom-of-kampuchea-1945.e: After [[e:japan|Japan's]] surrender, British and French forces arrived, and in October 1945 the French arrested [[e:son-ngoc-thanh|Son Ngoc Thanh]] and exiled him to [[e:france|France]]. [[s:kingdom-of-cambodia-1953-1970|Cambodia]] returned to the [[s:french-protectorate-of-cambodia|French protectorate of Cambodia]] as an autonomous kingdom within the [[s:french-fourth-republic|French Union]], regaining full independence in 1953.

kingdom-of-lysimachus.t: Short-lived Hellenistic kingdom of Alexander's general Lysimachus, ruling Thrace, Macedon and western Asia Minor before his death at Corupedium.
kingdom-of-lysimachus.o: After Alexander's death in 323 BCE, [[e:lysimachus|Lysimachus]] received [[e:thrace|Thrace]] as his [[e:satrapy|satrapy]] and spent years subduing the [[s:odrysian-kingdom|Odrysian Kingdom]] under [[e:seuthes-iii|Seuthes III]]. In 309 BCE he founded [[e:lysimachia|Lysimachia]] on the [[e:gallipoli|Gallipoli peninsula]] as his capital, and around 306 BCE he took the royal title with the other Successors.
kingdom-of-lysimachus.r: [[e:lysimachus|Lysimachus]] was a careful financier who built a large treasury and minted famous tetradrachms showing the deified Alexander. After the [[e:battle-of-ipsus|Battle of Ipsus]] in 301 BCE he gained most of western [[e:asia-minor|Asia Minor]], refounding [[s:ephesus|Ephesus]]. North of the [[e:balkan-mountains|Haemus]] he campaigned against the [[s:getae|Getae]], and around 292 BCE was captured by their king [[e:dromichaetes|Dromichaetes]]. In 288 BCE he and [[e:pyrrhus-of-epirus|Pyrrhus]] took [[e:kingdom-of-macedon|Macedon]], which he held alone from 285 BCE.
kingdom-of-lysimachus.e: Family murders, including the killing of his son [[e:agathocles-son-of-lysimachus|Agathocles]], alienated his supporters. [[e:seleucus-i-nicator|Seleucus I]] defeated and killed him at [[e:battle-of-corupedium|Corupedium]] in 281 BCE. His realm broke up, and [[e:thrace|Thrace]] soon fell to the Celtic invasions and the [[s:kingdom-of-tylis|Kingdom of Tylis]].

kingdom-of-fada-ngourma.t: Kingdom of the Gulmance people of eastern Burkina Faso, a neighbour and rival of the Mossi states.
kingdom-of-fada-ngourma.o: [[e:gurma-people|Gulmance]] tradition traces the ruling house to [[e:diaba-lompo|Diaba Lompo]], a hero said to have descended from the sky and founded the kingdom of Gulmu, traditionally around the 15th century. The kingdom covered the dry plains between the [[e:mossi|Mossi]] lands and the [[e:niger-river|Niger]], and its capital was eventually fixed at [[e:fada-ngourma|Fada N'Gourma]].
kingdom-of-fada-ngourma.r: The king, or Bado, presided over provincial chiefs drawn from royal lineages, with local earth-priests responsible for land and rites. The [[e:gurma-people|Gulmance]] farmed [[e:millet|millet]] and [[e:sorghum|sorghum]] and traded with [[e:hausa|Hausa]] and [[e:mossi|Mossi]] merchants. The kingdom had a loose structure and often fought the Mossi and [[e:fula|Fulani]] neighbours.
kingdom-of-fada-ngourma.e: [[e:france|France]] established a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] over Gulmu in 1895, and it became part of [[s:french-west-africa|French West Africa]] and later [[s:french-upper-volta|French Upper Volta]]. The king of [[e:fada-ngourma|Fada N'Gourma]] remains a traditional ruler in [[e:burkina-faso|Burkina Faso]].

kaitag-utsmiyate.t: A Dargin and Kumyk principality of Dagestan ruled by the utsmi, known today for its distinctive Kaitag embroideries.
kaitag-utsmiyate.o: Kaitag, in the foothills and mountains west of [[e:derbent|Derbent]], was ruled by a dynasty bearing the title utsmi from at least the 15th century. [[e:islam|Islam]] had become dominant there by then, after a long history of mixed beliefs; Arab geographers had earlier described the region as partly Christian and pagan.
kaitag-utsmiyate.r: The utsmi ruled through nobles over [[e:dargins|Dargin]] and [[e:kumyks|Kumyk]] villages from Majalis and other seats, with free communities keeping their own customs. The economy combined farming, herding and [[e:slave-raiding|slave raiding]]. Kaitag women produced [[e:silk|silk]] embroideries with bold abstract designs. Utsmi Amir Hamza captured the German naturalist [[e:samuel-gottlieb-gmelin|Samuel Gmelin]], who died in captivity in 1774.
kaitag-utsmiyate.e: The utsmiyate was a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the [[s:safavid-empire|Safavid Empire]] for long periods and later allied with or resisted [[e:russia|Russia]]. In 1820 the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] deposed the last utsmi and annexed Kaitag.

keonthal-state.t: The leading state of the Shimla hills, part of whose land was given up to the British for the hill station of Shimla in 1830.
keonthal-state.o: The ruling family claimed descent from the Sen dynasty of [[e:bengal|Bengal]]; tradition places the start of its rule around 1100. The capital was at Junga, south-east of [[e:shimla|Shimla]].
keonthal-state.r: Keonthal was the overlord of several smaller hill chiefships, including Koti, [[e:theog|Theog]] and Ratesh. [[e:gurkhas|Gurkha]] armies of the [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Kingdom of Nepal]] occupied it in the early 19th century. After 1815 the British restored the Raja, and in 1830 part of Keonthal's land was taken in exchange for other territory to create [[e:shimla|Shimla]], the later summer capital of the [[s:british-raj|British Raj]].
keonthal-state.e: Keonthal merged into [[e:himachal-pradesh|Himachal Pradesh]] in April 1948. Junga is now a village in [[e:shimla|Shimla]] district.

kingdom-of-bohemia.t: Central European kingdom centred on Prague, home of Charles IV's golden age and the Hussite revolution, and the crown at the heart of the Thirty Years War.
kingdom-of-bohemia.o: The [[e:premyslid-dynasty|Přemyslid]] dukes had ruled [[e:bohemia|Bohemia]] since the 9th century, and some held a personal royal title. In 1198 [[e:ottokar-i-of-bohemia|Ottokar I]] was crowned king, and the [[e:golden-bull-of-sicily|Golden Bull of Sicily]] of 1212 made the title hereditary. The kingdom held a special place within the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]], with its king among the [[e:prince-elector|electors]].
kingdom-of-bohemia.r: [[e:ottokar-ii-of-bohemia|Ottokar II]] extended [[e:premyslid-dynasty|Přemyslid]] rule to [[e:austria|Austria]], [[e:styria|Styria]] and [[e:carinthia|Carinthia]], and under Charles IV of the [[s:county-of-luxembourg|Luxembourg]] dynasty [[e:prague|Prague]] became an imperial capital with a university founded in 1348. The Hussite movement after [[e:jan-hus|Jan Hus's]] execution in 1415 created a reformed church and defeated several [[e:crusade|crusades]]. The [[e:lands-of-the-bohemian-crown|Lands of the Bohemian Crown]] included [[s:margraviate-of-moravia|Moravia]], [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]] and [[e:lusatia|Lusatia]]. [[e:silver|Silver]] from [[e:kutna-hora|Kutná Hora]] funded the crown, and Czech and German speakers lived side by side.
kingdom-of-bohemia.e: The [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] took the throne in 1526. The [[e:defenestration-of-prague-1618|Defenestration of Prague]] in 1618 began [[e:thirty-tyrants|the Thirty]] Years War, and defeat at the [[e:battle-of-white-mountain|White Mountain]] in 1620 brought forced [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]] and [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] absolutism. [[e:bohemia|Bohemia]] stayed a Habsburg crown land until 1918, when it became the core of [[s:czechoslovakia|Czechoslovakia]].

kingdom-of-uvea.t: The Polynesian kingdom of Wallis Island, shaped by Tongan conquest, whose king, the Lavelua, still holds customary authority under French rule.
kingdom-of-uvea.o: [[e:wallis-island|Wallis Island]], called ʻUvea by its people, was settled by [[e:polynesians|Polynesians]] around 1000 BCE. In the 15th century warriors from the [[s:tu-i-tonga-empire|Tuʻi Tonga Empire]] conquered the island, building forts such as [[e:talietumu|Talietumu]] and [[s:kingdom-of-tonga|Tonga]] Toto, and a Tongan-derived chiefly order took root. The paramount title of [[e:lavelua|Lavelua]] emerged from these struggles as the island's kingship.
kingdom-of-uvea.r: The [[e:lavelua|Lavelua]] rules with a council of ministers chosen from noble families, and the island is divided into three districts under chiefs. Society rested on yam and taro gardens, pigs and the lagoon fisheries, and on ceremonial exchanges of mats and kava. [[e:society-of-mary-marists|Marist]] missionaries led by [[e:pierre-bataillon|Pierre Bataillon]] arrived in 1837, and within a few years the entire island had become Catholic, with the church closely tied to the monarchy.
kingdom-of-uvea.e: A French [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] first requested in 1842 was formalised by Queen [[e:amelia-tokagahahau|Amelia Tokagahahau]] in 1887. Since 1961 Uvea has been one of three customary kingdoms in the French overseas collectivity of [[s:wallis-and-futuna|Wallis and Futuna]]; [[e:tomasi-kulimoetoke-ii|Tomasi Kulimoetoke II]] reigned from 1959 to 2007, and a [[e:lavelua|Lavelua]] still sits on the territorial council.

kingdom-of-kandy.t: The last independent kingdom of Sri Lanka, which kept the Portuguese, Dutch and British at bay in its central highlands for three centuries.
kingdom-of-kandy.o: [[e:kandy|Kandy]], in the central highlands, began as a sub-kingdom of the [[s:kingdom-of-kotte|Kingdom of Kotte]] in the later 15th century, under [[e:senasammata-vikramabahu|Senasammata Vikramabahu]]. After the Portuguese arrival it became a refuge of Sinhalese independence, and [[e:vimaladharmasuriya-i|Vimaladharmasuriya I]] secured its throne in the 1590s, defeating a Portuguese army at [[e:battle-of-danture|Danture]] in 1594.
kingdom-of-kandy.r: The kings guarded the [[e:relic-of-the-tooth-of-the-buddha|Tooth Relic]] in the [[e:temple-of-the-tooth|Temple of the Tooth]] at [[e:kandy|Kandy]], the symbol of Sinhalese kingship. [[e:rajasinha-ii-of-kandy|Rajasinha II]] allied with the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] to expel the Portuguese. From 1739 the [[e:nayaks-of-kandy|Nayak]] kings of south Indian origin ruled, and [[e:kirti-sri-rajasinha|Kirti Sri Rajasinha]] revived the Buddhist monastic order with monks from Siam. The hill country relied on [[e:rice|rice]] and areca, while forests and mountains defended it.
kingdom-of-kandy.e: Discontent among Kandyan nobles against [[e:sri-vikrama-rajasinha|Sri Vikrama Rajasinha]] allowed British forces to enter [[e:kandy|Kandy]] in 1815. The [[e:kandyan-convention|Kandyan Convention]] transferred [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] to the British Crown, and the kingdom became part of [[s:british-ceylon|British Ceylon]].

kingdom-of-the-isles.t: A Norse-Gaelic sea kingdom of Man and the Hebrides, ruled from the Isle of Man by the Crovan dynasty under Norwegian overlordship.
kingdom-of-the-isles.o: [[e:godred-crovan|Godred Crovan]], a [[e:norse-gaels|Norse-Gael]] who had fought at [[e:battle-of-stamford-bridge|Stamford Bridge]] in 1066, seized the [[s:isle-of-man|Isle of Man]] in 1079 after a battle at Sky Hill. His descendants ruled Man and the [[e:hebrides|Hebrides]], the Sudreys, as a kingdom under the nominal overlordship of [[e:norway|Norway]].
kingdom-of-the-isles.r: The kingdom was a maritime power of [[e:galley|galleys]] and island fortresses, with [[e:castle-rushen|Castle Rushen]] and the church at [[e:rushen-abbey|Rushen Abbey]]. Man's [[e:tynwald|Tynwald]] assembly descends from its Norse institutions. Its kings intervened in Irish and Scottish affairs. [[e:somerled|Somerled's]] revolt in 1156 took the southern [[e:hebrides|Hebrides]], leaving the Crovan line with Man, [[e:isle-of-lewis|Lewis]] and [[e:isle-of-skye|Skye]].
kingdom-of-the-isles.e: After the [[e:battle-of-largs|Battle of Largs]] in 1263, [[e:norway|Norway]] ceded Man and the Isles to the [[s:kingdom-of-scotland|Kingdom of Scotland]] by the [[e:treaty-of-perth|Treaty of Perth]] in 1266, the year after the last king, [[e:magnus-olafsson|Magnus Olafsson]], died. Man later came under English rule as the [[s:lordship-of-mann|Lordship of Mann]].

kingdom-of-jerusalem.t: The principal Crusader state, founded after the capture of Jerusalem in 1099 and ended with the fall of Acre in 1291.
kingdom-of-jerusalem.o: The [[e:first-crusade|First Crusade]] took [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]] in July 1099, massacring much of its population. [[e:godfrey-of-bouillon|Godfrey of Bouillon]] governed it as [[e:advocate-of-the-holy-sepulchre|Advocate of the Holy Sepulchre]], and on his death in 1100 his brother [[e:baldwin-i-of-jerusalem|Baldwin I]] was crowned the first king. Over the next decades the [[s:franks|Franks]] conquered the coastal cities with the help of Italian fleets.
kingdom-of-jerusalem.r: The king ruled with a [[e:haute-cour-kingdom-of-jerusalem|High Court]] of barons, and great lordships such as [[e:galilee|Galilee]], [[e:jaffa|Jaffa]] and Oultrejordain held wide powers. The [[e:knights-templar|Templars]] and [[e:knights-hospitaller|Hospitallers]] garrisoned castles, while Venetian, Genoese and Pisan communes controlled trade in [[e:acre|Acre]] and [[s:tyre|Tyre]]. Most subjects were Muslims and Eastern Christians. Under [[e:baldwin-iv-of-jerusalem|Baldwin IV]] the kingdom held off [[e:saladin|Saladin]], but in 1187 he destroyed its army at [[e:battle-of-hattin|Hattin]] and took [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]].
kingdom-of-jerusalem.e: The [[e:third-crusade|Third Crusade]] recovered the coast, and the kingdom continued from [[e:acre|Acre]]. [[e:frederick-ii|Frederick II]] regained [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]] by treaty in 1229, but it was lost for good in 1244. The [[e:mamluk|Mamluk]] sultan [[e:al-ashraf-khalil|al-Ashraf Khalil]] took Acre in May 1291, ending the kingdom; the title passed to the kings of [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]].

kingdom-of-kakheti.t: The eastern Georgian kingdom of Kakheti, a land of vineyards and silk routes that suffered terribly under Shah Abbas before uniting with Kartli in 1762.
kingdom-of-kakheti.o: In 1465, amid the disintegration of the [[s:kingdom-of-georgia|Kingdom of Georgia]], George I, a prince of the royal [[e:bagrationi-dynasty|Bagratid]] house, made [[s:principality-of-kakheti|Kakheti]] a separate kingdom. Its independence was confirmed when [[s:georgia|Georgia]] split into three kingdoms in 1490. His line, a branch of the Bagratids, held the throne of Kakheti for almost three centuries.
kingdom-of-kakheti.r: [[s:principality-of-kakheti|Kakheti]] prospered on wine, [[e:silk|silk]] and the caravan trade between [[s:shirvanshah-state|Shirvan]] and [[e:russia|Russia]]; King Levan built a royal residence at [[e:gremi|Gremi]]. The kings balanced between the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] and the [[s:safavid-empire|Safavid Empire]]. [[e:teimuraz-i-of-kakheti|Teimuraz I]]'s resistance provoked [[e:abbas-i-of-persia|Shah Abbas I]] to devastate the country in 1616, deporting many thousands of Kakhetians to [[e:iran|Iran]]; Teimuraz's mother [[e:ketevan-the-martyr|Ketevan]] was martyred in 1624.
kingdom-of-kakheti.e: [[s:principality-of-kakheti|Kakheti]] endured Persian governors and [[e:lezgins|Lezgin]] raids. [[e:erekle-ii|Erekle II]] became king in 1744, and on his father [[e:teimuraz-ii-of-kakheti|Teimuraz II]]'s death in 1762 he united Kakheti with [[s:kingdom-of-kartli|Kartli]] as the [[s:kingdom-of-kartli-kakheti|Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti]].

karabakh-khanate.t: A khanate founded by Panah Ali Khan in Karabakh, whose fortress capital Shusha withstood Agha Muhammad Khan Qajar and became a cultural centre.
karabakh-khanate.o: After [[e:nader-shah|Nader Shah's]] death in 1747, [[e:panah-ali-khan|Panah Ali Khan]] of the [[e:javanshir|Javanshir]] tribe returned from exile and made himself khan of [[e:karabakh|Karabakh]]. He built a series of fortresses and in the 1750s founded [[e:shusha|Shusha]] on a mountain plateau, while forcing the Armenian [[s:melikdoms-of-karabakh|Melikdoms of Karabakh]] to accept his authority.
karabakh-khanate.r: The khanate ruled over Turkic tribal groups in the lowlands and Armenian villages in the highlands. [[e:ibrahim-khalil-khan|Ibrahim Khalil Khan]], from 1763, was a powerful ruler, and his [[e:vizier|vizier]], the poet [[e:molla-panah-vagif|Molla Panah Vagif]], shaped court culture. In 1795 [[e:shusha|Shusha]] withstood a siege by [[e:agha-mohammad-khan-qajar|Agha Muhammad Khan Qajar]], who in 1797 took the town but was murdered there.
karabakh-khanate.e: In 1805 [[e:ibrahim-khalil-khan|Ibrahim Khalil Khan]] signed the [[e:treaty-of-kurekchay|Treaty of Kurekchay]] accepting Russian suzerainty. His son [[e:mehdi-qoli-khan|Mehdi Qoli Khan]] fled to [[e:persia|Persia]] in 1822, and the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] abolished the khanate.

kingdom-of-salamis.t: The leading city-kingdom of ancient Cyprus, whose king Evagoras I united much of the island and defied the Persian Empire for a decade.
kingdom-of-salamis.o: Salamis was founded on the east coast of [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]] in the 11th century BCE, succeeding nearby [[e:enkomi|Enkomi]] as its harbour silted up. Greek tradition named [[e:teucer|Teucer]], brother of [[e:ajax-the-great|Ajax]], as its founder. Its royal tombs of the 8th and 7th centuries BCE, with [[e:chariot|chariots]] and sacrificed horses, recall Homeric burial customs.
kingdom-of-salamis.r: The kings of Salamis were often the most powerful on [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]]. [[e:evelthon|Evelthon]] struck some of the island's earliest coins in the 6th century BCE, and [[e:onesilus|Onesilus]] led the Cypriot revolt against [[e:persia|Persia]] in 498 BCE. [[e:evagoras-i|Evagoras I]], who reigned from 411 to 374 BCE, promoted Greek culture, allied with [[s:athens|Athens]] and fought the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]] until a negotiated peace in 380 BCE.
kingdom-of-salamis.e: The last king, [[e:nicocreon|Nicocreon]], allied with [[e:ptolemy-i-soter|Ptolemy I]] and died c. 310 BCE, and in 306 BCE [[e:demetrius-i-of-macedon|Demetrius Poliorcetes]] won a great naval battle off Salamis. The kingdom then passed under the [[s:ptolemaic-empire|Ptolemaic Empire]]. Salamis remained a major city, renamed [[e:salamis-cyprus|Constantia]], until abandoned after the Arab raids of the 7th century CE.

kingdom-of-haiti.t: Henri Christophe's northern Haitian monarchy, with a new nobility, the palace of Sans-Souci and the colossal Citadelle Laferrière.
kingdom-of-haiti.o: The [[s:state-of-haiti|State of Haiti]] in the north became a kingdom in March 1811, when a council of state proclaimed [[e:henri-christophe|Henri Christophe]] king. He was crowned Henri I at [[e:cap-haitien|Cap-Haïtien]], renamed Cap-Henri, in June 1811, while [[e:alexandre-petion|Alexandre Pétion's]] [[s:republic-of-haiti-1806-1849|Republic of Haiti]] continued to rule the south and west.
kingdom-of-haiti.r: Henri created a hereditary nobility of dukes, counts and barons, a royal army and a legal code, the [[e:code-henry|Code Henry]]. Plantation labour was enforced to keep [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] and [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]] exports high, making the kingdom relatively wealthy. He built the palace of [[e:sans-souci-palace|Sans-Souci]] at [[e:milot|Milot]] and the [[e:citadelle-laferriere|Citadelle Laferrière]] on a mountaintop against a feared French return, and he invited English teachers to found schools. [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]] was the state religion.
kingdom-of-haiti.e: In August 1820 Henri suffered a stroke; troops mutinied and he shot himself on 8 October 1820. [[e:jean-pierre-boyer|Jean-Pierre Boyer]] then reunited the north with the [[s:republic-of-haiti-1806-1849|Republic of Haiti]]. The [[e:citadelle-laferriere|Citadelle]] and [[e:sans-souci-palace|Sans-Souci]] are now a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]].

khoshut-khanate.t: The Oirat Mongol khanate that conquered Tibet for the Fifth Dalai Lama in 1642 and whose khans held the title King of Tibet until the Dzungar invasion of 1717.
khoshut-khanate.o: [[e:gushi-khan|Güshi Khan]], a chief of the Khoshut, one of the [[s:four-oirat|Four Oirat]], answered an appeal from [[e:gelug|Gelug]] leaders threatened by their rivals. He moved to the [[e:qinghai-lake|Kokonor]] region, defeated the [[e:khalkha-mongols|Khalkha]] prince [[e:tsogt-taij|Choghtu Khong Tayiji]] in 1637, subdued the king of Beri in [[e:kham|Kham]] in 1640 and overthrew the [[s:tsangpa-dynasty|Tsangpa dynasty]] in 1642.
khoshut-khanate.r: [[e:gushi-khan|Güshi Khan]] took the title King of [[s:tibet-1912-1951|Tibet]] but handed civil and religious authority to the [[e:5th-dalai-lama|Fifth Dalai Lama]] in the [[s:ganden-phodrang|Ganden Phodrang]], keeping military power and protecting the [[e:gelug|Gelug]]. Khoshut nomads settled around [[e:qinghai-lake|Kokonor]], while the khans spent part of the year near [[e:lhasa|Lhasa]]. The relationship produced a joint government in which the khan's real influence varied with each generation.
khoshut-khanate.e: [[e:lhazang-khan|Lhazang Khan]] killed the regent [[e:sangye-gyatso|Sangye Gyatso]] in 1705 and deposed the Sixth [[e:dalai-lama|Dalai Lama]], making many [[e:tibetans|Tibetans]] hostile. In 1717 the [[s:dzungar-khanate|Dzungar Khanate]] invaded and killed him. The [[s:qing-empire|Qing Empire]] expelled the [[e:dzungars|Dzungars]] in 1720 and crushed a Khoshut revolt in [[e:qinghai-lake|Kokonor]] in 1723 to 1724.

kingdom-of-liaodong-206-bc.t: A remote north-eastern kingdom given to the deposed Yan king Han Guang in 206 BCE, who was killed within months for refusing to leave his old realm.
kingdom-of-liaodong-206-bc.o: [[e:han-guang|Han Guang]], once a commander sent north by [[e:wu-chen|Wu Chen]], the rebel king of Zhao, had made himself king of Yan during the rising against the [[s:qin-dynasty|Qin dynasty]]. In [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu's]] settlement of 206 BCE he was demoted to King of [[e:liaodong|Liaodong]], a distant territory beyond the [[e:liao-river|Liao River]] with its capital at Wuzhong, while his general [[e:zang-tu|Zang Tu]] received Yan.
kingdom-of-liaodong-206-bc.r: [[e:han-guang|Han Guang]] refused to give up Yan and move to [[e:liaodong|Liaodong]], so the kingdom hardly functioned as a separate state.
kingdom-of-liaodong-206-bc.e: Later in 206 BCE [[e:zang-tu|Zang Tu]] attacked and killed [[e:han-guang|Han Guang]] at Wuzhong and annexed [[e:liaodong|Liaodong]] to Yan (206 BC).

khorshidi-dynasty.t: The atabegs of Lesser Luristan who ruled from Khorramabad for four centuries until Shah Abbas I ended their line.
khorshidi-dynasty.o: [[e:shuja-al-din-khurshid|Shuja al-Din Khurshid]], a [[e:lurs|Lur]] chief, took control of Lur-i Kuchik (Lesser Luristan), the mountains north of the [[e:karkheh-river|Karkheh]], around 1184, as the [[s:seljuk-sultanate-of-iraq|Seljuk Sultanate of Iraq]] declined. His family, the Khurshidids, ruled the region from the fortress town of [[e:khorramabad|Khorramabad]].
khorshidi-dynasty.r: The atabegs governed a society of semi-nomadic [[e:lurs|Lur]] tribes who moved between summer and winter pastures, collecting tribute in livestock and controlling the routes between [[e:mesopotamia|Mesopotamia]] and the [[e:iranian-plateau|Iranian plateau]]. They submitted in turn to the [[s:ilkhanate|Ilkhanate]], the [[s:timurid-empire|Timurid Empire]] and the [[s:safavid-empire|Safavid Empire]], which recognised them as governors (valis). The fortress of [[e:falak-ol-aflak|Falak-ol-Aflak]] at [[e:khorramabad|Khorramabad]] was their seat.
khorshidi-dynasty.e: In 1597 [[e:abbas-i-of-persia|Shah Abbas I]] had the last atabeg, [[e:shahverdi-khan-khorshidi|Shahverdi Khan]], executed and replaced the dynasty with the Safavid-appointed valis of Luristan, a related family who ruled into the 20th century.

koga-kubo.t: A branch of the Ashikaga that ruled from Koga in the Kanto for over a century, fighting the Uesugi and later becoming clients of the Later Hojo.
koga-kubo.o: [[e:ashikaga-shigeuji|Ashikaga Shigeuji]], the restored [[s:kamakura-fu|Kamakura kubo]], killed the [[e:kanto-region|Kanto]] deputy [[e:uesugi-noritada|Uesugi Noritada]] in 1454, starting the long [[e:kyotoku-war|Kyotoku War]]. In 1455 he lost [[e:kamakura|Kamakura]] and moved his base to [[e:koga-ibaraki|Koga]] in [[e:shimosa-province|Shimousa]] province, from which his line took its name. The [[e:shogun|shogun]] sent a rival, [[e:ashikaga-masatomo|Ashikaga Masatomo]], who became the Horigoe kubo.
koga-kubo.r: The [[e:koga-ibaraki|Koga]] kubo claimed authority over the eastern provinces and relied on alliances with local warrior families of the northern and eastern [[e:kanto-region|Kanto]]. Shigeuji fought the Uesugi for nearly thirty years. Later kubo, [[e:ashikaga-masauji|Masauji]], [[e:ashikaga-takamoto|Takamoto]] and [[e:ashikaga-haruuji|Haruuji]], were drawn into family feuds and the rise of the Later Hojo, who married into the line and controlled it.
koga-kubo.e: The last kubo, [[e:ashikaga-yoshiuji|Ashikaga Yoshiuji]], was a Hojo puppet; on his death in 1583 the line ended. [[e:toyotomi-hideyoshi|Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] later gave his daughter's family a small estate as the Kitsuregawa.

kingdom-of-isandra.t: A Betsileo kingdom of the southern Malagasy highlands, a strong regional power before its absorption by the Merina early in the 19th century.
kingdom-of-isandra.o: Isandra emerged in the 18th century as one of the four main [[e:betsileo|Betsileo]] kingdoms of the southern highlands of [[e:madagascar|Madagascar]], west of the [[s:kingdom-of-lalangina|Kingdom of Lalangina]]. Its dynasty, like other Betsileo houses, claimed descent from noble immigrants, and much of its history survives only in oral tradition.
kingdom-of-isandra.r: Isandra's kings ruled through local lords over [[e:rice|rice]]-farming communities in highland valleys and drew prestige from ancestral tombs and royal rituals. The kingdom was considered among the strongest of the [[e:betsileo|Betsileo]] states and fought its neighbours for land, [[e:cattle|cattle]] and captives.
kingdom-of-isandra.e: Around 1811 the [[s:merina-kingdom|Merina Kingdom]] absorbed Isandra together with the other [[e:betsileo|Betsileo]] kingdoms, partly through alliances with local nobles. Its territory became part of the Merina province of Betsileo.

kingdom-of-burundi.t: A Great Lakes kingdom ruled by the Ganwa princes for nearly three centuries, which reached independence as a monarchy before being overthrown in 1966.
kingdom-of-burundi.o: Tradition names [[e:ntare-i-of-burundi|Ntare I Rushatsi]] as founder of Burundi's royal line in the late 17th century, uniting chiefdoms in the hills east of [[e:lake-tanganyika|Lake Tanganyika]]. The kingdom expanded greatly under [[e:ntare-iv-rugamba|Ntare IV Rugamba]] in the early 19th century, absorbing parts of the [[s:kingdom-of-bugesera|Kingdom of Bugesera]] and other neighbours.
kingdom-of-burundi.r: The mwami (king) was a sacred ruler, but much power lay with the ganwa, princes of royal blood who governed provinces and often fought each other. Society included [[e:hutu|Hutu]] farmers, Tutsi herders and [[e:great-lakes-twa|Twa]], with royal rituals such as the annual muganuro [[e:sorghum|sorghum]] festival. [[e:mwezi-iv-gisabo|Mwezi IV Gisabo]] resisted German forces until the [[e:treaty-of-kiganda|Treaty of Kiganda]] in 1903.
kingdom-of-burundi.e: Burundi became part of [[s:german-east-africa|German East Africa]] and then [[s:ruanda-urundi|Belgian Ruanda-Urundi]]. It gained independence in 1962 as a kingdom under [[e:mwambutsa-iv|Mwambutsa IV]], but political violence followed, and in 1966 [[e:michel-micombero|Michel Micombero]] deposed [[e:ntare-v-of-burundi|Ntare V]] and proclaimed the [[s:republic-of-burundi|Republic of Burundi]].

kingdom-of-leinster.t: Province-kingdom of south-east Ireland, whose exiled king Diarmait Mac Murchada invited the Anglo-Normans in and so opened eight centuries of English involvement.
kingdom-of-leinster.o: The Laigin, the people of Leinster, appear in the earliest Irish traditions as a major power whose kings once held the midlands and [[e:hill-of-tara|Tara]]. From the 5th century the rising [[e:ui-neill|Uí Néill]] drove them south, and Leinster settled into an over-kingdom covering most of the south-east, contested between dynasties such as the [[e:ui-dunlainge|Uí Dúnlainge]] in the north and the [[s:ui-chennselaig|Ui Chennselaig]] in the south.
kingdom-of-leinster.r: Kings ruled through tribute and alliances with subject peoples, and great monasteries such as [[e:kildare|Kildare]], [[e:glendalough|Glendalough]] and [[e:ferns|Ferns]] flourished. [[e:brandub-mac-echach|Brandub mac Echach]] defeated the high king at [[e:battle-of-dun-bolg|Dún Bolg]] in 598. [[e:vikings|Viking]] [[e:dublin|Dublin]] lay within Leinster, and from the 11th century its kings sought to control it; [[e:diarmait-mac-mael-na-mbo|Diarmait mac Máel na mBó]], who died in 1072, ruled Dublin and nearly became high king.
kingdom-of-leinster.e: In 1166 [[e:diarmait-mac-murchada|Diarmait Mac Murchada]] was expelled and sought help from [[e:henry-ii-of-england|Henry II]]. [[e:anglo-normans|Anglo-Norman]] knights led by [[e:richard-de-clare-2nd-earl-of-pembroke|Strongbow]], who married Diarmait's daughter [[e:aoife-macmurrough|Aoife]], took [[e:wexford|Wexford]], [[e:waterford|Waterford]] and [[e:dublin|Dublin]]. On Diarmait's death in 1171 Strongbow claimed Leinster, and Henry II's arrival brought it under the English crown.

kingdom-of-kanongesha.t: The Ndembu Lunda chiefdom of the upper Zambezi watershed, an outpost of Lunda kingship later made famous by anthropological studies of its rituals.
kingdom-of-kanongesha.o: The Kanongesha title was established in the 18th century by [[e:lunda-empire|Lunda]] nobles who moved south-west from the court of the [[s:lunda-empire|Lunda Empire]] into the headwaters of the [[e:zambezi|Zambezi]] and [[e:kabompo-river|Kabompo]] rivers. They settled among local peoples who became known as the [[e:ndembu-people|Ndembu]] or Southern Lunda.
kingdom-of-kanongesha.r: The Kanongesha held senior rank over [[e:ndembu-people|Ndembu]] sub-chiefs, but his power was limited and largely ritual, rooted in [[e:lunda-empire|Lunda]] titles, perpetual kinship between offices, and ties to the [[e:mwata-yamvo|Mwata Yamvo]]. Villages farmed [[e:cassava|cassava]] and hunted, and in the 19th century the area supplied slaves, [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and beeswax to [[e:ovimbundu|Ovimbundu]] and [[e:chokwe|Chokwe]] traders.
kingdom-of-kanongesha.e: Colonial boundaries drawn in the early 20th century divided the [[e:ndembu-people|Ndembu]] between [[s:northern-rhodesia|Northern Rhodesia]], [[s:portuguese-angola|Portuguese Angola]] and the [[s:belgian-congo|Belgian Congo]]. The chieftaincy continues in [[e:zambia|Zambia]], and [[e:victor-turner|Victor Turner's]] studies of Ndembu ritual in the 1950s made it well known.

kuwana-domain.t: A domain on the Tokaido road in Ise, guarding the sea crossing to Atsuta, whose last lord fought to the end for the shogunate.
kuwana-domain.o: After [[e:battle-of-sekigahara|Sekigahara]], [[e:tokugawa-ieyasu|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] gave [[e:kuwana|Kuwana]] to his famous general [[e:honda-tadakatsu|Honda Tadakatsu]] in 1601 with 100,000 koku. Tadakatsu rebuilt the castle and laid out the town at the mouth of the Ibi and [[e:kiso-river|Kiso]] rivers.
kuwana-domain.r: [[e:kuwana|Kuwana]] was the landing point of the Shichiri no watashi, the ferry across [[e:ise-bay|Ise Bay]] on the [[e:tokaido|Tokaido]], making it a busy post town. The domain was held by trusted Tokugawa [[e:vassal|vassal]] and related families, which were moved in and out; from 1823 it was ruled by the Hisamatsu-Matsudaira. Its last lord, [[e:matsudaira-sadaaki|Matsudaira Sadaaki]], served as [[e:kyoto|Kyoto]] deputy alongside his brother [[e:matsudaira-katamori|Matsudaira Katamori]] of [[e:aizu|Aizu]].
kuwana-domain.e: [[e:kuwana|Kuwana]] troops fought at [[e:battle-of-toba-fushimi|Toba-Fushimi]] in 1868, and Sadaaki continued the struggle in the north and [[e:hakodate|Hakodate]] while the domain surrendered. After abolition in 1871 it became part of [[e:mie-prefecture|Mie Prefecture]].

korea-under-japanese-rule.t: Korea's thirty-five years as a Japanese colony, a period of harsh rule, forced assimilation and uneven modernisation that still shapes relations in East Asia.
korea-under-japanese-rule.o: After making the [[s:korean-empire|Korean Empire]] a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] in 1905, [[e:japan|Japan]] formally annexed [[e:korea|Korea]] by treaty in August 1910. A Government-General headed by a governor-general, always a senior army or navy officer, was established at [[e:seoul|Keijo]], the Japanese name for Seoul.
korea-under-japanese-rule.r: Early rule relied on military police; a land survey transferred much land to the colonial state and Japanese companies. The nationwide [[e:march-first-movement|March First Movement]] of 1919 was suppressed, but Governor-General [[e:saito-makoto|Saito Makoto]] then allowed limited press and associations. Railways, ports and northern heavy industry grew to serve [[e:japan|Japan]]. From the late 1930s [[e:koreans|Koreans]] were forced to worship at [[e:shinto|Shinto]] shrines and adopt Japanese names, and many were conscripted for labour, military service and sexual [[e:slavery|slavery]].
korea-under-japanese-rule.e: [[e:japan|Japan's]] surrender on 15 August 1945 ended colonial rule. [[e:korea|Korea]] was divided at the 38th parallel between Soviet and [[e:occupation-of-japan|American occupation]], leading to two Korean states in 1948.

kashmir-sultanate.t: The Muslim sultanate of the Kashmir valley founded by Shah Mir, under which the region became predominantly Muslim.
kashmir-sultanate.o: [[e:shah-mir|Shah Mir]], a migrant from the north-west, rose to prominence at the court of the last [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] rulers of [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]]. After the death of Queen Kota [[s:rani|Rani]], he seized the throne in 1339, taking the title Shams al-Din, and founded the Shah Mir dynasty at Srinagar.
kashmir-sultanate.r: Under the Shah [[e:miri|Miris]] [[e:islam|Islam]] spread widely, encouraged by [[e:sufism|Sufi]] missionaries such as [[e:mir-sayyid-ali-hamadani|Mir Sayyid Ali Hamadani]], who brought Persian crafts including shawl-weaving and papier-mache. [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:sikandar-lodi|Sikandar]] is remembered for destroying temples, while [[e:zain-ul-abidin|Zain al-Abidin]], known as Budshah, the great king, restored tolerance, recalled [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] [[e:kashmiri-pandits|Pandits]], had [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] works translated into Persian and built canals and bridges.
kashmir-sultanate.e: After [[e:zain-ul-abidin|Zain al-Abidin]] the dynasty declined amid noble factions. The Mughal commander [[e:mirza-muhammad-haidar-dughlat|Mirza Haidar Dughlat]] ruled [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]] from 1540 to 1551, and in 1561 the [[s:chak-dynasty|Chak dynasty]] took the throne, ending [[e:shah-mir|Shah Mir]] rule. The [[s:mughal-empire|Mughal Empire]] annexed Kashmir in 1586.

kingdom-of-aboh.t: An Igbo river kingdom near the head of the Niger Delta whose canoe fleets controlled trade on the lower Niger in the era of palm oil.
kingdom-of-aboh.o: Aboh was founded, according to tradition, in the 17th or early 18th century by migrants from the area of the [[s:benin-empire|Benin Empire]], who settled at the point where the [[e:niger-river|Niger]] divides into the creeks of the delta. Ruled by an Obi in a style influenced by [[e:benin-empire|Benin]], it grew into the strongest power on the lower river.
kingdom-of-aboh.r: The Obi ruled with titled chiefs, and the kingdom commanded fleets of large war and trading canoes. Aboh was a middleman between the hinterland and the coastal states such as the [[s:bonny-kingdom|Bonny Kingdom]], carrying slaves and later [[e:palm-oil|palm oil]] downstream. [[e:obi-ossai|Obi Ossai]] received the explorers Richard and [[e:john-lander|John Lander]] in 1830 and negotiated with the British [[e:niger-river|Niger]] Expedition of 1841.
kingdom-of-aboh.e: British and company steamers in the late 19th century broke the river middlemen, and the [[s:royal-niger-company-territories|Royal Niger Company]] dominated trade. Aboh was absorbed into the [[s:protectorate-of-southern-nigeria|Protectorate of Southern Nigeria]] by 1900, and the Obi of Aboh continues as a traditional ruler in Delta State.

kingdom-of-kangaba.t: The small Mandinka kingdom on the upper Niger from which Sundiata Keita built the Mali Empire.
kingdom-of-kangaba.o: [[e:kangaba|Kangaba]] was one of several [[e:mandinka|Malinke]] chiefdoms of the [[e:manding|Manden]], the upland country along the upper [[e:niger-river|Niger]] near today's border of [[e:mali|Mali]] and [[e:guinea|Guinea]]. By the 11th century the [[e:keita-dynasty|Keita clan]] ruled there, and it lay within the orbit of the [[s:ghana-empire|Ghana Empire]], supplying gold from the nearby [[e:bure|Bure]] fields.
kingdom-of-kangaba.r: Its kings were hunters' and warriors' chiefs with a council of clan heads, and [[e:griots|griots]] kept their genealogies. Tradition names [[e:maghan-kon-fatta|Maghan Kon Fatta]] as the father of [[e:sundiata-keita|Sundiata]]. In the early 13th century the [[e:manding|Manden]] fell under the [[s:sosso-kingdom|Sosso kingdom]] of [[e:sumanguru-kante|Sumanguru Kante]], who killed or scattered the [[e:keita-dynasty|Keita]] princes.
kingdom-of-kangaba.e: [[e:sundiata-keita|Sundiata Keita]] returned from exile, united the [[e:mande-peoples|Mande]] clans and defeated [[e:sumanguru-kante|Sumanguru]] at [[e:battle-of-kirina|Kirina]] around 1235, founding the [[s:mali-empire|Mali Empire]]. [[e:kangaba|Kangaba]] remained the [[e:keita-dynasty|Keita]] heartland, and its [[e:kamabolon|Kamabolon]] sanctuary is still re-roofed every seven years in a ceremony recognised by [[e:unesco|UNESCO]].

kingdom-of-vaspurakan.t: An Armenian kingdom around Lake Van ruled by the Artsruni dynasty, best known for the sculpted Church of the Holy Cross on Aghtamar island.
kingdom-of-vaspurakan.o: The Artsruni family had long held the lands south and east of [[e:lake-van|Lake Van]]. In 908 the [[e:sajid-dynasty|Sajid]] emir Yusuf crowned [[e:gagik-i-of-vaspurakan|Gagik Artsruni]] king as a rival to [[e:smbat-i-of-armenia|Smbat I of Bagratid Armenia]], creating a separate kingdom under [[s:sajid-emirate|Sajid Emirate]] overlordship.
kingdom-of-vaspurakan.r: [[e:gagik-i-of-vaspurakan|Gagik I]] built a palace and the [[e:cathedral-of-the-holy-cross-aghtamar|Church of the Holy Cross]] on Aghtamar island between 915 and 921, its walls carved with biblical scenes, vines and royal portraits. The kingdom was rich in farmland, fish and trade, and kept a lively literary culture; the History of the House of Artsruni was written there. Its kings alternated between rivalry and alliance with the [[e:bagratuni-dynasty|Bagratids]].
kingdom-of-vaspurakan.e: Facing Seljuk raids, King [[e:senekerim-hovhannes-artsruni|Senekerim-Hovhannes]] ceded Vaspurakan to the [[s:byzantine-empire|Byzantine Empire]] in 1021 in exchange for estates around [[e:sivas|Sebasteia]], and many [[e:armenians|Armenians]] followed him west. The [[e:cathedral-of-the-holy-cross-aghtamar|Aghtamar]] church survives, restored in 2007, as the kingdom's most celebrated monument.

kenya-colony.t: The British settler colony in Kenya, shaped by land alienation in the White Highlands and shaken by the Mau Mau uprising.
kenya-colony.o: In 1920 [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] annexed the interior of the [[s:east-africa-protectorate|East Africa Protectorate]] as Kenya Colony, while the coastal strip, still nominally under the [[s:sultanate-of-zanzibar|Sultanate of Zanzibar]], became the Kenya [[e:protectorate|Protectorate]]. Annexation gave the white settler community, concentrated in the central highlands, more political weight. Nairobi remained the capital.
kenya-colony.r: Europeans held the best farmland and dominated the legislative council, while Africans faced taxes, pass laws and restrictions on growing [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]]. Indians campaigned for equal rights. African political protest began with [[e:harry-thuku|Harry Thuku]] in 1921 and grew through [[e:kikuyu-people|Kikuyu]] associations. The [[e:mau-mau-rebellion|Mau Mau uprising]] from 1952 led to a state of emergency under Governor [[e:evelyn-baring-1st-baron-howick-of-glendale|Evelyn Baring]] and mass detention.
