kenya-colony.e: The emergency ended in 1960, and the [[e:lancaster-house|Lancaster House]] conferences opened the way to majority rule. [[s:kenya|Kenya]] became independent on 12 December 1963 under [[e:jomo-kenyatta|Jomo Kenyatta]], who had been imprisoned during the emergency.

kingdom-of-lower-burgundy.t: The kingdom of Provence founded by Boso in 879, the first realm in the Carolingian West to elect a king from outside the Carolingian family.
kingdom-of-lower-burgundy.o: In 879, after the death of [[e:louis-the-stammerer|Louis the Stammerer]], [[e:bishop|bishops]] and nobles meeting at Mantaille elected [[e:boso-of-provence|Boso]], a brother-in-law of [[e:charles-the-bald|Charles the Bald]], as king of the lands around [[e:vienne|Vienne]], [[e:lyon|Lyon]] and [[s:county-of-provence|Provence]]. The Carolingian kings besieged Vienne in 880–882, but Boso's family kept control of the [[e:rhone|Rhône]] valley.
kingdom-of-lower-burgundy.r: The kingdom was a loose union of counties along the [[e:rhone|Rhône]] and in [[s:county-of-provence|Provence]], governed from [[e:vienne|Vienne]] with strong support from the [[e:bishop|bishops]]. [[e:boso-of-provence|Boso]]'s son [[e:louis-the-blind|Louis the Blind]] was crowned emperor in [[e:rome|Rome]] in 901 but was captured and blinded by [[e:berengar-i-of-italy|Berengar of Italy]] in 905. Afterwards real power lay with his kinsman [[e:hugh-of-arles|Hugh of Arles]].
kingdom-of-lower-burgundy.e: [[e:hugh-of-arles|Hugh of Arles]], busy with his ambitions as king of [[e:italy|Italy]], gave up his claims to [[e:rudolf-ii-of-burgundy|Rudolf II of Upper Burgundy]] around 933. The two Burgundian kingdoms were then united as the [[s:kingdom-of-arles|Kingdom of Arles]], which later passed to the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]].

kingdom-of-awsan.t: A short-lived south Arabian kingdom in Wadi Markha whose power over the coast was broken by Saba in the 7th century BCE.
kingdom-of-awsan.o: Awsan lay in [[e:wadi-markha|Wadi Markha]], south-west of the [[e:incense|incense]] valleys, with its capital at Hagar Yahirr. Known mainly from Sabaean inscriptions, it seems to have risen in the 8th century BCE and controlled territory towards the [[e:gulf-of-aden|Gulf of Aden]] coast and its harbours.
kingdom-of-awsan.r: Very little is known of its internal life. Its wealth probably came from coastal trade and the routes linking the [[e:arabian-sea|Arabian Sea]] with the inland [[e:incense|incense]] kingdoms. Later Awsanite inscriptions show kings who were honoured as gods after death, an unusual practice in south [[e:arabia|Arabia]].
kingdom-of-awsan.e: The Sabaean ruler [[e:karibil-watar|Karib'il Watar]] destroyed Awsan in the 7th century BCE, according to his great inscription at [[e:sirwah|Sirwah]], killing thousands and handing its lands to the [[s:kingdom-of-saba|Kingdom of Saba]] and its allies. A smaller Awsan reappeared later, and the Greek name of the Ausanitic coast of [[e:east-africa|East Africa]] recalls it.

kalachuris-of-kalyani.t: A short-lived dynasty that seized the Western Chalukya capital of Kalyani, remembered for the rise of the Lingayat movement under Basava.
kalachuris-of-kalyani.o: The Kalachuris were feudatories of the [[s:western-chalukya-empire|Chalukyas of Kalyani]] holding territory in the northern [[e:deccan|Deccan]]. As [[e:chalukya-dynasty|Chalukya]] power weakened, their chief [[e:bijjala-ii|Bijjala II]], a commander and minister of the Chalukya king [[e:tailapa-iii|Taila III]], took control of the capital [[e:basavakalyan|Kalyani]] around 1156 and by 1162 proclaimed himself emperor.
kalachuris-of-kalyani.r: The dynasty ruled much of the former [[e:chalukya-dynasty|Chalukya]] realm in northern [[e:karnataka|Karnataka]]. Its reign coincided with the career of [[e:basava|Basava]], a minister at [[e:bijjala-ii|Bijjala]]'s court, who led the [[e:lingayatism|Virashaiva]] or Lingayat reform movement, rejecting [[e:caste|caste]] hierarchy and temple ritual and promoting vachana poetry in [[e:kannada|Kannada]]. Tensions between the movement and orthodox society led to unrest in [[e:basavakalyan|Kalyani]].
kalachuris-of-kalyani.e: [[e:bijjala-ii|Bijjala]] was killed around 1167, and his sons ruled weakly amid revolts. In 1184 the [[e:chalukya-dynasty|Chalukya]] prince [[e:someshvara-iv|Someshvara IV]] recovered [[e:basavakalyan|Kalyani]], ending Kalachuri rule. The region soon passed to the [[s:hoysala-empire|Hoysalas]] and the [[s:seuna-yadava-dynasty|Seuna Yadava dynasty]], while the [[e:lingayatism|Lingayat]] tradition endured.

kingdom-of-tahiti.t: A Polynesian kingdom built by the Pōmare dynasty with European guns and missionary support, which became a French protectorate and then a colony.
kingdom-of-tahiti.o: Tahiti was divided among rival chiefdoms when European ships arrived from 1767. The chief Tu, later [[e:pomare-i|Pōmare I]], used [[e:musket|muskets]] obtained from visiting ships and the services of [[e:hms-bounty|Bounty]] mutineers to dominate the island from about 1788. His son [[e:pomare-ii|Pōmare II]], after defeat and exile on [[e:moorea|Moorea]], won the [[e:battle-of-fei-pi|Battle of Fei Pi]] in 1815 and secured rule over Tahiti.
kingdom-of-tahiti.r: [[e:pomare-ii|Pōmare II]] converted to [[e:christianity|Christianity]] under the [[e:london-missionary-society|London Missionary Society]] and issued a written legal code in 1819. Protestant missionaries shaped law, schooling and the use of written Tahitian. The kingdom traded pork, coconut oil and pearl shell. Under [[e:pomare-iv|Queen Pōmare]] IV, who reigned for fifty years, conflict between British Protestant missionaries and French Catholic priests drew [[e:france|France]] in.
kingdom-of-tahiti.e: In 1842 Admiral [[e:abel-aubert-du-petit-thouars|Dupetit-Thouars]] imposed a French [[e:protectorate|protectorate]], and the [[e:franco-tahitian-war|Franco-Tahitian War]] followed from 1844 to 1847. The protectorate was administered within the [[s:french-establishments-in-oceania|French Establishments in Oceania]], and in 1880 [[e:pomare-v|Pōmare V]] ceded the kingdom to [[e:france|France]].

kingdom-of-romania.t: Romanian monarchy that doubled its territory after the First World War as Greater Romania, then fell to dictatorship, war and a communist takeover.
kingdom-of-romania.o: [[s:romania|Romania]] won independence at the [[e:congress-of-berlin|Congress of Berlin]] in 1878, and in 1881 Prince Carol of [[s:principality-of-hohenzollern-sigmaringen|Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen]] was crowned king. The kingdom inherited the constitution of 1866 and the territory of the [[s:united-principalities|United Principalities]], with [[e:northern-dobruja|Northern Dobruja]] added in 1878. It gained [[e:southern-dobruja|Southern Dobruja]] from [[s:bulgaria|Bulgaria]] in the [[e:second-balkan-war|Second Balkan War]] of 1913.
kingdom-of-romania.r: Before 1914 [[s:romania|Romania]] was a [[e:constitutional-monarchy|constitutional monarchy]] run by landowners, exporting grain and oil from [[e:ploiesti|Ploiești]], and a great peasant revolt in 1907 was harshly put down. In 1918 [[e:bessarabia|Bessarabia]], [[s:duchy-of-bukovina|Bukovina]] and [[s:principality-of-transylvania|Transylvania]] joined, creating Greater [[e:romania|Romania]]. Land reform and the 1923 constitution followed, but the interwar years saw the fascist Iron Guard and [[e:carol-ii-of-romania|Carol II]]'s royal dictatorship from 1938.
kingdom-of-romania.e: In 1940 [[s:romania|Romania]] lost [[e:bessarabia|Bessarabia]] and northern [[s:duchy-of-bukovina|Bukovina]] to the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] and northern [[s:principality-of-transylvania|Transylvania]] to [[e:hungary|Hungary]]. [[e:ion-antonescu|Ion Antonescu]] led it into war as an [[e:axis-powers|Axis]] ally until King Michael's coup of August 1944. Under Soviet pressure the communists took power, and Michael was forced to abdicate on 30 December 1947.

khamag-mongol.t: The 12th-century confederation of Mongol clans in the Onon and Kherlen valleys, out of which Temüjin built the Mongol Empire.
khamag-mongol.o: Mongol clans of the [[e:onon-river|Onon]] and [[e:kherlen-river|Kherlen]] river valleys in north-eastern [[s:mongolia|Mongolia]] united in the early 12th century under [[e:khabul-khan|Khabul Khan]], an ancestor of [[e:genghis-khan|Genghis Khan]], who is said to have defied the [[s:jin-dynasty-1115-1234|Jin dynasty]] (1115-1234). The name means 'All the [[e:mongols|Mongols]]'.
khamag-mongol.r: The confederation was a loose alliance of [[e:borjigin|Borjigin]], [[e:tayichiud|Tayichiud]] and other clans, choosing khans at assemblies. Its second khan, [[e:ambaghai|Ambaghai]], was handed over by the [[e:tatars|Tatars]] to the Jin and executed; his successor [[e:hotula-khan|Hotula Khan]] fought the Tatars, but after him the khanship lapsed and clans feuded, as with [[e:yesugei|Yesügei]], father of [[e:genghis-khan|Temüjin]], and the Tayichiud.
khamag-mongol.e: [[e:genghis-khan|Temüjin]] gathered followers in the 1180s and was acclaimed khan of the [[e:mongols|Mongols]], then defeated the [[e:tatars|Tatars]], [[s:keraite-khanate|Keraites]] and [[s:naiman-khanate|Naimans]]. In 1206 an assembly on the [[e:onon-river|Onon]] proclaimed him Genghis Khan, turning the confederation into the [[s:mongol-empire|Mongol Empire]].

koya-temne-kingdom.t: Temne kingdom of the Sierra Leone peninsula whose rulers granted the land on which the Freetown settlement was founded.
koya-temne-kingdom.o: The [[e:temne-people|Temne]] kingdom of Koya lay on the north and south shores of the [[e:sierra-leone|Sierra Leone]] estuary. It took shape by the early 17th century, when Temne groups extended their rule over the peninsula, and Portuguese and later English traders bought slaves and [[e:timber|timber]] from its chiefs.
koya-temne-kingdom.r: Koya's king, the Bai, was installed by the [[e:poro|Poro society]] and senior chiefs, and ruled with subordinate headmen such as [[e:king-tom-koya|King Tom]] on the peninsula. In 1787 King Tom granted land to British abolitionists for the [[s:province-of-freedom|Province of Freedom]], and [[e:naimbana|King Naimbana]] confirmed the grant in 1788; the settlement grew into [[e:freetown|Freetown]], though disputes over the terms led to conflict.
koya-temne-kingdom.e: Koya steadily lost land to the [[s:sierra-leone-colony-and-protectorate|Sierra Leone Colony and Protectorate]], which annexed parts of it in the 19th century and declared a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] over the interior in 1896. The Hut Tax War of 1898 followed. Koya is now a chiefdom in [[e:sierra-leone|Sierra Leone]].

kingdom-of-bunyoro.t: Once the dominant power of the Great Lakes, Bunyoro-Kitara resisted British conquest under King Kabalega and survives as a cultural kingdom.
kingdom-of-bunyoro.o: Around 1500 Luo-speaking [[e:babito-dynasty|Babito]] rulers from the north established a dynasty over the lands of the earlier [[s:empire-of-kitara|Empire of Kitara]] in western [[s:uganda|Uganda]]. Their kingdom claimed Kitara's heritage and in the 16th and 17th centuries raided and dominated neighbours, including [[s:kingdom-of-buganda|Buganda]], [[s:kingdom-of-ankole|Ankole]] and [[s:kingdom-of-rwanda|Rwanda]].
kingdom-of-bunyoro.r: The omukama (king) ruled through chiefs and a court that kept regalia and rituals inherited from the [[e:chwezi|Chwezi]] tradition. Its wealth came from [[e:cattle|cattle]], iron working and the salt of [[e:kibiro|Kibiro]] on [[e:lake-albert|Lake Albert]]. From the 18th century it lost ground to [[s:kingdom-of-buganda|Buganda]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-toro|Kingdom of Toro]] broke away. Omukama [[e:kabalega|Kabalega]] (r. 1870 to 1899) rebuilt the army with firearms.
kingdom-of-bunyoro.e: [[e:kabalega|Kabalega]] fought the British and their [[e:baganda|Ganda]] allies until his capture in 1899. Bunyoro was absorbed into the [[s:uganda-protectorate|Uganda Protectorate]] and lost its 'lost counties' to [[s:kingdom-of-buganda|Buganda]], an issue settled by a 1964 referendum. The monarchy was abolished in 1967 and restored as a cultural institution in 1993.

kalhora-dynasty.t: A Sindhi dynasty of Sufi descent that ruled the Indus valley in the 18th century and dug many of Sindh's irrigation canals.
kalhora-dynasty.o: The Kalhoras were a family of hereditary [[e:sufism|Sufi]] leaders in northern [[e:sindh|Sindh]] whose followers formed an armed movement. [[e:mian-yar-muhammad-kalhoro|Mian Yar Muhammad Kalhoro]] was recognised by the [[s:mughal-empire|Mughal Empire]] as governor of parts of Sindh around 1701, and his successors extended their rule over the whole of the lower [[e:indus|Indus]] valley.
kalhora-dynasty.r: [[e:mian-nur-muhammad-kalhoro|Mian Nur Muhammad Kalhoro]], the most powerful ruler, governed [[e:sindh|Sindh]] as a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of [[e:nader-shah|Nadir Shah]] of [[e:persia|Persia]] and later of the [[s:durrani-empire|Durrani Empire]], paying heavy tribute. The Kalhoras built canals and founded towns, including [[e:khudabad|Khudabad]] and [[e:hyderabad-sindh|Hyderabad]]. The great Sindhi [[e:sufism|Sufi]] poet [[e:shah-abdul-latif-bhittai|Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai]] lived under their rule.
kalhora-dynasty.e: Rivalry between the Kalhora rulers and their [[e:baloch|Baloch]] Talpur commanders led to civil war after a Talpur leader was murdered. The Talpurs defeated the last Kalhora ruler, Abdul Nabi, at the [[e:battle-of-halani|Battle of Halani]] in 1783 and founded the [[s:talpur-dynasty|Talpur dynasty]].

kingdom-of-the-aures.t: A Berber mountain kingdom in the Aurès that defied Vandals and Byzantines and ended with Queen Dihya's resistance to the Arabs.
kingdom-of-the-aures.o: The [[e:berbers|Berbers]] of the [[e:aures-mountains|Aurès]] mountains broke away from the [[s:vandal-kingdom|Vandal Kingdom]] around 484. An inscription at [[e:arris|Arris]] records a ruler, [[e:masties|Masties]], who called himself duke for 67 years and emperor for ten, and claimed never to have broken faith with either [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] or Moors.
kingdom-of-the-aures.r: The kingdom drew on Roman titles and Christian faith while resting on [[e:berbers|Berber]] clans of the mountains. In the 530s [[e:iaudas|Iaudas]] (Iabdas) raided Byzantine [[s:numidia|Numidia]] and resisted the general [[e:solomon|Solomon]], who finally stormed his strongholds in 539. Little is known of the following century. In the 690s the [[e:jarawa-berbers|Jerawa]] tribal leader [[e:dihya|Dihya]], called al-Kahina by Arab writers, led Berber resistance and defeated [[e:hassan-ibn-al-numan|Hassan ibn al-Numan]].
kingdom-of-the-aures.e: Hassan returned, and [[e:dihya|Dihya]] was killed around 701 to 703. The [[s:umayyad-caliphate|Umayyad Caliphate]] absorbed the region, and many of her followers converted to [[e:islam|Islam]] and joined the Arab armies. Dihya became a lasting symbol of [[e:berbers|Berber]] resistance.

kuba-kingdom.t: A Bushong-led kingdom of the Kasai, famous for its royal portrait statues, raffia velvet textiles and long oral history of kings.
kuba-kingdom.o: Bushong tradition credits [[e:shyaam-a-mbul-a-ngoong|Shyaam a Mbul a Ngoong]] with founding the kingdom around 1625, uniting chiefdoms between the [[e:kasai|Kasai]] and [[e:sankuru-river|Sankuru]] rivers. He is remembered as a culture hero who brought new crops, including [[e:maize|maize]], tobacco and [[e:cassava|cassava]], from the west, together with new political institutions.
kuba-kingdom.r: The king (nyimi) ruled from the capital [[e:nsheng|Nsheng]] with an elaborate council of titled officials, and the court sponsored an exceptional art tradition: wooden ndop statues commemorating each king, carved cups, masks and embroidered [[e:raffia-cloth|raffia cloth]]. Agriculture and trade in raffia and camwood supported dense villages. [[e:quba|Kuba]] oral history was studied in detail by the historian [[e:jan-vansina|Jan Vansina]].
kuba-kingdom.e: In 1899 [[e:zappo-zap|Zappo Zap]] raiders working for the [[s:congo-free-state|Congo Free State]] sacked [[e:nsheng|Nsheng]], and Belgian administration followed, though the kingship continued under colonial rule. The [[e:quba|Kuba]] remain known worldwide for their art, and the nyimi is still a traditional ruler in the [[e:democratic-republic-of-the-congo|Democratic Republic of the Congo]].

karnat-dynasty.t: A dynasty of Karnataka origin that ruled Mithila from Simraungadh for two centuries and briefly held the Kathmandu Valley.
karnat-dynasty.o: [[e:nanyadeva|Nanyadeva]], a chief of Karnata descent who probably came north with the armies of the [[s:western-chalukya-empire|Chalukyas of Kalyani]], established himself in the [[e:tirhut|Tirhut]] plain around 1097. He made [[e:simraungadh|Simraungadh]], near the modern [[e:india|India]] and [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Nepal]] border, his capital and ruled the region of [[e:mithila|Mithila]] between the [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges]] and the Himalayan foothills.
karnat-dynasty.r: The Karnat court was a centre of [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] and Maithili learning. [[e:harisimhadeva|Harisimhadeva]], the last king, sponsored the codification of Maithil [[e:brahmins|Brahmin]] genealogies (the panji system) and his minister [[e:jyotirishvara-thakur|Jyotirishvara]] wrote the [[e:varna-ratnakara|Varna Ratnakara]], one of the earliest prose works in Maithili. The kings also intervened in the politics of the [[e:kathmandu-valley|Kathmandu Valley]], where some Karnat rulers were recognised as overlords.
karnat-dynasty.e: In 1324 [[e:ghiyath-al-din-tughluq|Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq]] of the [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]] invaded [[e:tirhut|Tirhut]] and took [[e:simraungadh|Simraungadh]]. [[e:harisimhadeva|Harisimhadeva]] fled into the hills of [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Nepal]]. [[e:mithila|Mithila]] soon passed to the [[s:oiniwar-dynasty|Oiniwar dynasty]], ruling as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of [[e:delhi|Delhi]], while Karnat traditions persisted in Nepalese court culture.

kingdom-of-badung.t: South Balinese kingdom centred on Denpasar, whose royal family marched to their deaths in the puputan of 1906.
kingdom-of-badung.o: Badung emerged in southern [[e:bali|Bali]] in the 18th century under the Pemecutan dynasty, part of the Arya noble lineages. Around 1788 a new palace was established at [[e:denpasar|Denpasar]], which became the leading court of the kingdom while the Pemecutan branch kept its own seat nearby.
kingdom-of-badung.r: Badung controlled [[e:rice|rice]] lands and the harbour of Kuta, through which slaves, rice and other goods were traded. In the mid 19th century the Danish trader [[e:mads-lange|Mads Lange]] ran a large trading post at Kuta under royal protection. Royal power was shared among the [[e:denpasar|Denpasar]], Pemecutan and Kesiman houses.
kingdom-of-badung.e: A dispute over the plunder of a wrecked Chinese ship in 1904 gave the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] a pretext. On 20 September 1906 their troops reached [[e:denpasar|Denpasar]], where the raja and his court, dressed in white, advanced into the guns in a puputan. Badung was annexed, and Denpasar later became the capital of [[e:bali|Bali]].

kumharsain-state.t: A small Rajput hill state north of Shimla, one of the Simla Hill States restored under British protection after the Gurkha wars.
kumharsain-state.o: Tradition holds that the ruling family descended from a [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] named Kirti Singh who came from the plains around 1000 and settled in the hills north of the Sutlej-Giri watershed.
kumharsain-state.r: Kumharsain was a small mountain state of terraced farms and forest, ruled by a Rana and at times a tributary of [[s:bashahr-state|Bashahr State]]. Little is recorded of its internal history before the 19th century. [[e:gurkhas|Gurkha]] forces of the [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Kingdom of Nepal]] occupied it in the early 1800s.
kumharsain-state.e: After the [[e:anglo-nepalese-war|Anglo-Nepalese War]] the British issued a sanad in 1815 restoring the Rana as one of the [[e:simla-hill-states|Simla Hill States]]. Kumharsain merged into [[e:himachal-pradesh|Himachal Pradesh]] in April 1948 and is now part of [[e:shimla|Shimla]] district.

kingdom-of-sicily.t: Southern Italy's Norman kingdom, famed for its Arab-Byzantine-Latin court culture, which after 1282 continued as the island realm of Sicily until 1816.
kingdom-of-sicily.o: [[e:roger-ii-of-sicily|Roger II]], ruler of the [[s:county-of-sicily|County of Sicily]] and the [[s:duchy-of-apulia-and-calabria|Duchy of Apulia and Calabria]], obtained a royal title from [[e:antipope-anacletus-ii|Antipope Anacletus II]] and was crowned in [[e:palermo|Palermo]] on Christmas Day 1130. The kingdom united [[e:sicily|Sicily]] and the Italian south, including the former principalities of [[s:principality-of-capua|Capua]] and [[s:principality-of-bari|Bari]].
kingdom-of-sicily.r: The Norman kings ran a centralised state with Arabic, Greek and [[e:latin|Latin]] chanceries, and built the [[e:palatine-chapel-palermo|Palatine Chapel]], [[e:cefalu-cathedral|Cefalù]] and [[e:monreale-cathedral|Monreale]]. Through marriage it passed to the [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]]: Frederick II issued the [[e:constitutions-of-melfi|Constitutions of Melfi]] in 1231. [[e:charles-i-of-anjou|Charles of Anjou]] took it in 1266, but the [[e:sicilian-vespers|Sicilian Vespers]] of 1282 brought [[e:peter-iii-of-aragon|Peter III of Aragon]] to the island, leaving the mainland as the [[s:kingdom-of-naples|Kingdom of Naples]].
kingdom-of-sicily.e: The island kingdom passed to Aragon and [[s:habsburg-spain|Habsburg Spain]] under [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroys]], then briefly to [[s:duchy-of-savoy|Savoy]] in 1713, to [[e:austria|Austria]] in 1720 and to the [[e:house-of-bourbon|Bourbons]] in 1735. In 1816 Ferdinand merged it with [[e:naples|Naples]] to form the [[s:kingdom-of-the-two-sicilies|Kingdom of the Two Sicilies]].

cr.a: Bandiera_del_Regno_di_Sicilia.svg: Oren neu dag Arms_of_the_Aragonese_Kings_of_Sicily.svg: Heralder derivative work: ...

kingdom-of-opobo.t: The trading state founded by Jaja, a former slave who broke away from Bonny and dominated the palm oil trade of the eastern Niger Delta until his deportation in 1887.
kingdom-of-opobo.o: [[e:jaja-of-opobo|Jaja]], born in [[e:igboland|Igboland]] and sold as a boy to Bonny, rose to head the Anna Pepple trading house of the [[s:bonny-kingdom|Bonny Kingdom]]. After a civil war between rival houses, he left Bonny in 1869 with his followers and in 1870 founded Opobo on the [[e:imo-river|Imo]] river, placing himself between Bonny and the interior [[e:palm-oil|palm oil]] markets.
kingdom-of-opobo.r: Opobo was a city-state built around trading houses, each with its own canoe fleet and dependants. [[e:jaja-of-opobo|Jaja]] controlled access to the [[e:igbo-people|Igbo]] producers of [[e:palm-oil|palm oil]], dealt directly with British firms and even shipped oil to [[e:liverpool|Liverpool]] on his own account. [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] recognised him as king in 1873. He kept missionaries out and maintained traditional religion while sending his children to be educated abroad.
kingdom-of-opobo.e: [[e:jaja-of-opobo|Jaja]] refused to let British traders bypass him. In 1887 the British consul [[e:harry-johnston|Harry Johnston]] lured him aboard a ship and deported him; he died in 1891. Opobo was absorbed into the [[s:oil-rivers-protectorate|Oil Rivers Protectorate]], and its king remains a traditional ruler.

kaithal-state.t: A Sikh chiefship ruled by the Bhai family, which lapsed to the British in 1843 when its last chief died without an heir.
kaithal-state.o: The Bhais of Kaithal descended from Bhai Bhagtu, a [[e:sikhism|Sikh]] devotee honoured by the [[e:sikh-gurus|Gurus]]. [[e:desu-singh|Desu Singh]], of that family, seized Kaithal around 1767 in the Sikh expansion across the former Mughal province of [[e:sirhind|Sirhind]].
kaithal-state.r: Kaithal was one of the larger [[e:cis-sutlej-states|Cis-Sutlej]] chiefships and accepted British protection in 1809. Its chiefs were known by the title Bhai. The state is thinly documented beyond its succession disputes.
kaithal-state.e: When Bhai [[e:udai-singh-of-kaithal|Udai Singh]] died childless in 1843, the British annexed most of Kaithal, and resistance by local supporters was put down. The town became a British district headquarters and is now a district of [[e:haryana|Haryana]].

cr.a: Cartographers and surveyors of the British East India Company

kushalgarh-state.t: A Rathore Rajput chiefship in southern Rajasthan, long a dependency of Banswara with a mostly Bhil population.
kushalgarh-state.o: Kushalgarh was held by a branch of [[e:rathore|Rathore Rajputs]] who settled in the hills of [[e:vagad|Vagad]]. The register dates it to 1671. Its chiefs held their land as feudatories of [[s:banswara-state|Banswara]].
kushalgarh-state.r: The Rao ruled a territory of hills and forest with a large [[e:bhils|Bhil]] population, practising subsistence farming. In the British period it was treated as a chiefship under [[s:banswara-state|Banswara]], supervised through the [[e:rajputana-agency|Rajputana Agency]], rather than as a fully separate salute state.
kushalgarh-state.e: Kushalgarh joined the [[s:united-state-of-rajasthan|United State of Rajasthan]] in 1948. It is now a town in [[s:banswara-state|Banswara]] district.

kingdom-of-doti.t: A hill kingdom of far-western Nepal ruled by the Raika kings, one of the successor states of the Khasa Malla realm.
kingdom-of-doti.o: Doti emerged from the break-up of the [[s:khasa-malla-kingdom|Khasa Malla kingdom]] in the late 14th century, in the hills between the Karnali and Mahakali rivers. Its rulers, the [[e:raika-dynasty|Raika dynasty]], are traditionally said to descend from the Katyuri kings of [[e:kumaon|Kumaon]] and established themselves at [[e:dipayal-silgadhi|Dipayal]] and nearby seats.
kingdom-of-doti.r: Doti was one of the larger of the [[e:baise-rajya|Baise Rajya]], the twenty-two hill kingdoms of the Karnali region. Its kings ruled through local chiefs and [[e:brahmins|Brahmin]] advisers, and fought their neighbours the [[s:kumaon-kingdom|Kumaon Kingdom]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-jumla|Kingdom of Jumla]]. Inscriptions and temple grants are the main sources, and the Doteli dialect of Nepali takes its name from the kingdom.
kingdom-of-doti.e: The expanding [[s:gorkha-kingdom|Gorkha]] armies of the [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Kingdom of Nepal]] conquered Doti around 1790, defeating its last [[e:raika-dynasty|Raika]] king. Doti became a district of [[e:nepal|Nepal]], and the name survives in Doti district and the Doteli language.

kamerun.t: The German colony in Central Africa, founded through treaties with the Duala in 1884, which expanded deep into the interior before Allied forces conquered it in 1916.
kamerun.o: On 12 July 1884 the [[e:duala-people|Duala]] kings Bell and Akwa signed a treaty with German agents, and [[e:gustav-nachtigal|Gustav Nachtigal]] raised the German flag at the [[s:duala-kingdoms|Duala kingdoms]] days later. From the coast German forces pushed inland over the next twenty years, defeating resistance from peoples such as the [[e:bulu-people|Bulu]] and from [[e:fula|Fulbe]] lamidates like [[s:lamidate-of-ngaoundere|Ngaoundere]], until the colony reached [[e:lake-chad|Lake Chad]].
kamerun.r: German rule depended on concession companies and plantations on the slopes of [[e:mount-cameroon|Mount Cameroon]], worked by forced and recruited labour; the governor [[e:jesko-von-puttkamer|Jesko von Puttkamer]] (1895-1907) was notorious for abuses. The seat of government moved between [[e:duala-people|Duala]] and [[e:buea|Buea]], on the cooler slopes of Mount [[e:cameroon|Cameroon]]. After the [[e:agadir-crisis|Agadir crisis]] of 1911 [[e:france|France]] ceded large territories, called [[e:neukamerun|Neukamerun]], from [[s:french-equatorial-africa|French Equatorial Africa]].
kamerun.e: In 1914 the Germans hanged [[e:rudolf-duala-manga-bell|Rudolf Duala Manga Bell]] for resisting land expropriation. British and French forces conquered Kamerun in 1914-1916, and it was divided into [[s:french-cameroon|French Cameroon]] and the [[s:british-cameroons|British Cameroons]].

cr.a: Original: Imperial Colonial Office of the German Empire Vector: David Liuzzo

kingdom-of-bafut.t: One of the largest kingdoms of the Cameroon Grassfields, whose Fon resisted German conquest and whose palace at Bafut is among the best preserved in the region.
kingdom-of-bafut.o: Bafut was founded by groups said to have migrated from the [[e:tikar-people|Tikar]] area in the north-east, probably in the 18th century, and settled north of what is now [[e:bamenda|Bamenda]]. Its rulers, the Fons, gradually conquered and absorbed neighbouring villages, building one of the larger chiefdoms of the [[e:cameroon-grassfields|Grassfields]].
kingdom-of-bafut.r: The [[e:fon-title|Fon]] was a sacred king, supported by palace societies, notables and a regulatory society, the Kwifon, that enforced his decisions and ritual law. The royal compound with its shrine house, the Achum, was the political and religious centre. Bafut farmed, raised livestock and took part in trade in [[e:palm-oil|palm oil]], kola and slaves across the [[e:cameroon-grassfields|Grassfields]].
kingdom-of-bafut.e: [[e:fon-title|Fon]] Abumbi I fought German troops in 1901 and 1907 before submitting, and Bafut was absorbed into [[s:kamerun|Kamerun]]. After 1916 it fell under [[s:british-cameroons|British Cameroons]]. The Fon still reigns; [[e:achirimbi-ii|Achirimbi II]] became widely known through [[e:gerald-durrell|Gerald Durrell's]] book [[e:the-bafut-beagles|The Bafut Beagles]].

kirghiz-assr.t: The autonomous Soviet republic that gave the Kyrgyz their first modern territorial state, the forerunner of today's Kyrgyzstan.
kirghiz-assr.o: In the national delimitation of 1924 the [[e:kyrgyz-people|Kyrgyz]] lands of the [[s:turkestan-assr|Turkestan ASSR]] were made the Kara-Kirghiz Autonomous Oblast within the [[s:russian-sfsr|Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic]]. In 1925 it was renamed the Kirghiz Autonomous Oblast and in 1926 raised to an Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic, with its capital at [[e:bishkek|Pishpek]], renamed Frunze.
kirghiz-assr.r: The republic introduced Soviet administration, schools and a written [[e:kyrgyz-people|Kyrgyz]] language, first in Arabic and then [[e:latin|Latin]] script. Collectivisation and settlement of nomadic herders from 1929 brought hardship and revolt, and many fled to [[e:china|China]]. Leading Kyrgyz communists such as [[e:yusup-abdrakhmanov|Yusup Abdrakhmanov]] were purged in the 1930s.
kirghiz-assr.e: Under the 1936 Soviet constitution the republic became a union republic, the [[s:kirghiz-ssr|Kirghiz SSR]]. Its borders, drawn in 1924, left large [[e:uzbeks|Uzbek]] and [[e:tajiks|Tajik]] communities inside the republic and [[e:kyrgyz-people|Kyrgyz]] communities outside it.

kedah-sultanate.t: One of the oldest continuous monarchies in the world, a Malay sultanate that converted to Islam in the 12th century and survives as a state of Malaysia.
kedah-sultanate.o: According to the Kedah annals, the ruler of [[s:old-kedah|Old Kedah]], [[e:phra-ong-mahawangsa|Phra Ong Mahawangsa]], accepted [[e:islam|Islam]] in 1136 and took the name [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Mudzaffar Shah, founding a line that continues today. The date is traditional. The sultans later moved their seat to [[e:alor-setar|Alor Setar]] on the [[e:rice|rice]] plains of the [[e:kedah-river|Kedah River]].
kedah-sultanate.r: Kedah was the [[e:rice|rice]] bowl of the peninsula, exporting grain, [[e:tin|tin]] and elephants. Its rulers sent the bunga mas, golden flowers, to Siam as a sign of tribute while seeking other allies. In 1786 [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:abdullah-mukarram-shah|Abdullah Mukarram Shah]] allowed [[e:francis-light|Francis Light]] of the [[e:east-india-company|British East India Company]] to occupy [[s:prince-of-wales-island|Penang]], hoping for protection that never came.
kedah-sultanate.e: Siam invaded in 1821 and ruled directly until 1842. By the [[e:anglo-siamese-treaty-of-1909|Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909]] Kedah passed to British protection as one of the [[s:unfederated-malay-states|Unfederated Malay States]], and it joined the [[s:federation-of-malaya|Federation of Malaya]] in 1948. Its royal house still reigns, and [[e:tunku-abdul-rahman|Tunku Abdul Rahman]], Malaysia's first prime minister, was a Kedah prince.

kediri-kingdom.t: The East Javanese kingdom ruled from Daha, whose 12th-century court produced classics of Old Javanese poetry and grew rich on the spice trade.
kediri-kingdom.o: Kediri, also called Panjalu, was the western half of the realm [[e:airlangga|Airlangga]] divided around 1045, with its capital at Daha on the [[e:brantas-river|Brantas River]]. For decades it is poorly documented, but by the 1130s it had absorbed [[s:janggala|Janggala]], and [[e:jayabaya|King Jayabaya]] proclaimed 'Panjalu jayati', Panjalu is victorious.
kediri-kingdom.r: Kediri controlled the [[e:rice|rice]] lands of the [[e:brantas-river|Brantas]] valley and the ports that shipped Moluccan [[e:cloves|cloves]] and [[e:nutmeg|nutmeg]] westward; Chinese writers such as [[e:zhou-qufei|Zhou Qufei]] counted [[e:java|Java]] among the richest lands overseas. Its court poets wrote the [[e:kakawin-bharatayuddha|Kakawin Bharatayuddha]], completed in 1157 under [[e:jayabaya|Jayabaya]], and the [[e:smaradahana|Smaradahana]]. Jayabaya is also remembered in Javanese prophecy.
kediri-kingdom.e: The last king, [[e:kertajaya|Kertajaya]], quarrelled with the clergy, who sided with [[e:ken-arok|Ken Arok]] of [[s:singhasari|Tumapel]]. Ken Arok defeated him at [[e:battle-of-ganter|Ganter]] in 1222 and founded [[e:singhasari|Singhasari]]. Kediri revived briefly as [[s:gelang-gelang|Gelang-gelang]] under [[e:jayakatwang|Jayakatwang]] in 1292.

kingdom-of-andarig.t: One of the small kingdoms of the Sinjar plain that rose after Shamshi-Adad's death and played the great powers against each other in the Mari letters.
kingdom-of-andarig.o: Andarig lay in the plain south of [[e:sinjar-mountains|Jebel Sinjar]] in northern [[e:iraq|Iraq]]; its site is uncertain. When the [[s:kingdom-of-upper-mesopotamia|Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia]] collapsed around 1776 BCE, local rulers took power there, among them Qarni-Lim, an ally of [[e:zimri-lim|Zimri-Lim]] of [[s:mari|Mari]].
kingdom-of-andarig.r: The [[s:mari|Mari]] archives show Andarig as a regional power competing with [[s:kingdom-of-karana|Karana]], [[s:kingdom-of-kurda|Kurda]] and [[s:kingdom-of-upper-mesopotamia|Ekallatum]] for control of the [[e:sinjar-mountains|Sinjar]] plain. Its kings bound themselves by oath to [[e:mari|Mari]], [[s:eshnunna|Eshnunna]] or [[e:elam|Elam]] as interests shifted. After Qarni-Lim was killed, Atamrum, a ruler from Allahad backed first by Elam and then by Mari, took the throne and became one of the leading kings of the region, with troops and treaties recorded in letters.
kingdom-of-andarig.e: After [[e:hammurabi|Hammurabi]] of [[e:babylon|Babylon]] conquered [[s:mari|Mari]] in 1761 BCE, he imposed his authority on the [[e:sinjar-mountains|Sinjar]] kingdoms, and Andarig vanishes from the sources, absorbed into Babylonian and later local northern powers.

kano-emirate.t: The richest emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate, centred on the walled city of Kano, the great manufacturing and trading hub of the central Sudan.
kano-emirate.o: Between 1805 and 1807 [[e:fula|Fulani]] jihadists loyal to [[e:usman-dan-fodio|Usman dan Fodio]] overthrew the last [[e:hausa|Hausa]] ruler of the [[s:kingdom-of-kano|Kingdom of Kano]], [[e:muhammad-alwali-ii|Muhammad Alwali]]. The scholar [[e:sulaimanu-of-kano|Sulaimanu]] became the first emir, and in 1819 he was succeeded by [[e:ibrahim-dabo|Ibrahim Dabo]], whose descendants, the Dabo dynasty, have provided [[e:kano|Kano's]] [[e:emir|emirs]] ever since.
kano-emirate.r: The emir governed through a council of titled officials, many inherited from [[e:hausa|Hausa]] [[e:kano|Kano]], with district heads collecting taxes from farms and crafts. Kano produced [[e:indigo|indigo]]-dyed cloth and [[e:leather|leather goods]] sold across the [[e:sahara|Sahara]] and the [[e:sudan|Sudan]], and its market drew caravans from [[s:county-of-tripoli|Tripoli]], [[e:bornu|Bornu]] and the forest. The explorer [[e:heinrich-barth|Heinrich Barth]] described it in 1851 as the commercial centre of the region.
kano-emirate.e: A civil war over the succession in 1893-1895 weakened the [[e:emirate|emirate]]. British forces took [[e:kano|Kano]] in February 1903, and [[e:emir|Emir]] [[e:aliyu-babba|Aliyu Babba]] was deposed. Kano became the centrepiece of [[e:indirect-rule|indirect rule]] in [[s:protectorate-of-northern-nigeria|Northern Nigeria]], and the emirate continues today.

kingdom-of-the-anglo-saxons.t: The realm created by Alfred the Great and his son Edward, joining Wessex and English Mercia into the direct ancestor of the Kingdom of England.
kingdom-of-the-anglo-saxons.o: In 886 Alfred occupied [[e:london|London]] and, according to the Chronicle, all the English not under the [[e:danes|Danes]] submitted to him. His charters began to use the title king of the [[e:anglo-saxons|Anglo-Saxons]], uniting the [[s:kingdom-of-wessex|Kingdom of Wessex]] with western [[s:kingdom-of-mercia|Mercia]] under [[e:aethelred-lord-of-the-mercians|Aethelred]], Lord of the Mercians, who married Alfred's daughter [[e:aethelflaed|Aethelflaed]].
kingdom-of-the-anglo-saxons.r: The kingdom was defended by burhs and a reorganised army. Alfred issued a law code and sponsored translations of [[e:latin|Latin]] works into English. [[e:edward-the-elder|Edward the Elder]] and [[e:aethelflaed|Aethelflaed]] reconquered the southern [[e:danelaw|Danelaw]], including the [[s:five-boroughs-of-the-danelaw|Five Boroughs]] and Danish [[s:kingdom-of-east-anglia|East Anglia]], between 910 and 920.
kingdom-of-the-anglo-saxons.e: After [[e:aethelflaed|Aethelflaed]]'s death Edward absorbed [[s:kingdom-of-mercia|Mercia]] in 918. In 927 his son [[e:aethelstan|Aethelstan]] took [[e:york|York]] and received the submission of northern rulers, becoming the first king of the [[s:kingdom-of-england|Kingdom of England]].

kingdom-of-yin-206-bc.t: One of the Eighteen Kingdoms created by Xiang Yu in 206 BCE, held by the Zhao general Sima Ang until he surrendered to Liu Bang a year later.
kingdom-of-yin-206-bc.o: After the fall of the [[s:qin-dynasty|Qin dynasty]], [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]] divided the empire into eighteen kingdoms in 206 BCE. [[e:sima-ang|Sima Ang]], a general of the revived state of Zhao who had captured the Henei region, was made King of Yin, ruling from [[e:zhaoge|Zhaoge]] in northern [[e:henan|Henan]], the old [[s:shang-dynasty|Shang]] capital area.
kingdom-of-yin-206-bc.r: The kingdom was a military holding with no time to develop institutions of its own. It covered the Henei commandery north of the [[e:yellow-river|Yellow River]] and served as a buffer between the kingdoms around [[e:luoyang|Luoyang]] and those of Zhao.
kingdom-of-yin-206-bc.e: In 205 BCE, as [[e:liu-bang|Liu Bang]] advanced east from the [[s:kingdom-of-han-206-bc|Kingdom of Han]] (206 BC), [[e:sima-ang|Sima Ang]] was captured or surrendered, and his realm became the Henei commandery of Han. Sima Ang was later claimed as an ancestor of the Sima family who founded the [[s:western-jin|Western Jin]].

kingdom-of-prilep.t: Western Macedonian realm of King Vukašin and his son Marko, whose life as an Ottoman vassal inspired the hero of South Slav epic poetry.
kingdom-of-prilep.o: [[e:vukasin-mrnjavcevic|Vukašin Mrnjavčević]], a Serbian noble, was crowned king in 1365 as co-ruler with Emperor [[e:stefan-uros-v|Uroš V]] of the [[s:serbian-empire|Serbian Empire]], ruling lands in western [[e:macedonia-region|Macedonia]] from [[e:prilep|Prilep]]. With his brother [[e:jovan-uglesa|Jovan Uglješa]] of the [[s:despotate-of-serres|Despotate of Serres]] he led the campaign against the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] in 1371.
kingdom-of-prilep.r: After [[e:vukasin-mrnjavcevic|Vukašin]] was killed at the [[e:maritsa|Maritsa]] in 1371, his son [[e:prince-marko|Marko]] inherited the royal title and a much smaller realm around [[e:prilep|Prilep]], [[e:ohrid|Ohrid]] and the Pelagonian plain. Marko became an Ottoman [[e:vassal|vassal]], minted coins and completed [[e:markos-monastery|Marko's Monastery]] near [[e:skopje|Skopje]], begun by his father. His neighbours took Ohrid and other lands.
kingdom-of-prilep.e: [[e:prince-marko|Marko]] died fighting for the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] against [[e:mircea-the-elder|Mircea the Elder of Wallachia]] at [[e:battle-of-rovine|Rovine]] in 1395, and his lands were annexed by the Ottomans. As Kraljević Marko, he became the best-loved hero of Serbian, Macedonian and Bulgarian folk epic.

khalji-dynasty-of-bengal.t: The first Muslim regime in Bengal, founded by Bakhtiyar Khalji's conquest of the Sena capital and ruled from Lakhnauti.
khalji-dynasty-of-bengal.o: [[e:bakhtiyar-khalji|Muhammad Bakhtiyar Khalji]], a Turkic-Afghan commander serving the [[s:ghurid-sultanate|Ghurids]], raided [[e:bihar|Bihar]] and then, around 1204, surprised the [[e:sena-dynasty|Sena]] king [[e:lakshmana-sena|Lakshmana Sena]] at [[e:nabadwip|Nadia]]. He established a capital at [[e:gaur|Lakhnauti]] (Gaur) and ruled northern and western [[e:bengal|Bengal]] with his Khalji officers, nominally under the Ghurid sultans.
khalji-dynasty-of-bengal.r: The Khalji chiefs governed as a military aristocracy, dividing land among commanders and founding mosques and [[e:madrasa|madrasas]]. [[e:bakhtiyar-khalji|Bakhtiyar]] died after a disastrous expedition towards [[s:tibet-1912-1951|Tibet]] around 1206. [[e:iwaz-khalji|Iwaz Khalji]], who took the title Ghiyath al-Din, was the most effective ruler: he built roads and embankments, created a river fleet and struck coins in his own name.
khalji-dynasty-of-bengal.e: [[e:iltutmish|Iltutmish]] of the [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]] sent his son Nasir al-Din Mahmud against [[e:iwaz-khalji|Iwaz]], who was defeated and killed in 1227. [[e:bengal|Bengal]] became a province of [[e:delhi|Delhi]], governed from [[e:gaur|Lakhnauti]], until independent sultans arose again, leading eventually to the [[s:bengal-sultanate|Bengal Sultanate]].

kos.t: Dorian island state off Anatolia, birthplace of Hippocrates and home of the famous healing sanctuary of Asclepius.
kos.o: Kos, an island off the Carian coast near [[s:halicarnassus|Halicarnassus]], was settled from the [[e:bronze-age|Bronze Age]], with Mycenaean remains. [[e:dorians|Dorian Greeks]] occupied it in the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]], and it joined the [[e:dorian-hexapolis|Dorian Hexapolis]] with [[s:knidos|Knidos]], Halicarnassus and the Rhodian cities. Its first chief town was Astypalaia in the south-west.
kos.r: Kos was known for wine and fine translucent [[e:silk|silk]] cloth. [[e:hippocrates|Hippocrates]] was born there c. 460 BCE and the Coan school of medicine bears his name. After Persian rule the island joined the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]]. In 366 BCE the Coans founded a new capital on the north-east tip, and the [[e:asclepieion-of-kos|Asclepieion]] was later built nearby.
kos.e: Kos was a favoured base of the [[s:ptolemaic-empire|Ptolemaic Empire]], where [[e:ptolemy-ii-philadelphus|Ptolemy II]] was born and the poet [[e:philitas-of-cos|Philitas]] taught. It later allied with [[e:rome|Rome]] and became part of the province of Asia in 129 BCE, remaining a free city prized for its sanctuary.

kingdom-of-zimbabwe.t: The builders of Great Zimbabwe, whose dry-stone city controlled the gold trade of the southern African plateau for over two centuries.
kingdom-of-zimbabwe.o: After the decline of the [[s:kingdom-of-mapungubwe|Kingdom of Mapungubwe]] in the early 13th century, a [[e:shona|Shona]]-speaking elite on the [[e:zimbabwean-plateau|Zimbabwe plateau]] took over the routes carrying gold and [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] to the coast. Building at [[e:great-zimbabwe|Great Zimbabwe]] began with walls on the [[e:hill-complex-great-zimbabwe|Hill Complex]] and grew into the largest stone-built settlement in [[e:sub-saharan-africa|sub-Saharan Africa]] south of [[s:federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia|Ethiopia]].
kingdom-of-zimbabwe.r: Kings ruled from the [[e:hill-complex-great-zimbabwe|Hill Complex]], while the Great Enclosure, with its conical tower and walls up to 11 metres high, probably served royal or ritual purposes. The economy rested on [[e:cattle|cattle]], farming and gold mined across the plateau and sent via [[e:sofala|Sofala]] to [[s:kilwa-sultanate|Kilwa]]. Finds include soapstone bird carvings, Chinese [[e:porcelain|porcelain]], Persian pottery and a Kilwa [[e:copper|copper]] coin. The city may have held 10,000 to 18,000 people.
kingdom-of-zimbabwe.e: [[e:great-zimbabwe|Great Zimbabwe]] declined from the mid-15th century, perhaps through [[e:overgrazing|overgrazing]], exhausted resources and a northward shift of the [[e:gold-trade|gold trade]]. Its heirs were the [[e:mutapa-empire|Mutapa]] state in the north and the [[s:kingdom-of-butua|Kingdom of Butua]] at [[e:khami|Khami]] in the south-west. The ruins gave modern [[e:zimbabwe|Zimbabwe]] its name and its national emblem, the Zimbabwe bird.

kimek-khanate.t: A confederation of Turkic tribes on the Irtysh whose western Kipchak wing became the Cumans, masters of the western steppe.
kimek-khanate.o: The Kimek confederation formed in the mid-8th century on the [[e:irtysh|Irtysh River]] from tribes, including the Imek and [[e:kipchaks|Kipchaks]], who left the Mongolian steppe as the [[s:uyghur-khaganate|Uyghur Khaganate]] rose. By the 9th century their ruler held the title [[e:khagan|khagan]].
kimek-khanate.r: Arab and Persian geographers such as [[e:gardizi|Gardizi]] and the [[e:hudud-al-alam|Hudud al-Alam]] describe the Kimek as a confederation of seven tribes, pastoral but with towns along the [[e:irtysh|Irtysh]], with Imakiya as the ruler's seat. They traded [[e:fur-trade|furs]] and slaves south to the [[s:samanid-empire|Samanid Empire]] and the [[e:oghuz-turks|Oghuz]]. Religion included [[e:tengrism|Tengrism]] and [[e:manichaeism|Manichaean]] and Buddhist influences, and they burned their dead.
kimek-khanate.e: In the early 11th century the confederation broke up as the [[e:kipchaks|Kipchaks]], its western component, moved west across the steppe. Pressure from the Qai and other peoples of the east also played a part. The Kipchaks became the [[e:cumans|Cumans]], who dominated the Pontic steppe until the Mongol conquest.

kingdom-of-pontus.t: Pontus, a Hellenistic kingdom on the Black Sea whose king Mithridates VI fought Rome in three wars and nearly drove it from Asia.
kingdom-of-pontus.o: [[e:mithridates-i-of-pontus|Mithridates I Ktistes]], a noble of Persian descent, fled the wars of Alexander's successors and seized lands in north-eastern [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]]. He took the title king in 281 BCE, with his capital at [[e:amasya|Amaseia]], where royal tombs are cut into the cliffs. [[e:pharnaces-i-of-pontus|Pharnaces I]] captured [[s:sinope|Sinope]] in 183 BCE and made it the capital.
kingdom-of-pontus.r: The kings combined Persian court traditions with Greek city culture, ruling over Greek ports and rural temple estates. Pontus was rich in metals, [[e:timber|timber]] and grain. [[e:mithridates-vi-of-pontus|Mithridates VI]] extended his rule around the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] and in 88 BCE ordered the massacre of [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] and Italians in Asia.
kingdom-of-pontus.e: [[e:mithridates-vi-of-pontus|Mithridates VI]] fought [[e:sulla|Sulla]], [[e:lucius-licinius-lucullus|Lucullus]] and [[e:pompey|Pompey]] in three wars. Defeated, he died at [[e:panticapaeum|Panticapaeum]] in 63 BCE, and Pompey divided Pontus between Roman provinces and client kings, later including [[s:polemonid-pontus|Polemonid Pontus]].

kingdom-of-tambapanni.t: The first kingdom of Sri Lanka in the island's chronicles, founded by the legendary prince Vijaya on the north-west coast.
kingdom-of-tambapanni.o: The [[e:mahavamsa|Mahavamsa]] and [[e:dipavamsa|Dipavamsa]] chronicles tell how [[e:prince-vijaya|Prince Vijaya]], exiled from northern [[e:india|India]], landed with 700 followers on the day of the Buddha's death, traditionally 543 BCE. He married Kuveni, a local woman of the [[e:yakkha-sri-lanka|Yakkha]] people, and founded a settlement called Tambapanni, probably near [[e:mannar|Mannar]] or [[e:puttalam|Puttalam]]. The account is legendary, though it may reflect the arrival of Indo-Aryan speakers.
kingdom-of-tambapanni.r: Nothing is known of the kingdom from contemporary sources. The chronicles say [[e:prince-vijaya|Vijaya]] later sent Kuveni away and married a princess from the [[e:pandya-dynasty|Pandya]] country, and that his followers founded villages across the north of the island. Archaeology shows early iron-using settlements in the region, notably at [[e:anuradhapura|Anuradhapura]], that predate the chronicles' kings.
kingdom-of-tambapanni.e: According to the chronicles, [[e:prince-vijaya|Vijaya]]'s nephew [[e:panduvasudeva|Panduvasudeva]] moved the seat of rule to Upatissa Gama, and his grandson [[e:pandukabhaya|Pandukabhaya]] founded [[e:anuradhapura|Anuradhapura]] around 437 BCE, beginning the [[s:anuradhapura-kingdom|Anuradhapura Kingdom]]. The Greek name for [[s:sri-lanka|Sri Lanka]], [[e:taprobane|Taprobane]], derives from Tambapanni.

kingdom-of-hermopolis.t: A short-lived Middle Egyptian kingdom whose king Nimlot defied, then surrendered to, the Kushite conqueror Piye.
kingdom-of-hermopolis.o: As the [[s:twenty-second-dynasty-of-egypt|Twenty-second Dynasty of Egypt]] fragmented in the 8th century BCE, [[e:hermopolis|Hermopolis]], the cult centre of the god [[e:thoth|Thoth]], became the seat of an independent local king. Its ruler [[e:nimlot-of-hermopolis|Nimlot]] (Namart), probably of Libyan descent, held the region of [[e:middle-egypt|Middle Egypt]] around the city by about 750 BCE.
kingdom-of-hermopolis.r: Almost all that is known comes from the [[e:victory-stela-of-piye|Victory Stela of Piye]]. [[e:nimlot-of-hermopolis|Nimlot]] first acknowledged Kushite overlordship, then joined the coalition of [[e:tefnakht|Tefnakht of Sais]], which brought on a Kushite siege. After a long siege his queen pleaded with [[e:piye|Piye's]] women, and Nimlot surrendered his treasures and horses; Piye, a lover of horses, was angered to find them starving.
kingdom-of-hermopolis.e: [[e:nimlot-of-hermopolis|Nimlot]] was allowed to keep his throne as a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the [[s:kushite-empire|Kushite Empire]] after about 728 BCE, but the kingdom vanishes from the record soon after.

kingdom-of-paris.t: Merovingian kingdom centred on Paris, created when Clovis' realm was divided among his sons in 511.
kingdom-of-paris.o: On the death of [[e:clovis-i|Clovis]] in 511 the [[s:kingdom-of-the-franks|Kingdom of the Franks]] was shared among his four sons. [[e:childebert-i|Childebert I]] received the lands around [[e:paris|Paris]], together with the [[e:english-channel|Channel]] coast and later parts of [[s:duchy-of-aquitaine|Aquitaine]] and [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Burgundy]].
kingdom-of-paris.r: [[e:childebert-i|Childebert]] ruled for nearly fifty years, campaigning against the [[s:kingdom-of-the-burgundians|Kingdom of the Burgundians]] and the [[e:visigoths|Visigoths]] in [[e:spain|Spain]], from where he brought back relics of [[e:vincent-of-saragossa|Saint Vincent]]. For them he founded the abbey later called [[e:saint-germain-des-pres|Saint-Germain-des-Prés]]. He joined his brother [[e:chlothar-i|Chlothar I]] in murdering their nephews, the sons of [[e:chlodomer|Chlodomer of Orléans]].
kingdom-of-paris.e: [[e:childebert-i|Childebert]] died without sons in 558, and [[e:chlothar-i|Chlothar I]] briefly reunited the Frankish lands. In 561 [[e:paris|Paris]] passed to Chlothar's son [[e:charibert-i|Charibert I]], and after Charibert's death in 567 his kingdom was divided among his brothers, with Paris shared between them.

kingdom-of-portugal.t: One of Europe's oldest kingdoms, which fixed its borders by 1249, led the age of oceanic exploration and lasted until the revolution of 1910.
kingdom-of-portugal.o: The [[s:county-of-portugal|County of Portugal]], a fief of León, passed to [[e:afonso-i-of-portugal|Afonso Henriques]], who styled himself king after his victory at [[e:battle-of-ourique|Ourique]] in 1139. León recognised him at [[e:zamora|Zamora]] in 1143 and the [[e:papacy|papacy]] in 1179. With crusader help he took [[e:lisbon|Lisbon]] in 1147, and [[e:afonso-iii-of-portugal|Afonso III]] completed the conquest of the [[e:algarve|Algarve]] in 1249.
kingdom-of-portugal.r: Portugal was a Catholic monarchy with [[e:cortes|Cortes]], military orders and a strong maritime economy. In 1385 [[e:john-i-of-portugal|John I]], founder of the [[e:house-of-aviz|Aviz]] dynasty, defeated [[s:kingdom-of-castile|Castile]] at [[e:battle-of-aljubarrota|Aljubarrota]], and his descendants launched the voyages that created the [[s:portuguese-empire|Portuguese Empire]]. [[e:pepper|Pepper]], Brazilian [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] and gold financed the crown. [[e:manuel-i-of-portugal|Manuel I]] ruled at the peak of the spice trade.
kingdom-of-portugal.e: The kingdom fell under Spanish kings in the [[s:iberian-union|Iberian Union]] from 1580 to 1640, then revived under the [[e:house-of-braganza|Braganzas]]. After the 1908 assassination of Carlos I, a revolution on 5 October 1910 ended the monarchy and created the [[s:first-portuguese-republic|First Portuguese Republic]].

cr.a: Tonyjeff, based on ancient national symbol.

kingdom-of-toro.t: A kingdom of western Uganda that broke away from Bunyoro in the 1830s, was restored by the British, and survives as a cultural monarchy.
kingdom-of-toro.o: Around 1830 Prince [[e:kaboyo-olimi-i|Kaboyo Olimi I]], a son of the omukama of the [[s:kingdom-of-bunyoro|Kingdom of Bunyoro]], rebelled and set up an independent kingdom in the fertile lands around the [[e:rwenzori-mountains|Rwenzori Mountains]]. Bunyoro's king [[e:kabalega|Kabalega]] reconquered Toro in 1876, but in 1891 [[e:frederick-lugard|Frederick Lugard]] of the [[s:imperial-british-east-africa-company|Imperial British East Africa Company]] restored the Toro dynasty under [[e:kasagama-kyebambe-iv|Kasagama]].
kingdom-of-toro.r: The omukama ruled through chiefs over a population of farmers and herders, with royal regalia and rituals taken from [[s:kingdom-of-bunyoro|Bunyoro]]. Under [[e:kasagama-kyebambe-iv|Kasagama Kyebambe IV]] the court adopted [[e:anglicanism|Anglicanism]], and the [[e:toro-agreement|Toro Agreement]] of 1900 defined the kingdom's place in the [[s:uganda-protectorate|Uganda Protectorate]], with its capital at [[e:fort-portal|Fort Portal]].
kingdom-of-toro.e: The kingdom was abolished with Uganda's other monarchies in 1967 and restored as a cultural institution in 1993. In 1995 [[e:rukidi-iv-of-toro|Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV]] was crowned at the age of three.

kingdom-of-judah.t: The southern Kingdom of Judah, ruled from Jerusalem by the House of David, whose fall and exile shaped the Hebrew Bible.
kingdom-of-judah.o: [[e:judah|Judah]] emerged as a separate kingdom c. 930 BCE when [[e:solomon|Solomon's]] son [[e:rehoboam|Rehoboam]] kept only the southern tribes after the split of the [[s:united-kingdom-of-israel|United Kingdom of Israel]]. It remained smaller and poorer than the [[s:kingdom-of-israel|Kingdom of Israel]], but its capital [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]] held the temple of [[e:yhwh|Yahweh]].
kingdom-of-judah.r: Kings of the line of [[e:david|David]] ruled throughout. [[e:hezekiah|Hezekiah]] dug the [[e:siloam-tunnel|Siloam tunnel]] and survived [[e:sennacherib|Sennacherib's]] invasion of 701 BCE, though [[s:lachish|Lachish]] fell. [[e:josiah|Josiah]] centralised worship in [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]]. Prophets such as [[e:isaiah|Isaiah]] and [[e:jeremiah|Jeremiah]] were active, and inscriptions such as the Lachish letters reveal daily administration.
kingdom-of-judah.e: [[e:judah|Judah]] became a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the [[s:chaldean-empire|Chaldean Empire]]. After revolts, [[e:nebuchadnezzar-ii|Nebuchadnezzar II]] destroyed [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]] and its temple in 587 BCE and deported King [[e:zedekiah|Zedekiah]] and the elite to [[e:babylon|Babylon]]. The exile shaped [[e:judaism|Judaism]], and later [[s:yehud-medinata|Yehud Medinata]] arose under Persian rule.

kingdom-of-klungkung.t: Senior royal house of Bali, heir to Gelgel, whose Dewa Agung was recognised as paramount king of the island until the puputan of 1908.
kingdom-of-klungkung.o: After a revolt destroyed the court of [[s:kingdom-of-gelgel|Gelgel]], the [[e:dewa-agung-jambe|Dewa Agung Jambe]] re-established the main Balinese dynasty at Klungkung (Semarapura) in 1686. Though other kingdoms such as [[s:kingdom-of-karangasem|Karangasem]], [[s:kingdom-of-buleleng|Buleleng]] and [[s:kingdom-of-badung|Badung]] became stronger, they still acknowledged the Dewa Agung as first among the rajas of [[e:bali|Bali]], the heir of the Majapahit-descended kings.
kingdom-of-klungkung.r: Klungkung was small, but its ruler held ritual primacy and presided over Balinese law and ceremonial. The court built the [[e:kertha-gosa|Kertha Gosa]] hall of justice, whose painted ceilings in the Kamasan style survive. In 1849 the [[e:dewa-agung-istri-kanya|Dewa Agung Istri Kanya]], a woman ruler, led resistance at Kusamba, where the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] commander [[e:andreas-victor-michiels|Andreas Michiels]] was killed.
kingdom-of-klungkung.e: When the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] invaded in April 1908, the [[e:dewa-agung-jambe-ii|Dewa Agung Jambe II]] led his family and followers into a puputan, a ritual suicidal march into rifle fire. Klungkung was annexed into the [[s:dutch-east-indies|Dutch East Indies]], and later restored as a regency under the descendants of the royal house.

kamakura-fu.t: The Ashikaga branch government that ruled eastern Japan from Kamakura and repeatedly challenged the shoguns in Kyoto.
kamakura-fu.o: To control the [[e:kanto-region|Kanto]], the [[s:ashikaga-shogunate|Ashikaga shogunate]] created a regional government in [[e:kamakura|Kamakura]]. In 1349 [[e:ashikaga-takauji|Ashikaga Takauji]] sent his son Motouji there as Kamakura kubo, assisted by a deputy, the Kanto kanrei, an office soon held by the Uesugi family.
kamakura-fu.r: The kubo governed the eight [[e:kanto-region|Kanto]] provinces and later [[e:mutsu-province|Mutsu]] and Dewa, with their own [[e:vassal|vassals]] and courts, and acted almost as rival [[e:shogun|shoguns]]. Successors [[e:ashikaga-ujimitsu|Ujimitsu]], [[e:ashikaga-mitsukane|Mitsukane]] and Mochiuji resented [[e:kyoto|Kyoto's]] authority, and tension with the Uesugi deputies led to the [[e:uesugi-zenshu-rebellion|Uesugi Zenshu revolt]] of 1416.
kamakura-fu.e: [[e:ashikaga-mochiuji|Ashikaga Mochiuji]] openly defied [[e:shogun|Shogun]] [[e:ashikaga-yoshinori|Yoshinori]]; in the [[e:eikyo-rebellion|Eikyo Rebellion]] he was defeated and forced to kill himself in 1439. The office was revived in 1449 for his son Shigeuji, who after fighting the Uesugi moved to [[e:koga-ibaraki|Koga]] in 1455 as the [[s:koga-kubo|Koga kubo]].

kingdom-of-ui-maine.t: Kingdom of the O'Kellys in east Galway and south Roscommon, one of the largest subject kingdoms of Connacht, which lasted until the Composition of 1585.
kingdom-of-ui-maine.o: The Uí [[s:county-of-maine|Maine]] claimed descent from Maine Mór, said to have won lands west of the [[e:river-shannon|Shannon]] in the 5th century. By the early [[e:middle-ages|medieval period]] they held a large kingdom in what is now east [[e:county-galway|County Galway]] and south [[e:county-roscommon|Roscommon]], within the over-kingdom of the [[s:kingdom-of-connacht|Kingdom of Connacht]], with privileges of their own.
kingdom-of-ui-maine.r: Their kings, from the 10th century the [[e:o-ceallaigh|Ua Cellaig]], O'Kelly, served the kings of [[s:kingdom-of-connacht|Connacht]] in war and sometimes contested the kingship. [[e:tadhg-mor-ua-cellaig|Tadhg Mór Ua Cellaig]] fell fighting for [[e:brian-boru|Brian Bóruma]] at [[e:battle-of-clontarf|Clontarf]] in 1014. The O'Kellys were famous patrons of learning: [[e:uilliam-buidhe-o-ceallaigh|Uilliam Buidhe Ó Ceallaigh]] held a great Christmas feast for the poets of Ireland in 1351, and the [[e:book-of-ui-maine|Book of Uí Maine]] was compiled for the family.
kingdom-of-ui-maine.e: [[e:anglo-normans|Anglo-Norman]] lords, especially the de Burghs, took part of Uí [[s:county-of-maine|Maine]] in the 13th century, but the [[e:o-ceallaigh|O'Kellys]] kept much of it. Under the [[e:composition-of-connacht|Composition of Connacht]] in 1585 their lordship was converted into crown tenure, ending the kingdom's independent status.
kingdom-of-ui-maine.la: Old Irish, later Middle and Early Modern Irish

kingdom-of-kutai.t: The earliest documented kingdom in Indonesia, known from King Mulavarman's Sanskrit pillar inscriptions of around 400 at Muara Kaman in East Kalimantan.
kingdom-of-kutai.o: Seven stone yupa, sacrificial posts inscribed in [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] with [[e:pallava-script|Pallava script]], were found at [[e:muara-kaman|Muara Kaman]] on the [[e:mahakam-river|Mahakam River]]. They name [[e:kudungga|Kudungga]], his son Asvavarman, called the founder of the dynasty, and grandson [[e:mulavarman|Mulavarman]]. Kudungga's name is not Sanskrit, suggesting a local chief whose descendants adopted Indian kingship and ritual.
kingdom-of-kutai.r: The inscriptions praise [[e:mulavarman|Mulavarman]] for giving thousands of [[e:cattle|cattle]] to [[e:brahmins|Brahmins]] and for performing Vedic sacrifices, showing a court shaped by [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] ideas of kingship. Its position on the [[e:mahakam-river|Mahakam]] allowed it to gather forest products and gold from the interior. After the inscriptions almost nothing is recorded for centuries.
kingdom-of-kutai.e: The later history of Kutai Martadipura is known mainly from the chronicles of its rival, the [[s:kutai-kartanegara-sultanate|Kutai Kartanegara Sultanate]], which conquered it in 1635 and merged the two under the name Kutai Kartanegara ing Martadipura. The yupa inscriptions are held in the National Museum in [[e:jakarta|Jakarta]].

kingdom-of-ife.t: The sacred city of the Yoruba, cradle of their royal dynasties and home of some of Africa's finest naturalistic bronze and terracotta sculpture.
kingdom-of-ife.o: Ile-[[e:ife|Ife]] was a substantial town by the end of the first millennium. [[e:yoruba|Yoruba]] tradition makes it the place where the world was created and where [[e:oduduwa|Oduduwa]], ancestor of the Yoruba kings, established the first throne; his descendants are said to have founded the other Yoruba kingdoms and the [[e:oba-dynasty|Oba dynasty]] of the [[s:benin-empire|Benin Empire]].
kingdom-of-ife.r: The Ooni of [[e:ife|Ife]] ruled as a sacred king. Between the 12th and 15th centuries Ife artists cast [[e:copper|copper]]-alloy heads and modelled terracottas of striking realism, and the city made glass [[e:bead|beads]] that were traded widely. Streets and courtyards were paved with potsherds. Ife's authority was chiefly religious, conferring legitimacy on other [[e:yoruba|Yoruba]] rulers.
kingdom-of-ife.e: Political power passed to the [[s:oyo-empire|Oyo Empire]] and other states, and in the 19th century [[e:ife|Ife]] was devastated in the [[e:yoruba|Yoruba]] civil wars and long conflict with neighbouring [[e:modakeke|Modakeke]]. It came under British rule around 1900. The Ooni still reigns in Ile-Ife, one of [[e:nigeria|Nigeria's]] most senior traditional rulers.

kingdom-of-tenkodogo.t: Mossi kingdom of south-eastern Burkina Faso, held by tradition to be the oldest of the Mossi states.
kingdom-of-tenkodogo.o: [[e:mossi|Mossi]] tradition tells that [[e:yennenga|Yennenga]], a princess of [[s:mamprugu|Mamprugu]], rode north and bore a son, [[e:ouedraogo|Ouedraogo]], to a hunter named Riale. Ouedraogo and his descendants founded the Mossi kingdoms, and Tenkodogo, 'the old land', is regarded as the first of them, established around the 15th century in the [[e:white-volta|White Volta]] basin.
kingdom-of-tenkodogo.r: The Naaba of Tenkodogo ruled through chiefs descended from the royal house over farming villages, whose earth-priests (tengsoba) kept rites of the land. The [[e:mossi|Mossi]] system combined mounted aristocracies with local religious authority. Tenkodogo later became less powerful than the [[s:kingdom-of-ouagadougou|Kingdom of Ouagadougou]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-yatenga|Kingdom of Yatenga]].
kingdom-of-tenkodogo.e: French forces brought Tenkodogo under colonial control in 1897, and it became part of [[s:french-west-africa|French West Africa]], later [[s:french-upper-volta|French Upper Volta]]. The Naaba of Tenkodogo remains a recognised traditional ruler in [[e:burkina-faso|Burkina Faso]].

kingdom-of-poland-1025-1385.t: The Piast kingdom of Poland, which fragmented into rival duchies, was reunited in 1320 and flourished under Casimir the Great.
kingdom-of-poland-1025-1385.o: [[e:boleslaw-i-the-brave|Boleslaw I the Brave]] was crowned king in 1025, turning the [[s:duchy-of-poland|Duchy of Poland]] into a kingdom. His son [[e:mieszko-ii-lambert|Mieszko II]] faced invasion and revolt, and in the 1030s a pagan uprising and a Bohemian raid devastated [[s:duchy-of-greater-poland|Greater Poland]]. Casimir I the Restorer rebuilt the state and made [[e:krakow|Krakow]] its main seat.
kingdom-of-poland-1025-1385.r: Under the testament of [[e:boleslaw-iii-wrymouth|Boleslaw III]] in 1138 the realm was divided among his sons, with the senior duke ruling [[e:krakow|Krakow]]. For almost two centuries [[e:poland|Poland]] was a patchwork of duchies, settled by German colonists and towns under German law and hit by the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] in 1241. The church, with the archbishopric of [[e:gniezno|Gniezno]], held it together.
kingdom-of-poland-1025-1385.e: [[e:wladyslaw-i-lokietek|Wladyslaw I the Elbow-high]] reunited much of the country and was crowned in 1320. His son [[e:casimir-iii-the-great|Casimir III the Great]] codified law, founded the [[e:jagiellonian-university|University of Krakow]] in 1364 and added [[e:red-ruthenia|Red Ruthenia]]. After Louis of [[e:hungary|Hungary]], his daughter [[e:jadwiga-of-poland|Jadwiga]] married [[e:w-adys-aw-ii-jagie-o|Jogaila]] of [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] under the [[e:union-of-krewo|Union of Krewo]] of 1385, beginning the [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1385-1569|Kingdom of Poland]] (1385-1569).

kingdom-of-niumi.t: Mandinka kingdom at the mouth of the Gambia river, whose rulers taxed European ships and traders for four centuries.
kingdom-of-niumi.o: Niumi, called Barra by Europeans, was one of the [[e:mandinka|Mandinka]] kingdoms founded along the [[e:the-gambia|Gambia]] river as [[s:mali-empire|Mali Empire]] influence spread westward, probably by the 15th century. It occupied the north bank at the river mouth, including the villages of [[e:juffure|Juffure]] and [[e:albreda|Albreda]], opposite [[e:kunta-kinteh-island|James Island]].
kingdom-of-niumi.r: The [[e:mansa|mansa]] was chosen in rotation from royal lineages based in several towns, with [[e:essau|Essau]] as the royal seat. Niumi collected customs from European ships entering the river and supplied food, water and slaves. English and French posts on [[e:kunta-kinteh-island|James Island]] and at [[e:albreda|Albreda]] depended on its goodwill.
kingdom-of-niumi.e: In 1826 Niumi ceded a strip of land, the [[e:ceded-mile|Ceded Mile]], to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], and in 1831 the [[e:barra-war|Barra War]] between Niumi and the British ended in its defeat. It was made part of the [[s:gambia-colony-and-protectorate|Gambia Colony and Protectorate]] in the 1890s and is now a district of the [[e:the-gambia|Gambia]].
kingdom-of-niumi.re: Sunni Islam and Mandinka traditional religion

kingdom-of-cyrene-under-magas.t: The breakaway Hellenistic kingdom of Magas, stepson of Ptolemy I, who ruled Cyrenaica independently of Egypt.
kingdom-of-cyrene-under-magas.o: [[e:magas-of-cyrene|Magas]], son of [[e:ptolemy-i-soter|Ptolemy I's]] queen [[s:euesperides|Berenice]] I by an earlier marriage, became governor of [[s:republic-of-cyrene|Cyrene]] around 300 BCE after a revolt there was suppressed. On the death of his stepfather he grew restive and around 276 BCE proclaimed himself king, breaking away from the [[s:ptolemaic-empire|Ptolemaic Empire]].
kingdom-of-cyrene-under-magas.r: [[e:magas-of-cyrene|Magas]] married [[e:apama-wife-of-magas|Apama]], daughter of the [[e:seleucid-empire|Seleucid]] king Antiochus I, and in alliance with the Seleucids marched on [[e:egypt|Egypt]] in the mid-270s BCE, but was forced back by a Libyan revolt. He ruled [[s:republic-of-cyrene|Cyrene]] and the [[e:pentapolis-cyrenaica|Pentapolis]] for decades, minting his own coins. Later he made peace with his half-brother [[e:ptolemy-ii-philadelphus|Ptolemy II]] and betrothed his daughter [[s:euesperides|Berenice]] to the heir, the future [[e:ptolemy-iii-euergetes|Ptolemy III]].
kingdom-of-cyrene-under-magas.e: After [[e:magas-of-cyrene|Magas]] died around 250 BCE, [[e:apama-wife-of-magas|Apama]] invited [[e:demetrius-the-fair|Demetrius the Fair]] to marry [[s:euesperides|Berenice]] and rule, but Berenice had him killed. She then married [[e:ptolemy-iii-euergetes|Ptolemy III]] in 246 BCE, reuniting [[s:republic-of-cyrene|Cyrene]] with [[e:egypt|Egypt]], and became the queen [[e:berenice-ii|Berenice II]].

kholodny-yar-republic.t: A partisan self-governing district in the forests of central Ukraine, which held out against Whites and Bolsheviks from 1919 to 1922.
kholodny-yar-republic.o: [[e:kholodny-yar|Kholodny Yar]] is a forested ravine area near [[e:chyhyryn|Chyhyryn]], rich in memories of the [[s:cossack-hetmanate|Cossack Hetmanate]] and the 18th-century haidamaka rebels. In 1919 villagers around the [[e:motronynskyi-monastery|Motronynskyi Monastery]] formed a self-defence force under [[e:vasyl-chuchupak|Vasyl Chuchupak]], which took control of some twenty villages and declared loyalty to the [[s:ukrainian-peoples-republic|Ukrainian People's Republic]].
kholodny-yar-republic.r: The district was governed by village councils and its partisan otamans, with the monastery as headquarters. The insurgents fought [[e:anton-denikin|Denikin]]'s Whites and then the [[e:red-army|Red Army]], raiding railways and Soviet detachments, and kept contact with the exiled government of the [[s:ukrainian-peoples-republic|Ukrainian People's Republic]]. Its forces numbered from a few hundred to several thousand fighters.
kholodny-yar-republic.e: [[e:vasyl-chuchupak|Vasyl Chuchupak]] was killed in 1920, and Soviet campaigns slowly broke the resistance. In 1922 the [[e:cheka|Cheka]] lured several leading otamans to a fake meeting and arrested them, ending organised resistance. The story was later told in [[e:yuri-horlis-horsky|Yuri Horlis-Horsky's]] memoir [[e:kholodny-yar|Kholodny Yar]].

kingdom-of-mengwi.t: Powerful 18th-century kingdom of southern Bali, builder of the moated royal temple of Taman Ayun, destroyed by its neighbours in 1891.
kingdom-of-mengwi.o: Mengwi was founded around 1700 by I Gusti Agung Putu, a noble who broke away from the declining [[s:kingdom-of-gelgel|Gelgel]] order and built a new realm in the [[e:rice|rice]] lands of south-central [[e:bali|Bali]]. Through war and marriage alliances it became one of the strongest Balinese states of the 18th century.
kingdom-of-mengwi.r: The rulers dominated an extensive network of irrigation societies and temple congregations, and their state temple, [[e:pura-taman-ayun|Pura Taman Ayun]], surrounded by moats, expressed royal claims to fertility and order. In the 18th century Mengwi also held [[s:blambangan-kingdom|Blambangan]] in eastern [[e:java|Java]] for a time. Power depended on shifting loyalties of [[e:vassal|vassal]] lords.
kingdom-of-mengwi.e: Rivalries with neighbouring courts wore the kingdom down, and in 1891 a coalition of neighbouring courts led by the [[s:kingdom-of-badung|Kingdom of Badung]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-tabanan|Kingdom of Tabanan]] conquered Mengwi and divided its lands. [[e:pura-taman-ayun|Taman Ayun]] is now part of a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage]] cultural landscape.

kingdom-of-dalmatia.t: Austrian crown land along the Adriatic coast, where Croatian and Italian national movements competed for a century before it joined Yugoslavia.
kingdom-of-dalmatia.o: [[e:austria|Austria]] had taken [[e:venetian-dalmatia|Venetian Dalmatia]] in 1797 but lost it to [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]]. After the [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] it recovered the coast, now including the former [[s:republic-of-ragusa|Republic of Ragusa]] and the [[e:bay-of-kotor|Bay of Kotor]], and organised it in 1815 as the Kingdom of [[e:dalmatia|Dalmatia]], a crown land of the [[s:austrian-empire|Austrian Empire]] governed from [[e:zadar|Zara]].
kingdom-of-dalmatia.r: [[e:dalmatia|Dalmatia]] was poor and rural, living from wine, [[e:olive-oil|olive oil]], fishing and seafaring, and many emigrated to the [[e:americas|Americas]]. Its diet, created in 1861, was at first dominated by the Italian-speaking [[e:autonomist-party-dalmatia|Autonomist Party]], but the [[e:peoples-party-dalmatia|Croatian People's Party]] won control in 1870. [[e:croats|Croats]] sought union with [[s:kingdom-of-croatia-slavonia|Croatia-Slavonia]], which [[e:vienna|Vienna]] refused. The Austrian navy defeated [[e:italy|Italy]] off [[e:battle-of-lissa-1866|Lissa]] in 1866.
kingdom-of-dalmatia.e: In October 1918 [[e:dalmatia|Dalmatia]] joined the [[s:state-of-slovenes-croats-and-serbs|State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs]], and then the [[s:kingdom-of-yugoslavia|Kingdom of Yugoslavia]]. [[e:zadar|Zara]] and some islands passed to [[e:italy|Italy]] under the [[e:treaty-of-rapallo-1920|Treaty of Rapallo]] in 1920, returning to [[e:yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]] after 1945.

khanate-of-maragheh.t: A local khanate of the Muqaddam tribe around Maragheh, the old Ilkhanid capital, in the decades between the Afsharids and the Qajars.
khanate-of-maragheh.o: After [[e:nader-shah|Nader Shah's]] death in 1747, the town of [[e:maragha|Maragheh]], south of [[e:tabriz|Tabriz]], and its fertile district came under the hereditary control of khans of the Muqaddam tribe. Maragheh had been the first capital of the [[s:ilkhanate|Ilkhanate]] and site of Nasir al-Din al-Tusi's observatory.
khanate-of-maragheh.r: The Muqaddam khans ruled a small agricultural region of orchards and vineyards near [[e:lake-urmia|Lake Urmia]], maintaining their own troops and paying tribute to the dominant power of the moment, including [[e:karim-khan-zand|Karim Khan]] of the [[s:zand-empire|Zand Empire]]. [[e:ahmad-khan-muqaddam|Ahmad Khan Muqaddam]] is the best-known ruler. They were in frequent conflict with the khans of [[e:tabriz|Tabriz]] and [[e:urmia|Urmia]].
khanate-of-maragheh.e: [[e:agha-mohammad-khan-qajar|Agha Mohammad Khan]]'s [[s:qajar-iran|Qajar Iran]] subdued the Azerbaijani khanates in the 1790s, and around 1800 [[e:maragha|Maragheh]] was absorbed, its Muqaddam khans continuing as governors under the [[e:qajar-dynasty|Qajars]].

kingdom-of-benin-restored.t: The monarchy of Benin, restored by the British in 1914 after the sack of 1897, whose Oba remains a central figure of Edo culture in Nigeria.
kingdom-of-benin-restored.o: After the British expedition of 1897 sacked [[e:benin-city|Benin City]] and ended the [[s:benin-empire|Benin Empire]], [[e:ovonramwen|Oba Ovonramwen]] was exiled to [[s:old-calabar|Calabar]]. When he died in 1914, the British allowed his son to succeed as [[e:oba-dynasty|Oba]] [[e:eweka-ii|Eweka II]], restoring the monarchy within [[s:colonial-nigeria|Colonial Nigeria]] as the head of the [[e:benin-empire|Benin]] Native Authority.
kingdom-of-benin-restored.r: [[e:eweka-ii|Eweka II]] rebuilt the royal palace and revived court ceremonies and the royal [[e:guild|guilds]], including the bronze casters of [[e:igun-street|Igun Street]], who continue to make brass works. The [[e:oba-dynasty|Oba]] had a recognised role in local government under [[e:indirect-rule|indirect rule]], though real authority lay with British officials. Oba [[e:akenzua-ii|Akenzua II]] (1933-1978) took part in Nigerian politics in the late colonial period.
kingdom-of-benin-restored.e: After Nigerian independence the [[e:oba-dynasty|Oba]] remained a traditional ruler, today in [[e:edo-state|Edo State]], with ceremonial and religious authority. [[e:erediauwa|Erediauwa]] reigned from 1979 and [[e:ewuare-ii|Ewuare II]] from 2016, amid campaigns that have brought the return of some [[e:benin-bronzes|Benin Bronzes]] looted in 1897.

kumaon-kingdom.t: The Himalayan hill kingdom of the Chand rajas, who ruled Kumaon for centuries from Champawat and later Almora until the Gorkha conquest.
kumaon-kingdom.o: According to tradition the [[e:chand-dynasty|Chand dynasty]] was founded by Som Chand, a [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] prince from the plains, who established himself at [[e:champawat|Champawat]] in eastern [[e:kumaon|Kumaon]]. The early chronology is legendary, but by the 15th and 16th centuries the Chands had subdued rival hill chiefs, and [[e:kalyan-chand|Kalyan Chand]] moved the capital to [[e:almora|Almora]] around 1563.
kumaon-kingdom.r: The rajas ruled a society of farming villages on terraced slopes, administered through local headmen and land grants to temples and [[e:brahmins|Brahmins]]. They warred with the neighbouring [[s:garhwal-kingdom|Garhwal Kingdom]] and with the [[s:rohilla-state|Rohilla State]] in the plains. [[e:baz-bahadur-chand|Baz Bahadur Chand]], a contemporary of the Mughal emperor [[e:shah-jahan|Shah Jahan]], extended the kingdom to the Tibetan border and is credited with building temples, including the Bhimeshwar temple at [[e:bhimtal|Bhimtal]].
kumaon-kingdom.e: Weakened by court intrigue in the 18th century, [[e:kumaon|Kumaon]] was conquered by the [[s:gorkha-kingdom|Gorkha]] army of the [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Kingdom of Nepal]], which took [[e:almora|Almora]] in 1790. After the [[e:anglo-nepalese-war|Anglo-Nepalese War]] of 1814 to 1816 the region passed to British control and is now part of [[e:uttarakhand|Uttarakhand]].

kingdom-of-khwarazm.t: The ancient oasis kingdom of the lower Amu Darya, a land of canals and fortified towns that kept its own kings and Iranian culture for eight centuries.
kingdom-of-khwarazm.o: [[e:khwarazm|Khwarazm]], or Chorasmia, grew from irrigation farming on the [[e:oxus|Amu Darya]] delta south of the [[e:aral-sea|Aral Sea]]. It appears as a province of the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]] under [[e:darius-i|Darius I]] and seems to have regained independence by the 4th century BCE, when its king [[e:pharasmanes-of-khwarazm|Pharasmanes]] offered alliance to [[e:alexander-the-great|Alexander the Great]] in 328 BCE.
kingdom-of-khwarazm.r: Its economy rested on a dense canal network feeding wheat, [[e:cotton|cotton]], vines and orchards, protected by walled settlements and fortresses such as [[e:toprak-kala|Toprak-Kala]], [[e:koy-krylgan-kala|Koy-Krylgan-Kala]] and [[e:ayaz-kala|Ayaz-Kala]]. Kings issued their own [[e:silver|silver]] coinage, and later Khwarazmian tradition traced their line to the hero [[e:siyavash|Siyavush]]. Zoroastrian practice included bone burial in ossuaries, and the Khwarazmian language had its own Aramaic-derived script.
kingdom-of-khwarazm.e: In the early 4th century CE the ancient royal house gave way to the [[s:afrighid-khwarazm|Afrighid Khwarazm]] dynasty, which al-Biruni dates to 305. The [[s:kushan-empire|Kushan Empire]] and [[e:sasanian-empire|Sasanians]] may have held loose overlordship at times. [[e:khwarazm|Khwarazm's]] distinct language and calendar survived until the Mongol era.
