kingdom-of-circinn.t: A Pictish kingdom or province in the area of Angus and the Mearns, named in early Irish annals and in the legend of the seven sons of Cruithne.
kingdom-of-circinn.o: Circinn appears as one of the seven Pictish provinces in the origin legend that named them after the sons of [[e:cruithne-legendary-king|Cruithne]], and in Irish annals, which record a battle of Circinn in 598. It is usually placed in [[e:angus|Angus]] and the [[e:kincardineshire|Mearns]], south of the [[e:the-mounth|Mounth]].
kingdom-of-circinn.r: Almost nothing is known of its government. It was probably one of the regional lordships within the Pictish kingdom, and the fertile lowlands of [[e:angus|Angus]] held important church sites such as [[e:aberlemno|Aberlemno]] and later [[e:brechin|Brechin]], with their carved Pictish stones.
kingdom-of-circinn.e: Circinn's identity merged into the [[s:kingdom-of-scotland|Kingdom of Scotland]] when [[s:kingdom-of-the-picts|Pictland]] became Alba in the 9th and 10th centuries. The later earldoms of [[e:angus|Angus]] and the [[e:kincardineshire|Mearns]] may continue its territory.

kingdom-of-kullu.t: An ancient kingdom of the upper Beas valley, whose 17th-century Raja Jagat Singh founded the Dussehra festival that still draws gods from across the valley to Kullu.
kingdom-of-kullu.o: [[e:kullu|Kullu]] appears in early Indian texts as Kuluta, and local tradition traces its Pal dynasty to a founder called Behangamani Pal. The early capital was at Jagatsukh and later Naggar. Firm history begins only in the 16th and 17th centuries, when the Rajas took the name Singh and expanded across the surrounding valleys.
kingdom-of-kullu.r: Raja [[e:jagat-singh-of-kullu|Jagat Singh]] (r. 1637–1672) moved the capital to Sultanpur, now [[e:kullu|Kullu]] town, and installed the image of Raghunath, making him the kingdom's divine sovereign. The annual [[e:kullu-dussehra|Dussehra]], at which village deities are carried to Raghunath's presence, dates from his reign. Kullu controlled trade routes to [[e:lahaul|Lahaul]], [[e:spiti|Spiti]] and [[s:kingdom-of-ladakh|Ladakh]], and under Man Singh it reached its greatest extent.
kingdom-of-kullu.e: Weakened by succession quarrels, [[e:kullu|Kullu]] fell under the [[s:sikh-empire|Sikh Empire]], which took direct control in 1840. After the [[e:first-anglo-sikh-war|First Anglo-Sikh War]] it passed to the British in 1846 and became part of [[s:kangra-state|Kangra]] district; the royal family kept only the [[e:jagir|jagir]] of Rupi. Kullu is now a district of [[e:himachal-pradesh|Himachal Pradesh]].

kingdom-of-mycenae.t: The leading Bronze Age Greek kingdom in the Argolid, whose shaft graves, Lion Gate and tholos tombs gave its name to the Mycenaean civilisation.
kingdom-of-mycenae.o: Mycenae occupies a hill in the north-east [[e:argolid|Argolid]] controlling routes to [[s:corinth|Corinth]]. Its rise is shown by Grave Circles A and B, used c. 1650 to 1500 BCE, with gold masks and weapons. In the 14th and 13th centuries BCE a palace, Cyclopean walls and great tholos tombs such as the [[e:treasury-of-atreus|Treasury of Atreus]] were built.
kingdom-of-mycenae.r: Mycenae was ruled by a wanax from a palace with a central megaron and frescoes, and was probably the most powerful of several [[e:argolid|Argolid]] centres including [[s:kingdom-of-tiryns|Tiryns]]. [[e:linear-b|Linear B]] tablets record perfumed oil and other goods. Its pottery spread across the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]], and some scholars link it to the [[s:ahhiyawa|Ahhiyawa]] known from Hittite texts. The [[e:lion-gate|Lion Gate]] dates to c. 1250 BCE.
kingdom-of-mycenae.e: The citadel suffered destructions c. 1200 BCE and the palace system collapsed, though occupation continued until c. 1100 BCE. Later the small town was destroyed by [[s:argos|Argos]] c. 468 BCE. [[e:homer|Homer]] made it the seat of [[e:agamemnon|Agamemnon]], and [[e:heinrich-schliemann|Schliemann]]'s excavations from 1876 made it famous.

kingdom-of-norway.t: One of Europe's oldest kingdoms, forged by Harald Fairhair in the Viking Age and, after five centuries of union with its neighbours, independent again since 1905.
kingdom-of-norway.o: [[e:norway|Norway]] grew out of the petty kingdoms of the [[e:viking-age|Viking Age]]. [[e:harald-fairhair|Harald Fairhair]] of [[s:vestfold|Vestfold]] united much of the coast, traditionally after the [[e:battle-of-hafrsfjord|Battle of Hafrsfjord]] around 872. [[e:olaf-tryggvason|Olaf Tryggvason]] and [[e:olaf-ii-of-norway|Olaf Haraldsson]] imposed [[e:christianity|Christianity]]; Olaf fell at [[e:battle-of-stiklestad|Stiklestad]] in 1030 and, as Saint Olaf, became the kingdom's patron and eternal king.
kingdom-of-norway.r: After a century of civil wars, [[e:haakon-iv-of-norway|Haakon IV]] restored strong monarchy, and [[e:magnus-vi-of-norway|Magnus the Lawmender]] issued a national law code in 1274. Medieval [[e:norway|Norway]] ruled [[s:republic-of-iceland|Iceland]], [[e:greenland|Greenland]], the [[e:faroe-islands|Faroes]] and the [[e:northern-isles|Northern Isles]], and lived from fishing, especially the stockfish trade through [[e:bergen|Bergen]], dominated by the [[s:hanseatic-league|Hanseatic League]]. The [[e:black-death|Black Death]] of 1349 severely weakened it.
kingdom-of-norway.e: From 1380 [[e:norway|Norway]] shared its kings with [[e:denmark|Denmark]], in the [[s:kalmar-union|Kalmar Union]] and then [[s:denmark-norway|Denmark-Norway]] until 1814, when it adopted a constitution at [[e:eidsvoll|Eidsvoll]] but was joined to [[e:sweden|Sweden]] as [[s:sweden-norway|Sweden-Norway]]. Full independence came in 1905 under [[e:haakon-vii|Haakon VII]]. Occupied by [[e:germany|Germany]] in 1940-1945, it became a wealthy oil-producing [[e:constitutional-monarchy|constitutional monarchy]].

kingdom-of-cologne.t: Kingdom of the Rhineland Franks at Cologne, absorbed by Clovis through murder around 509.
kingdom-of-cologne.o: The [[s:franks|Franks]] of the middle [[e:rhine|Rhine]], later called [[e:ripuarian-franks|Ripuarian Franks]], took over [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]] in the mid 5th century as Roman power collapsed. By the late 5th century they had their own king, [[e:sigibert-the-lame|Sigibert]], who ruled from the former Roman capital of [[e:germania-inferior|Germania Inferior]].
kingdom-of-cologne.r: [[e:sigibert-the-lame|Sigibert]], called the Lame from a wound received fighting the [[s:alemanni|Alemanni]] at [[e:zulpich|Zülpich]], was an ally of [[e:clovis-i|Clovis]] and sent his son [[e:chloderic|Chloderic]] to fight the [[e:visigoths|Visigoths]] at [[e:battle-of-vouille|Vouillé]] in 507. The [[e:ripuarian-franks|Ripuarian Franks]] kept their own law, the [[e:lex-ripuaria|Lex Ripuaria]], written down in the 7th century.
kingdom-of-cologne.e: [[e:gregory-of-tours|Gregory of Tours]] relates that [[e:clovis-i|Clovis]] incited [[e:chloderic|Chloderic]] to murder his father, then had Chloderic killed and was raised on a shield as king by the people of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]], around 509. The realm became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-franks|Kingdom of the Franks]] and later of [[s:austrasia|Austrasia]].

kedatuan-of-dapitan.t: A Visayan polity on Bohol whose people, after a raid from Ternate around 1563, moved to northern Mindanao and gave their name to Dapitan.
kedatuan-of-dapitan.o: Dapitan is known from Spanish accounts, especially the [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] historian [[e:francisco-combes|Francisco Combes]], and from Boholano tradition. It was a settlement of the [[e:bohol|Bohol]] coast, probably on [[e:panglao-island|Panglao Island]], ruled by datus and trading with other Visayan and [[e:mindanao|Mindanao]] ports. Its founding date is unknown.
kedatuan-of-dapitan.r: Spanish sources describe a prosperous community of seafarers, traders and boat builders, led by datus over freemen and dependants, with indigenous religion and ties to [[s:rajahnate-of-butuan|Butuan]] and [[e:cebu|Cebu]].
kedatuan-of-dapitan.e: Around 1563 raiders from [[s:ternate-sultanate|Ternate]], perhaps with Portuguese help, attacked [[e:bohol|Bohol]]. [[e:datu-pagbuaya|Datu Pagbuaya]] led many of the survivors to the north coast of [[e:mindanao|Mindanao]], where they founded Dapitan, in today's [[e:zamboanga-del-norte|Zamboanga del Norte]]. Pagbuaya later helped the Spanish, and Dapitan became an early mission centre.

kingdom-of-maynila.t: The Muslim Tagalog kingdom on the south bank of the Pasig River, closely tied to Brunei, whose capture in 1571 gave Spain its Philippine capital.
kingdom-of-maynila.o: Maynila grew on the southern side of the [[e:pasig-river|Pasig River]] mouth, across from [[s:kingdom-of-tondo|Tondo]]. Tradition holds that around 1500 [[e:bolkiah|Sultan Bolkiah]] of [[s:brunei-sultanate|Brunei]] conquered it and set up a ruling family allied to Brunei, beginning with [[e:rajah-salalila|Rajah Salalila]]. By the 16th century its elite was Muslim and spoke of the Bruneian court as kin.
kingdom-of-maynila.r: Maynila was a fortified port with a palisade and bronze [[e:field-artillery|cannon]], trading with Chinese, Bornean and Japanese merchants. Power was shared between [[e:rajah-matanda|Rajah Matanda]] and his nephew [[e:rajah-sulayman|Rajah Sulayman]], who led a nobility of datus over freemen and dependants.
kingdom-of-maynila.e: In 1570 a Spanish force under [[e:martin-de-goiti|Martin de Goiti]] burned the town after a clash with Sulayman. In 1571 [[e:miguel-lopez-de-legazpi|Miguel Lopez de Legazpi]] occupied the site and founded Spanish [[e:manila|Manila]]. A coalition led by [[e:tarik-sulayman|Tarik Sulayman]] of Macabebe, often confused with [[e:rajah-sulayman|Rajah Sulayman]], was defeated at [[e:battle-of-bangkusay-channel|Bangkusay]] that June, and Manila became the capital of the [[s:captaincy-general-of-the-philippines|Captaincy General of the Philippines]].

kingdom-of-vatsa.t: The kingdom of Kaushambi on the Yamuna, ruled by the romantic hero Udayana and one of the four great powers of the Buddha's age.
kingdom-of-vatsa.o: Vatsa lay along the [[e:yamuna|Yamuna]] south-west of modern [[e:prayagraj|Prayagraj]], with its capital at [[e:kausambi|Kaushambi]]. Tradition says the Kuru royal house moved there after [[e:hastinapura|Hastinapura]] was destroyed by a flood, and the Vatsa kings claimed that descent. By the 6th century BCE it was one of the four leading kingdoms, alongside [[s:kingdom-of-magadha|Magadha]], [[s:kingdom-of-kosala|Kosala]] and [[s:kingdom-of-avanti|Avanti]].
kingdom-of-vatsa.r: [[e:kausambi|Kaushambi]] was a large walled city on the trade routes between the [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges plain]] and the west. Its best-known king, [[e:udayana-of-vatsa|Udayana]], a contemporary of the [[e:gautama-buddha|Buddha]], became the hero of later [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] plays such as [[e:bhasa|Bhasa's]] [[e:svapnavasavadatta|Svapnavasavadatta]], which tells of his love for [[e:vasavadatta|Vasavadatta]], daughter of [[e:pradyota|Chanda Pradyota]] of [[s:kingdom-of-avanti|Avanti]]. Kaushambi had important Buddhist monasteries, including the [[e:ghositarama|Ghositarama]].
kingdom-of-vatsa.e: After [[e:udayana-of-vatsa|Udayana]] the kingdom declined. It appears to have passed under the [[s:kingdom-of-avanti|Kingdom of Avanti]] and then, with Avanti, under the [[s:kingdom-of-magadha|Kingdom of Magadha]] by the 4th century BCE. [[e:kausambi|Kaushambi]] stayed an important city under the [[e:maurya-empire|Mauryas]] and [[e:shunga-empire|Shungas]].

kingdom-of-singapura.t: The 14th-century Malay port kingdom on Singapore island, founded according to legend by Sang Nila Utama and ancestor of the Malacca Sultanate.
kingdom-of-singapura.o: The [[e:malay-annals|Malay Annals]] tell how [[e:sang-nila-utama|Sang Nila Utama]], a prince of [[e:palembang|Palembang]], landed on the island of [[e:temasek|Temasek]], saw a beast he took for a lion and named the place Singapura, lion city. The register follows the traditional date of 1299. Chinese traveller Wang [[s:kingdom-of-dayuan|Dayuan]] described Danmaxi, Temasek, around 1330, with a settlement on a hill and [[e:piracy|pirates]] in the strait.
kingdom-of-singapura.r: Excavations on [[e:fort-canning-hill|Fort Canning Hill]] and along the [[s:singapore|Singapore]] River have uncovered Chinese ceramics, gold ornaments and workshops, confirming a busy 14th-century port. Its rulers, called raja, presided over a Malay court and trade in forest goods, [[e:tin|tin]] and textiles, under pressure from both [[e:majapahit-empire|Majapahit]] and Siam.
kingdom-of-singapura.e: Around 1398 the kingdom fell to an attack, attributed by the [[e:malay-annals|Malay Annals]] to [[e:majapahit-empire|Majapahit]] and by Portuguese sources to Siam. The last ruler, [[e:parameswara|Iskandar Shah]], also known as Parameswara, fled north and founded the [[s:malacca-sultanate|Malacca Sultanate]]. [[s:singapore|Singapore]] was refounded as a British port in 1819.

kingdom-of-kent.t: The first English kingdom to accept Christianity, under Æthelberht in 597, and the home of the earliest laws written in English.
kingdom-of-kent.o: [[e:bede|Bede]] says Kent was settled by [[e:jutes|Jutes]] led by [[e:hengist-and-horsa|Hengest and Horsa]], who came as [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]] of [[e:vortigern|Vortigern]] around 449 and then turned against the [[e:britons-celtic-people|Britons]]. The story is legendary, but archaeology shows strong links with [[e:jutland|Jutland]] and Frankish [[e:gaul|Gaul]] by the 6th century. The kingdom took its name from the British [[s:cantiaci|Cantiaci]], and its centre was [[e:canterbury|Canterbury]].
kingdom-of-kent.r: [[e:aethelberht-of-kent|Æthelberht]], king from about 589 to 616, married the Frankish Christian princess [[e:bertha-of-kent|Bertha]] and in 597 received [[e:augustine-of-canterbury|Augustine]]'s mission from [[e:pope-gregory-i|Pope Gregory]], making [[e:canterbury|Canterbury]] the seat of the English Church. His law code is the earliest document in English. Kent was rich from trade with [[s:kingdom-of-the-franks|Francia]], producing fine garnet jewellery and gold coinage, and later kings such as [[e:wihtred-of-kent|Wihtred]] issued further laws.
kingdom-of-kent.e: From the 760s Kent fell under [[e:offa-of-mercia|Offa of Mercia]]; a revolt by [[e:eadberht-praen|Eadberht Præn]] was crushed in 798. In 825 [[e:egbert-of-wessex|Egbert of Wessex]] took Kent, which was ruled as a sub-kingdom by [[e:wessex|West Saxon]] princes until it was merged into [[s:kingdom-of-wessex|Wessex]] in the 860s, later becoming an English shire.

kingdom-of-norway-1814.t: The brief independent Norway of 1814, which adopted the Eidsvoll constitution, still in force, before entering union with Sweden.
kingdom-of-norway-1814.o: When the [[e:treaty-of-kiel|Treaty of Kiel]] in January 1814 transferred [[e:norway|Norway]] from [[e:denmark|Denmark]] to [[e:sweden|Sweden]], the Danish prince [[e:christian-viii-of-denmark|Christian Frederik]], governor in Norway, led resistance. A constituent assembly at [[e:eidsvoll|Eidsvoll]] adopted a liberal constitution on 17 May 1814 and elected him king.
kingdom-of-norway-1814.r: The constitution, inspired by the American and French revolutions, divided power between king, an elected parliament, the [[e:storting|Storting]], and independent courts, and gave the vote to a relatively broad group of men. The new state had little time to govern: the great powers backed [[e:sweden|Sweden's]] claim, and the country was blockaded.
kingdom-of-norway-1814.e: [[e:sweden|Sweden]] invaded in July 1814, and after a short war the [[e:convention-of-moss|Convention of Moss]] on 14 August preserved the constitution in return for union. [[e:christian-viii-of-denmark|Christian Frederik]] abdicated in October, and on 4 November the [[e:storting|Storting]] elected [[e:charles-xiii-of-sweden|Charles XIII]] king, beginning [[s:sweden-norway|Sweden-Norway]]. 17 May remains [[e:norway|Norway's]] national day.

cr.a: Original: Fredrik Meltzer Vector: Gutten på Hemsen

kingdom-of-deheubarth.t: The kingdom of south-west Wales, founded by Hywel Dda and later led by the Lord Rhys, a centre of Welsh law, poetry and resistance to Norman conquest.
kingdom-of-deheubarth.o: Deheubarth, 'the southern part', was formed around 920 when [[e:hywel-dda|Hywel Dda]] united his inheritance of the [[s:kingdom-of-seisyllwg|Kingdom of Seisyllwg]] with [[s:kingdom-of-dyfed|Dyfed]]. Hywel later also ruled [[s:kingdom-of-gwynedd|Gwynedd]] and [[s:kingdom-of-powys|Powys]], and became the only Welsh king to issue coins.
kingdom-of-deheubarth.r: Hywel was credited with codifying Welsh law, the [[e:cyfraith-hywel|Cyfraith Hywel]], which governed inheritance, compensation and status. The kingdom's centre was Dinefwr in the Tywi valley. Norman lords overran much of it after 1093, but [[e:rhys-ap-gruffydd|Rhys ap Gruffydd]], the Lord Rhys, rebuilt its power, held the first recorded eisteddfod at [[e:cardigan-wales|Cardigan]] in 1176 and patronised [[e:strata-florida-abbey|Strata Florida Abbey]].
kingdom-of-deheubarth.e: After [[e:rhys-ap-gruffydd|the Lord Rhys]] died in 1197, his sons divided Deheubarth in bitter feuds. Its remnants came under Gwynedd's [[s:principality-of-wales|Principality of Wales]], and its lands were absorbed by the English crown after 1283.

kingdom-of-gelgel.t: The Balinese kingdom founded after Majapahit's conquest, whose 16th-century court shaped classical Balinese Hindu culture.
kingdom-of-gelgel.o: After [[e:majapahit-empire|Majapahit's]] conquest of the [[s:bedulu-kingdom|Bedulu Kingdom]] in 1343, Javanese rulers of the Kepakisan line were installed at Samprangan. By the late 14th century the court moved to Gelgel, near [[s:kingdom-of-klungkung|Klungkung]] in southeast [[e:bali|Bali]], which became the island's royal centre.
kingdom-of-gelgel.r: Under [[e:dalem-waturenggong|Dalem Waturenggong]] in the 16th century Gelgel ruled [[e:bali|Bali]], [[e:lombok|Lombok]], [[s:blambangan-kingdom|Blambangan]] in [[e:java|Java]] and parts of [[e:sumbawa|Sumbawa]]. The Javanese priest [[e:dang-hyang-nirartha|Dang Hyang Nirartha]], who came to Bali in that era, reshaped Balinese [[e:hinduism|Hinduism]] and founded temples such as [[e:tanah-lot|Tanah Lot]] and [[e:pura-luhur-uluwatu|Uluwatu]]. Many Javanese nobles and priests fled to Gelgel as [[e:islam|Islam]] spread in Java. [[e:dutch|Dutch]] sailors under [[e:cornelis-de-houtman|Cornelis de Houtman]] visited in 1597.
kingdom-of-gelgel.e: In the 17th century Gelgel lost its overseas lands and faced revolts, including that of [[e:gusti-agung-maruti|Gusti Agung Maruti]] around 1651. In 1686 [[e:dewa-agung-jambe|Dewa Agung Jambe]] moved the court to [[s:kingdom-of-klungkung|Klungkung]], and [[e:bali|Bali]] divided into several kingdoms, among which Klungkung kept the senior title.

kingdom-of-kars.t: A small Armenian kingdom centred on the fortress city of Kars, ruled by a junior Bagratid line until it was handed to Byzantium.
kingdom-of-kars.o: In 963 [[e:ashot-iii-of-armenia|Ashot III of Bagratid Armenia]] gave the district of [[e:vanand|Vanand]], with the fortress of [[e:kars|Kars]], to his brother [[e:mushegh-of-kars|Mushegh]], who took the title king. The kingdom remained linked to the senior line at Ani while governing its own affairs.
kingdom-of-kars.r: [[e:kars|Kars]] was a strong fortress town on the route from [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]] to the [[e:caucasus|Caucasus]], and its [[e:church-of-the-holy-apostles-kars|Cathedral of the Holy Apostles]], built by King [[e:abas-i-of-armenia|Abas]] in the 930s-40s when Kars was still the [[e:bagratuni-dynasty|Bagratid]] capital, dominated the city. The kings ruled local nobles and peasants and acted as allies and rivals of the kings at Ani.
kingdom-of-kars.e: After [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] annexed Ani in 1045 and the [[e:seljuk-empire|Seljuks]] sacked it in 1064, King [[e:gagik-abas-of-kars|Gagik-Abas]] surrendered [[e:kars|Kars]] to the [[s:byzantine-empire|Byzantine Empire]] in 1065 for lands in [[s:kingdom-of-cappadocia|Cappadocia]]. The Seljuks took the city soon after.

kingdom-of-lori.t: An Armenian Bagratid kingdom in the gorges of northern Armenia, known for the monasteries of Haghpat and Sanahin.
kingdom-of-lori.o: Around 979 [[e:gurgen-i-of-lori|Gurgen]], son of [[e:ashot-iii-of-armenia|Ashot III of Bagratid Armenia]], was given the northern provinces of Tashir and Dzoraget and took the title king, founding the [[e:kiurikian-dynasty|Kyurikian]] line, named after his Georgian-style name Kyurike. The kingdom straddled the borderlands between [[s:armenia|Armenia]] and [[s:georgia|Georgia]].
kingdom-of-lori.r: Kings ruled from fortresses such as [[e:samshvilde|Samshvilde]] and later [[e:lori-berd|Lori]], controlling routes between [[s:armenia|Armenia]] and [[s:georgia|Georgia]]. The royal family endowed the monasteries of [[e:sanahin-monastery|Sanahin]] and [[e:haghpat-monastery|Haghpat]], founded by Queen [[e:khosrovanuysh|Khosrovanuysh]] in the 960s and 970s, which became major centres of learning and [[e:manuscript|manuscript]] copying. The kingdom survived the fall of Ani in 1045 by allying with neighbours.
kingdom-of-lori.e: Seljuk attacks reduced the kingdom to [[e:lori-berd|Lori]] and its gorges, and it paid tribute to the [[s:seljuk-empire|Seljuk Empire]]. In 1118 [[e:david-iv-of-georgia|David IV]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-georgia|Kingdom of Georgia]] took Lori; the [[e:kiurikian-dynasty|Kyurikians]] later held Tavush and Matsnaberd in the north-east.

kingdom-of-sabe.t: Yoruba kingdom in central Benin, on the north-western edge of the Yoruba world, ruled by the Onisabe.
kingdom-of-sabe.o: Known mainly from local tradition. Sabe, or Save, was founded by [[e:yoruba|Yoruba-speakers]] who traced their kings to [[s:kingdom-of-ife|Ile-Ife]], and took shape by the 16th century in the hilly country west of the [[e:oyo-empire|Oyo]] lands.
kingdom-of-sabe.r: The Onisabe ruled with town chiefs and religious societies. Sabe traded with the [[s:oyo-empire|Oyo Empire]], [[e:borgu|Borgu]] and the coast, and was exposed to raids from the [[s:kingdom-of-dahomey|Kingdom of Dahomey]] and the [[e:bariba|Bariba]] of Borgu. It was a small state that survived by shifting alliances.
kingdom-of-sabe.e: Sabe came under French control after the conquest of [[s:kingdom-of-dahomey|Dahomey]] and was included in [[s:french-dahomey|French Dahomey]] in 1894. The Onisabe remains a traditional ruler in the town of Save in [[e:benin-empire|Benin]].

kingdom-of-laos.t: The constitutional monarchy of Laos from 1947 to 1975, independent from 1953 and torn apart by civil war between royalists and the Pathet Lao.
kingdom-of-laos.o: In 1946 [[e:france|France]] and King [[e:sisavang-vong|Sisavang Vong]] agreed to unite [[e:luang-prabang|Luang Phrabang]], [[s:kingdom-of-vientiane|Vientiane]], Champasak and other Lao provinces into a single kingdom, with [[e:boun-oum|Prince Boun Oum of Champasak]] renouncing his claims. A [[e:constitution-of-japan|constitution of 1947]] made [[e:laos|Laos]] a [[e:constitutional-monarchy|constitutional monarchy]] within the [[s:french-fourth-republic|French Union]], and full independence came in 1953.
kingdom-of-laos.r: The royal capital was [[s:kingdom-of-luang-phrabang|Luang Prabang]] and the administrative capital [[s:kingdom-of-vientiane|Vientiane]]. Neutralist, rightist and communist factions competed, and the [[s:republic-of-geneva|Geneva]] conference of 1962 created a coalition under [[e:souvanna-phouma|Souvanna Phouma]]. The communist [[e:pathet-lao|Pathet Lao]], backed by [[s:democratic-republic-of-vietnam|North Vietnam]], controlled the east, through which the [[e:ho-chi-minh-trail|Ho Chi Minh Trail]] ran, and the [[s:united-states|United States]] waged a massive secret bombing campaign.
kingdom-of-laos.e: After the [[e:paris|Paris]] accords of 1973 a new coalition government formed, but in 1975 the [[e:pathet-lao|Pathet Lao]] took power as communist forces won in [[s:socialist-republic-of-vietnam|Vietnam]] and [[s:kingdom-of-cambodia-1953-1970|Cambodia]]. [[e:savang-vatthana|King Savang Vatthana]] abdicated on 2 December 1975, and the [[s:lao-peoples-democratic-republic|Lao People's Democratic Republic]] was proclaimed.

kingdom-of-sweden.t: Scandinavian kingdom formed by uniting the Svear and Geats, which became a 17th-century great power and later a model of neutrality and welfare.
kingdom-of-sweden.o: The medieval kingdom emerged when [[e:eric-the-victorious|Eric the Victorious]] and his son [[e:olof-skotkonung|Olof Skötkonung]], the first Christian king, ruled both the [[e:svear|Svear]] around [[e:uppsala|Uppsala]] and the [[e:geats|Geats]] of [[s:kingdom-of-the-geats|Götaland]], around 1000. [[e:christianity|Christianity]] and royal power spread slowly, and in the 13th century [[e:birger-jarl|Birger Jarl]] strengthened the crown, founded [[e:stockholm|Stockholm]] and conquered [[s:tavastia|Tavastia]].
kingdom-of-sweden.r: [[e:sweden|Sweden]] joined the [[s:kalmar-union|Kalmar Union]] in 1397 but broke away when [[e:gustav-i-of-sweden|Gustav Vasa]] was elected king in 1523 and introduced the [[e:protestant-reformation|Lutheran Reformation]]. [[e:gustavus-adolphus|Gustav II Adolf]] made Sweden a great power in [[e:thirty-tyrants|the Thirty]] Years' War, and its empire ringed the Baltic, from [[s:grand-duchy-of-finland|Finland]] and [[s:livonian-confederation|Livonia]] to [[s:duchy-of-pomerania|Pomerania]]. [[e:copper|Copper]] and iron mining at [[e:falun-mine|Falun]] and [[e:bergslagen|Bergslagen]] funded the state, and the [[e:riksdag|Riksdag]] shared power with the crown.
kingdom-of-sweden.e: Defeat by [[e:russia|Russia]] under [[e:charles-xii-of-sweden|Charles XII]] in the [[e:great-northern-war|Great Northern War]] ended the empire in 1721, and [[s:grand-duchy-of-finland|Finland]] was lost in 1809. The [[e:house-of-bernadotte|Bernadotte dynasty]] took the throne in 1818, and [[e:sweden|Sweden]] ruled [[e:norway|Norway]] in union until 1905. It stayed neutral in both world wars, built an extensive welfare state, joined the EU in 1995 and [[e:nato|NATO]] in 2024.

kingdom-of-wukari.t: The Jukun kingdom of Wukari in the Benue valley, ruled by a sacred king, the Aku Uka, and heir to the older power known as Kwararafa.
kingdom-of-wukari.o: Wukari emerged as the main [[e:jukun-people|Jukun]] centre as the older Jukun power, [[s:kwararafa|Kwararafa]], declined in the 18th century. Jukun tradition holds that the royal line moved south from earlier capitals such as Kororofa and Puje, and by about 1800 Wukari, south of the [[e:benue-river|Benue]] river, was the seat of the paramount Jukun ruler.
kingdom-of-wukari.r: The [[e:aku-uka|Aku Uka]] was a sacred king, surrounded by taboos and ritual, whose well-being was believed to govern the harvest and the rains; [[e:jukun-people|Jukun]] ritual kingship became a classic case in anthropology. Real administration lay with officials and the heads of related Jukun communities. The economy rested on farming, salt from the [[e:benue-river|Benue]] valley and regional trade.
kingdom-of-wukari.e: In the 19th century Wukari was hemmed in by the [[s:muri-emirate|Muri Emirate]] and [[e:fula|Fulani]] raids. It came under British control in the early 1900s within the [[s:protectorate-of-northern-nigeria|Protectorate of Northern Nigeria]], and the [[e:aku-uka|Aku Uka]] remains a traditional ruler in [[e:taraba-state|Taraba State]].

kingdom-of-kaarta.t: A Bambara kingdom north of the upper Senegal, ruled by the Massasi branch of the Kulibali, rival of Segou until its conquest by Umar Tall in 1854.
kingdom-of-kaarta.o: Kaarta was founded by the Massasi, a branch of the Kulibali dynasty that lost a struggle for power at [[e:segou|Segou]] and moved north-west. Around 1753 their leader Sebamana established a kingdom in the [[e:sahel|Sahel]] country north of the [[e:senegal|Senegal]] river, among [[e:soninke|Soninke]] and [[e:fula|Fulbe]] communities, eventually with its capital at [[e:nioro-du-sahel|Nioro]].
kingdom-of-kaarta.r: Kaarta was a warrior state like the [[s:bamana-empire|Bamana Empire]], with an army of slave soldiers and [[e:bambara-people|Bambara]] warriors and a mostly non-Muslim ruling class over Muslim [[e:soninke|Soninke]] and [[e:fula|Fulbe]] subjects. It raided and fought [[e:segou|Segou]], [[s:kingdom-of-khasso|Khasso]], [[s:kingdom-of-bundu|Bundu]] and the Moors to the north, and controlled routes linking the [[e:sahara|Sahara]] [[e:salt-trade|salt trade]] with the upper [[e:senegal|Senegal]]. Under Desse Koro around 1800 it reached the peak of its power.
kingdom-of-kaarta.e: In 1854 [[e:el-hadj-umar-tall|Umar Tall]] conquered Kaarta and killed its king [[e:mamadi-kandia|Mamadi Kandia]]. [[e:nioro-du-sahel|Nioro]] became an important garrison and religious centre of the [[s:toucouleur-empire|Toucouleur Empire]], and the region later passed into [[s:french-sudan|French Sudan]].

kingdom-of-makwanpur.t: A Sen kingdom on the southern approaches to the Kathmandu Valley, whose fall in 1762 opened the way for the Gorkha conquest of the valley.
kingdom-of-makwanpur.o: Makwanpur was formed in the early 16th century when the Sen realm of [[e:mukunda-sen|Mukunda Sen]] of [[s:kingdom-of-palpa|Palpa]] was divided among his heirs. One branch took the hill fort of Makwanpur and the adjacent lowlands of the [[e:terai|Terai]], controlling the main route from [[e:bihar|Bihar]] to the [[e:kathmandu-valley|Kathmandu Valley]].
kingdom-of-makwanpur.r: The Makwanpur [[e:sens|Sens]] ruled hill and [[e:terai|Terai]] territory with a mixed population of [[e:magar-people|Magars]], [[e:tharu-people|Tharus]] and [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] settlers, drawing revenue from agriculture and trade with [[e:bihar|Bihar]]. They maintained ties with the [[s:nawabate-of-bengal|Nawabate of Bengal]] and its governors in Bihar, from whom they at times sought help.
kingdom-of-makwanpur.e: [[e:prithvi-narayan-shah|Prithvi Narayan Shah]] of the [[s:gorkha-kingdom|Gorkha Kingdom]] captured Makwanpur in 1762. In 1763 he defeated an army sent by [[e:mir-qasim|Mir Qasim]], Nawab of [[e:bengal|Bengal]], to restore its king. The conquest cut the [[e:kathmandu-valley|Kathmandu Valley's]] southern supply lines.

kingdom-of-the-burgundians.t: East Germanic kingdom of the Rhône and Saône valleys, whose destruction on the Rhine inspired the Nibelungenlied and whose laws shaped Burgundy.
kingdom-of-the-burgundians.o: The [[e:burgundians|Burgundians]] crossed the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] in the early 5th century, and in 411 their king [[e:gundahar|Gundahar]] set up a realm on the Rhine, traditionally placed around [[s:free-imperial-city-of-worms|Worms]], as Roman allies. In 436 the general [[e:flavius-aetius|Aetius]] had them crushed by Hunnic troops, a disaster remembered in the [[e:nibelungenlied|Nibelungenlied]]. In 443 the survivors were resettled in [[e:sapaudia|Sapaudia]], around [[s:republic-of-geneva|Geneva]].
kingdom-of-the-burgundians.r: From there they spread across the [[e:rhone|Rhône]] and [[e:saone|Saône]] valleys, ruling from [[e:lyon|Lyon]] and [[s:republic-of-geneva|Geneva]]. King [[e:gundobad|Gundobad]] issued a law code for his Burgundian subjects and another for [[e:roman-empire|Romans]], and [[e:burgundians|Burgundians]] and [[e:gallo-romans|Gallo-Romans]] shared land. The kings were [[e:arianism|Arians]], but Sigismund converted to Catholic [[e:christianity|Christianity]].
kingdom-of-the-burgundians.e: [[e:clovis-i|Clovis]]' sons attacked them in 523 and captured Sigismund, who was put to death in 524. After a final defeat in 534 King [[e:godomar-ii|Godomar]] disappeared and the land became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-franks|Kingdom of the Franks]], later the [[s:frankish-kingdom-of-burgundy|Frankish Kingdom of Burgundy]]. The name [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Burgundy]] has endured for fifteen centuries.

kingdom-of-iceland.t: Sovereign Iceland in personal union with Denmark from 1918, until Icelanders voted to become a republic in 1944.
kingdom-of-iceland.o: After a century of national struggle led by figures such as [[e:jon-sigurdsson|Jón Sigurðsson]], [[s:republic-of-iceland|Iceland]] won home rule in 1904. The [[e:danish-icelandic-act-of-union|Danish-Icelandic Act of Union]], effective 1 December 1918, recognised Iceland as a sovereign kingdom sharing a king, Christian X, with [[e:denmark|Denmark]], with the right to end the union after 25 years.
kingdom-of-iceland.r: [[s:republic-of-iceland|Iceland]] governed itself through the [[e:althing|Althing]] and its own cabinet, while [[e:denmark|Denmark]] handled foreign affairs and fisheries protection on its behalf. A Supreme Court was set up in 1920, and in 1930 the Althing celebrated its millennium at [[e:thingvellir|Þingvellir]]. The economy depended on fishing, and the [[e:great-depression|Depression]] hit hard.
kingdom-of-iceland.e: When [[e:germany|Germany]] occupied [[e:denmark|Denmark]] in 1940, [[s:republic-of-iceland|Iceland]] took over its own foreign affairs and [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], then the [[s:united-states|United States]], occupied the island. [[e:sveinn-bjornsson|Sveinn Björnsson]] became regent in 1941. In a 1944 referendum Icelanders voted overwhelmingly to end the union, and the Republic of Iceland was proclaimed on 17 June 1944.

kalabari-kingdom.t: Ijaw trading state of the eastern Niger delta whose 'canoe houses' dealt in slaves and later palm oil with European ships.
kalabari-kingdom.o: Kalabari tradition tells of migrants from the central delta who settled on an island in the eastern delta and founded Elem Kalabari, known to Europeans as New [[s:old-calabar|Calabar]]. Fishing and salt making gave way to trade with the hinterland by the 15th century, and Portuguese ships arrived soon afterward.
kalabari-kingdom.r: The [[e:amanyanabo|Amanyanabo]], or king, ruled with the heads of wari, the trading houses that owned war canoes and absorbed slaves as members who could rise to lead them. Under King Amakiri, in the 18th century, Kalabari became a major slave port. After abolition it turned to [[e:palm-oil|palm oil]]. The Ekine masquerade society governed much of public ritual.
kalabari-kingdom.e: Rivalry with the [[s:bonny-kingdom|Bonny Kingdom]] and a civil war led to Elem Kalabari's abandonment in the early 1880s, the people regrouping at [[e:buguma|Buguma]], [[e:abonnema|Abonnema]] and Bakana. Kalabari signed a British protection treaty in 1884 and became part of the [[s:oil-rivers-protectorate|Oil Rivers Protectorate]]. The [[e:amanyanabo|Amanyanabo]] still reigns at Buguma.

kittur-state.t: A Lingayat chiefdom in northern Karnataka whose queen, Rani Chennamma, led one of the earliest armed revolts against the East India Company.
kittur-state.o: Kittur was founded in the late 16th century by a family of [[e:lingayatism|Lingayat]] chiefs who served the [[e:adil-shahi-dynasty|Adil Shahi]] sultans of [[e:bijapur|Bijapur]] and held the title Desai. The territory lay between [[e:belagavi|Belgaum]] and [[e:dharwad|Dharwad]] in the fertile black-soil country of northern [[e:karnataka|Karnataka]].
kittur-state.r: The Desais ruled from the fort of Kittur, paying tribute successively to [[e:bijapur|Bijapur]], the [[e:mughal-empire|Mughals]], the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] and Mysore. Mallasarja, who died in 1816, was its best-known ruler. The state was predominantly [[e:lingayatism|Lingayat]] and [[e:kannada|Kannada]]-speaking, with an economy based on [[e:cotton|cotton]] and grain.
kittur-state.e: When Shivalingarudra Sarja died in 1824 the Company refused to recognise his adopted heir. [[e:kittur-chennamma|Rani Chennamma]] resisted, and her forces killed the collector St John Thackeray, but Kittur was captured in December 1824 and annexed. She is honoured today as a pioneer of Indian resistance.

kingdom-of-lombardy-venetia.t: The Austrian-ruled kingdom of Lombardy and Venetia, centre of Habsburg power in Italy and target of the wars of Italian independence.
kingdom-of-lombardy-venetia.o: In 1815 the [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] gave [[e:lombardy|Lombardy]] and the former [[s:republic-of-venice|Republic of Venice]] to the [[s:austrian-empire|Austrian Empire]], which joined them as a kingdom with the emperor as king, governed by a [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]], at first [[e:archduke-rainer-joseph-of-austria|Archduke Rainer]].
kingdom-of-lombardy-venetia.r: Lombardy-[[e:venetia|Venetia]] had an efficient administration, good schools and a prosperous economy, but censorship and police repression made [[e:austria|Austria]] unpopular; the patriot [[e:silvio-pellico|Silvio Pellico]] described his imprisonment in the [[e:spilberk-castle|Spielberg]] fortress. In 1848 the Five Days of [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]] and the [[s:republic-of-san-marco|Republic of San Marco]] drove out the Austrians, but [[e:joseph-radetzky-von-radetz|Marshal Radetzky]] reconquered both. [[e:maximilian-i-of-mexico|Archduke Maximilian]] tried liberal reforms as governor-general in 1857–1859.
kingdom-of-lombardy-venetia.e: Defeat by [[e:france|France]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]] at [[e:battle-of-solferino|Solferino]] in 1859 cost [[e:austria|Austria]] [[e:lombardy|Lombardy]]. After the war of 1866, [[e:venetia|Venetia]] passed to the [[s:kingdom-of-italy|Kingdom of Italy]].

kaga-ikko-ikki.t: A province of Japan ruled for almost a century by leagues of Jodo Shinshu Buddhist believers after they overthrew its governor in 1488.
kaga-ikko-ikki.o: The preaching of [[e:rennyo|Rennyo]] spread the [[e:jodo-shinshu|True Pure Land]], or Ikko, sect among farmers, local warriors and townspeople of the [[e:hokuriku-region|Hokuriku region]]. In 1488 a league of believers rose against the governor [[e:togashi-masachika|Togashi Masachika]], besieged his castle and drove him to suicide.
kaga-ikko-ikki.r: A Togashi relative remained nominal governor, but real power lay with leagues of local warriors and village communities organised around temples of the [[s:ishiyama-hongan-ji|Hongan-ji]], whose head priests in [[e:yamashina-hongan-ji|Yamashina]] and later Ishiyama directed affairs. In 1546 the [[e:oyama-gobo|Oyama Gobo]] temple was founded at the site of modern [[e:kanazawa|Kanazawa]] as the regional centre. Contemporaries called [[e:kaga-province|Kaga]] a province held by peasants.
kaga-ikko-ikki.e: [[e:oda-nobunaga|Oda Nobunaga]] fought the [[e:ikko-ikki|Ikko leagues]] for years. After the [[s:ishiyama-hongan-ji|Ishiyama Hongan-ji]] surrendered in 1580, his general [[e:shibata-katsuie|Shibata Katsuie]] captured the [[e:oyama-gobo|Oyama Gobo]] and crushed resistance. [[e:kaga-province|Kaga]] later became the domain of the [[e:maeda-clan|Maeda]].

kingdom-of-hungary-1000-1301.t: Christian kingdom of the Árpád dynasty in the Carpathian basin, founded by Stephen I, which survived the Mongol invasion and united with Croatia.
kingdom-of-hungary-1000-1301.o: [[e:stephen-i-of-hungary|Stephen I]], son of [[e:geza-grand-prince-of-the-hungarians|Grand Prince Géza]] of the [[s:principality-of-hungary|Principality of Hungary]], was crowned in 1000 or 1001. He defeated rival chiefs, annexed the [[s:realm-of-the-gyulas|Realm of the Gyulas]] and the [[s:duchy-of-ahtum|Duchy of Ahtum]], and built a [[e:latin|Latin]] church with archbishoprics at [[e:esztergom|Esztergom]] and [[e:kalocsa|Kalocsa]].
kingdom-of-hungary-1000-1301.r: Royal counties centred on castles organised the realm, and the king owned vast estates. [[e:ladislaus-i-of-hungary|Ladislaus I]] and Coloman extended rule to [[e:croatia|Croatia]], crowned in 1102. Germans settled in [[s:principality-of-transylvania|Transylvania]] and the towns, and the [[e:golden-bull-of-1222|Golden Bull of 1222]] under [[e:andrew-ii-of-hungary|Andrew II]] limited royal power. The [[e:mongols|Mongols]] devastated the country in 1241–1242; [[e:bela-iv-of-hungary|Béla IV]] rebuilt it with stone castles and new towns.
kingdom-of-hungary-1000-1301.e: Royal power weakened as barons such as [[e:matthew-iii-csak|Matthew Csák]] built regional domains. With the death of [[e:andrew-iii-of-hungary|Andrew III]] in 1301 the [[e:arpad|Árpád]] male line ended, and the throne was contested, leading to the Angevin [[s:kingdom-of-hungary-1301-1526|Kingdom of Hungary]] (1301-1526).

kingdom-of-luang-phrabang.t: The northern successor of Lan Xang, whose royal house survived Siamese and French overlordship to become the monarchy of modern Laos.
kingdom-of-luang-phrabang.o: During the succession conflicts after [[e:sourigna-vongsa|Sourigna Vongsa's]] death, his grandson [[e:kingkitsarath|Kingkitsarath]], with backing from [[e:xishuangbanna|Sipsongpanna]], established himself at [[e:luang-prabang|Luang Prabang]] in 1707 as king, separate from the court of the [[s:kingdom-of-vientiane|Kingdom of Vientiane]]. [[s:lan-xang|Lan Xang]] was thereby formally divided.
kingdom-of-luang-phrabang.r: The kingdom ruled the northern Lao highlands, with Lao, [[e:khmu-people|Khmu]] and [[e:hmong-people|Hmong]] subjects, and was frequently threatened by [[s:myanmar|Burma]], [[s:kingdom-of-vientiane|Vientiane]] and Siam. From 1779 it was a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of Siam. Its capital, with temples such as [[e:wat-xieng-thong|Wat Xieng Thong]] and the [[e:phra-bang|Phra Bang]] image, was the religious heart of Lao kingship.
kingdom-of-luang-phrabang.e: After [[e:haw-wars|Chinese Haw]] raiders sacked [[e:luang-prabang|Luang Prabang]] in 1887, the French consul [[e:auguste-pavie|Auguste Pavie]] rescued King [[e:oun-kham|Oun Kham]], and the kingdom came under the [[s:french-protectorate-of-laos|French protectorate of Laos]] in 1893. Its king [[e:sisavang-vong|Sisavang Vong]] became monarch of the unified [[s:kingdom-of-laos|Kingdom of Laos]] in 1946 to 1947.

kingdom-of-linjiang.t: The middle Yangtze kingdom of Gong Ao and his son, the last ally of Xiang Yu to hold out, conquered by Han forces in 202 BCE.
kingdom-of-linjiang.o: [[e:gong-ao|Gong Ao]] had served as Pillar of State to [[e:emperor-yi-of-chu|King Huai of Chu]], the figurehead of the rebellion against the [[s:qin-dynasty|Qin dynasty]], and led an army into the Nanjun region. In 206 BCE [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]] made him King of Linjiang, with his capital at [[e:jiangling|Jiangling]] in [[e:hubei|Hubei]], the former heartland of the [[s:state-of-chu|State of Chu]].
kingdom-of-linjiang.r: Linjiang controlled the rich Jianghan plain and the river routes to the south. [[e:gong-ao|Gong Ao]] died in 204 BCE and was succeeded by his son [[e:gong-wei|Gong Wei]], who remained loyal to [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]] when other kings defected.
kingdom-of-linjiang.e: After [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu's]] death in 202 BCE, [[e:liu-bang|Liu Bang]] sent [[e:lu-wan|Lu Wan]] and [[e:liu-jia|Liu Jia]] to attack Linjiang. [[e:gong-wei|Gong Wei]] was captured and executed, and his lands became part of the [[s:han-dynasty|Han Dynasty]].

kingdom-of-dedan.t: An oasis kingdom at al-Ula in the Hejaz, a key stop on the incense road and precursor of the Lihyanite kings.
kingdom-of-dedan.o: [[s:dedan-state|Dedan]], the ancient name of the oasis at [[e:alula|al-Ula]], is mentioned in the [[e:hebrew-bible|Hebrew Bible]] as a trading people. A local monarchy is attested in Dadanitic inscriptions from around the 7th century BCE. The oasis grew rich supplying water and provisions to caravans moving between south [[e:arabia|Arabia]] and the [[e:levant|Levant]].
kingdom-of-dedan.r: Kings of [[s:dedan-state|Dedan]] are known by name from short inscriptions, and the town had sanctuaries of the god [[e:dhu-ghabat|Dhu Ghabat]]. In the mid-6th century BCE the Babylonian king [[e:nabonidus|Nabonidus]] campaigned in the [[s:kingdom-of-hejaz|Hejaz]] and listed Dedan among the oases he took while residing at [[e:tayma|Tayma]]. A colony of Minaean merchants from the [[s:kingdom-of-main|Kingdom of Ma'in]] was later based there.
kingdom-of-dedan.e: After the Babylonian interlude the oasis came under the Lihyanite dynasty, and the [[s:kingdom-of-lihyan|Kingdom of Lihyan]] ruled from the same site. The ruins at [[e:al-khuraybah|al-Khuraybah]] near [[e:alula|al-Ula]], with their temple and lion tombs, are now excavated.

kingdom-of-syrmia.t: Realm of the former Serbian king Stefan Dragutin on the Sava and Danube, held as a Hungarian fief and rival to his brother's Serbia.
kingdom-of-syrmia.o: In 1282 [[e:stefan-dragutin|Stefan Dragutin]], king of [[s:serbia|Serbia]], gave up the throne to his brother [[e:stefan-milutin|Milutin]] after a riding accident, keeping some Serbian lands. Through his wife [[e:catherine-of-hungary-queen-of-serbia|Catherine]], daughter of Stephen V of [[e:hungary|Hungary]], he received from [[e:ladislaus-iv-of-hungary|Ladislaus IV]] in 1284 the [[s:banate-of-macso|Banate of Macsó]], [[e:belgrade|Belgrade]], [[e:usora|Usora]] and Soli.
kingdom-of-syrmia.r: [[e:stefan-dragutin|Dragutin]], styled king, ruled from Debrc near [[e:belgrade|Belgrade]], supporting the Catholic Church in his lands as well as [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] monasteries. He joined [[e:stefan-milutin|Milutin]] against the Bulgarian lords of [[e:branicevo|Braničevo]], but from about 1301 the brothers fought for years over the Serbian succession.
kingdom-of-syrmia.e: After [[e:stefan-dragutin|Dragutin]]'s death in 1316 [[e:stefan-milutin|Milutin]] seized most of his lands, imprisoning Dragutin's son [[e:vladislav-ii-of-serbia|Vladislav II]]. [[e:hungary|Hungary]] soon retook [[e:macva|Mačva]] and [[e:belgrade|Belgrade]], restoring the [[s:banate-of-macso|Banate of Macsó]].

kingdom-of-dunoding.t: Small early kingdom of north-west Wales, named in legend after a son of Cunedda, which became the cantrefi of Eifionydd and Ardudwy in Gwynedd.
kingdom-of-dunoding.o: According to Welsh genealogical tradition, Dunoding was named after Dunod, a son of [[e:cunedda|Cunedda]], who received the land as his share when Cunedda's family settled north [[e:wales|Wales]] in the 5th century. Historians treat the Cunedda story as a later origin legend, but Dunoding existed as a distinct territory on the coast south of [[e:snowdonia|Snowdonia]].
kingdom-of-dunoding.r: Little is recorded of its rulers or government. The kingdom comprised two districts, [[e:eifionydd|Eifionydd]] around [[e:criccieth|Criccieth]] and [[e:ardudwy|Ardudwy]] around [[e:harlech|Harlech]], a land of coastal farmland backed by mountains, rich in prehistoric monuments. It seems to have been ruled by a local branch of the dynasty of the [[s:kingdom-of-gwynedd|Kingdom of Gwynedd]].
kingdom-of-dunoding.e: Dunoding was absorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-gwynedd|Kingdom of Gwynedd]] as two cantrefi, probably by the 10th century. [[e:eifionydd|Eifionydd]] and [[e:ardudwy|Ardudwy]] remained administrative districts, later guarded by the castles of [[e:criccieth|Criccieth]] and [[e:harlech|Harlech]] after the English conquest of 1283.

kontagora-emirate.t: A late emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate in western Nigeria, built by a grandson of Usman dan Fodio and notorious for large-scale slave raiding.
kontagora-emirate.o: [[e:kontagora|Kontagora]] was founded around 1859 by [[e:umaru-nagwamatse|Umaru Nagwamatse]], a son of the [[e:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto]] [[e:caliphate|caliph]] [[e:abu-bakr-atiku|Abubakar Atiku]] and grandson of [[e:usman-dan-fodio|Usman dan Fodio]]. Leaving Sokoto, he gathered followers and conquered lands among the Kamuku, Gbagyi and other peoples between the [[e:niger-river|Niger]] and [[e:kaduna-river|Kaduna]] rivers, establishing his capital at Kontagora.
kontagora-emirate.r: Nagwamatse styled himself Sarkin [[e:sudan|Sudan]], and his [[e:emirate|emirate]] lived largely by war. Its armies raided surrounding communities for captives, who were sold or settled on estates, and much of the region was depopulated. The emirate's rulers owed allegiance to [[e:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto]] but acted with considerable independence. Under his son [[e:ibrahim-nagwamatse|Ibrahim Nagwamatse]], from 1880, the raiding reached its peak.
kontagora-emirate.e: British forces under [[e:frederick-lugard|Frederick Lugard]] attacked [[e:kontagora|Kontagora]] in 1901, and Ibrahim was captured in 1902 and later restored. The [[e:emirate|emirate]] became part of the [[s:protectorate-of-northern-nigeria|Protectorate of Northern Nigeria]], and its emir still reigns in [[e:niger-river|Niger]] State.

kadamba-dynasty.t: The first native dynasty of Karnataka, founded by a Brahmin turned warrior, whose reign produced the earliest known Kannada inscription.
kadamba-dynasty.o: According to the [[e:talagunda-inscription|Talagunda inscription]], [[e:mayurasharma|Mayurasharma]], a [[e:brahmins|Brahmin]] scholar, was insulted by a Pallava guard while studying at [[e:kanchipuram|Kanchipuram]]. He took up arms, gathered forest chiefs and forced the [[s:pallava-dynasty|Pallava dynasty]] to recognise him as ruler of the region around [[e:banavasi|Banavasi]] in the mid-4th century.
kadamba-dynasty.r: [[e:mayurasharma|Mayurasharma's]] descendants took the warrior title varma and ruled from [[e:banavasi|Banavasi]], with a branch at Triparvata. [[e:kakusthavarma|Kakusthavarma]] made marriage alliances with the [[s:gupta-empire|Gupta Empire]] and the [[s:vakataka-dynasty|Vakataka dynasty]]. The Halmidi inscription, from around 450, is the oldest known inscription in [[e:kannada|Kannada]], though [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] remained the main court language. The kings patronised [[e:brahmins|Brahmins]] and [[e:jainism|Jains]], and their temple style influenced later [[e:karnataka|Karnataka]] architecture.
kadamba-dynasty.e: Weakened by divisions between branches, the Kadambas were conquered around 540 by [[e:pulakeshin-i|Pulakeshin I]] of the [[s:chalukyas-of-badami|Chalukyas of Badami]]. Later families claiming Kadamba descent ruled smaller states, notably the [[s:kadambas-of-goa|Kadambas of Goa]] and the Kadambas of Hangal.

kingdom-of-adiabene.t: A Parthian vassal kingdom centred on Arbela (Erbil) whose royal family converted to Judaism in the 1st century CE.
kingdom-of-adiabene.o: Adiabene lay between the Great and [[e:little-zab|Lesser Zab]] rivers east of the [[e:tigris|Tigris]], the heartland of ancient [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyria]]. After [[e:seleucid-empire|Seleucid]] control weakened in the 2nd century BCE, a local dynasty emerged at [[e:erbil|Arbela]], becoming a client of the [[s:parthian-empire|Parthian Empire]] and at times of [[s:armenia|Armenia]].
kingdom-of-adiabene.r: [[e:josephus|Josephus]] tells how Queen [[e:helena-of-adiabene|Helena]] and her son King [[e:izates-ii|Izates II]] adopted [[e:judaism|Judaism]] in the 1st century CE; Helena sent food to [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]] during a famine and was buried in the so-called Tomb of the Kings there, and Adiabenian princes fought for the [[e:jews|Jews]] against [[e:rome|Rome]] in 66 to 70 CE. The population spoke [[e:aramaic|Aramaic]] and practised a mix of Iranian, Mesopotamian, Jewish and, from early on, Christian faiths. Adiabene played a role in Parthian succession struggles.
kingdom-of-adiabene.e: [[e:trajan|Trajan]] briefly occupied Adiabene in 116 CE. Under the [[s:sasanian-empire|Sasanian Empire]] it became a dependent kingdom and then a province, ending in the 4th century; [[e:erbil|Arbela]] became a major centre of the [[e:church-of-the-east|Church of the East]].

kingdom-of-cyprus.t: Crusader kingdom of the Lusignan dynasty that ruled Cyprus for three centuries, the last Latin outpost in the Levant after the fall of Acre.
kingdom-of-cyprus.o: In 1192 [[e:richard-i-of-england|Richard I]] sold [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]], recently taken from [[e:isaac-komnenos-of-cyprus|Isaac Komnenos]] and returned by the [[e:knights-templar|Templars]], to [[e:guy-of-lusignan|Guy of Lusignan]], the deposed king of [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]]. Guy settled Frankish knights on the island. His brother [[e:aimery-of-cyprus|Aimery]] obtained a crown from the [[e:henry-vi-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Henry VI]] and was crowned king in 1197.
kingdom-of-cyprus.r: A French-speaking Catholic nobility ruled a mostly Greek [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] population, using the laws of the [[s:kingdom-of-jerusalem|Kingdom of Jerusalem]] and a High Court of barons. The Orthodox church was subordinated to [[e:latin|Latin]] [[e:bishop|bishops]]. After the fall of [[e:acre|Acre]] in 1291 [[s:genoese-famagusta|Famagusta]] became a great [[e:entrepot|entrepot]] for Italian merchants. Gothic cathedrals in [[e:nicosia|Nicosia]] and Famagusta and the abbey of [[e:bellapais-abbey|Bellapais]] survive. Peter I led a [[e:crusade|crusade]] that sacked [[e:alexandria|Alexandria]] in 1365.
kingdom-of-cyprus.e: [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]] seized [[s:genoese-famagusta|Famagusta]] in 1373, and a [[e:mamluk|Mamluk]] invasion in 1426 captured King [[e:janus-of-cyprus|Janus]] and made the kingdom tributary to [[e:egypt|Egypt]]. [[e:james-ii-of-cyprus|James II]] married the Venetian [[e:catherine-cornaro|Catherine Cornaro]]; after his death she ruled as queen until [[e:venice|Venice]] forced her to abdicate in 1489, creating [[s:venetian-cyprus|Venetian Cyprus]].

kubota-domain.t: The Satake domain of northern Dewa, rich in timber and mines, which broke with its northern neighbours to side with the imperial government in 1868.
kubota-domain.o: [[e:tokugawa-ieyasu|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] punished [[e:satake-yoshinobu|Satake Yoshinobu]] for his neutrality at [[e:battle-of-sekigahara|Sekigahara]] by moving him in 1602 from [[e:hitachi-province|Hitachi]] to Dewa, with about 205,800 koku. Yoshinobu built Kubota castle in 1604 at the site of modern [[e:akita|Akita]] city.
kubota-domain.r: The domain drew income from [[e:akita|Akita]] cedar forests and from the Innai [[e:silver|silver]] mine and Ani [[e:copper|copper]] mine, among the most productive in [[e:japan|Japan]]. In the 18th century [[e:satake-yoshiatsu|Satake Yoshiatsu]], known as Shozan, and his retainer [[e:odano-naotake|Odano Naotake]] developed the Akita school of Western-style painting under the influence of [[e:hiraga-gennai|Hiraga Gennai]].
kubota-domain.e: In 1868 Kubota left the [[s:ouetsu-reppan-domei|Ouetsu Reppan Domei]] and fought for the imperial side, suffering invasion by Shonai and other neighbours. After abolition in 1871 it became [[e:akita-prefecture|Akita Prefecture]].

kokand-autonomy.t: A short-lived Muslim autonomous government in Turkestan, set up by Jadid reformers in 1917 and crushed by Soviet forces months later.
kokand-autonomy.o: After the [[e:october-revolution|October Revolution]], the [[e:tashkent-soviet|Tashkent Soviet]], dominated by Russian settlers, excluded Muslims from power. In November 1917 the Fourth Extraordinary Regional Muslim Congress met in [[e:kokand|Kokand]] and proclaimed the Turkestan Autonomy within a future democratic Russian federation.
kokand-autonomy.r: The government, led first by [[e:muhammadjan-tynyshbaev|Muhammadjan Tynyshbaev]] and then by [[e:mustafa-chokay|Mustafa Chokay]], included [[e:jadidism|Jadid]] reformers and some Russian members. It planned a constituent assembly and a militia, but lacked money and troops and depended on the support of the [[e:kokand|Kokand]] population and local strongmen.
kokand-autonomy.e: In February 1918 [[e:red-guards-russia|Red Guards]] and [[e:armenian-revolutionary-federation|Armenian Dashnak]] units from [[e:tashkent|Tashkent]] stormed [[e:kokand|Kokand]], killing thousands and burning much of the city. The government collapsed, and [[e:mustafa-chokay|Chokay]] fled into exile. Its destruction helped spark the Basmachi resistance against Soviet rule.

kingdom-of-alania.t: The medieval Christian kingdom of the Alans in the North Caucasus, a Byzantine ally and Georgian partner until the Mongols destroyed it in 1239.
kingdom-of-alania.o: The [[s:alans|Alans]] who stayed in the [[e:north-caucasus|North Caucasus]] after the Hunnic invasions came under the [[s:khazar-khaganate|Khazar Khaganate]]. As [[e:khazar-khaganate|Khazar]] power declined in the 10th century, Alanian rulers formed a kingdom along the upper Kuban and [[e:terek-river|Terek]] rivers, and around 916 they accepted [[e:christianity|Christianity]] from a Byzantine mission sent by Patriarch [[e:nicholas-i-mystikos|Nicholas Mystikos]].
kingdom-of-alania.r: Kings ruled a land of fortified towns and [[e:hill-fort|hill forts]], controlling the [[e:darial-pass|Darial Pass]] and trade with the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] and the steppe. The Alanian church had its own metropolitan, and stone churches survive in the Zelenchuk valley. Royal marriages linked the [[s:alans|Alans]] to the [[s:kingdom-of-georgia|Kingdom of Georgia]] and [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]]; [[e:tamar-of-georgia|Queen Tamar's]] husband [[e:david-soslan|David Soslan]] was an Alanian prince.
kingdom-of-alania.e: The [[e:mongols|Mongols]] defeated the [[s:alans|Alans]] in 1222, and in 1239 they stormed the capital [[e:kalinga-magha|Maghas]]. Survivors withdrew into the mountains, where their descendants became the [[e:ossetians|Ossetians]]. Others fled to [[e:hungary|Hungary]], the [[e:crimea|Crimea]] and Mongol service in [[e:china|China]], and the name of Alania survives in the official title of [[e:north-ossetia-alania|North Ossetia]].

kingdom-of-idalion.t: Inland Cypriot kingdom famous for the Idalion Tablet, a bronze contract recording how the city paid a doctor to treat the wounded during a siege.
kingdom-of-idalion.o: Idalion grew on the hills of central [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]], near the [[e:copper|copper]]-bearing foothills of [[e:troodos-mountains|Troodos]], in the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]]. By the 7th century BCE it was a city-kingdom listed among Cypriot states paying tribute to the Assyrian king [[e:esarhaddon|Esarhaddon]]. Its acropolis held sanctuaries of the goddesses later called [[e:athena|Athena]] and Aphrodite.
kingdom-of-idalion.r: Idalion controlled [[e:copper|copper]] production and fertile land. The [[e:idalion-tablet|Idalion Tablet]], a bronze plaque of the early 5th century BCE written in the Cypriot syllabary, records that King Stasicypros and the city granted land to the physician Onasilos and his brothers for treating those wounded when 'the [[e:medes|Medes]] and the Kitians' besieged the town.
kingdom-of-idalion.e: Idalion was conquered by the Phoenician [[s:kingdom-of-kition|Kingdom of Kition]] c. 450 BCE and lost its independence, Kition then ruling it with Phoenician administration. The town continued under Ptolemaic and Roman rule but declined.

kingdom-of-macedon.t: The Argead kingdom of northern Greece that Philip II turned into the dominant power of the Greek world, launching the conquests of his son Alexander.
kingdom-of-macedon.o: The [[e:argead-dynasty|Argead]] kings, who claimed descent from [[e:temenos|Temenos]] of [[s:argos|Argos]], built a kingdom in the plains of [[e:lower-macedonia|Lower Macedonia]] around [[e:aigai|Aigai]], modern Vergina. [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]] names [[e:perdiccas-i-of-macedon|Perdiccas I]] as founder in the 7th century BCE; later writers added an earlier [[e:caranus-of-macedon|Caranus]], traditionally dated 808 BCE. The kingdom expanded over the [[e:haliacmon|Haliacmon]] and [[e:vardar|Axios]] plains.
kingdom-of-macedon.r: Macedon was a monarchy whose king ruled with a warrior aristocracy of Companions. It was a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]] c. 512 to 479 BCE; [[e:alexander-i-of-russia|Alexander I]] then courted Greek opinion. Archelaus I moved the capital to [[s:pella|Pella]] c. 400 BCE and hosted [[e:euripides|Euripides]]. [[e:timber|Timber]], [[e:silver|silver]] and horses supported it. [[e:philip-ii-of-macedon|Philip II]], from 359 BCE, built a professional army with the long [[e:sarissa|sarissa]] pike.
kingdom-of-macedon.e: [[e:philip-ii-of-macedon|Philip II]] took [[s:amphipolis|Amphipolis]] and the [[e:chalcidice|Chalcidice]], defeated [[s:athens|Athens]] and [[s:thebes|Thebes]] at [[e:battle-of-chaeronea-338-bce|Chaeronea]] in 338 BCE and founded the [[s:league-of-corinth|League of Corinth]]. His murder at [[e:aigai|Aigai]] in 336 BCE brought Alexander to the throne, opening the age of the [[s:macedonian-empire|Macedonian Empire]].

khairpur-state.t: The Talpur Mirs' state in upper Sindh, the one Talpur principality to survive the British conquest of Sindh in 1843.
khairpur-state.o: The Talpurs, a [[e:baloch-people|Baloch]] clan, overthrew the Kalhora rulers of [[e:sindh|Sindh]] at the [[e:battle-of-halani|Battle of Halani]] in 1783. The victors divided Sindh, and Mir Sohrab Khan Talpur took the northern share with his capital at Khairpur.
khairpur-state.r: When the British conquered [[e:sindh|Sindh]] in 1843 after the [[e:battle-of-miani|Battle of Miani]], Mir [[e:ali-murad-khan-zand|Ali Murad Khan]] of Khairpur had sided with them and kept his state, though he later lost land after being accused of forging a treaty. Khairpur was a Shia-ruled state with a 15-gun salute, a Sindhi-speaking population and an economy of dates, grain and [[e:cotton|cotton]]. The fort of [[e:kot-diji|Kot Diji]] guarded it.
khairpur-state.e: Mir George [[e:ali-murad-khan-zand|Ali Murad Khan]] acceded to [[s:islamic-republic-of-pakistan|Pakistan]] in October 1947. Khairpur was merged into [[e:west-pakistan|West Pakistan]] in 1955 and is now a district of [[e:sindh|Sindh]].

kingdom-of-montenegro.t: Montenegro's brief kingdom under Nikola I, which fought in the Balkan Wars and the First World War before being merged into Yugoslavia.
kingdom-of-montenegro.o: On the fiftieth anniversary of his reign, on 28 August 1910, Prince [[e:nikola-i-of-montenegro|Nikola I]] of the [[s:principality-of-montenegro|Principality of Montenegro]] proclaimed himself king, with the agreement of the Great Powers. The new kingdom kept its capital at [[e:cetinje|Cetinje]] and its constitution of 1905.
kingdom-of-montenegro.r: Nikola continued to rule as a patriarchal monarch, clashing with opponents who favoured union with [[s:serbia|Serbia]]. In the [[e:first-balkan-war|First Balkan War]] [[s:montenegro|Montenegro]] besieged and took [[e:shkoder|Scutari]] in 1913, but the powers forced it to hand the town to the new [[s:albania|Albania]]; it did gain much of the [[e:sandzak|Sandžak]] and [[e:metohija|Metohija]], including Peć and [[e:gjakova|Đakovica]].
kingdom-of-montenegro.e: [[s:montenegro|Montenegro]] joined [[s:serbia|Serbia]] in the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] but was occupied by [[e:austro-hungarian-empire|Austria-Hungary]] in January 1916, and Nikola went into exile. In November 1918 the [[e:podgorica-assembly|Podgorica Assembly]] deposed him and voted for union with [[e:serbia|Serbia]], provoking the [[e:christmas-uprising|Christmas Uprising]] of 1919. Montenegro became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-yugoslavia|Kingdom of Yugoslavia]].

kingdom-of-the-suebi.t: A Germanic kingdom that ruled Gallaecia from Braga for over 170 years, one of the first barbarian realms in the former Roman West.
kingdom-of-the-suebi.o: The [[s:suebi|Suebi]] crossed the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] in 406 with the [[e:vandals|Vandals]] and [[s:alans|Alans]] and entered [[e:hispania|Hispania]] in 409. In 411 they received lands in [[s:gallaecia|Gallaecia]] under their king [[e:hermeric|Hermeric]]. After the Vandals left for [[e:africa|Africa]] in 429, [[e:rechila|Rechila]] expanded south, taking [[e:emerita-augusta|Emerita Augusta]] in 439 and [[e:seville|Seville]] in 441.
kingdom-of-the-suebi.r: The kingdom was centred on [[e:bracara-augusta|Bracara Augusta]] and ruled a Hispano-Roman majority through [[e:bishop|bishops]] and local elites. [[e:rechiar|Rechiar]] became the first Catholic Germanic king around 448 and minted [[e:silver|silver]] coins, but was defeated and killed by the Visigoth [[e:theodoric-ii-king-of-the-visigoths|Theodoric II]] in 456. The [[s:suebi|Suebi]] later turned Arian, then returned to [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]] under [[e:martin-of-braga|Martin of Braga's]] influence around 560. The [[e:councils-of-braga|Councils of Braga]] of 561 and 572 organised the church.
kingdom-of-the-suebi.e: King [[e:miro-king-of-the-suebi|Miro]] was drawn into Visigothic conflicts and died in 583. In 585 the Visigothic king [[e:liuvigild|Leovigild]] overthrew the usurper [[e:andeca|Andeca]] and annexed the kingdom, ending Suebic rule. Its territory shaped the later [[s:kingdom-of-galicia|Kingdom of Galicia]].

kingdom-of-dacia.t: Kingdom of the Dacians in the Carpathian basin, united by Burebista and defended by Decebalus against Trajan, whose conquest created Roman Dacia.
kingdom-of-dacia.o: About 82 BCE [[e:burebista|Burebista]] united the [[s:getae|Getae]] and Dacian tribes, aided by the high priest [[e:deceneus|Deceneus]]. He built a realm from the middle [[e:danube|Danube]] to the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]], defeating the [[s:boii|Boii]] and [[s:scordisci|Scordisci]] and taking Greek coastal cities such as [[s:olbia-pontica|Olbia]] and Apollonia.
kingdom-of-dacia.r: The heart of the kingdom lay in the [[e:orastie-mountains|Orăștie Mountains]], where fortresses and sanctuaries ringed the capital, [[e:sarmizegetusa-regia|Sarmizegetusa Regia]]. Kings ruled with a priestly elite devoted to [[e:zalmoxis|Zalmoxis]]. Gold and [[e:silver|silver]] mining, iron working and trade with [[e:rome|Rome]] supported the state. After [[e:burebista|Burebista's]] murder in 44 BCE the realm split, but it was again a strong kingdom under [[e:decebalus|Decebalus]], whose forces destroyed a Roman army under [[e:cornelius-fuscus|Cornelius Fuscus]] in 86 or 87 CE.
kingdom-of-dacia.e: [[e:trajan|Trajan's]] two [[e:trajans-dacian-wars|Dacian Wars]] (101–102 and 105–106 CE) destroyed the kingdom; [[e:sarmizegetusa-regia|Sarmizegetusa]] fell and [[e:decebalus|Decebalus]] killed himself in 106 CE. Most of the land became the province of [[e:dacia|Dacia]], commemorated on [[e:trajans-column|Trajan's Column]], and Dacian identity later became central to Romanian national history.

kengtung-state.t: The largest of the Shan states, in Myanmar's far east near China, Laos and Thailand, with close cultural ties to Lan Na.
kengtung-state.o: [[e:kengtung|Kengtung]], [[e:tai-khun-people|Tai Khun]] Chiang Tung, was settled by [[e:khun-people|Tai Khun]] people and, according to tradition, brought under [[e:mangrai|Mangrai of Lan Na]] in the 13th century, who installed a governor there. Its ruling house dates from this period, and the city stands by Naung Tung lake.
kengtung-state.r: [[e:kengtung|Kengtung's]] Khun culture, script and [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] were closely related to [[s:lan-na|Lan Na]] and [[s:sipsong-panna|Chiang Hung]], and its rulers balanced between Lan Na, Burmese kings and [[e:china|China]]. From the 16th century it was a tributary of the [[s:first-toungoo-empire|First Toungoo Empire]] and later Konbaung, while trading [[e:tea|tea]], horses and opium across the borderlands.
kengtung-state.e: [[e:kengtung|Kengtung]] came under British protection in 1890 and joined the [[s:federated-shan-states|Federated Shan States]]. The saopha's powers ended in 1959, and the Burmese military demolished his palace in 1991. Kengtung remains the main town of eastern [[e:shan-state|Shan State]].

kroraina.t: The kingdom of Loulan, later Shanshan, on the shores of Lop Nur, whose desert-preserved documents give an unusually detailed view of Silk Road life.
kroraina.o: Kroraina, called Loulan in Chinese, was an oasis state on the north-western shore of [[e:lop-nur|Lop Nur]] in the eastern [[e:tarim-basin|Tarim Basin]], the first stop for travellers leaving [[e:china|China]] westward. It appears in a [[e:xiongnu-empire|Xiongnu]] letter to the Han of 176 BCE. In 77 BCE the Han envoy [[e:fu-jiezi|Fu Jiezi]] assassinated its pro-Xiongnu king, and the Han installed Weituqi, renaming the kingdom Shanshan and moving its centre south to Yuni.
kroraina.r: In the 3rd and 4th centuries Shanshan used [[e:gandhari-language|Gandhari Prakrit]] in Kharoshthi script for government; hundreds of wooden tablets found at [[s:niya|Niya]] record taxes, lawsuits, [[e:camel|camels]] and slaves. [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] flourished, and its monasteries and paintings show Indian and Hellenistic influence. Chinese garrisons were stationed at Loulan, and its kings balanced between [[e:china|China]] and the steppe.
kroraina.e: Weakened by the drying of [[e:lop-nur|Lop Nur]] and wars with its neighbours, Shanshan was conquered by the [[s:northern-wei|Northern Wei]] in 445. The ruins of Loulan and [[s:niya|Niya]] were rediscovered by [[e:sven-hedin|Sven Hedin]] and [[e:aurel-stein|Aurel Stein]] around 1900.
