kingdom-of-wolaita.t: A long-lived kingdom of southern Ethiopia whose last king, Kawo Tona, fought a costly war against Menelik II's expanding empire.
kingdom-of-wolaita.o: Wolaita traditions describe a first royal dynasty, the Wolaita Malla, which ruled from about the 13th century, followed by the [[s:tigray|Tigre]] dynasty, founded according to tradition by a northerner who settled in the region and seized power in the 17th century. The kingdom lay between the [[e:omo-river|Omo]] river and the [[e:east-african-rift|Rift Valley]] lakes, south of the [[e:gurage-people|Gurage]] and [[s:hadiya-sultanate|Hadiya]] lands.
kingdom-of-wolaita.r: The king, or kawo, ruled from fortified residences such as Dalbo with a court of officials and a council of clan leaders, and the kingdom was defended by ditches and walls. Farming of ensete (false banana), cereals and [[e:cattle|cattle]] supported a dense population. Wolaita traded cloth, [[e:cotton|cotton]] and slaves and absorbed neighbouring peoples. Traditional religion coexisted with older Christian traces.
kingdom-of-wolaita.e: In 1894 [[e:menelik-ii|Menelik II]] invaded with a large army, and after fierce resistance [[e:kawo-tona-gaga|Kawo Tona Gaga]] was wounded and captured. Tens of thousands died or were enslaved, and Wolaita was annexed to the [[s:ethiopian-empire|Ethiopian Empire]]. Its memory remains strong in the [[e:wolaita-zone|Wolaita Zone]] today.

kingdom-of-the-algarve.t: Portugal's southern coast, held as a nominally separate kingdom by the Portuguese crown from its conquest until 1910.
kingdom-of-the-algarve.o: [[e:afonso-iii-of-portugal|Afonso III of Portugal]] completed the conquest of the [[e:algarve|Algarve]] by taking [[e:faro|Faro]] in 1249. [[s:kingdom-of-castile|Castile]] disputed the territory until the Treaty of [[e:badajoz|Badajoz]] of 1267, after which Portuguese kings styled themselves Kings of Portugal and the Algarve.
kingdom-of-the-algarve.r: The [[e:algarve|Algarve]] had no separate institutions: it was governed from [[e:lisbon|Lisbon]] as part of the [[s:kingdom-of-portugal|Kingdom of Portugal]], though its title and arms were kept as a mark of conquest. Its ports, especially [[s:kingdom-of-lagos|Lagos]], served as bases for [[e:prince-henry-the-navigator|Henry the Navigator]]'s voyages to [[e:africa|Africa]]. Fishing, salt, figs and almonds sustained its economy.
kingdom-of-the-algarve.e: The title was later expanded under Afonso V, from 1471, to cover territories in [[e:africa|Africa]]. The Kingdom of the [[e:algarve|Algarve]] ended in law with the Portuguese monarchy in the revolution of 1910 and became a region of the [[s:first-portuguese-republic|First Portuguese Republic]].

kingdom-of-viguera.t: A short-lived sub-kingdom in La Rioja, carved out of Pamplona for a royal younger son and soon folded back into the realm of Navarre.
kingdom-of-viguera.o: Around 970 King [[e:sancho-ii-of-pamplona|Sancho II Garcés of Pamplona]], following the will of his father [[e:garcia-sanchez-i-of-pamplona|García Sánchez I]], granted the [[e:la-rioja|Rioja]] lands around Viguera to his younger brother [[e:ramiro-garces-of-viguera|Ramiro Garcés]] with the title of king. The territory, recently won from the Muslims, guarded the upper [[e:ebro-river|Ebro]] and the approaches to [[e:najera|Nájera]].
kingdom-of-viguera.r: Viguera was an [[e:appanage|appanage]] rather than a fully independent state: its kings acknowledged the senior line in [[e:pamplona|Pamplona]] and fought alongside it against the [[s:caliphate-of-cordoba|Caliphate of Córdoba]]. [[e:ramiro-garces-of-viguera|Ramiro]] is said to have died at the [[e:battle-of-torrevicente|Battle of Torrevicente]] in 981. Charters show his sons [[e:sancho-ramirez|Sancho Ramírez]] and [[e:garcia-ramirez-of-viguera|García Ramírez]] styled as kings, though little else is recorded.
kingdom-of-viguera.e: After the line of [[e:ramiro-garces-of-viguera|Ramiro]] faded out in the early 11th century, Viguera was reabsorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-navarre|Kingdom of Navarre]], by then under [[e:sancho-iii-of-navarre|Sancho III the Great]]. It survives chiefly as a case study in how Iberian kings provided for younger sons with subordinate royal titles.

kadana-state.t: A small Rajput state on the upper Mahi river in eastern Gujarat, in the forested borderland with Rajasthan.
kadana-state.o: Kadana was held by a [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] family in the hilly country of the upper Mahi, on the border of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] and [[e:rajasthan|Rajasthan]]. The estate emerged around 1600, though its founding is known mainly from local tradition.
kadana-state.r: The ruler governed forested hills with a sizeable [[e:bhils|Bhil]] population. In the British period Kadana was a minor state of the [[e:rewa-kantha-agency|Rewa Kantha Agency]]. Few details of its rulers are widely recorded.
kadana-state.e: Kadana was merged into [[s:bombay-presidency|Bombay Province]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960. The Kadana dam on the Mahi now stands in its former territory.

kingdom-of-ondonga.t: An Ovambo kingdom of northern Namibia and the first to welcome Finnish Lutheran missionaries, whose influence reshaped its society.
kingdom-of-ondonga.o: Ondonga was one of the [[e:ovambo-people|Ovambo]] kingdoms on the floodplains south of the [[e:kunene-river|Kunene]] river, formed by the 17th century under rulers drawn from a royal matriclan. Its people farmed [[e:millet|millet]], kept [[e:cattle|cattle]] and traded salt from the [[e:etosha-pan|Etosha]] pan and [[e:copper|copper]] with neighbours.
kingdom-of-ondonga.r: The king held wide powers over land and justice and governed through district headmen. Finnish Lutheran missionaries arrived in 1870, and [[e:martti-rautanen|Martti Rautanen]] worked at [[e:olukonda|Olukonda]], translating the Bible into [[e:ndonga-dialect|Oshindonga]]. In 1904 [[e:nehale-lyampingana|Nehale lyaMpingana]], ruler of eastern Ondonga, attacked the German fort at [[e:namutoni|Namutoni]]. Under Martin Elifas, a Christian king who came to power in 1912, Ondonga became largely Christian.
kingdom-of-ondonga.e: German colonial claims reached [[e:ovamboland|Ovamboland]] but had little effect until [[s:republic-of-south-africa|South Africa]] occupied [[s:south-west-africa|South West Africa]] in 1915, after which the kingdom came under South African administration. Ondonga's kingship survives as a traditional authority in independent [[e:namibia|Namibia]].

kingdom-of-amurru.t: Amurru, a kingdom on the Syrian-Lebanese coast built by adventurers in the Amarna age, which changed sides between Egypt and the Hittites.
kingdom-of-amurru.o: Amurru was the mountainous land behind the coast between [[s:byblos|Byblos]] and [[s:kingdom-of-ugarit|Ugarit]], home to fugitives and landless groups. In the 14th century BCE [[e:abdi-ashirta|Abdi-Ashirta]] united them into a kingdom at the expense of Egyptian [[e:vassal|vassals]], and his son [[e:aziru|Aziru]] captured [[s:simyra|Simyra]] and made it his capital, despite angry letters from [[e:rib-hadda|Rib-Hadda]] of [[e:byblos|Byblos]].
kingdom-of-amurru.r: [[e:aziru|Aziru]] defected from the [[s:egyptian-empire-new-kingdom|Egyptian Empire New Kingdom]] to the [[s:hittite-empire|Hittite Empire]] and signed a treaty with [[e:suppiluliuma-i|Suppiluliuma I]]. His successors ruled as Hittite [[e:vassal|vassals]] with family ties to the Hittite court; a treaty with [[e:shaushgamuwa|Shaushgamuwa]] ordered him to stop Ahhiyawan ships from trading with [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyria]].
kingdom-of-amurru.e: [[e:benteshina|Bentesina]] was deposed for siding with [[e:egypt|Egypt]] after [[s:kadesh|Kadesh]] but restored by [[e:hattusili-iii|Hattusili III]]. Around 1190 BCE Amurru was overrun in the attacks by the [[e:sea-peoples|Sea Peoples]] recorded at [[e:medinet-habu|Medinet Habu]], and the kingdom disappeared.

kart-dynasty.t: A Tajik dynasty of maliks who rebuilt Herat after the Mongol destruction and ruled it for more than a century.
kart-dynasty.o: [[e:shams-al-din-muhammad-kart|Shams al-Din Muhammad Kart]], of a family linked to the [[s:ghurid-sultanate|Ghurid Sultanate]], was appointed ruler of [[e:herat|Herat]] by the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] around 1245. The Mongol khan [[e:mongke|Möngke]] confirmed him, and he and his successors became [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[s:ilkhanate|Ilkhanate]].
kart-dynasty.r: The Karts rebuilt [[e:herat|Herat]], which had been devastated by the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] in 1221, restoring its walls, mosques and irrigation. They ruled over Herat, [[e:ghor|Ghor]] and parts of [[e:khorasan|Khurasan]] as maliks, balancing Ilkhanid and Chagatai pressures. After the [[s:ilkhanate|Ilkhanate]] collapsed in 1335, [[e:muizz-al-din-husayn-kart|Mu'izz al-Din Husayn Kart]] ruled as an independent sovereign, patronising Persian scholarship and [[e:sunni-islam|Sunni]] learning.
kart-dynasty.e: In 1381 [[e:timur|Timur]] took [[e:herat|Herat]] and deposed [[e:ghiyath-al-din-pir-ali|Ghiyath al-Din Pir Ali]]. After a revolt in 1383 the dynasty was exterminated. Herat later became the brilliant [[e:timurid-empire|Timurid]] capital.

kingdom-of-jumla.t: The leading kingdom of the Karnali basin in western Nepal, heir to the Khasa Malla realm and head of the Baise Rajya confederation.
kingdom-of-jumla.o: After the [[s:khasa-malla-kingdom|Khasa Malla kingdom]] broke up in the late 14th century, a Kalyal dynasty established itself in Jumla, the former Khasa heartland near [[e:sinja|Sinja]], around 1400. Its rulers claimed the prestige of the earlier Malla kings and became the most powerful of the hill states of the Karnali region.
kingdom-of-jumla.r: Jumla was regarded as the senior state of the [[e:baise-rajya|Baise Rajya]], the twenty-two kingdoms of western [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Nepal]], and at its height received tribute from neighbouring rajas and from the [[s:kingdom-of-mustang|Kingdom of Mustang]]. Its economy rested on farming in high valleys and on the trade of salt and wool from [[s:tibet-1912-1951|Tibet]] for grain. [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] temples and the [[e:khas-people|Khas]] language marked its culture.
kingdom-of-jumla.e: The [[s:gorkha-kingdom|Gorkha]] army of the [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Kingdom of Nepal]] conquered Jumla in 1789 after hard fighting, and its royal family fled to [[s:tibet-1912-1951|Tibet]]. Jumla became a district of [[e:nepal|Nepal]].

kingdom-of-rwanda.t: A centralised kingdom of the Great Lakes ruled by the Nyiginya dynasty, whose colonial-era transformation shaped the tragic politics of modern Rwanda.
kingdom-of-rwanda.o: Rwanda's kingdom grew from a small state near [[e:lake-muhazi|Lake Muhazi]] in the 16th or 17th century, though court traditions push its origins earlier. The [[e:nyiginya-dynasty|Nyiginya dynasty]] expanded through conquest of neighbouring states such as the [[s:kingdom-of-bugesera|Kingdom of Bugesera]], the [[s:kingdom-of-gisaka|Kingdom of Gisaka]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-ndorwa|Kingdom of Ndorwa]]. [[e:ruganzu-ii-ndori|Ruganzu II Ndori]] is remembered as a refounder of the kingdom in the 17th century.
kingdom-of-rwanda.r: The mwami (king) was a sacred ruler with ritual specialists, army chiefs and land and [[e:cattle|cattle]] chiefs. Cattle clientage, ubuhake, bound clients to patrons, and the political divide between the largely Tutsi elite and [[e:hutu|Hutu]] farmers hardened under [[e:kigeli-iv-rwabugiri|Kigeli IV Rwabugiri]] (r. c. 1867 to 1895), who centralised power and campaigned widely. [[e:kinyarwanda|Kinyarwanda]] was shared by all.
kingdom-of-rwanda.e: [[s:rwanda|Rwanda]] became part of [[s:german-east-africa|German East Africa]] in 1897 and of [[s:ruanda-urundi|Belgian Ruanda-Urundi]] from 1916, where colonial rule rigidified ethnic categories. [[e:mutara-iii-rudahigwa|Mutara III Rudahigwa]] died in 1959, the [[e:hutu|Hutu]] revolution followed, and the monarchy was abolished in 1961, confirmed by referendum before the independence of Rwanda.

khaniadhana-state.t: A small Bundela Rajput principality in Bundelkhand, an offshoot of the ruling house of Orchha.
khaniadhana-state.o: Khaniadhana was founded in the early 18th century by a branch of the [[e:bundela|Bundela Rajputs]] of [[s:orchha-state|Orchha]], one of several small holdings created as the [[e:bundelas|Bundela]] kingdoms divided among heirs.
khaniadhana-state.r: Little is recorded of its internal history. Under British paramountcy it was a minor state of the [[e:bundelkhand-agency|Bundelkhand Agency]], ruled by a Raja over a few dozen villages, without a gun salute.
khaniadhana-state.e: Khaniadhana acceded to [[e:india|India]] after 1947 and was absorbed in 1948. Its former territory lies in Shivpuri district of [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]].

kingdom-of-manipur.t: The Meitei kingdom of the Imphal valley, one of the longest-lived monarchies of South Asia, which kept its own royal chronicle for nearly two thousand years of claimed history.
kingdom-of-manipur.o: The royal chronicle, the [[e:cheitharol-kumbaba|Cheitharol Kumbaba]], traditionally dates the founding to 33 CE, when [[e:nongda-lairen-pakhangba|Nongda Lairen Pakhangba]] became ruler of the [[e:ningthouja-dynasty|Ningthouja]] clan. Over the following centuries the Ningthouja kings absorbed the other Meitei clans of the [[e:imphal|Imphal]] valley into a single kingdom known to its people as Kangleipak.
kingdom-of-manipur.r: Kings ruled through the lallup system, under which adult men owed periodic labour and military service to the state. In the early 18th century [[e:pamheiba|Pamheiba]], known as Garib Niwaz, made [[e:vaishnavism|Vaishnavism]] the court religion, though the older Sanamahi faith survived. Manipuri cavalry and polo were famous, and the kingdom fought repeated wars with the Burmese kingdoms to the east.
kingdom-of-manipur.e: Burmese occupation from 1819 was ended in 1826 by [[e:gambhir-singh|Gambhir Singh]] with British help. After the [[e:anglo-manipur-war|Anglo-Manipur War]] of 1891 Manipur became a princely state under British control. [[e:maharaja|Maharaja]] [[e:bodhachandra-singh|Bodhachandra Singh]] signed a merger agreement with the [[s:dominion-of-india|Dominion of India]] in 1949, and Manipur became a full state of the [[s:republic-of-india|Republic of India]] in 1972.

kingdom-of-hungary-1301-1526.t: Late medieval Hungary under the Angevins, Sigismund and Matthias Corvinus, a gold-rich central European power that fell at Mohács in 1526.
kingdom-of-hungary-1301-1526.o: When the [[e:arpad|Árpád]] line ended in 1301, rival claimants fought for the crown. [[e:charles-i-of-hungary|Charles Robert of Anjou]], grandson of a Hungarian princess, won out, was crowned in 1310 and broke the power of oligarchs such as [[e:matthew-iii-csak|Matthew Csák]] by 1321.
kingdom-of-hungary-1301-1526.r: [[e:charles-i-of-hungary|Charles I]] reformed finances, and gold from [[e:kremnica|Kremnica]] and [[s:principality-of-transylvania|Transylvania]] made the Hungarian florin a standard coin. [[e:louis-i-of-hungary|Louis I]] also became king of [[e:poland|Poland]] in 1370. Sigismund, later [[e:holy-roman-emperor|Holy Roman Emperor]], led the [[e:crusade|crusade]] crushed at [[e:battle-of-nicopolis|Nicopolis]] in 1396. [[e:john-hunyadi|John Hunyadi]] held off the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]], saving [[e:belgrade|Belgrade]] in 1456, and his son [[e:matthias-corvinus|Matthias Corvinus]] built the [[e:black-army-of-hungary|Black Army]], a famous [[e:renaissance|Renaissance]] library, and took [[e:vienna|Vienna]] in 1485.
kingdom-of-hungary-1301-1526.e: Under the Jagiellonian kings royal power weakened, and the [[e:gyorgy-dozsa|Dózsa]] peasant revolt of 1514 was brutally suppressed. In 1526 [[e:suleiman-the-magnificent|Suleiman the Magnificent]] destroyed the Hungarian army at [[e:battle-of-mohacs|Mohács]], killing [[e:louis-ii-of-hungary|Louis II]]; the kingdom was then divided between the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]], [[e:john-zapolya|John Zápolya]] and the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]].

kuban-black-sea-soviet-republic.t: A Soviet republic formed in May 1918 by merging the Kuban and Black Sea soviets during the Russian Civil War.
kuban-black-sea-soviet-republic.o: On 28 May 1918 the [[e:communist-party-of-the-soviet-union|Bolsheviks]] united the [[s:kuban-soviet-republic|Kuban Soviet Republic]], centred on [[e:krasnodar|Yekaterinodar]], and the [[s:black-sea-soviet-republic|Black Sea Soviet Republic]], based in [[e:novorossiysk|Novorossiysk]], into a single Kuban-[[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] Soviet Republic, as an autonomous part of the [[s:russian-sfsr|Russian SFSR]]. The merger reflected the threat posed by the [[e:volunteer-army|Volunteer Army]] and by German forces advancing from [[e:ukraine|Ukraine]].
kuban-black-sea-soviet-republic.r: The republic was governed by a council of commissars and fought both the [[e:volunteer-army|Volunteer Army]] and the Kuban [[e:cossacks|Cossack]] government. In June 1918, on [[e:vladimir-lenin|Lenin]]'s orders, much of the [[e:black-sea-fleet|Black Sea Fleet]] was scuttled in the bay of [[e:novorossiysk|Novorossiysk]] to prevent its capture by [[e:germany|Germany]]. The republic struggled with grain requisitions and Cossack resistance.
kuban-black-sea-soviet-republic.e: In July 1918 it was merged with the Terek and [[e:stavropol|Stavropol]] soviet republics into the [[s:north-caucasian-soviet-republic|North Caucasian Soviet Republic]], which the White armies overran by the end of the year.

kingdom-of-georgia.t: The united medieval Georgian monarchy, which under David the Builder and Queen Tamar became the leading power of the Caucasus and the setting of a golden age.
kingdom-of-georgia.o: [[e:bagrat-iii-of-georgia|Bagrat III]], heir to both the [[s:kingdom-of-abkhazia|Kingdom of Abkhazia]] and the [[e:bagrationi-dynasty|Bagratid]] lands of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-iberians|Kingdom of the Iberians]], united western and eastern [[s:georgia|Georgia]] in 1008. The young kingdom first faced Byzantine pressure and then the Seljuk invasions, paying tribute to the [[s:seljuk-empire|Seljuk Empire]] from the 1080s.
kingdom-of-georgia.r: [[e:david-iv-of-georgia|David IV the Builder]] reformed the army, settled [[e:kipchaks|Kipchak]] warriors, won the [[e:battle-of-didgori|Battle of Didgori]] in 1121 and took [[e:tbilisi|Tbilisi]]. Under [[e:tamar-of-georgia|Queen Tamar]], who ruled from 1184, [[s:georgia|Georgia]] dominated [[s:shirvanshah-state|Shirvan]] and [[s:armenia|Armenia]], the [[e:zakarids|Zakarids]] governed Ani, and culture flourished: [[e:shota-rustaveli|Rustaveli]]'s poem [[e:the-knight-in-the-panthers-skin|The Knight in the Panther's Skin]], the cave monastery of [[e:vardzia|Vardzia]] and the Gelati academy. The church and great nobles balanced royal power.
kingdom-of-georgia.e: Mongol conquest in the 1230s made [[s:georgia|Georgia]] a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the [[s:ilkhanate|Ilkhanate]]; [[e:george-v|George V]] the Brilliant restored unity after 1327, but [[e:timur|Timur's]] invasions devastated the country. After 1490 it split into the [[s:kingdom-of-kartli|Kingdom of Kartli]], the [[s:kingdom-of-kakheti|Kingdom of Kakheti]], the [[s:kingdom-of-imereti|Kingdom of Imereti]] and the [[s:principality-of-samtskhe|Principality of Samtskhe]].

kingdom-of-brazil.t: The kingdom created when Brazil was raised to equal status with Portugal, with Rio de Janeiro as the capital of the whole Portuguese monarchy.
kingdom-of-brazil.o: The Portuguese royal court had moved to [[e:rio-de-janeiro|Rio de Janeiro]] in 1808 to escape [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]]. On 16 December 1815 the [[e:john-vi-of-portugal|Prince Regent John]] raised [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]] to a kingdom within the [[s:united-kingdom-of-portugal-brazil-and-the-algarves|United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves]], ending colonial status for the [[s:state-of-brazil|State of Brazil]]. He was acclaimed [[e:john-king-of-england|King John]] VI in Rio in 1818.
kingdom-of-brazil.r: [[e:rio-de-janeiro|Rio]] grew into a royal capital with the [[e:bank-of-brazil|Bank of Brazil]], a royal library, a botanical garden and a French artistic mission. [[e:brazil|Brazil's]] ports had been open to friendly nations since 1808. The crown crushed the [[s:republic-of-pernambuco|Republic of Pernambuco]] in 1817 and annexed the [[s:eastern-province|Banda Oriental]] as [[s:cisplatina|Cisplatina]]. [[e:slavery|Slavery]] and the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]] continued to expand.
kingdom-of-brazil.e: The liberal revolution in [[e:porto|Porto]] in 1820 forced [[e:john-vi-of-portugal|John VI]] to return to [[e:lisbon|Lisbon]] in 1821, leaving his son Pedro as regent. When the [[e:cortes|Portuguese Cortes]] sought to reduce [[e:brazil|Brazil's]] status, Pedro declared independence on 7 September 1822 and founded the [[e:brazilian-empire|Empire of Brazil]].

kingdom-of-yatenga.t: Northern Mossi kingdom of Burkina Faso, a long-standing rival of Ouagadougou, ruled from Ouahigouya.
kingdom-of-yatenga.o: [[e:mossi|Mossi]] tradition says Yatenga was founded around 1540 by [[e:yadega|Yadega]], a prince who left the [[s:kingdom-of-ouagadougou|Kingdom of Ouagadougou]] after a succession dispute and carried off part of the royal regalia. He and his successors conquered the northern lands of the [[e:white-volta|White Volta]] basin from earlier inhabitants.
kingdom-of-yatenga.r: The Yatenga Naaba ruled with ministers and provincial chiefs, while earth-priests kept their role in rites of the land. Under [[e:naaba-kango|Naaba Kango]], who reigned in the late 18th century, the kingdom was reorganised and the capital fixed at [[e:ouahigouya|Ouahigouya]]. Yatenga traded with [[e:timbuktu|Timbuktu]] and the [[e:niger-bend|Niger bend]] and fought the [[s:kingdom-of-ouagadougou|Kingdom of Ouagadougou]] and neighbouring peoples.
kingdom-of-yatenga.e: Weakened by civil wars in the late 19th century, Yatenga accepted French protection in 1895 and became part of [[s:french-west-africa|French West Africa]] and later [[e:burkina-faso|Burkina Faso]]. The Yatenga Naaba remains a traditional ruler at [[e:ouahigouya|Ouahigouya]].

kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria.t: The Habsburg crown land carved from partitioned Poland, a poor but politically lively province that shaped modern Polish and Ukrainian identity.
kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria.o: In the [[e:first-partition-of-poland|First Partition of Poland]] in 1772 the [[s:habsburg-monarchy|Habsburg Monarchy]] took the lands around [[e:lviv|Lviv]] and south of the [[e:vistula|Vistula]]. It justified the annexation through old Hungarian claims to the medieval principalities of [[s:principality-of-galicia|Halych]] and Volodymyr, hence the name [[e:galicia|Galicia]] and [[e:lodomeria|Lodomeria]]. [[e:krakow|Krakow]] was added in 1846.
kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria.r: [[e:lviv|Lviv]], called Lemberg, was the capital. After 1867 the province gained wide autonomy within the [[s:austro-hungarian-empire|Austro-Hungarian Empire]], run by Polish nobles through a Diet, with Polish schools and universities in [[e:krakow|Krakow]] and Lviv. It was a land of [[e:poles|Poles]], [[e:ukrainians|Ukrainians]] and a large Jewish population, known for rural poverty and mass emigration, but also for oil [[e:well|wells]] at [[e:boryslav|Boryslav]] and a flourishing Ukrainian national movement.
kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria.e: [[e:galicia|Galicia]] was a major battlefield in the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]]. When the empire collapsed in 1918, [[e:ukrainians|Ukrainians]] in [[e:lviv|Lviv]] proclaimed the [[s:west-ukrainian-peoples-republic|West Ukrainian People's Republic]], and the [[s:second-polish-republic|Second Polish Republic]] won the war that followed, taking all of Galicia by 1919.
kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria.re: Catholic and Greek Catholic Christianity, Judaism

kharan-state.t: A Baloch chiefdom of the deserts of western Balochistan, ruled by the Nausherwani family and long a feudatory of Kalat.
kharan-state.o: Kharan was ruled by the Nausherwani [[e:baloch|Baloch]], who claimed descent from Persian nobles. The register dates its founding to 1697. Through much of its history it acknowledged the [[s:khanate-of-kalat|Khanate of Kalat]], while contending for independence.
kharan-state.r: The chiefs ruled a vast, arid territory of sand desert and scattered oases, with a small nomadic and farming population. The British treated Kharan as a feudatory of [[s:khanate-of-kalat|Kalat]] but dealt with its chiefs directly.
kharan-state.e: Kharan acceded to [[s:islamic-republic-of-pakistan|Pakistan]] in 1948, joined the [[s:baluchistan-states-union|Baluchistan States Union]] in 1952 and was absorbed into [[e:west-pakistan|West Pakistan]] in 1955. It is now a district of [[e:balochistan|Balochistan]].

kamarina.t: Syracusan colony on Sicily's south coast, destroyed and refounded several times, whose restless history became a Greek proverb.
kamarina.o: [[s:syracuse|Syracuse]] founded Kamarina around 598 BCE near the mouth of the Hipparis river, on the south-east coast of [[e:sicily|Sicily]], to extend its reach towards the territory of [[s:gela|Gela]]. The settlers laid out a regular town on a coastal hill beside a marsh.
kamarina.r: Kamarina repeatedly defied its mother city: it revolted around 553 BCE and was destroyed, was refounded by [[e:hippocrates-of-gela|Hippocrates of Gela]] around 492 BCE, emptied again by [[e:gelon|Gelon]] in 484 BCE and refounded from [[s:gela|Gela]] in 461 BCE. [[e:pindar|Pindar]] wrote odes for its Olympic victor [[e:psaumis-of-camarina|Psaumis]]. The Greek proverb 'do not move Camarina', said to come from a disastrous draining of the marsh, warned against stirring up trouble.
kamarina.e: Its people evacuated before the [[e:carthage|Carthaginians]] in 405 BCE, and [[e:timoleon|Timoleon]] resettled it in the 4th century. In 258 BCE, during the [[e:first-punic-war|First Punic War]], the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] captured it and sold most inhabitants into [[e:slavery|slavery]]. The site, near Santa Croce Camerina, was excavated from the 19th century.

kadesh.t: Kadesh, a fortified Syrian city on the Orontes that led resistance to Egypt and gave its name to the great chariot battle of 1274 BCE.
kadesh.o: [[e:battle-of-kadesh|Kadesh]], at [[e:tell-nebi-mend|Tell Nebi Mend]] south of [[e:homs|Homs]], controlled the route through the Homs gap between the coast and inner [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]]. In the 15th century BCE its king, backed by the [[s:mitanni-empire|Mitanni Empire]], led the Canaanite and Syrian coalition that [[e:thutmose-iii|Thutmose III]] of the [[s:egyptian-empire-new-kingdom|Egyptian Empire New Kingdom]] defeated at [[s:megiddo|Megiddo]].
kadesh.r: Its kings governed a compact territory of the upper [[e:orontes-river|Orontes]] and were courted by every great power. In the [[e:akhetaten|Amarna]] age King [[e:aitakkama|Aitakkama]] went over to the [[s:hittite-empire|Hittite Empire]] and raided Egyptian [[e:vassal|vassals]], and the [[e:hittite-empire|Hittites]] kept [[e:battle-of-kadesh|Kadesh]] as a vassal kingdom.
kadesh.e: In 1274 BCE [[e:ramesses-ii|Ramesses II]] fought [[e:muwatalli-ii|Muwatalli II]] outside the city in the [[e:battle-of-kadesh|Battle of Kadesh]], after which the city stayed in Hittite hands. Kadesh was destroyed around 1200 BCE in the end of the [[e:late-bronze-age|Late Bronze Age]] and survived only as a village.

kingdom-of-gwynedd.t: The most enduring Welsh kingdom, ruled from Aberffraw on Anglesey, whose princes led Welsh resistance until Edward I's conquest in 1283.
kingdom-of-gwynedd.o: Gwynedd arose in north-west [[e:wales|Wales]] after Roman rule ended. Its dynasty traced descent from [[e:cunedda|Cunedda]], said to have come from [[e:manaw-gododdin|Manaw Gododdin]] in the 5th century. By the 6th century it was a leading power under [[e:maelgwn-gwynedd|Maelgwn Gwynedd]], whom [[e:gildas|Gildas]] denounced as Maglocunus, the dragon of the island, and its core lay in [[e:snowdonia|Snowdonia]] and the grain lands of [[e:anglesey|Anglesey]].
kingdom-of-gwynedd.r: Kings ruled from llysoedd, royal courts, with [[e:aberffraw|Aberffraw]] as the chief seat, governing through cantrefi and kin-based Welsh law. [[e:cadwallon-ap-cadfan|Cadwallon ap Cadfan]] killed [[e:edwin-of-northumbria|Edwin of Northumbria]] in 633. [[e:rhodri-the-great|Rhodri the Great]], who died in 878, joined the [[s:kingdom-of-powys|Kingdom of Powys]] and [[s:kingdom-of-seisyllwg|Seisyllwg]] to Gwynedd. Later princes such as [[e:owain-gwynedd|Owain Gwynedd]] and [[e:llywelyn-the-great|Llywelyn the Great]] built castles and charters, and [[e:llywelyn-ap-gruffudd|Llywelyn ap Gruffudd]] won recognition as [[e:prince-of-wales|Prince of Wales]] by the [[e:treaty-of-montgomery|Treaty of Montgomery]] in 1267.
kingdom-of-gwynedd.e: Edward I invaded in 1277 and again in 1282. [[e:llywelyn-ap-gruffudd|Llywelyn ap Gruffudd]] was killed at [[e:cilmeri|Cilmeri]] in 1282, and his brother [[e:dafydd-ap-gruffydd|Dafydd]] was executed in 1283. The [[e:statute-of-rhuddlan|Statute of Rhuddlan]] of 1284 turned Gwynedd into English shires, guarded by castles such as [[e:caernarfon|Caernarfon]], Conwy and [[e:harlech|Harlech]].

kingdom-of-sedang.t: A self-proclaimed kingdom in the Central Highlands of Vietnam created by the French adventurer Charles-Marie David de Mayrena, which lasted barely two years.
kingdom-of-sedang.o: In 1888 [[e:charles-marie-david-de-mayrena|Charles-Marie David de Mayrena]], a French adventurer and former soldier, travelled to the [[e:kon-tum|Kon Tum]] highlands, nominally to explore for the colonial administration. With the support of local Catholic missionaries he persuaded Sedang, [[e:bahnar-people|Bahnar]] and Rengao chiefs to accept him as king, and he proclaimed himself Marie I.
kingdom-of-sedang.r: Marie I issued a constitution, created orders of chivalry, designed a flag and printed postage stamps, which he sold to collectors. He made [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]] the state religion and set up his court at Kon Gung. Real authority among the highland villages remained with local chiefs, and the kingdom existed mostly on paper.
kingdom-of-sedang.e: French officials refused to recognise the kingdom and blocked [[e:charles-marie-david-de-mayrena|Mayrena]]'s return when he went to [[e:europe|Europe]] seeking backers in 1889. The area was absorbed into French [[s:french-protectorate-of-annam|Annam]], and Mayrena died on the island of [[e:tioman-island|Tioman]] in 1890.

kingdom-of-sitawaka.t: A short-lived Sinhalese kingdom that led the fight against the Portuguese, reaching its height under Rajasinha I.
kingdom-of-sitawaka.o: In 1521 the [[s:kingdom-of-kotte|Kingdom of Kotte]] was divided after the [[e:vijayabahu-kollaya|Vijayabahu Kollaya]], a palace revolt in which three princes killed their father. [[e:mayadunne|Mayadunne]] received Sitawaka, an inland district east of [[e:colombo|Colombo]], and became the bitter rival of his brother [[e:bhuvanaikabahu-vii-of-kotte|Bhuvanaikabahu VII of Kotte]], who relied on Portuguese support.
kingdom-of-sitawaka.r: [[e:mayadunne|Mayadunne]] waged almost continuous war on [[s:kingdom-of-kotte|Kotte]] and its Portuguese allies. His son [[e:rajasinha-i-of-sitawaka|Rajasinha I]] conquered most of the west and central highlands, besieged [[e:colombo|Colombo]] in 1587 to 1588 and converted to [[e:shaivism|Shaivism]], which alienated the Buddhist clergy. The kingdom relied on a large peasant army and control of [[e:cinnamon|cinnamon]] lands.
kingdom-of-sitawaka.e: After [[e:rajasinha-i-of-sitawaka|Rajasinha I]] died in 1593 the kingdom quickly collapsed; the Portuguese occupied Sitawaka by 1594, and much of its territory went to [[s:portuguese-ceylon|Portuguese Ceylon]] while the hill country passed to the [[s:kingdom-of-kandy|Kingdom of Kandy]].

kamboja.t: A warlike people of the Hindu Kush borderlands, counted among the sixteen mahajanapadas and famous across ancient India for their horses.
kamboja.o: The Kambojas are named by the grammarian [[e:panini|Panini]] and in Buddhist lists of the sixteen great states. They lived north-west of [[s:kingdom-of-gandhara|Gandhara]], probably in north-eastern [[s:islamic-emirate-of-afghanistan-2021-present|Afghanistan]] and the hills of north-western [[s:islamic-republic-of-pakistan|Pakistan]]. The Vedic etymologist [[e:yaska|Yaska]] noted that they used an Iranian word for to go, and many scholars see them as an Iranian-speaking people.
kamboja.r: [[e:chanakya|Kautilya's]] [[e:arthashastra|Arthashastra]] describes the Kambojas as a sangha whose members lived by trade and arms, suggesting rule by a warrior aristocracy rather than a king. Indian literature praised Kamboja horses and cavalry, and the epics place Kamboja horsemen on the battlefield. Little else is known of their society or religion.
kamboja.e: Their lands fell under Achaemenid rule and were overrun by Alexander's army around 327 BCE; some scholars identify the [[e:aspasioi|Aspasioi]] and [[e:assakenoi|Assakenoi]] he fought as Kamboja groups. The [[s:maurya-empire|Maurya Empire]] later absorbed them, and [[e:ashoka|Ashoka's]] edicts name the Kambojas among the frontier peoples of his realm.

kingdom-of-tir-eoghain.t: The O'Neill kingdom of mid-Ulster, the most powerful Gaelic lordship of late medieval Ireland, whose last ruler led the Nine Years' War.
kingdom-of-tir-eoghain.o: [[e:tir-eoghain|Tir Eoghain]], '[[e:eogan-mac-neill|Eogan]]'s land', descends from the Cenel nEogain, the northern [[e:ui-neill|Ui Neill]] kindred traced to Eogan, son of [[e:niall-of-the-nine-hostages|Niall of the Nine Hostages]]. From the late 12th century the [[e:o-neill-dynasty|O'Neills]] contested the kingship with the [[e:mac-lochlainn-dynasty|Mac Lochlainn]] line, which they finally overthrew in 1241, ruling from [[e:dungannon|Dungannon]] with inaugurations at [[e:tullyhogue-fort|Tullyhogue]].
kingdom-of-tir-eoghain.r: The [[e:o-neill-dynasty|O'Neills]] dominated [[s:northern-ireland|Ulster]], taking tribute from lesser lords such as the [[e:ocahan-dynasty|O'Cahans]] and [[e:maguire-dynasty|Maguires]]. Their power rested on [[e:cattle|cattle]], a large army including Scottish gallowglasses, and a court of poets and lawyers. [[e:conn-bacach-oneill|Conn Bacach O'Neill]] became Earl of Tyrone in 1542, but conflict with the crown continued under [[e:shane-oneill|Shane O'Neill]].
kingdom-of-tir-eoghain.e: [[e:hugh-oneill-earl-of-tyrone|Hugh O'Neill]] led the [[e:nine-years-war-ireland|Nine Years' War]] against [[e:england|England]], but defeat at [[e:battle-of-kinsale|Kinsale]] in 1601 forced his submission. He left in the Flight of the Earls in 1607, and Tyrone was confiscated for the [[e:plantation-of-ulster|Plantation of Ulster]] in the [[s:kingdom-of-ireland|Kingdom of Ireland]].

kingdom-of-karana.t: A northern Mesopotamian kingdom of the Mari age, centred on Tell al-Rimah, whose queen Iltani left a remarkable archive of letters.
kingdom-of-karana.o: Karana lay south of [[e:sinjar-mountains|Jebel Sinjar]] in northern [[e:iraq|Iraq]]. The site of [[e:tell-al-rimah|Tell al-Rimah]], excavated by [[e:david-oates|David Oates]] in the 1960s, is usually identified as Karana or its twin city Qattara. After the death of [[e:shamshi-adad-i|Shamshi-Adad]] around 1776 BCE, Karana became an independent kingdom under Asqur-Addu, son of its earlier king Samu-Addu, and later under Aqba-hammu.
kingdom-of-karana.r: Karana's kings competed with [[s:kingdom-of-andarig|Andarig]] and [[s:kingdom-of-kurda|Kurda]] and swore alliances with [[e:zimri-lim|Zimri-Lim]] of [[s:mari|Mari]] and other powers. The temple and palace at [[e:tell-al-rimah|Tell al-Rimah]] contained tablets of Queen [[e:iltani|Iltani]], wife of King Aqba-hammu, who managed textile production, grain and personnel and corresponded with her family, a rare view of a royal woman's administration. The kingdom rested on dry-farmed barley and sheep.
kingdom-of-karana.e: Aqba-hammu became a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of [[e:hammurabi|Hammurabi of Babylon]] after the fall of [[s:mari|Mari]] in 1761 BCE, and Karana lost its independence. [[e:tell-al-rimah|Tell al-Rimah]] continued to be occupied in later periods.

kurundwad-junior.t: The junior of two Patwardhan Brahmin states at Kurundwad, formed by the division of 1855.
kurundwad-junior.o: The [[e:patwardhan|Patwardhan]] holding of Kurundwad, created in the family partition of 1811, was divided in 1855 between two branches, and the Junior branch received its own scattered villages.
kurundwad-junior.r: Kurundwad Junior was a small state of the [[e:southern-maratha-country|Southern Maratha Country]], later the [[e:deccan-states-agency|Deccan States Agency]], sharing the town of Kurundwad with [[s:kurundwad-senior|Kurundwad Senior]]. Little else of its history is recorded.
kurundwad-junior.e: After accession to [[e:india|India]] Kurundwad Junior was merged into [[e:bombay-state|Bombay State]] in 1948 and has been part of [[e:maharashtra|Maharashtra]] since 1960, in [[s:kolhapur-state|Kolhapur]] district.

kingdom-of-jolof.t: The Wolof heartland kingdom left after the break-up of the Jolof Empire, whose last king Alboury Ndiaye resisted French conquest.
kingdom-of-jolof.o: Until the mid-16th century the [[e:buurba-jolof|Buurba Jolof]] ruled an empire over all the [[e:wolof|Wolof]] states. In 1549 [[e:amari-ngone-sobel-fall|Amari Ngoone Sobel Fall]] of [[s:cayor|Cayor]] defeated and killed the Buurba at the battle of [[e:battle-of-danki|Danki]], and the coastal provinces broke away. What remained was an inland kingdom centred on Yang-Yang, cut off from direct trade with European ships.
kingdom-of-jolof.r: The Buurba was chosen by [[e:prince-elector|electors]] from royal lineages and ruled over [[e:wolof|Wolof]] farmers and [[e:fula|Fulani]] herders of the dry interior. Without access to the coast, [[e:jolof-empire|Jolof]] was poorer than [[s:cayor|Cayor]] or [[s:waalo|Waalo]] and was often drawn into their wars. [[e:islam|Islam]] spread steadily during the 18th and 19th centuries.
kingdom-of-jolof.e: [[e:alboury-ndiaye|Alboury Ndiaye]], who became Buurba in 1875, built alliances against the French but was forced out in 1890 and fled east, dying in exile around 1901. [[e:jolof-empire|Jolof]] was absorbed into [[s:french-senegal|French Senegal]], and its name is still used for the region of [[e:linguere|Linguere]].

kingdom-of-scotland.t: The medieval and early modern kingdom of the Scots, forged from Pictland and Dal Riata, which kept its independence until the Union with England in 1707.
kingdom-of-scotland.o: Tradition dates the kingdom to [[e:kenneth-macalpin|Kenneth MacAlpin]], who ruled the [[e:picts|Picts]] from about 843. The Pictish and Gaelic realms merged into the kingdom of Alba by around 900, centred on [[e:scone-scotland|Scone]] and [[e:dunkeld|Dunkeld]]. It expanded over [[e:lothian|Lothian]], Strathclyde, and in 1266 the [[e:hebrides|Western Isles]] from [[e:norway|Norway]].
kingdom-of-scotland.r: [[e:scotland|Scotland]] developed royal burghs, feudal lordship and a church of its own under [[e:david|David]] I. The Wars of Independence, with [[e:william-wallace|William Wallace]] and [[e:robert-the-bruce|Robert the Bruce's]] victory at [[e:battle-of-bannockburn|Bannockburn]] in 1314, secured independence. The [[e:house-of-stuart|Stewart]] monarchy followed in 1371, [[e:edinburgh|Edinburgh]] became the capital, and the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] of 1560 created a Protestant church, Presbyterian in its final settlement of 1690.
kingdom-of-scotland.e: In 1603 [[e:james-vi-and-i|James VI]] inherited [[e:england|England]], joining the crowns. The [[e:acts-of-union-1707|Acts of Union]] of 1707 merged the Scottish and English parliaments into the [[s:kingdom-of-great-britain|Kingdom of Great Britain]], though [[e:scotland|Scotland]] kept its own law, church and education.

kingdom-of-kition.t: Phoenician kingdom on Cyprus, founded by Tyre, that conquered its Greek neighbours Idalion and Tamassos and was the birthplace of Zeno the Stoic.
kingdom-of-kition.o: Kition, at modern [[e:larnaca|Larnaca]], was a [[e:late-bronze-age|Late Bronze Age]] [[e:copper|copper]]-working town. In the 9th century BCE [[e:phoenicians|Phoenicians]] from [[s:tyre|Tyre]] settled there and built a great temple of [[e:astarte|Astarte]] on the ruins of an earlier sanctuary. Kition probably began as a Tyrian dependency, and in 707 BCE [[e:sargon-ii|Sargon II]] of [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyria]] set up a stele there recording Cypriot submission.
kingdom-of-kition.r: From the early 5th century BCE an independent Phoenician dynasty ruled Kition, beginning with Baalmelek I, and it was loyal to the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]]. Kition conquered [[s:kingdom-of-idalion|Idalion]] c. 450 BCE, its kings then styling themselves rulers of both, and [[e:pumiyaton|Pumiyaton]] later bought [[s:kingdom-of-tamassos|Tamassos]]. Its harbour served Persian fleets, and its kings issued coins showing [[e:melqart|Heracles-Melqart]].
kingdom-of-kition.e: [[e:ptolemy-i-soter|Ptolemy I]] executed [[e:pumiyaton|Pumiyaton]] and annexed the kingdom in 312 BCE. Kition continued as a Ptolemaic and Roman city; its most famous son, [[e:zeno-of-citium|Zeno]], founded Stoic philosophy at [[s:athens|Athens]].
kingdom-of-kition.re: Phoenician religion; cults of Astarte and Melqart

kingdom-of-onitsha.t: An Igbo kingdom on the east bank of the Niger, ruled by an Obi in a court style borrowed from Benin and later a gateway for missions and British trade.
kingdom-of-onitsha.o: According to tradition, Onitsha was founded in the 17th century by migrants from the west of the [[e:niger-river|Niger]], led by Eze Chima, who left the area of the [[s:benin-empire|Benin Empire]] after a dispute and crossed the river. They settled among existing [[e:igbo-people|Igbo]] communities on the east bank and created a kingdom unusual in a region where most Igbo lived in small, chiefless village groups.
kingdom-of-onitsha.r: The Obi ruled with the Ndichie, a council of titled chiefs ranked in grades, and the ozo title system gave wealthy men a route into public life. Royal ceremony, such as the annual [[e:ofala-festival|Ofala festival]], echoed the court of [[e:benin-empire|Benin]]. The town lived from river trade in yams, [[e:palm-oil|palm oil]] and slaves. Anglican missionaries under [[e:samuel-ajayi-crowther|Samuel Ajayi Crowther]] arrived in 1857.
kingdom-of-onitsha.e: From the 1870s British traders and the [[s:royal-niger-company-territories|Royal Niger Company]] made Onitsha a commercial base, and a British gunboat shelled the town in 1879. It was absorbed into the [[s:protectorate-of-southern-nigeria|Protectorate of Southern Nigeria]] around 1900. The Obi survives as a traditional ruler and Onitsha became one of [[e:nigeria|Nigeria's]] largest market towns.

kingdom-of-osraige.t: Irish kingdom between Leinster and Munster, centred on Kilkenny, whose Mac Giolla Phádraig rulers survived as lords until the Tudor surrender of 1541.
kingdom-of-osraige.o: Osraige emerged in early medieval Ireland as the kingdom of a people living in the valleys of the [[e:river-nore|Nore]] and its tributaries, in modern [[e:county-kilkenny|County Kilkenny]] and south [[s:kingdom-of-loigis|Laois]]. Its kings traced descent from ancestors distinct from both the [[s:kingdom-of-leinster|Laigin]] and the [[e:eoganachta|Eóganachta]], and the kingdom stood between the Kingdom of Leinster and the [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Kingdom of Munster]], usually as a tributary of Munster.
kingdom-of-osraige.r: The monasteries of [[e:seir-kieran|Saighir]], linked with St [[e:ciaran-of-saighir|Ciarán]], and later [[e:aghaboe|Aghaboe]] and [[e:kilkenny|Kilkenny]], where St [[e:canice|Canice]] is honoured, were centres of learning and gave their names to the diocese of Ossory. [[e:cerball-mac-dunlainge|Cerball mac Dúnlainge]], who died in 888, made Osraige a major power by fighting and allying with [[e:vikings|Viking]] leaders. His descendants, the [[e:mac-giolla-phadraig|Mac Giolla Phádraig]], briefly held the kingship of [[s:kingdom-of-leinster|Leinster]] under [[e:donnchad-mac-gilla-patraic|Donnchad mac Gilla Pátraic]] in the 1030s.
kingdom-of-osraige.e: After the [[e:anglo-norman-invasion-of-ireland|Anglo-Norman invasion]] of 1169, [[e:kilkenny|Kilkenny]] became the seat of English lords, and the [[e:mac-giolla-phadraig|Mac Giolla Phádraig]] held only [[e:upper-ossory|Upper Ossory]]. In 1541 their chief, Brian, surrendered his lands to [[e:henry-viii-of-england|Henry VIII]] and received them back as Baron of Upper Ossory, ending the kingdom.

kingdom-of-france.t: The monarchy that grew from the Capetians' small domain around Paris into Europe's most populous and centralised state, ending with the Revolution.
kingdom-of-france.o: In 987 the [[e:magnates|magnates]] elected [[e:hugh-capet|Hugh Capet]], duke of the [[s:franks|Franks]], as king after the last Carolingian died. The early [[e:capetian-dynasty|Capetians]] directly controlled only the [[e:ile-de-france|Île-de-France]] and [[e:orleans|Orléans]], while dukes and counts of [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Normandy]], [[s:duchy-of-aquitaine|Aquitaine]], [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Burgundy]] and [[s:county-of-flanders|Flanders]] were in practice independent.
kingdom-of-france.r: Kings slowly extended the royal domain by war, marriage and law: [[e:philip-ii-of-france|Philip II]] took [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Normandy]] in 1204, [[e:louis-ix-of-france|Louis IX]] became a model of Christian kingship, and the [[e:house-of-valois|Valois]] survived the [[e:hundred-years-war|Hundred Years' War]]. After the Wars of Religion, [[e:henry-iv-of-france|Henry IV]] issued the [[e:edict-of-nantes|Edict of Nantes]] in 1598. [[e:louis-xiv|Louis XIV]] built absolute rule at [[e:versailles|Versailles]], and [[e:french-language|French language]] and culture dominated [[e:europe|Europe]].
kingdom-of-france.e: Debt and political crisis led [[e:louis-xvi|Louis XVI]] to call the [[e:estates-general-france|Estates-General]] in 1789, beginning the Revolution. The monarchy became constitutional in 1791 and was abolished in September 1792, replaced by the [[s:french-first-republic|French First Republic]]; Louis XVI was executed in 1793.

kingdom-of-igara.t: A small kingdom of western Uganda, merged into the Kingdom of Ankole under British rule in 1901.
kingdom-of-igara.o: Igara lay in the hills west of today's [[e:bushenyi-district|Bushenyi]], between [[s:kingdom-of-buhweju|Buhweju]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-ankole|Kingdom of Ankole]]. It emerged as a separate state in the 18th century, with a royal line remembered in local tradition. Little is reliably known of its early history.
kingdom-of-igara.r: Igara was a farming and [[e:cattle|cattle]]-keeping kingdom, governed by a king with clan heads and drums of office in the manner of its neighbours. It was often drawn into the wars between [[s:kingdom-of-ankole|Ankole]] and [[s:kingdom-of-bunyoro|Bunyoro]].
kingdom-of-igara.e: The [[e:ankole-agreement|Ankole Agreement]] of 1901 merged Igara into the [[s:kingdom-of-ankole|Kingdom of Ankole]] as one of its counties. It is now part of western Uganda's [[e:bushenyi-district|Bushenyi]] area.

kaska.t: The Kaska, tribal peoples of the Pontic mountains who for three centuries raided the Hittite heartland and once burned Hattusa.
kaska.o: The Kaska lived in the wooded mountains between the Hittite heartland and the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]]. They appear in Hittite texts from the 15th century BCE, when they overran the holy city of [[e:nerik|Nerik]] and pushed into central [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]].
kaska.r: They were not a state but groups of villages under local chiefs, living from herding and farming and raiding Hittite lands. Hittite kings made short-lived treaties with individual groups. [[e:mursili-ii|Mursili II]] wrote that one chief, [[e:pihhuniya|Pihhuniya]], ruled not in the Kaska way but like a king.
kaska.e: Kaska raiders sacked [[e:hattusa|Hattusa]] in the 14th century BCE, and [[e:hattusili-iii|Hattusili III]] only recovered [[e:nerik|Nerik]] in the 13th. After the Hittite collapse they moved south-east, where [[e:tiglath-pileser-i|Tiglath-Pileser I]] of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]] fought them c. 1100 BCE; then they vanish.

kingdom-of-hatra.t: A fortified caravan city in the desert of northern Iraq, ruled by 'kings of the Arabs', that twice beat off Roman emperors before falling to the Sasanians.
kingdom-of-hatra.o: Hatra grew in the [[e:upper-mesopotamia|Jazira]] steppe west of the [[e:tigris|Tigris]] as a religious and caravan centre in the 1st century BCE under Parthian protection. Its rulers at first bore the title 'lord' (mry'), and from the mid-2nd century CE, under [[e:sanatruq-i|Sanatruq I]], they styled themselves 'king of the [[e:arabs|Arabs]]'.
kingdom-of-hatra.r: At its centre stood a vast temple precinct to the sun god [[e:utu|Shamash]], called Maran ('our lord'), with shrines to [[e:allat|Allat]], [[e:baalshamin|Baalshamin]] and other deities. Hundreds of inscriptions in Hatran [[e:aramaic|Aramaic]] and statues of kings, nobles and priests reveal a society blending Arab, Aramaean, Mesopotamian and Parthian traditions. Its round double walls withstood sieges by [[e:trajan|Trajan]] in 117 CE and [[e:septimius-severus|Septimius Severus]] in 198 to 199.
kingdom-of-hatra.e: Hatra allied with [[e:rome|Rome]] against the new [[s:sasanian-empire|Sasanian Empire]] but was captured by [[e:shapur-i|Shapur I]] around 240 to 241 and abandoned. Its ruins, a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]], were damaged by Islamic State fighters in 2015.

kingdom-of-agona.t: Akan kingdom of the central Gold Coast, known in 17th century European reports for being ruled by queens.
kingdom-of-agona.o: Agona was a small [[e:akan|Akan]] state on the coast and hinterland between the [[e:fante|Fante]] lands and [[e:accra|Accra]]. It existed by the 16th century, with its political centre inland at Nyakrom and coastal towns that traded with European ships.
kingdom-of-agona.r: European visitors in the 17th century recorded female rulers of Agona, reflecting the importance of royal women in [[e:akan|Akan]] politics. The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] built Fort Patience at Apam on its coast in the 1690s. Agona traded gold, slaves and food with European companies, but was often subject to stronger neighbours such as [[s:akwamu|Akwamu]].
kingdom-of-agona.e: In the 18th century Agona was drawn into the [[e:fante|Fante]] sphere and the wars against the [[s:ashanti-empire|Ashanti Empire]]. It came under British rule with the [[s:gold-coast-colony|Gold Coast Colony]] in 1874, and survives as a traditional area in Ghana's Central Region.

kingdom-of-dublin.t: The Norse kingdom founded around Dublin's harbour, a hub of the Viking trade network that linked Ireland to Scandinavia, Britain and the slave markets.
kingdom-of-dublin.o: [[e:vikings|Vikings]] built a fortified base, the longphort, at [[e:dublin|Dublin]] in 841. From 853 the annals record [[e:amlaib-conung|Amlaib]] and later [[e:imar|Imar]], ancestors of a dynasty of kings who ruled both Dublin and, at times, the [[s:kingdom-of-york|Kingdom of York]]. Expelled by the Irish in 902, they returned in 917.
kingdom-of-dublin.r: [[e:dublin|Dublin]] was a trading town of streets, houses and workshops, revealed by excavations at Wood Quay, dealing in slaves, [[e:silver|silver]], [[e:fur-trade|furs]] and craft goods. It minted coins from about 997. Its rulers converted to [[e:christianity|Christianity]] in the 10th century and [[e:sitric-silkbeard|Sitric Silkbeard]] founded [[e:christ-church-cathedral-dublin|Christ Church Cathedral]] around 1030. Irish kings often controlled it as a valuable prize.
kingdom-of-dublin.e: After defeat at [[e:battle-of-clontarf|Clontarf]] in 1014, [[e:dublin|Dublin]] was dominated by Irish overkings. In 1170 [[e:richard-de-clare-2nd-earl-of-pembroke|Strongbow]] and [[e:diarmait-mac-murchada|Diarmait Mac Murchada]] captured it, and in 1171 [[e:henry-ii-of-england|Henry II]] made it the capital of the [[s:lordship-of-ireland|Lordship of Ireland]].
kingdom-of-dublin.re: Norse paganism; Christianity from the 10th century

kingdom-of-upper-burgundy.t: The Alpine kingdom of the Welf dynasty, founded at Saint-Maurice in 888, which later absorbed Provence to form the Kingdom of Arles.
kingdom-of-upper-burgundy.o: After the deposition of Emperor [[e:charles-the-fat|Charles the Fat]] in 888, the [[e:house-of-welf|Welf]] noble Rudolf, margrave of Transjurane [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Burgundy]], had himself crowned king at the abbey of [[e:abbey-of-saint-maurice-dagaune|Saint-Maurice d'Agaune]]. His kingdom covered western [[s:swiss-confederation|Switzerland]], the [[e:jura-mountains|Jura]] and parts of [[s:free-county-of-burgundy|Franche-Comté]], and he held it against the East Frankish king [[e:arnulf-of-carinthia|Arnulf]].
kingdom-of-upper-burgundy.r: The kings controlled the [[e:great-st-bernard-pass|Great St Bernard]] pass and relied on rich abbeys such as [[e:abbey-of-saint-maurice-dagaune|Saint-Maurice]] and on alliances with local [[e:bishop|bishops]] at [[e:lausanne|Lausanne]], [[s:republic-of-geneva|Geneva]] and [[e:sion-switzerland|Sion]]. [[e:rudolf-ii-of-burgundy|Rudolf II]] was defeated by Swabia at [[e:winterthur|Winterthur]] in 919, then reached for the Italian crown in the 920s before trading those claims for [[s:county-of-provence|Provence]].
kingdom-of-upper-burgundy.e: Around 933 [[e:rudolf-ii-of-burgundy|Rudolf II]] obtained [[e:lower-burgundy|Lower Burgundy]] from [[e:hugh-of-arles|Hugh of Arles]], merging the two realms into the [[s:kingdom-of-arles|Kingdom of Arles]]. His son [[e:conrad-i-of-burgundy|Conrad the Peaceful]] ruled the united kingdom under strong Ottonian influence, and in 1032 it passed to the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]].

kingdom-of-leon.t: The Christian kingdom that succeeded Asturias in 910, claimed Visigothic heritage and held the first European parliament with townsmen in 1188.
kingdom-of-leon.o: In 910 the sons of [[e:alfonso-iii-of-asturias|Alfonso III of Asturias]] divided his realm, García I taking León. In 914 [[e:ordono-ii-of-leon|Ordoño II]] made the city of León the royal seat, and the kingdom took its name from it, incorporating [[e:asturia|Asturias]] and [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Galicia]] and the newly resettled lands of the [[e:douro|Douro]] plain.
kingdom-of-leon.r: The Leonese kings claimed to restore the Visigothic monarchy, some styling themselves emperor. [[e:ramiro-ii-of-leon|Ramiro II]] beat [[e:abd-al-rahman-iii|Abd al-Rahman III]] at [[e:battle-of-simancas|Simancas]] in 939, though [[e:almanzor|Almanzor]] later sacked León and [[s:spanish-jamaica|Santiago]]. [[e:alfonso-v-of-leon|Alfonso V]]'s fuero of 1017 regulated the city, and [[e:alfonso-vi-of-castile|Alfonso VI]] took [[e:toledo|Toledo]] in 1085. [[e:alfonso-ix-of-leon|Alfonso IX]] summoned the [[e:cortes-of-leon-of-1188|Cortes of León]] in 1188, with representatives of towns alongside nobles and clergy.
kingdom-of-leon.e: León was united with [[s:kingdom-of-castile|Castile]] under Ferdinand I and his successors, separated again from 1157, and definitively joined with [[e:kingdom-of-castile|Castile]] in 1230 under Ferdinand III, forming the [[s:crown-of-castile|Crown of Castile]].

kidarite-kingdom.t: The first of the Hunnic dynasties to rule Bactria and Gandhara, named after its founder Kidara and long locked in war with Sasanian Persia.
kidarite-kingdom.o: The Kidarites emerged in [[s:greco-bactrian-kingdom|Bactria]] in the 4th century, probably from among the [[s:chionites|Chionites]] who invaded the lands of the [[s:kushano-sasanian-kingdom|Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom]]. Their eponymous leader [[e:kidara|Kidara]] issued coins in the Kushan style and claimed the old Kushan title, ruling from [[e:balkh|Balkh]] and later spreading into [[s:kingdom-of-gandhara|Gandhara]].
kidarite-kingdom.r: They governed a mixed population of Bactrians and Indians, issuing gold coins modelled on Kushan and Sasanian types, some with Brahmi legends naming [[e:kidara|Kidara]]. They fought repeated wars with Sasanian kings such as [[e:yazdegerd-ii|Yazdegerd II]] and [[e:peroz-i|Peroz I]], and probably clashed with the [[s:gupta-empire|Gupta Empire]] in northern [[e:india|India]].
kidarite-kingdom.e: Around 467 the [[e:sasanian-empire|Sasanians]] under [[e:peroz-i|Peroz I]] drove them from [[s:greco-bactrian-kingdom|Bactria]], and the [[s:hephthalite-empire|Hephthalite Empire]] soon took over their northern lands. Remnant Kidarite principalities held out in [[s:kingdom-of-gandhara|Gandhara]] and [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]] until the [[s:alchon-huns|Alchon Huns]] absorbed them in the late 5th century.

kingdom-of-ugarit.t: Ugarit, a rich Late Bronze Age port-kingdom on the Syrian coast whose scribes invented an alphabetic cuneiform and recorded the myths of Baal.
kingdom-of-ugarit.o: Ugarit, at [[e:ras|Ras]] Shamra north of [[e:latakia|Latakia]], was settled from the [[e:neolithic|Neolithic]]. In the early 2nd millennium BCE it became the capital of a coastal kingdom with an outlet at [[e:minet-el-beida|Minet el-Beida]], and it appears in the [[s:mari|Mari]] letters when [[e:zimri-lim|Zimri-Lim]] travelled there. A farmer's discovery of a tomb in 1928 led to excavations by [[e:claude-schaeffer|Claude Schaeffer]].
kingdom-of-ugarit.r: Its kings ruled a cosmopolitan trading state linking [[e:egypt|Egypt]], [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]], the [[e:aegean|Aegean]] and [[e:mesopotamia|Mesopotamia]]. Scribes wrote in Akkadian, Hurrian, Hittite, Egyptian and the local Ugaritic, using a 30-sign [[e:cuneiform|cuneiform]] alphabet. Temple libraries preserved the [[e:baal|Baal]] cycle and the epics of [[e:epic-of-kirta|Kirta]] and [[e:tale-of-aqhat|Aqhat]], close relatives of later [[e:hebrew|Hebrew]] poetry.
kingdom-of-ugarit.e: Ugarit was a [[e:vassal|vassal]] first of the [[s:egyptian-empire-new-kingdom|Egyptian Empire New Kingdom]] and then, from [[e:niqmaddu-ii|Niqmaddu II]], of the [[s:hittite-empire|Hittite Empire]]. Around 1185 BCE seaborne raiders destroyed it; letters of its last king Ammurapi describe enemy ships. The city was never rebuilt.

kingdom-of-the-two-sicilies.t: The largest pre-unification Italian state, the Bourbon kingdom of Naples and Sicily, overthrown by Garibaldi's Thousand in 1860.
kingdom-of-the-two-sicilies.o: After the [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] restored him, [[e:ferdinand-i-of-the-two-sicilies|Ferdinand IV of Naples]] and III of [[e:sicily|Sicily]] merged the [[s:kingdom-of-naples|Kingdom of Naples]] and the [[s:sicilian-kingdom-of-1848|Kingdom of Sicily]] in December 1816, becoming Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies, with [[e:naples|Naples]] as capital.
kingdom-of-the-two-sicilies.r: The kingdom was an absolute monarchy that put down revolts in 1820 and 1848; Sicilians resented losing their autonomy. [[e:ferdinand-ii-of-the-two-sicilies|Ferdinand II]] opened [[e:italy|Italy's]] first railway, from [[e:naples|Naples]] to [[e:portici|Portici]], in 1839 and built a strong navy, but his harsh repression earned him the nickname King Bomba. The south remained largely rural, with powerful landowners and widespread poverty.
kingdom-of-the-two-sicilies.e: In 1860 [[e:giuseppe-garibaldi|Giuseppe Garibaldi's]] [[e:expedition-of-the-thousand|Expedition of the Thousand]] conquered [[e:sicily|Sicily]] and [[e:naples|Naples]]. [[e:francis-ii|Francis II]] held out at [[e:gaeta|Gaeta]] until February 1861, and the kingdom was annexed to the new [[s:kingdom-of-italy|Kingdom of Italy]].
ru: Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies
Ferdinand II of the Two Sicilies
Francis II of the Two Sicilies

kingdom-of-croatia-habsburg.t: Croatian kingdom under the Habsburgs, reduced by Ottoman conquest to the 'remnants of the remnants' and later a centre of the Croatian national revival.
kingdom-of-croatia-habsburg.o: On 1 January 1527 the Croatian nobles assembled at [[e:1527-election-in-cetin|Cetin]] elected [[e:ferdinand-i-holy-roman-emperor|Ferdinand of Habsburg]] as king, in return for his help against the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]]. By the late 16th century Ottoman conquests had reduced [[e:croatia|Croatia]] to a narrow band around [[e:zagreb|Zagreb]], [[e:karlovac|Karlovac]] and the coast, the reliquiae reliquiarum of the old kingdom.
kingdom-of-croatia-habsburg.r: [[e:croatia|Croatia]] was governed by a ban and its own [[e:croatian-parliament|Sabor]], within the [[e:lands-of-the-crown-of-saint-stephen|Lands of the Hungarian Crown]], while much of its territory was detached into the [[s:military-frontier|Military Frontier]] under [[e:vienna|Vienna]]. The victory at [[e:sisak|Sisak]] in 1593 halted the Ottoman advance. Nobility, Catholic Church and [[e:latin|Latin]] dominated public life until the Illyrian movement of [[e:ljudevit-gaj|Ljudevit Gaj]] revived Croatian in the 1830s.
kingdom-of-croatia-habsburg.e: In 1848 Ban [[e:josip-jelacic|Josip Jelačić]] led Croatian forces against the Hungarian revolution. The [[e:croatian-hungarian-settlement|Croatian-Hungarian Settlement]] of 1868 joined the kingdom with [[e:slavonia|Slavonia]] as the [[s:kingdom-of-croatia-slavonia|Kingdom of Croatia-Slavonia]], an autonomous part of the Hungarian half of [[e:austro-hungarian-empire|Austria-Hungary]].

katagum-emirate.t: An emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate on the western frontier of Bornu, founded by Fulani fighters who once sacked the Bornu capital.
katagum-emirate.o: Katagum was founded by [[e:ibrahim-zaki|Ibrahim Zaki]], a [[e:fula|Fulani]] scholar and commander who took up the [[e:jihad|jihad]] in the western borderlands of the [[s:kanem-bornu-empire|Kanem-Bornu Empire]]. In 1808 he joined other Fulani leaders in capturing the [[e:bornu|Bornu]] capital, Birni [[e:ngazargamu|Ngazargamu]], and in about 1807-1809 he founded the town of Katagum as the seat of his [[e:emirate|emirate]].
katagum-emirate.r: Katagum remained a frontier state facing [[e:bornu|Bornu]], which recovered under al-Kanemi and pushed back the [[e:fula|Fulani]]. The emir ruled through titled officials and district heads on the [[e:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto]] model, and the [[e:emirate|emirate]]'s economy rested on farming, [[e:cattle|cattle]] and trade in grain and [[e:natron|natron]]. It had rivalries with neighbouring [[e:hadejia|Hadejia]].
katagum-emirate.e: British forces occupied Katagum in 1903 and it became part of the [[s:protectorate-of-northern-nigeria|Protectorate of Northern Nigeria]]. The [[e:emirate|emirate]]'s seat later moved to [[e:azare|Azare]], where the [[e:emir|Emir]] of Katagum still reigns in [[e:bauchi-state|Bauchi State]].

kingdom-of-lar.t: A long-lived local kingdom in southern Iran on the trade road to Hormuz, whose silver 'larin' coins circulated across the Indian Ocean.
kingdom-of-lar.o: The rulers of Lar, often called the Miladi dynasty, claimed descent from Gurgin son of Milad, a hero of the [[e:shahnameh|Shahnameh]]. They are attested from the 12th century in [[e:laristan|Laristan]], the arid region of southern [[e:fars|Fars]] between [[e:shiraz|Shiraz]] and the Gulf, with their capital at Lar.
kingdom-of-lar.r: Lar prospered from its position on the caravan route between [[e:shiraz|Shiraz]] and the port of [[s:kingdom-of-ormus|Hormuz]], through which Indian, Arabian and Persian goods passed. The kingdom was famous for the larin, a strip of [[e:silver|silver]] wire bent into a hook and stamped, which became a common currency in the Gulf, [[e:india|India]] and the [[s:republic-of-maldives|Maldives]] in the 16th century. Its rulers accepted the overlordship of the [[s:ilkhanate|Ilkhanate]], the [[s:timurid-empire|Timurid Empire]] and the [[s:safavid-empire|Safavid Empire]] while keeping local autonomy. The population remained largely [[e:sunni-islam|Sunni]].
kingdom-of-lar.e: In 1601 to 1602 the Safavid general [[e:alivardi-khan|Allahverdi Khan]] conquered Lar for [[e:abbas-i-of-persia|Shah Abbas I]] and deposed its last ruler, [[e:ibrahim-khan-of-lar|Ibrahim Khan]], and [[e:laristan|Laristan]] became a Safavid province.

kingdom-of-akure.t: Yoruba city-kingdom of the Ekiti uplands, ruled by the Deji of Akure and long a borderland between Yoruba and Benin influence.
kingdom-of-akure.o: Akure traditions trace the dynasty to Omoremilekun Asodeboyede, a descendant of [[e:oduduwa|Oduduwa]] who is said to have left [[s:kingdom-of-ife|Ile-Ife]] and settled with his followers in the forest east of [[e:ife|Ife]]. The kingdom is traditionally dated to the 12th century, though its early history is known mainly from oral tradition.
kingdom-of-akure.r: The Deji ruled with councils of senior chiefs and town quarters, over farmers of yams, cocoyams and later cocoa. Lying close to the [[s:benin-empire|Benin Empire]], Akure was for long periods subject to [[e:benin-empire|Benin]], whose influence shows in its titles and court customs. In the 19th century it joined the [[s:ekiti-parapo|Ekiti Parapo]] alliance against [[s:ibadan|Ibadan]].
kingdom-of-akure.e: Akure came under British control in the 1890s and was incorporated into the [[s:protectorate-of-southern-nigeria|Protectorate of Southern Nigeria]]. The city is now the capital of [[e:ondo-state|Ondo State]], and the Deji of Akure remains its traditional ruler.

kingdom-of-the-picts.t: Early medieval kingdom of northern and eastern Scotland, known for its carved symbol stones, which merged with the Gaels to form the kingdom of Alba.
kingdom-of-the-picts.o: The [[e:picts|Picts]] are first named in a Roman panegyric of 297 as enemies of [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] alongside the Irish. The name, [[e:latin|Latin]] for 'painted people', was applied to the peoples north of the [[e:firth-of-forth|Forth]], descendants of the [[s:caledonii|Caledonii]], [[s:maeatae|Maeatae]] and other [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] groups. Over the following centuries their many districts were drawn together under powerful over-kings.
kingdom-of-the-picts.r: The [[e:picts|Picts]] left few written records but carved distinctive symbol stones with combs, mirrors, crescents and animals, later combined with Christian crosses. Kings such as [[e:bridei-son-of-maelchon|Bridei son of Maelchon]], visited by [[e:columba|Columba]] in the 560s, ruled through regional lords. [[e:bridei-son-of-beli|Bridei son of Beli]] defeated the Northumbrians at [[e:battle-of-dun-nechtain|Dun Nechtain]] in 685, and [[e:oengus-i-of-the-picts|Óengus son of Fergus]] dominated northern [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in the 8th century. [[e:christianity|Christianity]] spread from [[e:iona|Iona]] and [[s:kingdom-of-northumbria|Northumbria]].
kingdom-of-the-picts.e: [[e:vikings|Viking]] attacks in the 9th century devastated the Pictish elite, notably in a great defeat in 839. [[e:kenneth-macalpin|Cináed mac Ailpín]], a king of Gaelic descent, took power around 843, and by about 900 Pictland had become the Gaelic-speaking kingdom of Alba, the core of medieval [[e:scotland|Scotland]].
kingdom-of-the-picts.re: Celtic polytheism; Christianity from the 6th century

kingdom-of-maroboduus.t: The first large Germanic kingdom known by name, built in Bohemia by Maroboduus, who drilled an army on Roman lines and alarmed Augustus.
kingdom-of-maroboduus.o: [[e:maroboduus|Maroboduus]], a Marcomannic noble who had spent his youth in [[e:rome|Rome]], led his people from the Main region into [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]] around 9 BCE to escape Roman offensives. There he subjected neighbouring peoples, including the [[s:quadi|Quadi]], [[e:lugii|Lugii]], [[e:semnones|Semnones]] and Langobardi, building a realm that stretched from the [[e:danube|Danube]] to the [[e:elbe|Elbe]] and beyond.
kingdom-of-maroboduus.r: [[e:velleius-paterculus|Velleius Paterculus]] describes a centralised monarchy with a standing army of about 70,000 foot and 4,000 horse trained in Roman fashion; its royal seat may be the Marobudum named by Ptolemy. Roman merchants lived there. Augustus planned to crush him in 6 CE with twelve legions, but the Pannonian revolt forced a treaty recognising [[e:maroboduus|Maroboduus]] as a friend of [[e:rome|Rome]].
kingdom-of-maroboduus.e: [[e:maroboduus|Maroboduus]] stayed neutral when [[e:arminius|Arminius]] destroyed [[e:publius-quinctilius-varus|Varus]]' legions in 9, and in 17 Arminius defeated him; the [[e:semnones|Semnones]] and Langobardi deserted. In 19 the Gothic exile [[e:catualda|Catualda]] seized his capital, and Maroboduus fled to Roman territory, dying in [[s:lordship-of-ravenna|Ravenna]] in 37. [[e:rome|Rome]] then created the client [[s:kingdom-of-vannius|Kingdom of Vannius]].

kingdom-of-kakheti-hereti.t: An eastern Georgian kingdom that resisted absorption into the united Georgian monarchy for nearly a century before David the Builder conquered it.
kingdom-of-kakheti-hereti.o: Around 1010 [[e:kvirike-iii-of-kakheti|Kvirike III]] became chorepiscopus of the [[s:principality-of-kakheti|Principality of Kakheti]], which had already absorbed the [[s:principality-of-hereti|Principality of Hereti]], and later took the title king of the Kakhs and Rans. His realm, centred on [[e:telavi|Telavi]], was overrun by [[e:bagrat-iii-of-georgia|Bagrat III]], who was uniting the rest of [[s:georgia|Georgia]], but regained its independence after Bagrat's death in 1014.
kingdom-of-kakheti-hereti.r: [[e:kvirike-iii-of-kakheti|Kvirike III]], called the Great, was a strong ruler and builder who allied with neighbours against the Georgian kings. The kingdom lived from the vineyards and pastures of the Alazani valley and controlled routes towards [[s:shirvanshah-state|Shirvan]]. [[e:aghsartan-i-of-kakheti|Aghsartan I]] submitted to the Seljuk sultan [[e:alp-arslan|Alp Arslan]] in 1068 and outwardly converted to [[e:islam|Islam]] to keep his throne.
kingdom-of-kakheti-hereti.e: Seljuk overlordship weakened the kingdom, and in 1104 nobles of [[s:principality-of-hereti|Hereti]] handed King [[e:aghsartan-ii-of-kakheti|Aghsartan II]] to [[e:david-iv-of-georgia|David IV]], who annexed it to the [[s:kingdom-of-georgia|Kingdom of Georgia]]. [[s:principality-of-kakheti|Kakheti]] re-emerged as a separate kingdom in 1465.

kingdom-of-essex.t: The kingdom of the East Saxons north of the Thames, which controlled London for long periods and had a dynasty with unusual 'S' names.
kingdom-of-essex.o: The East [[s:saxons|Saxons]] settled Essex, [[e:middlesex|Middlesex]] and parts of [[e:hertfordshire|Hertfordshire]]. Their royal genealogy traces kings to [[e:aescwine-of-essex|Aescwine]], traditionally placed in 527, and later kings bore names beginning with S, such as [[e:saeberht-of-essex|Saeberht]], Sigeberht and Swithred.
kingdom-of-essex.r: Essex held [[e:london|London]], which [[e:bede|Bede]] called a market of many peoples. [[e:saeberht-of-essex|Saeberht]] accepted [[e:christianity|Christianity]] around 604 and [[e:mellitus|Mellitus]] became [[e:bishop|bishop]] of London, but the kingdom reverted to paganism after his death until [[e:cedd|Cedd's]] mission in the 650s. Several kings often ruled jointly. Essex usually stood under the overlordship of Kent or [[s:kingdom-of-mercia|Mercia]].
kingdom-of-essex.e: After 825 Essex submitted to [[e:egbert-of-wessex|Ecgberht]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-wessex|Kingdom of Wessex]], and later fell within the [[e:danelaw|Danelaw]]. In the 10th century it was absorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-england|Kingdom of England]] as a shire, which survives as the county of Essex.

khanate-of-bukhara.t: The Uzbek khanate of Transoxiana under the Shaybanid and Janid dynasties, whose capital Bukhara was a leading centre of Islamic learning.
khanate-of-bukhara.o: In 1500 [[e:muhammad-shaybani|Muhammad Shaybani]], grandson of [[e:abul-khayr-khan|Abu'l-Khayr]] of the [[s:uzbek-khanate|Uzbek Khanate]], took [[e:samarkand|Samarkand]] from the [[e:timurid-empire|Timurids]] and soon conquered [[e:transoxiana|Transoxiana]] and [[e:khorasan|Khurasan]]. After he was killed by the Safavid [[e:ismail-i|Shah Ismail]] at [[e:merv|Merv]] in 1510, his kinsmen restored [[e:shaybanids|Shaybanid]] rule in Transoxiana, with [[e:bukhara|Bukhara]] becoming the capital in the mid-16th century.
khanate-of-bukhara.r: The [[e:shaybanids|Shaybanids]] ruled through [[e:appanage|appanages]] held by members of the dynasty and [[e:uzbeks|Uzbek]] tribal chiefs. [[e:abdullah-khan-ii|Abdullah Khan II]] reunited the realm in the late 16th century, building [[e:caravanserai|caravanserais]], bridges and [[e:madrasa|madrasas]]. In 1599 the [[e:janid-dynasty|Janids]], or Ashtarkhanids, a branch of the [[e:astrakhan-khanate|Astrakhan Khanate's]] [[e:jochids|Jochid]] line, took over. Trade with [[e:india|India]], [[e:russia|Russia]] and [[e:persia|Persia]] continued, and Naqshbandi [[e:sufism|Sufi]] orders were influential.
khanate-of-bukhara.e: [[e:janid-dynasty|Janid]] power declined, and in 1740 [[e:nader-shah|Nader Shah]] of [[e:persia|Persia]] made [[e:bukhara|Bukhara]] a [[e:vassal|vassal]]. The [[e:manghit-dynasty|Manghit]] atalik [[e:muhammad-rahim-of-bukhara|Muhammad Rahim]] took effective power, and in 1785 his relative [[e:shah-murad|Shah Murad]] formally founded the [[s:emirate-of-bukhara|Emirate of Bukhara]].

kingdom-of-dyfed.t: South-west Welsh kingdom ruled by a dynasty of Irish descent, home of St Davids, which became the core of Deheubarth under Hywel Dda.
kingdom-of-dyfed.o: Dyfed grew from the Roman civitas of the [[s:demetae|Demetae]] after Roman rule ended around 410. Irish settlers crossed to the region in the 4th and 5th centuries, and its royal line traced descent from the [[s:deisi-muman|Déisi]] of Ireland, a link supported by the many ogham-inscribed stones of the area.
kingdom-of-dyfed.r: In the 6th century [[e:gildas|Gildas]] denounced its king [[e:vortiporius|Vortiporius]] as tyrant of the [[s:demetae|Demetae]], and a memorial stone at [[s:county-of-castell|Castell]] Dwyran bearing his name in [[e:latin|Latin]] and ogham may be his. The monastery of St [[e:david|Davids]], founded by [[e:saint-david|Dewi Sant]], became the leading church of [[e:wales|Wales]]. [[e:asser|Asser]] records that its king [[e:hyfaidd-ap-bleddri|Hyfaidd ap Bleddri]] submitted to [[e:alfred-the-great|Alfred of Wessex]] in the 880s to escape pressure from [[s:kingdom-of-gwynedd|Gwynedd]].
kingdom-of-dyfed.e: After [[e:llywarch-ap-hyfaidd|Llywarch ap Hyfaidd]] died around 904, his daughter Elen married [[e:hywel-dda|Hywel Dda]] of [[s:kingdom-of-seisyllwg|Seisyllwg]], who took over Dyfed. Hywel joined the two realms to form the kingdom of [[s:kingdom-of-deheubarth|Deheubarth]], and Dyfed survived as a region and, much later, as a county name.

kussara.t: Kussara, the Anatolian kingdom of Pithana and Anitta, who forged the first large state of central Anatolia and paved the way for the Hittites.
kussara.o: Kussara was a city in central or eastern [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]] whose site is still unknown. In the 18th century BCE its king [[e:pithana|Pithana]] seized Nesa, the city of [[s:kanesh|Kanesh]], and made it a second capital, launching the kingdom's rise.
kussara.r: His son [[e:anitta|Anitta]] conquered [[s:zalpa|Zalpa]] and [[s:hattum|Hattus]], received the submission of the great king of [[s:purushanda|Purushanda]], and took that title himself. His deeds are told in the Anitta text, the oldest known text in the Hittite language. Anitta built temples to the storm god and his own god Siusummi and celebrated victories with hunts of wild animals.
kussara.e: The kingdom of [[e:anitta|Anitta]] did not last long, but the Hittite royal line traced its origins to Kussara; [[e:hattusili-i|Hattusili I]] called himself a man of Kussara. His move to [[e:hattusa|Hattusa]] c. 1650 BCE marks the start of the [[s:hittite-empire|Hittite Empire]].

kingdom-of-naples.t: The southern Italian kingdom ruled from Naples for five centuries by Angevins, Aragonese, Spanish viceroys and Bourbons.
kingdom-of-naples.o: The [[e:sicilian-vespers|Sicilian Vespers]] of 1282 drove [[e:charles-i-of-anjou|Charles of Anjou]] from [[e:sicily|Sicily]], leaving him only the mainland part of the [[s:kingdom-of-sicily|Kingdom of Sicily]]. He and his heirs kept calling themselves kings of Sicily but ruled from [[e:naples|Naples]], which became the capital of a separate kingdom.
kingdom-of-naples.r: [[e:robert-king-of-naples|Robert the Wise]] made [[e:naples|Naples]] a cultural centre, hosting [[e:petrarch|Petrarch]] and [[e:giotto|Giotto]]. Alfonso V of Aragon conquered the kingdom in 1442. After French invasions, [[e:spain|Spain]] ruled it from 1504 through [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroys]], making Naples one of [[e:europe|Europe's]] largest cities. A powerful baronage, heavy taxes and the [[e:masaniello|Masaniello]] revolt of 1647 marked this period. [[e:austria|Austria]] took the kingdom in 1707, and in 1734 [[e:charles-iii-of-spain|Charles of Bourbon]] made it independent again.
kingdom-of-naples.e: [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] armies drove out the [[e:house-of-bourbon|Bourbons]] in 1806, creating the [[s:kingdom-of-naples-1806-1815|Kingdom of Naples]] (1806–1815). [[e:ferdinand-i-of-the-two-sicilies|Ferdinand IV]] returned in 1815 and in 1816 united [[e:naples|Naples]] and [[e:sicily|Sicily]] as the [[s:kingdom-of-the-two-sicilies|Kingdom of the Two Sicilies]].

cr.a: See File history below for details.

kingdom-of-shewa.t: An Amhara kingdom in central Ethiopia that rose to virtual independence and became the power base of Menelik II, the founder of modern Ethiopia.
kingdom-of-shewa.o: While the [[e:gondar|Gondar]] emperors weakened, [[e:negasi-krestos|Negasi Krestos]], a Shewan noble claiming Solomonic descent, established an autonomous lordship in northern Shewa around 1682. His successors, at first with the title meridazmach, gradually extended their rule over the surrounding [[e:oromo|Oromo]] and [[e:amhara|Amhara]] districts, with capitals at [[e:ankober|Ankober]] and later Angolalla and [[e:debre-berhan|Debre Berhan]].
kingdom-of-shewa.r: The rulers combined [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] Christian kingship with pragmatic alliances with [[e:oromo|Oromo]] and Muslim neighbours. [[e:sahle-selassie|Sahle Selassie]] (r. 1813 to 1847), who took the title negus, built a wealthy state and received British and French missions. Shewa controlled trade routes from the [[e:gibe-river|Gibe]] region and [[e:harar|Harar]] to the coast at [[s:sultanate-of-tadjoura|Tadjoura]] and [[e:zeila|Zeila]].
kingdom-of-shewa.e: In 1855 to 1856 [[e:tewodros-ii|Tewodros II]] conquered Shewa, but [[e:menelik-ii|Menelik]], [[e:sahle-selassie|Sahle Selassie's]] grandson, escaped from [[e:magdala|Magdala]] and restored the kingdom in 1865. When Menelik became emperor in 1889, Shewa merged into the [[s:ethiopian-empire|Ethiopian Empire]], with its new capital at [[e:addis-ababa|Addis Ababa]].

kingdom-of-bora-bora.t: A warrior kingdom of the Society Islands whose chiefs conquered neighbouring Raiatea and Tahaʻa and remained independent until French annexation in 1888.
kingdom-of-bora-bora.o: [[e:bora-bora|Bora Bora]], a high island ringed by a wide lagoon in the [[e:leeward-islands-society-islands|Leeward Society Islands]], was known in tradition as Porapora. Its chiefs were famed warriors, and in the mid-18th century the chief Puni led conquests of [[e:tahaa|Tahaʻa]], [[s:kingdom-of-raiatea|Raiatea]] and [[e:maupiti|Maupiti]], making Bora Bora the leading power of the Leeward group when Europeans first arrived in the 1760s.
kingdom-of-bora-bora.r: Kings ruled through a hierarchy of chiefs, with the marae of Fare Opu and others serving as ritual centres. The island's warriors and canoes gave it influence over its neighbours, and marriage ties linked its royal family to [[s:kingdom-of-raiatea|Raiatea]] and to the [[s:kingdom-of-tahiti|Kingdom of Tahiti]].
