Missionaries of the [[e:london-missionary-society|London Missionary Society]] arrived in the 1820s, and the island adopted [[e:christianity|Christianity]] and written laws.
kingdom-of-bora-bora.e: The [[e:jarnac-convention|Jarnac Convention]] of 1847 recognised [[e:bora-bora|Bora Bora's]] independence. Its last queen, [[e:teriimaevarua-iii|Teriimaevarua III]], reigned from 1873 until [[e:france|France]] annexed the island in 1888. It became part of [[s:french-polynesia|French Polynesia]] and, during the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]], a [[s:united-states|United States]] supply base.

karluk-yabgu.t: A Turkic confederation that fought beside the Arabs at Talas and seized Suyab, preparing the ground for the Kara-Khanid Khanate.
karluk-yabgu.o: The [[e:karluks|Karluks]] lived in the [[e:altai-mountains|Altai]] and joined the [[e:uyghurs|Uyghurs]] and [[e:basmyls|Basmyls]] in overthrowing the [[s:second-turkic-khaganate|Second Turkic Khaganate]] in 744. Driven west by the [[s:uyghur-khaganate|Uyghur Khaganate]], they moved to the [[e:semirechye|Zhetysu]] region, and in 751 their defection to the Abbasid side helped decide the [[e:battle-of-talas|Battle of Talas]] against [[e:tang-dynasty|Tang China]].
karluk-yabgu.r: Led by a yabghu, the [[e:karluks|Karluks]] took [[e:suyab|Suyab]] and the lands of the [[s:turgesh-khaganate|Turgesh Khaganate]] by 766, ruling a mix of nomadic tribes and the Sogdian towns of the Chu valley. They controlled [[e:silk-road|Silk Road]] routes between [[e:transoxiana|Transoxiana]] and the [[e:tarim-basin|Tarim]], and Muslim geographers describe them as rich in livestock and towns. Some groups converted to [[e:islam|Islam]] early.
karluk-yabgu.e: After the [[s:uyghur-khaganate|Uyghur Khaganate]] fell in 840, the [[e:karluks|Karluk]] leader [[e:bilge-kul-qadir-khan|Bilge Kul Qadir Khan]] proclaimed himself [[e:khagan|khagan]], an event many historians take as the founding of the [[s:kara-khanid-khanate|Kara-Khanid Khanate]], which absorbed the Karluk lands.

kalinyamat.t: The north Javanese state of Ratu Kalinyamat, the warrior queen of Jepara who twice sent fleets against Portuguese Malacca.
kalinyamat.o: Kalinyamat, near the port of [[e:jepara|Jepara]], was ruled by [[e:sultan-hadlirin|Sultan Hadlirin]] and his wife, a daughter of [[e:trenggana|Sultan Trenggana of Demak]]. In 1549, during the [[s:demak-sultanate|Demak]] succession war, Hadlirin was murdered by agents of [[e:arya-penangsang|Arya Penangsang]]. His widow became ruler, remembered as [[e:ratu-kalinyamat|Ratu Kalinyamat]].
kalinyamat.r: [[e:ratu-kalinyamat|Ratu Kalinyamat]] helped [[e:hadiwijaya|Hadiwijaya of Pajang]] defeat [[e:arya-penangsang|Arya Penangsang]] and made [[e:jepara|Jepara]] a leading port and shipbuilding centre. She sent fleets to support attacks on [[s:portuguese-malacca|Portuguese Malacca]] in 1551 and 1574, and Portuguese writers called her the queen of Japara. She also patronised mosques such as the one at [[e:mantingan-mosque|Mantingan]].
kalinyamat.e: After [[e:ratu-kalinyamat|Ratu Kalinyamat]] died around 1579, [[e:jepara|Jepara]] came under [[s:pajang-sultanate|Pajang]] and then the [[s:mataram-sultanate|Mataram Sultanate]]. She was named a [[e:national-hero-of-indonesia|National Hero of Indonesia]] in 2023.

karkota-dynasty.t: The dynasty that made Kashmir a regional empire under Lalitaditya Muktapida and built the Sun temple at Martand.
karkota-dynasty.o: According to [[e:rajatarangini|Kalhana's Rajatarangini]], [[e:durlabhavardhana|Durlabhavardhana]] founded the dynasty around 625, succeeding the last king of the [[s:gonanda-dynasty|Gonanda dynasty]] through marriage. [[e:xuanzang|Xuanzang]] visited [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]] during his reign and described a powerful kingdom with many Buddhist monasteries.
karkota-dynasty.r: [[e:lalitaditya-muktapida|Lalitaditya Muktapida]], who ruled in the 8th century, led campaigns into the [[e:punjab|Punjab]], [[e:kannauj|Kannauj]] and beyond, defeating [[e:yashovarman-of-kannauj|Yashovarman]] of the [[s:varman-dynasty-of-kannauj|Varman dynasty of Kannauj]], and sent envoys to [[e:tang-dynasty|Tang China]]. He founded the city of [[e:parihaspora|Parihaspora]] and built the [[e:martand-sun-temple|Martand Sun temple]], whose ruins still dominate the valley. [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]] became a centre of [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] poetry and philosophy, and [[e:jayapida|Jayapida]] later patronised scholars and poets at his court. Irrigation and saffron supported the economy.
karkota-dynasty.e: Later Karkota kings were weak and dominated by ministers and court factions. In 855 [[e:avantivarman|Avantivarman]] took the throne, founding the [[s:utpala-dynasty|Utpala dynasty]].

khanate-of-sibir.t: The Tatar khanate of western Siberia whose defeat by Yermak's Cossacks in 1582 began Russia's conquest of Siberia.
khanate-of-sibir.o: The khanate emerged from the [[s:tyumen-khanate|Tyumen Khanate]] when the local [[e:taibugids|Taibugid dynasty]] seized power around 1495 and moved the capital to [[e:qashliq|Qashliq]] (Isker) on the [[e:irtysh|Irtysh]]. The [[e:shaybanids|Shibanid]] descendants of Jochi later contested the throne with the Taibugids.
khanate-of-sibir.r: Sibir ruled Siberian [[e:tatars|Tatars]] and tribute-paying forest peoples such as the [[e:khanty|Khanty]] and [[e:mansi|Mansi]], whose fur tribute was its main wealth. The [[e:taibugids|Taibugid]] ruler Yadegar paid tribute to [[e:ivan-iv-of-russia|Ivan IV]] from 1555, but in 1563 the [[e:shaybanids|Shibanid]] [[e:kuchum|Kuchum]] seized power, stopped payments and promoted [[e:islam|Islam]] among his subjects with missionaries from [[e:bukhara|Bukhara]].
khanate-of-sibir.e: In 1582 the [[e:cossacks|Cossack]] leader [[e:yermak-timofeyevich|Yermak]], employed by the [[e:stroganov-family|Stroganov]] merchants, took [[e:qashliq|Qashliq]]. [[e:kuchum|Kuchum]] fought on from the steppe until his final defeat on the Ob in 1598, after which the khanate's lands became part of [[e:russia|Russia]].

kingdom-of-aquitaine.t: Carolingian sub-kingdom of south-western Francia, created by Charlemagne for his son Louis the Pious.
kingdom-of-aquitaine.o: After crushing the last independent dukes of the [[s:early-duchy-of-aquitaine|Early Duchy of Aquitaine]], [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]] made [[s:duchy-of-aquitaine|Aquitaine]] a kingdom for his three-year-old son Louis, crowned by the pope in [[e:rome|Rome]] in 781. It reached from the [[e:loire|Loire]] to the [[e:pyrenees|Pyrenees]] and was meant to secure the frontier against [[e:al-andalus|Al-Andalus]].
kingdom-of-aquitaine.r: Louis governed with Frankish counts and advisers, reformed monasteries with [[e:benedict-of-aniane|Benedict of Aniane]] and led campaigns into [[e:spain|Spain]], taking [[e:barcelona|Barcelona]] in 801. Royal residences included [[s:county-of-toulouse|Toulouse]], [[e:poitiers|Poitiers]] and [[e:chasseneuil-du-poitou|Chasseneuil]]. After he became emperor in 814 the kingdom passed to his son Pepin I.
kingdom-of-aquitaine.e: After Pepin I died in 838, his son [[e:pepin-ii-of-aquitaine|Pepin II]] fought a long war against his uncle [[e:charles-the-bald|Charles the Bald]] of [[s:west-francia|West Francia]]. Charles installed his own sons, [[e:charles-the-child|Charles the Child]] and [[e:louis-the-stammerer|Louis the Stammerer]], and when Louis succeeded to [[e:west-francia|West Francia]] in 877 the kingdom merged into it.

kingdom-of-denmark.t: The world's oldest continuing monarchy, founded by Gorm the Old and Harald Bluetooth, which once ruled England, Norway and much of the Baltic.
kingdom-of-denmark.o: Danish kings are mentioned from the 8th century, but the continuous kingdom is traced to [[e:gorm-the-old|Gorm the Old]], who ruled from [[e:jelling|Jelling]] around 936. His son [[e:harald-bluetooth|Harald Bluetooth]] raised the Jelling stone, which claims that he won all [[e:denmark|Denmark]] and [[e:norway|Norway]] and made the [[e:danes|Danes]] Christian, and built ring fortresses such as [[e:trelleborg-slagelse|Trelleborg]].
kingdom-of-denmark.r: [[e:sweyn-forkbeard|Sweyn Forkbeard]] and [[e:cnut-the-great|Cnut the Great]] ruled [[e:england|England]], and the Valdemar kings of the 12th and 13th centuries expanded into the Baltic. [[e:margaret-i-of-denmark|Margaret I]] united [[e:denmark|Denmark]], [[e:norway|Norway]] and [[e:sweden|Sweden]] in the [[s:kalmar-union|Kalmar Union]] in 1397. The Lutheran [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] came in 1536, and [[e:frederick-iii-of-denmark|Frederick III]] made the monarchy absolute in 1660. [[e:copenhagen|Copenhagen]] grew rich from [[e:oresund|the Sound]] Toll on Baltic shipping.
kingdom-of-denmark.e: [[e:denmark|Denmark]] lost [[e:scania|Scania]] to [[e:sweden|Sweden]] in 1658, [[e:norway|Norway]] in 1814 and [[e:schleswig|Schleswig]] and [[s:county-of-holstein|Holstein]] to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] and [[e:austria|Austria]] in 1864. A liberal constitution was adopted in 1849. Occupied by [[e:germany|Germany]] in 1940-1945, Denmark became a welfare state and joined the [[e:european-communities|European Community]] in 1973; the [[e:faroe-islands|Faroe Islands]] and [[e:greenland|Greenland]] remain self-governing parts of the realm.

kotda-sangani-state.t: A small Jadeja Rajput state of central Kathiawar, a branch of the Gondal ruling family.
kotda-sangani-state.o: Kotda Sangani was held by a [[e:jadeja|Jadeja Rajput]] family related to the ruling house of [[s:gondal-state|Gondal]]. It emerged as a separate holding around 1650, though details of its founding are sparse.
kotda-sangani-state.r: The Thakor ruled a small group of farming villages, paying tribute before 1807 and then coming under British supervision in the [[e:kathiawar-agency|Kathiawar Agency]]. Little else is recorded in standard references.
kotda-sangani-state.e: Kotda Sangani merged into the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960, in present [[s:rajkot-state|Rajkot]] district.

kingdom-of-samoa.t: A Samoan national government contested by rival chiefly lines and by Germany, Britain and the United States, which ended in the islands' partition in 1899.
kingdom-of-samoa.o: [[e:samoan-islands|Samoa]] was divided among districts and great titles such as Malietoa, Tupua [[e:tupua-tamasese-titimaea|Tamasese]] and Mataʻafa. As the German firm [[e:j-c-godeffroy-and-sohn|Godeffroy]] developed plantations near [[e:apia|Apia]], Samoan chiefs formed a central government at [[e:mulinuu|Mulinuʻu]] in 1873, with a council of chiefs and an assembly. The American adventurer [[e:albert-steinberger|Albert Steinberger]] acted as premier until British and American consuls had him deported in 1876.
kingdom-of-samoa.r: Kingship, held mostly by [[e:malietoa-laupepa|Malietoa Laupepa]], was repeatedly disputed in civil wars, with each rival courting a foreign power. [[e:germany|Germany]] backed [[e:tupua-tamasese-titimaea|Tamasese]] against Laupepa in 1887, and a naval confrontation at [[e:apia|Apia]] ended only when a hurricane wrecked the German and American warships in 1889. The [[e:treaty-of-berlin-1889|Berlin Treaty]] of 1889 restored Laupepa under a three-power supervision. [[e:robert-louis-stevenson|Robert Louis Stevenson]], living at [[e:vailima|Vailima]], wrote against foreign meddling.
kingdom-of-samoa.e: After [[e:malietoa-laupepa|Laupepa]]'s death in 1898, war between supporters of [[e:mataafa-iosefo|Mataʻafa Iosefo]] and [[e:malietoa-tanumafili-i|Malietoa Tanumafili I]] drew in foreign navies. The [[e:tripartite-convention-1899|Tripartite Convention of 1899]] abolished the kingship and partitioned the islands into [[s:german-samoa|German Samoa]] and [[s:american-samoa|American Samoa]].

cr.a: Original: Malietoa Laupepa Vector: Orange Tuesday

kingdom-of-livonia.t: Puppet kingdom created by Ivan the Terrible for the Danish prince Magnus during the Livonian War, which collapsed within eight years.
kingdom-of-livonia.o: [[e:ivan-iv-of-russia|Ivan IV of Russia]], seeking to win the [[e:baltic-germans|Baltic Germans]] to his side in the [[e:livonian-war|Livonian War]], proclaimed [[e:magnus-duke-of-holstein|Magnus of Holstein]], brother of [[e:frederick-ii-of-denmark|Frederick II of Denmark]] and ruler of [[s:danish-osel|Danish Ösel]], king of [[s:livonian-confederation|Livonia]] in 1570. Magnus was to rule all [[e:livonia|Livonia]] as the tsar's [[e:vassal|vassal]], and he married Ivan's relative [[e:maria-vladimirovna-staritskaya|Maria Staritskaya]].
kingdom-of-livonia.r: [[e:magnus-duke-of-holstein|Magnus]] resided at [[e:poltsamaa|Oberpahlen]] (Põltsamaa) in central [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]]. His kingdom depended entirely on Russian troops and never controlled the major towns. A 30-week siege of [[s:reval|Reval]] in 1570-1571 failed, and the Estonian and Livonian nobility largely refused to accept him.
kingdom-of-livonia.e: In 1577 [[e:magnus-duke-of-holstein|Magnus]] tried to act independently and was punished by Ivan, who seized his towns. Magnus fled to Polish protection in 1578, renounced his royal title and died at [[e:piltene|Pilten]] in 1583. The kingdom disappeared, and its lands were divided among Poland-[[e:lithuania|Lithuania]], [[e:sweden|Sweden]] and [[e:russia|Russia]].

kingdom-of-england.t: The medieval and early modern kingdom unified by Aethelstan, transformed by the Norman Conquest and joined with Scotland in 1707.
kingdom-of-england.o: In 927 [[e:aethelstan|Aethelstan]] took [[e:york-maine|York]] and received the submission of the northern rulers, completing the work of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-anglo-saxons|Kingdom of the Anglo-Saxons]]. [[e:vikings|Viking]] kings briefly regained York until 954, and Danish kings [[e:cnut-the-great|Cnut]] and his sons ruled [[e:england|England]] from 1016 to 1042.
kingdom-of-england.r: Late [[e:anglo-saxons|Anglo-Saxon]] [[e:england|England]] had shires, a strong coinage and royal writs. After [[e:william-the-conqueror|William the Conqueror's]] victory at [[e:battle-of-hastings|Hastings]] in 1066, Norman lords, [[e:domesday-book|Domesday Book]] and a French-speaking elite reshaped society. [[e:magna-carta|Magna Carta]] in 1215, the growth of Parliament and [[e:common-law|common law]], the wool trade and the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] under [[e:henry-viii-of-england|Henry VIII]] defined later centuries.
kingdom-of-england.e: [[e:england|England]] annexed [[e:wales|Wales]] between 1283 and 1543 and ruled the [[s:lordship-of-ireland|Lordship of Ireland]]. [[e:james-vi-and-i|James VI of Scotland]] inherited the crown in 1603, and after the Civil War and the [[s:commonwealth-of-england|Commonwealth of England]], the [[e:acts-of-union-1707|Acts of Union]] of 1707 created the [[s:kingdom-of-great-britain|Kingdom of Great Britain]].

kingdom-of-the-geats.t: The kingdom or kingdoms of the Geats in southern Sweden's Götaland, the people of Beowulf, later merged with the Svear to form Sweden.
kingdom-of-the-geats.o: Ptolemy and [[e:jordanes|Jordanes]] mention Gautoi and Gautigoths in southern [[e:scandinavia|Scandinavia]], and the Old English poem [[e:beowulf|Beowulf]] makes the [[e:geats|Geats]] and their king [[e:hygelac|Hygelac]] its heroes. Hygelac's raid on [[e:frisia|Frisia]], recorded by [[e:gregory-of-tours|Gregory of Tours]] around 520, is one of the few datable events. Their heartland lay in [[e:vastergotland|Västergötland]] and [[e:ostergotland|Östergötland]], around lakes [[e:lake-vanern|Vänern]] and [[e:lake-vattern|Vättern]].
kingdom-of-the-geats.r: Whether the [[e:geats|Geats]] formed one kingdom or several regional lordships is uncertain. Each land kept its own assembly and laws, later written down as the [[e:vastgotalagen|Västgötalagen]]. Society was based on farming, [[e:iron-technology|ironworking]] and a warrior aristocracy, and the region kept close ties with [[e:denmark|Denmark]] across the [[e:kattegat|Kattegat]].
kingdom-of-the-geats.e: Around 1000 the [[e:geats|Geats]] came under the kings of the [[e:svear|Svear]], and [[e:olof-skotkonung|Olof Skötkonung]], traditionally baptised at [[e:husaby|Husaby]] in [[e:vastergotland|Västergötland]], ruled both peoples. Götaland remained a distinct part of the [[s:kingdom-of-sweden|Kingdom of Sweden]], with its own lawmen, and its people sometimes elected rival kings into the 12th century.

klein-venedig.t: A short-lived German colony in Venezuela, leased by Emperor Charles V to the Welser banking house of Augsburg to pay off his debts.
klein-venedig.o: In 1528 [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]] granted the [[e:welser-family|Welser family]] of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-augsburg|Augsburg]] the right to colonise and govern the province of [[s:venezuela|Venezuela]] in return for loans. The Welsers took over [[e:coro-venezuela|Coro]], founded the year before by [[e:juan-de-ampies|Juan de Ampíes]], and sent the first German governor, [[e:ambrosius-ehinger|Ambrosius Ehinger]], in 1529.
klein-venedig.r: The [[e:welser-family|Welser]] governors used the colony mainly as a base for expeditions into the interior in search of gold and the legendary [[e:el-dorado|El Dorado]]. Ehinger, [[e:nikolaus-federmann|Nikolaus Federmann]], [[e:georg-hohermuth-von-speyer|Georg Hohermuth von Speyer]] and [[e:philipp-von-hutten|Philipp von Hutten]] led long marches into the [[s:andecavi|Andes]] and llanos, often with great brutality towards indigenous peoples. Little permanent settlement or farming developed, and German miners brought to the colony achieved little. Indigenous people were enslaved and sold.
klein-venedig.e: In 1546 the Spaniard [[e:juan-de-carvajal|Juan de Carvajal]] killed [[e:philipp-von-hutten|Philipp von Hutten]] and Bartholomäus [[e:welser-family|Welser]] the younger. The [[e:council-of-the-indies|Council of the Indies]] withdrew the Welser lease, confirmed in 1556, and the territory reverted to the Spanish [[s:province-of-venezuela|Province of Venezuela]].

kingdom-of-dagbon.t: The largest kingdom of northern Ghana, ruled by the Ya Na from Yendi, whose drummers preserve one of Africa's richest oral histories.
kingdom-of-dagbon.o: Dagbon traces its royal house to [[e:na-gbewaa|Na Gbewaa]], founder of [[s:mamprugu|Mamprugu]], through his son [[e:sitobu|Sitobu]]. Under [[e:na-nyagse|Na Nyagse]], probably in the 15th century, [[e:dagomba-people|Dagomba]] horsemen conquered the local peoples of the [[e:white-volta|White Volta]] basin, killing or displacing their earth-priests and installing princes as chiefs. Later pressure from [[s:kingdom-of-gonja|Gonja]] pushed the capital east to [[e:yendi|Yendi]].
kingdom-of-dagbon.r: The Ya Na ruled through a hierarchy of chieftaincies held by royal sons and grandsons, who competed to rise toward the paramountcy. Royal drummers, the lunsi, recited genealogies and history at festivals. [[e:islam|Islam]] was adopted at court under [[e:na-zangina|Na Zangina]] in the early 18th century, and Muslim traders linked Dagbon to the kola routes between [[s:hausa-kingdoms|Hausaland]] and the forest.
kingdom-of-dagbon.e: In 1744 Dagbon was defeated by the [[s:ashanti-empire|Ashanti Empire]] and paid an annual tribute of slaves. In 1896 German forces defeated the [[e:dagomba-people|Dagomba]] at [[e:battle-of-adibo|Adibo]] and burned [[e:yendi|Yendi]], and in 1899 Dagbon was divided between the [[s:gold-coast-colony|British Gold Coast]] and [[s:german-togoland|German Togoland]], separating Yendi from its western lands. The Ya Na still reigns at Yendi in [[e:ghana|Ghana's]] Northern Region.

kingdom-of-al-abwab.t: A Christian Nubian kingdom on the Nile south of Makuria, once a province of Alodia, known mainly from Mamluk-era Arabic sources.
kingdom-of-al-abwab.o: Al-Abwab, Arabic for 'the gates', was originally the northern province of [[s:alodia|Alodia]], centred near Kabushiya close to the junction of the [[e:nile|Nile]] and the [[e:atbara-river|Atbara]]. By 1276 it appears as an independent kingdom, apparently having broken away as Alodian power declined.
kingdom-of-al-abwab.r: Almost nothing is known of its internal government. In 1276 its king Adur captured the fugitive Makurian king [[e:david|David]], who had fled the [[e:mamluk-sultanate|Mamluk Sultanate's]] invasion, and handed him over to [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:baybars|Baybars]]. Adur later corresponded with Sultan [[e:qalawun|Qalawun]], offering alliance against [[s:makuria|Makuria]]. Its people were Christian [[e:nubians|Nubians]].
kingdom-of-al-abwab.e: The kingdom fades from the record in the late 14th century, probably absorbed by advancing Arab tribes and the general collapse of Christian [[e:nubia|Nubia]]. The area later fell within the sphere of the [[s:abdallab-sheikhdom|Abdallab Sheikhdom]] and the [[s:funj-sultanate|Funj Sultanate]].

kenya.t: East Africa's leading economy, independent since 1963, which moved from one-party rule to a multi-party democracy with a new constitution in 2010.
kenya.o: [[s:kenya-colony|Kenya Colony]] became independent on 12 December 1963 under [[e:jomo-kenyatta|Jomo Kenyatta]], leader of the [[e:kenya-african-national-union|Kenya African National Union]] (KANU), after the [[e:mau-mau-rebellion|Mau Mau]] emergency and negotiations at [[e:lancaster-house|Lancaster House]]. It became a republic a year later, with Kenyatta as president.
kenya.r: [[e:jomo-kenyatta|Kenyatta]] built a centralised state, favouring capitalist development, land purchase by Africans and close ties with the West, while tourism, [[e:tea|tea]] and [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]] drove growth. Daniel arap Moi, president from 1978, made [[e:kenya-african-national-union|KANU]] the sole legal party in 1982. Domestic and foreign pressure restored multi-party politics in 1991, and [[e:mwai-kibaki|Mwai Kibaki's]] victory in 2002 ended KANU's rule.
kenya.e: A disputed election in 2007 led to violence that killed more than 1,000 people, followed by a power-sharing deal and a new constitution in 2010 that devolved power to 47 counties. Kenya remains a republic, with [[e:william-ruto|William Ruto]] president since 2022.

kingdom-of-owo.t: Yoruba kingdom between Ife and Benin, known for its ivory carving, terracotta sculpture and court culture shaped by both neighbours.
kingdom-of-owo.o: Owo traditions trace its royal line, the [[e:olowo|Olowo]], to Ojugbelu, a son or grandson of [[e:oduduwa|Oduduwa]] who left [[s:kingdom-of-ife|Ile-Ife]] and settled in the forest to the south-east. The kingdom is usually dated from around the 15th century, though settlement on the site is older.
kingdom-of-owo.r: The [[e:olowo|Olowo]] ruled with chiefs organised in grades and with town quarters that kept their own titles. Lying close to the [[s:benin-empire|Benin Empire]], Owo paid tribute to [[e:benin-empire|Benin]] for long periods and adopted Benin styles of regalia and ritual. Terracotta sculptures excavated at [[e:igbo-people|Igbo]]'Laja, dated to the 15th century, and [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] work made for the court show a distinctive art blending [[e:ife|Ife]] and Benin traditions.
kingdom-of-owo.e: Owo came under British rule in the 1890s and was incorporated into the [[s:protectorate-of-southern-nigeria|Protectorate of Southern Nigeria]]. It is now a town in [[e:ondo-state|Ondo State]], where the [[e:olowo|Olowo]] remains a senior traditional ruler.

kuthar-state.t: A small Rajput hill state in the Shimla hills, part of whose land became the British cantonment of Subathu.
kuthar-state.o: The ruling family claimed [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] descent and tradition dates the state to around 1500. Its early history is not reliably documented.
kuthar-state.r: Kuthar was a small hill state near the Gambhar river. It was occupied by the [[e:gurkhas|Gurkhas]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Kingdom of Nepal]] in the early 19th century. After the [[e:anglo-nepalese-war|Anglo-Nepalese War]] the British restored its Rana in 1815 but kept [[e:subathu|Subathu]], which became one of their first hill cantonments.
kuthar-state.e: Kuthar merged into [[e:himachal-pradesh|Himachal Pradesh]] in April 1948 and is now part of Solan district.

kingdom-of-dambadeniya.t: The Sinhalese kingdom that moved the island's capital south-west to Dambadeniya after the fall of Polonnaruwa and restored Buddhist learning.
kingdom-of-dambadeniya.o: After [[e:kalinga-magha|Kalinga Magha's]] invasion devastated the [[e:polonnaruwa|Polonnaruwa]] kingdom around 1215, Sinhalese resistance gathered in the south-west. [[e:vijayabahu-iii-of-dambadeniya|Vijayabahu III]] established himself at Dambadeniya, a defensible rock fortress in the wet zone, and by the 1230s had founded a new royal line there, recovering the [[e:relic-of-the-tooth-of-the-buddha|Tooth Relic]] and the Alms Bowl.
kingdom-of-dambadeniya.r: [[e:parakramabahu-ii|Parakramabahu II]], the dynasty's most celebrated king, drove out [[e:kalinga-magha|Magha's]] forces from [[e:polonnaruwa|Polonnaruwa]], held a coronation there and convened a Buddhist council to reform the monastic order. He was himself an author, and the period produced classic [[e:sinhala-language|Sinhala]] prose such as the [[e:pujavaliya|Pujavaliya]] and [[e:saddharma-ratnavaliya|Saddharma Ratnavaliya]]. The kings faced invasions by the [[s:later-pandyan-empire|Later Pandyan Empire]] and the Malay ruler [[e:chandrabhanu|Chandrabhanu]].
kingdom-of-dambadeniya.e: Under later kings the capital moved repeatedly, to [[e:yapahuwa|Yapahuwa]] and [[e:kurunegala|Kurunegala]], as the [[s:later-pandyan-empire|Pandyas]] raided and carried off the [[e:relic-of-the-tooth-of-the-buddha|Tooth Relic]]. Power drifted towards the central hills, and by 1341 the court had settled at [[s:kingdom-of-gampola|Gampola]], beginning the Kingdom of Gampola.

kangra-state.t: The kingdom of the Katoch Rajputs, among the oldest ruling families in India, whose court under Sansar Chand gave rise to the Kangra school of painting.
kangra-state.o: The Katoch dynasty claimed descent from the Trigarta kingdom of the [[e:mahabharata|Mahabharata]], and tradition gives it great antiquity. Its seat was the fort of [[e:kangra-fort|Nagarkot]], or Kangra, with its rich temple of [[e:bajreshwari-devi-temple|Vajreshwari]], which [[e:mahmud-of-ghazni|Mahmud of Ghazni]] plundered in 1009.
kangra-state.r: Kangra fort fell to the [[e:mughal-empire|Mughals]] in 1620, and the Katoch Rajas were reduced to [[e:vassal|vassals]] until the empire weakened. [[e:sansar-chand-katoch|Sansar Chand Katoch]] (r. 1775–1823) regained the fort in 1786, dominated the neighbouring hill states and made his courts at [[e:sujanpur-tira|Tira Sujanpur]] and [[e:nadaun|Nadaun]] centres of the delicate Kangra style of [[e:persian-miniature|miniature painting]], known for its scenes of [[e:krishna|Krishna]].
kangra-state.e: A [[e:gurkhas|Gurkha]] siege from 1806 forced [[e:sansar-chand-katoch|Sansar Chand]] to call in [[e:ranjit-singh|Ranjit Singh]], who took Kangra fort for the [[s:sikh-empire|Sikh Empire]] in 1809. In 1828 his son [[e:anirudh-chand|Anirudh Chand]] fled to British territory and the state was annexed. Kangra passed to the British in 1846 and is now a district of [[e:himachal-pradesh|Himachal Pradesh]].

kingdom-of-jiaodong.t: A short-lived kingdom on the eastern Shandong peninsula, given to the young Qi king Tian Shi in 206 BCE, whose ruler was killed within months.
kingdom-of-jiaodong.o: [[e:tian-shi-king-of-qi|Tian Shi]] had been installed as king of Qi by his uncle [[e:tian-rong|Tian Rong]] during the war against the [[s:qin-dynasty|Qin dynasty]]. In 206 BCE [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]] demoted him to King of Jiaodong, with his capital at [[e:jimo|Jimo]], giving [[e:linzi|Linzi]] to [[e:tian-du|Tian Du]].
kingdom-of-jiaodong.r: [[e:tian-rong|Tian Rong]] ordered his nephew to stay in [[e:linzi|Linzi]], but [[e:tian-shi-king-of-qi|Tian Shi]], fearing [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]], slipped away to Jiaodong. The kingdom existed for only a few months and left no trace of separate government.
kingdom-of-jiaodong.e: Enraged, [[e:tian-rong|Tian Rong]] pursued [[e:tian-shi-king-of-qi|Tian Shi]] and killed him at [[e:jimo|Jimo]] in 206 BCE, absorbing Jiaodong into Qi (206 BC).

kumamoto-domain.t: The domain of Higo in central Kyushu, ruled from Kumamoto's mighty castle by the Kato and then the Hosokawa family.
kumamoto-domain.o: [[e:kato-kiyomasa|Kato Kiyomasa]], one of [[e:toyotomi-hideyoshi|Toyotomi Hideyoshi's]] leading generals, received northern Higo in 1588 and the whole province after supporting [[e:tokugawa-ieyasu|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] in 1600. He completed [[e:kumamoto|Kumamoto]] castle around 1607, one of the strongest fortresses in [[e:japan|Japan]], and carried out major river and land reclamation works.
kumamoto-domain.r: In 1632 the [[e:shogun|shogunate]] removed [[e:kato-kiyomasa|Kiyomasa]]'s son [[e:kato-tadahiro|Tadahiro]] and gave Higo to [[e:hosokawa-tadatoshi|Hosokawa Tadatoshi]] with 540,000 koku; the Hosokawa ruled until 1871. Tadatoshi hosted the swordsman [[e:miyamoto-musashi|Miyamoto Musashi]] in his last years. In the 18th century [[e:hosokawa-shigekata|Hosokawa Shigekata]] reformed finances and administration and founded the Jishukan school and a medical academy.
kumamoto-domain.e: [[e:kumamoto|Kumamoto]] took a cautious line in the Restoration and joined the new government. After abolition in 1871 it became [[e:kumamoto-prefecture|Kumamoto Prefecture]], and in 1877 the castle withstood a siege by [[e:saigo-takamori|Saigo Takamori's]] rebels.

khariar-state.t: A Chauhan chiefship of western Orissa, a branch of the Patna ruling house, transferred from the Central Provinces to Orissa in 1936.
khariar-state.o: Khariar was held by a branch of the [[e:chauhan|Chauhan]] family of [[e:patna|Patna]] ([[s:patna-state|Patnagarh]]), one of the dynasties that dominated the hill country of western [[e:odisha|Orissa]] from the 14th century. The register dates its separate existence to around 1600.
khariar-state.r: The ruler governed an upland of forest and dry farming. In the 18th century Khariar fell under the [[s:nagpur-kingdom|Bhonsles of Nagpur]], and under British rule it was treated as a large zamindari of [[e:raipur|Raipur]] district in the [[e:central-provinces|Central Provinces]] rather than as a full princely state.
khariar-state.e: Khariar was transferred to the new province of [[e:odisha|Orissa]] in 1936, and the zamindari was abolished after independence. Its territory lies in today's [[e:nuapada-district|Nuapada district]] of Odisha.

khmer-republic.t: The US-backed Cambodian republic of Lon Nol, which deposed Sihanouk in 1970 and fell to the Khmer Rouge in April 1975.
khmer-republic.o: On 18 March 1970 [[e:cambodia|Cambodia's]] national assembly, led by Prime Minister [[e:lon-nol|Lon Nol]] and Prince [[e:sisowath-sirik-matak|Sisowath Sirik Matak]], voted to remove [[e:norodom-sihanouk|Norodom Sihanouk]] as head of state while he was abroad. The monarchy was abolished and the [[e:khmer-empire|Khmer]] Republic proclaimed on 9 October 1970.
khmer-republic.r: [[e:lon-nol|Lon Nol]], who became president in 1972, sought to expel North Vietnamese forces from [[s:kingdom-of-cambodia-1953-1970|Cambodia]] and received US military aid. The republic was weakened by corruption, an inexperienced army and Lon Nol's ill health. US bombing of the countryside intensified, and the [[e:khmer-rouge|Khmer Rouge]], now allied with the exiled [[e:norodom-sihanouk|Sihanouk]], gained recruits. Refugees swelled [[e:phnom-penh|Phnom Penh]] to over two million.
khmer-republic.e: [[e:khmer-rouge|Khmer Rouge]] forces besieged [[e:phnom-penh|Phnom Penh]] in early 1975. [[e:lon-nol|Lon Nol]] fled on 1 April, the US evacuated its embassy, and on 17 April 1975 the city fell. The [[e:khmer-empire|Khmer]] Rouge emptied the capital and established [[s:democratic-kampuchea|Democratic Kampuchea]].

kingdom-of-cornwall.t: The last surviving British kingdom of the south-west peninsula, which held out against Wessex until the 9th and 10th centuries.
kingdom-of-cornwall.o: [[e:cornwall|Cornwall]] emerged as a separate British kingdom as the larger kingdom of [[s:kingdom-of-dumnonia|Dumnonia]] shrank under [[e:wessex|West Saxon]] pressure. By the early 8th century [[s:kingdom-of-wessex|Wessex]] had taken [[e:devon|Devon]], and the British realm beyond the [[e:river-tamar|Tamar]] became known as Kernow or Cornwall. Its kings are poorly recorded; [[e:geraint-of-dumnonia|Geraint]] fought [[e:ine-of-wessex|Ine of Wessex]] around 710.
kingdom-of-cornwall.r: [[e:cornwall|Cornwall]] kept its Brittonic language, saints' cults and links with [[e:wales|Wales]] and [[s:duchy-of-brittany|Brittany]]. [[e:tin|Tin]] mining and sea trade continued from Roman times. A defeat of a combined Cornish and [[e:vikings|Viking]] army at [[e:battle-of-hingston-down|Hingston Down]] in 838 shows its kings still resisting the [[s:kingdom-of-wessex|Kingdom of Wessex]]. The [[e:annales-cambriae|Annales Cambriae]] record the drowning of King [[e:dungarth|Dungarth]] in 875.
kingdom-of-cornwall.e: [[e:cornwall|Cornwall]] was brought under English control by the 9th century, and Aethelstan fixed the [[e:river-tamar|Tamar]] as the boundary around 936. It became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-england|Kingdom of England]], while the Cornish language survived into the 18th century.

kishangarh-state.t: A Rathore Rajput state of Rajasthan celebrated for the Kishangarh school of painting and its iconic image of Bani Thani.
kishangarh-state.o: Kishangarh was founded in 1611 by [[e:kishan-singh-of-kishangarh|Kishan Singh]], a son of [[e:udai-singh-of-marwar|Raja Udai Singh of Marwar]], who received the territory near [[e:ajmer|Ajmer]] from the Mughal emperor [[e:jahangir|Jahangir]]. The state took its name from him.
kishangarh-state.r: The [[e:maharaja|Maharajas]] served as Mughal mansabdars and later accepted British protection in 1818. The court became a centre of [[e:krishna|Krishna]] devotion and art: under Raja [[e:sawant-singh|Sawant Singh]], the poet Nagari Das, painters such as [[e:nihal-chand|Nihal Chand]] created the elongated, lyrical Kishangarh style, epitomised by the portrait known as [[e:bani-thani|Bani Thani]]. It was a fifteen-gun salute state.
kishangarh-state.e: Kishangarh joined the [[s:united-state-of-rajasthan|United State of Rajasthan]] in 1948. The town, in [[e:ajmer|Ajmer]] district, is now known for its marble trade and the [[e:persian-miniature|miniature painting]] tradition that still bears its name.

kakatiya-dynasty.t: The Telugu dynasty of Warangal that united the Andhra country, built the Thousand Pillar Temple and was famed for its diamonds and tanks.
kakatiya-dynasty.o: The Kakatiyas began as feudatories of the [[s:western-chalukya-empire|Chalukyas of Kalyani]] in the [[e:telangana|Telangana]] region. As [[e:chalukya-dynasty|Chalukya]] power declined, [[e:prola-ii|Prola II]] and then [[e:rudradeva-kakatiya|Rudradeva]] asserted independence; Rudradeva declared [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] around 1163, built the Thousand Pillar Temple at [[e:hanamkonda|Hanamkonda]] and laid out a new capital at [[e:warangal|Orugallu]] (Warangal).
kakatiya-dynasty.r: [[e:ganapati-kakatiya|Ganapatideva]] united most [[e:telugu-language|Telugu]]-speaking lands and encouraged trade through the port of [[e:motupalli|Motupalli]]. His daughter Rudramadevi ruled as one of the few reigning queens of medieval [[e:india|India]], praised by [[e:marco-polo|Marco Polo]]. The kingdom built large irrigation tanks such as [[e:ramappa-temple|Ramappa]] and [[e:pakhal-lake|Pakhal]], and the Ramappa temple is now a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]]. [[e:nayaka|Nayaka]] military chiefs held land in return for service.
kakatiya-dynasty.e: The [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]] attacked [[e:warangal|Warangal]] repeatedly from 1309. In 1323 an army under [[e:muhammad-bin-tughluq|Ulugh Khan]], the future Muhammad bin Tughluq, captured the city and took [[e:prataparudra-kakatiya|Prataparudra]] prisoner. Former Kakatiya [[e:nayaka|Nayakas]] soon led a revolt, founding the [[s:musunuri-nayaks|Musunuri Nayaks]] and [[s:recherla-nayakas|Recherla Nayakas]].

kalsia-state.t: A Sikh princely state on the Punjab–Haryana border with its capital at Chhachhrauli, founded by a sardar of the Karorsinghia misl.
kalsia-state.o: [[e:gurbakhsh-singh-of-kalsia|Gurbakhsh Singh]], a Sandhu Jat of the village of Kalsia near [[e:lahore|Lahore]] and a member of the [[e:karorsinghia-misl|Karorsinghia]] misl, took territory south of the [[e:sutlej-river|Sutlej]] around 1760. His son [[e:jodh-singh-of-kalsia|Jodh Singh]] enlarged the holding, and the family made [[e:chhachhrauli|Chhachhrauli]] its seat.
kalsia-state.r: Kalsia entered British protection with the other [[e:cis-sutlej-states|Cis-Sutlej states]] in 1809. It was a small Sikh-ruled state with a mixed [[e:sikhism|Sikh]], [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] and Muslim population, ruled by a Raja and supervised through the [[e:punjab-states-agency|Punjab States Agency]].
kalsia-state.e: [[e:ravi-sher-singh|Ravi Sher Singh]] acceded to [[e:india|India]] in 1947, and in 1948 Kalsia was merged into the [[s:patiala-and-east-punjab-states-union|Patiala and East Punjab States Union]]. Its former lands are in [[e:yamunanagar-district|Yamunanagar district]] of [[e:haryana|Haryana]].

kingdom-of-kaffa.t: A forested kingdom of south-western Ethiopia, often linked with the origin of coffee, that kept its independence until 1897.
kingdom-of-kaffa.o: According to tradition the Kingdom of [[s:theodosia|Kaffa]] was founded around 1390 by the Minjo dynasty, which united the Kafa-speaking clans of the highland forests south of the [[e:gojeb-river|Gojeb]] river. It later absorbed the remnants of the [[s:kingdom-of-ennarea|Kingdom of Ennarea]], whose rulers fled south in the 18th century, and expanded over neighbouring peoples.
kingdom-of-kaffa.r: The king, or tato, was a sacred ruler secluded from his subjects and advised by a council of seven great officials. The kingdom was defended by deep ditches and fortified gates. [[s:theodosia|Kaffa]] exported [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]], civet, [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]], [[e:spice-trade|spices]] and slaves, and its religion blended traditional beliefs with Christian elements. The highland province gave its name, by some accounts, to coffee.
kingdom-of-kaffa.e: In 1897 [[e:menelik-ii|Menelik II's]] armies conquered [[s:theodosia|Kaffa]] after a long resistance, and its last king, [[e:gaki-sherocho|Gaki Sherocho]], was taken captive. War, famine and [[e:slave-raiding|slave raiding]] devastated the population, and the kingdom became a province of the [[s:ethiopian-empire|Ethiopian Empire]]. The [[e:kafa-zone|Kafa Zone]] preserves the name.

kingdom-of-bulgaria.t: Bulgarian tsardom that fought on the losing side of three wars in search of Macedonia and Thrace, before its monarchy was abolished under Soviet influence.
kingdom-of-bulgaria.o: On 5 October 1908 Prince Ferdinand of the [[s:principality-of-bulgaria|Principality of Bulgaria]] proclaimed independence from the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]] and took the title of tsar. [[s:bulgaria|Bulgaria]] joined the [[e:balkan-league|Balkan League]] and won the [[e:first-balkan-war|First Balkan War]] in 1912, but its attack on [[s:serbia|Serbia]] and [[e:greece|Greece]] in 1913 led to defeat in the [[e:second-balkan-war|Second Balkan War]] and loss of most of its gains.
kingdom-of-bulgaria.r: Hoping to win [[e:macedonia-region|Macedonia]], [[s:bulgaria|Bulgaria]] joined the [[e:central-powers|Central Powers]] in 1915; defeat in 1918 brought Ferdinand's abdication in favour of [[e:boris-iii-of-bulgaria|Boris III]] and the harsh [[e:treaty-of-neuilly-sur-seine|Treaty of Neuilly]]. [[e:aleksandar-stamboliyski|Aleksandar Stamboliyski's]] agrarian government was overthrown in 1923, and Boris ruled personally from 1935. As an [[e:axis-powers|Axis]] ally from 1941 [[e:bulgaria|Bulgaria]] occupied [[e:vardar-macedonia|Yugoslav Macedonia]] and [[e:thrace|Thrace]]; [[e:jews|Jews]] of the old kingdom were saved from [[e:deportation|deportation]] in 1943.
kingdom-of-bulgaria.e: After [[e:boris-iii-of-bulgaria|Boris]] died in 1943, the Soviet army entered [[s:bulgaria|Bulgaria]] in September 1944 and the communist-led [[e:fatherland-front-bulgaria|Fatherland Front]] seized power. A referendum in 1946 abolished the monarchy, and the boy king [[e:simeon-saxe-coburg-gotha|Simeon II]] went into exile, leading to the [[s:peoples-republic-of-bulgaria|People's Republic of Bulgaria]].

kingdom-of-lalitpur.t: The Malla kingdom of Patan in the Kathmandu Valley, whose Durbar Square is among the finest groups of Newar temples and palaces.
kingdom-of-lalitpur.o: [[e:lalitpur-nepal|Patan]], an ancient Buddhist city long dominated by its own nobles, was brought under the [[e:kathmandu|Kathmandu]] king [[e:shiva-simha-malla|Shiva Simha Malla]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-kantipur|Kingdom of Kantipur]], who around 1597 placed it under his son Hariharasimha. Hariharasimha's son [[e:siddhi-narasimha-malla|Siddhi Narasimha Malla]] ruled it as a fully separate kingdom from about 1620, alongside Kantipur and the [[s:kingdom-of-bhaktapur|Kingdom of Bhaktapur]].
kingdom-of-lalitpur.r: [[e:siddhi-narasimha-malla|Siddhi Narasimha Malla]], a devout ruler, built the stone [[e:krishna-mandir-patan|Krishna Mandir]]. His son [[e:shrinivasa-malla|Shrinivasa Malla]] added to the palace complex. [[e:lalitpur-nepal|Patan]] was known for Buddhist monasteries and metalwork, and its nobles were powerful, often deposing kings. The city competed with its neighbours for the trade with [[s:tibet-1912-1951|Tibet]].
kingdom-of-lalitpur.e: [[e:prithvi-narayan-shah|Prithvi Narayan Shah]] of the [[s:gorkha-kingdom|Gorkha Kingdom]] captured [[e:lalitpur-nepal|Patan]] in 1768, shortly after [[e:kathmandu|Kathmandu]], and its last ruler [[e:tej-narsingh-malla|Tej Narsingh Malla]] fled to [[e:bhaktapur|Bhaktapur]]. Patan became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Kingdom of Nepal]], and its [[e:patan-durbar-square|Durbar Square]] is a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]].

karamanids.t: The most powerful Turkish beylik of Anatolia after the Ottomans, centred on Karaman and Konya and their chief rival for two centuries.
karamanids.o: The Karamanids took their name from [[e:karaman-bey|Karaman Bey]], son of Nure [[e:sufism|Sufi]], a [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] leader in the [[e:taurus-mountains|Taurus]] mountains. Around 1250 they rose against the weakened [[s:sultanate-of-rum|Sultanate of Rum]], and [[e:karaman|Karaman's]] son [[e:karamanoglu-mehmed-bey|Mehmed Bey]] briefly occupied [[e:konya|Konya]] in 1277, where he reportedly decreed that Turkish alone be used in government.
karamanids.r: The Karamanids held the old Seljuk heartland, including [[e:karaman|Larende]] (Karaman) and later [[e:konya|Konya]], and saw themselves as heirs of the [[e:seljuk-empire|Seljuks]]. They allied with [[e:venice|Venice]], the [[e:mamluk|Mamluks]] and the [[s:aq-qoyunlu|Aq Qoyunlu]] against the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]]. [[e:alaeddin-bey|Alaeddin Bey]] was defeated and executed by [[e:bayezid-i|Bayezid I]] in 1397, but [[e:timur|Timur]] restored the dynasty in 1402. They built mosques and [[e:madrasa|madrasas]], such as the [[e:aktekke-mosque|Ak Tekke]] and [[e:hatuniye-madrasa|Hatuniye]] in Karaman.
karamanids.e: [[e:mehmed-ii|Mehmed II]] conquered most of the [[e:beylik|beylik]] in 1468, and the last Karamanid claimants were defeated by the 1480s; the region became the Ottoman province of [[e:karaman|Karaman]].

kingdom-of-fermanagh.t: The Maguire lordship around Lough Erne, a Gaelic lordship of islands and churches whose last chief joined the Flight of the Earls.
kingdom-of-fermanagh.o: The [[e:maguire-dynasty|Maguires]] rose in [[e:county-fermanagh|Fermanagh]] in the 13th century, with [[e:donn-carrach-maguire|Donn Carrach Maguire]], who died in 1302, counted as their first king from about 1264. They displaced earlier rulers and became [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[e:o-neill-dynasty|O'Neills]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-tir-eoghain|Kingdom of Tir Eoghain]].
kingdom-of-fermanagh.r: [[e:county-fermanagh|Fermanagh]] was organised around [[e:lough-erne|Lough Erne]], with islands, crannogs and monasteries such as [[e:devenish-island|Devenish]]. The [[e:maguire-dynasty|Maguires]] built [[e:enniskillen-castle|Enniskillen Castle]] in the 15th century. Their learned families compiled the [[e:annals-of-ulster|Annals of Ulster]] on [[e:belle-isle-fermanagh|Belle Isle]] under [[e:cathal-mac-maghnusa|Cathal Mac Maghnusa]]. Their economy rested on [[e:cattle|cattle]] and fishing.
kingdom-of-fermanagh.e: [[e:hugh-maguire-lord-of-fermanagh|Hugh Maguire]] fought with [[e:hugh-oneill-earl-of-tyrone|Hugh O'Neill]] in the [[e:nine-years-war-ireland|Nine Years' War]] and died in 1600. His brother [[e:cu-chonnacht-maguire|Cuchonnacht]] left with the Flight of the Earls in 1607. [[e:county-fermanagh|Fermanagh]] was then planted with English and Scottish settlers, and [[e:enniskillen|Enniskillen]] became a Protestant garrison town.

kingdom-of-butua.t: The Torwa kingdom centred on Khami, heir to Great Zimbabwe in the south-west of the plateau and builder of richly decorated stone platforms.
kingdom-of-butua.o: Butua arose in the mid-15th century as the [[s:kingdom-of-zimbabwe|Kingdom of Zimbabwe]] declined, when the [[e:torwa-dynasty|Torwa dynasty]] took control of the south-western plateau around modern [[e:bulawayo|Bulawayo]]. Its capital at [[e:khami|Khami]] continued the [[e:great-zimbabwe|Great Zimbabwe]] building tradition, and the kingdom controlled gold-bearing lands and rich [[e:cattle|cattle]] pastures.
kingdom-of-butua.r: [[e:khami|Khami]] was built on terraced stone platforms faced with chequered and herringbone patterns, a style later seen at [[e:danangombe|Danangombe]] and [[e:naletale|Naletale]]. Kings drew wealth from [[e:cattle|cattle]] and gold, trading with the Portuguese and [[e:swahili|Swahili]] through the [[e:mutapa-empire|Mutapa]] lands and the coast. Portuguese sources describe Butua as a rich gold country but give few details of its rulers or government.
kingdom-of-butua.e: In the mid-17th century a succession dispute brought in Portuguese allies and [[e:khami|Khami]] was burnt. In the 1680s [[e:changamire-dombo|Changamire Dombo]], a former [[e:mutapa-empire|Mutapa]] herder-general, overthrew the [[e:torwa-dynasty|Torwa]] and founded the [[e:rozvi-empire|Rozvi]] state on the same lands.

kenmu-restoration.t: Emperor Go-Daigo's brief attempt to restore direct imperial rule in Japan after the fall of the Kamakura shogunate.
kenmu-restoration.o: [[e:emperor-go-daigo|Emperor Go-Daigo]] plotted against the [[e:hojo-clan|Hojo]] regents for years and was exiled to the Oki islands, but he escaped. When the warlords [[e:ashikaga-takauji|Ashikaga Takauji]] and [[e:nitta-yoshisada|Nitta Yoshisada]] turned against the [[e:shogun|shogunate]] and destroyed it in 1333, Go-Daigo returned to [[e:kyoto|Kyoto]] to rule in person, naming his era Kenmu in 1334.
kenmu-restoration.r: [[e:emperor-go-daigo|Go-Daigo]] abolished the office of regent and sought to govern through new offices such as the Records Office and a court for rewards. Yet he favoured courtiers over warriors in distributing confiscated lands, and the new regime proved slow and confused, as satirised in the Nijo-gawara lampoons posted in the capital.
kenmu-restoration.e: In 1335 Takauji went east to suppress a [[e:hojo-clan|Hojo]] revolt and then broke with the emperor. He defeated [[e:kusunoki-masashige|Kusunoki Masashige]] at [[e:battle-of-minatogawa|Minatogawa]] in 1336, installed a rival emperor and founded the [[s:ashikaga-shogunate|Ashikaga shogunate]], while [[e:emperor-go-daigo|Go-Daigo]] fled to [[e:yoshino-nara|Yoshino]] to found the [[s:southern-court|Southern Court]].

kingdom-of-lotharingia.t: Northern share of Middle Francia, named after its king Lothair II, whose name survives in Lorraine.
kingdom-of-lotharingia.o: At the [[e:treaty-of-prum|Treaty of Prüm]] in 855 [[e:lothair-i|Lothair I]] left the northern part of [[s:middle-francia|Middle Francia]], from [[e:frisia|Frisia]] through the [[e:low-countries|Low Countries]] and the [[e:rhineland|Rhineland]] to the [[e:vosges|Vosges]], to his son [[e:lothair-ii|Lothair II]]. The kingdom took its name from him as the realm of Lothair.
kingdom-of-lotharingia.r: It held the old Carolingian heartland around [[s:free-imperial-city-of-aachen|Aachen]], [[e:metz|Metz]], [[e:trier|Trier]] and [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]], with wealthy abbeys and episcopal cities. [[e:lothair-ii|Lothair II's]] reign was dominated by his attempt to divorce his childless wife [[e:teutberga|Teutberga]] and marry [[e:waldrada|Waldrada]], which Pope Nicholas I blocked, leaving him without a legitimate heir.
kingdom-of-lotharingia.e: After [[e:lothair-ii|Lothair II]] died in 869 his uncles divided the kingdom at [[e:treaty-of-meerssen|Meerssen]] in 870, and in 880 all of it passed to [[s:east-francia|East Francia]]. [[e:arnulf-of-carinthia|Arnulf of Carinthia]] made his son [[e:zwentibold|Zwentibold]] king in 895, but he was killed in 900, and the land became the [[s:duchy-of-lotharingia|Duchy of Lotharingia]].

kaminaljuyu.t: The great highland centre of the Valley of Guatemala, which controlled obsidian and jade routes and later had close ties with Teotihuacan.
kaminaljuyu.o: Settled by about 800 BCE in what is now [[e:guatemala-city|Guatemala City]], Kaminaljuyu grew rich in the [[e:late-preclassic|Late Preclassic]] period from irrigated farming, using canals fed by Lake Miraflores, and from control of the nearby [[e:el-chayal|El Chayal]] obsidian source. In the Late Preclassic it became a large centre of earthen platform mounds, eventually numbering some 200.
kaminaljuyu.r: Preclassic rulers were buried in elaborate tombs within earthen platforms, and carved monuments show an early writing system related to the southern Maya and [[e:epi-olmec-culture|Epi-Olmec]] traditions. In the Early Classic, around 400 CE, buildings in the talud-tablero style and Teotihuacan-style pottery show strong links with [[s:teotihuacan|Teotihuacan]], whether through alliance, trade or settlement.
kaminaljuyu.e: Kaminaljuyu declined in the [[e:late-classic-period|Late Classic]] and was largely abandoned by about 900 CE. Most of its mounds have been destroyed by the growth of [[e:guatemala-city|Guatemala City]], but it remains essential for understanding highland Maya origins.

kingdom-of-jiujiang.t: The Huai River kingdom of Ying Bu, the tattooed convict turned general, whose defection from Xiang Yu to Liu Bang in 204 BCE helped decide the Chu-Han war.
kingdom-of-jiujiang.o: [[e:ying-bu|Ying Bu]], also called Qing Bu after the tattoo that marked him as a convict, led a band of escaped labourers in the rising against the [[s:qin-dynasty|Qin dynasty]] and became one of [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu's]] fiercest generals. In 206 BCE Xiang Yu made him King of Jiujiang, with his capital at Lu (near Lu'an, Anhui).
kingdom-of-jiujiang.r: Jiujiang was [[e:ying-bu|Ying Bu's]] personal military domain on the [[e:huai-river|Huai River]], covering the old Jiujiang commandery. When [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]] demanded troops, Ying Bu sent only token forces and became estranged from his overlord.
kingdom-of-jiujiang.e: Persuaded by [[e:liu-bang|Liu Bang's]] envoy [[e:sui-dynasty|Sui]] He, [[e:ying-bu|Ying Bu]] defected in 204 BCE; Chu troops overran Jiujiang and he fled to Liu Bang. In 203 BCE he was made King of [[s:wu-ten-kingdoms|Huainan]] over much the same land, but he rebelled against the [[s:han-dynasty|Han Dynasty]] in 196 BCE and was killed.

kingdom-of-porto-novo.t: A Gun kingdom on the lagoon coast of Benin, rival of Dahomey, whose kings sought French protection and whose capital became the capital of French Dahomey.
kingdom-of-porto-novo.o: Tradition holds that [[e:te-agbanlin|Te Agbanlin]], a prince of the [[s:kingdom-of-allada|Kingdom of Allada]], founded the kingdom around 1688 at Hogbonu on the coastal lagoon, among [[e:yoruba|Yoruba]] communities who called it Ajashe. Portuguese traders named the place [[e:porto-novo|Porto-Novo]], and the kingdom grew as a port for the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|Atlantic trade]], often under pressure from the [[s:oyo-empire|Oyo Empire]] and later the [[s:kingdom-of-dahomey|Kingdom of Dahomey]].
kingdom-of-porto-novo.r: Kings, chosen in rotation among royal branches, ruled with ministers and nobles in a court shaped by [[s:kingdom-of-allada|Allada]] traditions and by [[e:yoruba|Yoruba]] neighbours. The [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]] was the mainstay until the mid-19th century, when [[e:palm-oil|palm oil]] took over. The population mixed Gun, Yoruba and returning [[e:agudas|Afro-Brazilians]], who brought [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]], [[e:islam|Islam]] and Brazilian-style architecture.
kingdom-of-porto-novo.e: King Soji accepted a French [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] in 1863, and [[e:toffa-i|Toffa]] renewed it in 1882 as protection against [[s:kingdom-of-dahomey|Dahomey]]. [[e:porto-novo|Porto-Novo]] became the capital of [[s:french-dahomey|French Dahomey]], and after Toffa's death in 1908 the French ended the monarchy's political role. It remains the official capital of [[e:benin-empire|Benin]].

keladi-nayaka-kingdom.t: A Kannada kingdom of the western Ghats ruled from Ikkeri and Bednore, famous for its pepper trade and for Queen Chennamma's defiance of Aurangzeb.
keladi-nayaka-kingdom.o: The [[e:keladi-nayakas|Keladi Nayakas]] began as local chiefs at [[e:keladi|Keladi]] in the [[e:malnad|Malnad]] hills, serving the [[s:vijayanagara-empire|Vijayanagara Empire]] as governors from around 1499. After Vijayanagara's defeat at [[e:battle-of-talikota|Talikota]] in 1565 they became effectively independent, moving their capital to [[e:ikkeri|Ikkeri]] and later, around 1639, to [[e:bednur|Bidanur]] (Bednore).
keladi-nayaka-kingdom.r: [[e:shivappa-nayaka|Shivappa Nayaka]], the greatest ruler, introduced a celebrated land revenue system, the shist, and expanded the kingdom to the coast of [[e:kanara|Kanara]], driving the Portuguese from several ports. The kingdom profited from [[e:pepper|pepper]] and [[e:rice|rice]] exports. [[e:keladi-chennamma|Keladi Chennamma]], who ruled from 1671, sheltered [[e:shivaji|Shivaji's]] son [[e:rajaram-i|Rajaram]] from the [[s:mughal-empire|Mughal Empire]]. The [[e:aghoreshwara-temple|Aghoreshwara temple]] at [[e:ikkeri|Ikkeri]] shows the dynasty's patronage.
keladi-nayaka-kingdom.e: [[e:hyder-ali|Hyder Ali]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-mysore-1399-1799|Kingdom of Mysore]] conquered [[e:bednur|Bednore]] in 1763, seizing its treasury, and renamed it Haidarnagar. The territory remained part of Mysore and later [[s:british-raj|British India]].

kara-del.t: A Mongol-ruled oasis kingdom at Hami, gateway between Ming China and Central Asia, which fell under the control of Turfan in the early 16th century.
kara-del.o: After the fall of the [[s:yuan-dynasty|Yuan Dynasty]], a branch of the [[e:genghisid-principle|Chinggisid]] family descended from Chagatai held the oasis of [[e:hami|Hami]] (Kumul) at the eastern end of the Tarim routes. Its prince Gunashiri sent tribute to the [[s:ming-empire|Ming Empire]] from the 1380s, and in 1404 the [[e:ming-empire|Ming]] recognised his successor [[e:engke-temur|Engke Temür]] as Prince of Zhongshun and soon set up the Hami Guard.
kara-del.r: Kara Del controlled the road between the [[e:gansu-corridor|Hexi Corridor]] and [[e:turfan|Turfan]], and its rulers lived by taxing caravans and by the tribute trade with [[e:china|China]]. Its population included [[e:uyghurs|Uyghurs]], [[e:mongols|Mongols]] and Hui; [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] was giving way to [[e:islam|Islam]]. The [[e:ming-empire|Ming]] treated it as the key outpost of its western frontier system.
kara-del.e: From the 1470s the Muslim rulers of [[e:turfan|Turfan]], descendants of the khans of [[s:moghulistan|Moghulistan]], repeatedly seized [[e:hami|Hami]], and [[e:ming-empire|Ming]] attempts to restore its princes failed. In 1513 Hami submitted to [[e:mansur-khan|Mansur Khan]] of Turfan, and the kingdom ended. [[e:islam|Islam]] became the dominant faith of the oasis.

kingdom-of-chimor.t: The largest kingdom of the Andean coast before the Incas, ruled from the vast adobe city of Chan Chan and stretching some 1,000 km along northern Peru.
kingdom-of-chimor.o: Chimor arose around 900 in the [[s:moche|Moche]] valley, where the Moche had once ruled. According to a legend recorded by the Spanish, its founder [[e:tacaynamo|Tacaynamo]] came by sea and established a dynasty at [[e:chan-chan|Chan Chan]]. Later rulers expanded by conquest, and [[e:nancen-pinco|Ñancen Pinco]] extended the kingdom over neighbouring valleys.
kingdom-of-chimor.r: The Chimú kings ruled from [[e:chan-chan|Chan Chan]], the largest adobe city in the [[e:americas|Americas]], with walled palace compounds called ciudadelas that each served a ruler in life and as his tomb after death. The state managed extensive irrigation canals, including one linking the [[e:chicama-valley|Chicama]] and [[s:moche|Moche]] valleys. Chimú craftsmen excelled in gold and [[e:silver|silver]] work and black burnished pottery. Around 1375 Chimor conquered the lands of the [[s:sican|Sicán]], and under [[e:minchancaman|Minchancaman]] it reached as far as [[e:tumbes|Tumbes]].
kingdom-of-chimor.e: Around 1470 the [[e:inca-empire|Incas]] under [[e:tupac-inca-yupanqui|Túpac Inca Yupanqui]] conquered Chimor, captured [[e:minchancaman|Minchancaman]] and moved its craftsmen to [[e:cusco|Cusco]]. [[e:chan-chan|Chan Chan]] was later looted for gold by the Spanish. It became a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]] in 1986.

kingdom-of-gisaka.t: An eastern rival of the Kingdom of Rwanda, ruled by its own dynasty until Rwanda annexed it in the mid-19th century.
kingdom-of-gisaka.o: Gisaka occupied the lands of south-eastern [[s:kingdom-of-rwanda|Rwanda]] near the [[e:kagera-river|Kagera river]]. Its rulers belonged to the Bagesera clan, and court traditions present it as one of the older kingdoms of the region, already established when the [[e:nyiginya-dynasty|Nyiginya dynasty]] of the Kingdom of Rwanda was still small.
kingdom-of-gisaka.r: Gisaka was a [[e:cattle|cattle]]-keeping and farming kingdom with [[e:sacred-kingship|sacred kingship]], royal drums and rituals similar to those of [[s:kingdom-of-rwanda|Rwanda]]. For generations it fought Rwanda over borderlands and cattle, at times defeating its rival in the 17th and 18th centuries, according to Rwandan court traditions.
kingdom-of-gisaka.e: [[s:kingdom-of-rwanda|Rwanda]] conquered and annexed Gisaka around 1852 under Mwami [[e:mutara-ii-rwogera|Mutara II Rwogera]]. In the colonial period the British briefly claimed the region in 1919 before it returned to [[s:ruanda-urundi|Belgian Ruanda-Urundi]]. Gisaka's identity survived as a region of eastern Rwanda.

kingdom-of-coorg.t: A hill kingdom of the Western Ghats ruled by the Haleri Rajas until the British annexed it in 1834.
kingdom-of-coorg.o: Around 1600 a member of the Haleri family, a [[e:lingayatism|Lingayat]] house related to the [[e:keladi-nayakas|Nayakas of Ikkeri]] ([[e:keladi|Keladi]]), established himself in [[e:kodagu|Kodagu]], the hilly country at the source of the Kaveri. His successors built a kingdom with its capital at [[e:madikeri|Madikeri]] (Mercara).
kingdom-of-coorg.r: The Rajas ruled the warrior [[e:kodava-people|Kodava]] landholders through their own officials. Coorg resisted [[e:hyder-ali|Hyder Ali]] and [[e:tipu-sultan|Tipu Sultan of Mysore]], who occupied it at intervals from the 1770s. [[e:dodda-vira-rajendra|Dodda Vira Rajendra]] regained the throne and allied with the British in the [[e:anglo-mysore-wars|Anglo-Mysore wars]]. The economy rested on [[e:rice|rice]] and forest produce; [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]] arrived later.
kingdom-of-coorg.e: After [[e:chikka-vira-rajendra|Chikka Vira Rajendra]] quarrelled with the Company, a British force deposed him in 1834 and annexed Coorg. It became a province of [[s:british-raj|British India]], then a state of [[e:india|India]] until 1956, when it joined [[s:mysore-state|Mysore State]], now [[e:karnataka|Karnataka]].

kingdom-of-banda.t: Kingdom of the Nafana people in west-central Ghana, near the old trading town of Begho.
kingdom-of-banda.o: Known mainly from oral tradition. Banda was established by the [[e:nafana-people|Nafana people]] in the hills north-west of the [[s:bono-state|Bono State]], close to [[e:begho|Begho]], a [[e:mande-peoples|Mande]] trading town of the gold and kola routes. It took shape around the 17th century.
kingdom-of-banda.r: Banda's ruler governed with clan chiefs over farming villages, while [[e:wangara|Dyula]] traders linked the area to the [[e:niger-bend|Niger bend]]. From the 18th century Banda was a tributary of the [[s:ashanti-empire|Ashanti Empire]], sending troops and tribute, and it suffered from [[e:ashanti-empire|Ashanti's]] wars against [[s:kingdom-of-gyaman|Gyaman]].
kingdom-of-banda.e: In the 1890s Banda was disrupted by the armies of [[e:samori-ture|Samori Ture]], then came under British rule in the [[s:northern-territories-of-the-gold-coast|Northern Territories of the Gold Coast]]. It remains a traditional area in [[e:ghana|Ghana's]] [[e:bono-region|Bono Region]].

kingdom-of-soloi.t: Cypriot kingdom on Morphou Bay, said to have taken its name from the Athenian lawgiver Solon, who advised its king.
kingdom-of-soloi.o: Soloi lay on the bay of [[e:morphou|Morphou]] in north-western [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]], near the [[e:copper|copper]] mines of [[e:skouriotissa|Skouriotissa]]. Founded in the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]], it was a city-kingdom by the 7th century BCE. [[e:plutarch|Plutarch]] tells that King [[e:philocyprus|Philocyprus]] moved the city to a better site on [[e:solon|Solon's]] advice and named it after him.
kingdom-of-soloi.r: Soloi grew rich on [[e:copper|copper]] and farmland. Its king [[e:aristocyprus|Aristocyprus]] fell fighting the [[e:persians|Persians]] at [[e:salamis-cyprus|Salamis]] in 497 BCE, after which Soloi endured a five-month siege. The palace of [[e:palace-of-vouni|Vouni]] on a nearby hill, built in the 5th century BCE, may have been used to watch over Soloi. King Pasicrates supported Alexander and staged a dramatic contest for him at [[s:tyre|Tyre]] in 331 BCE.
kingdom-of-soloi.e: Its last king, [[e:eunostos-of-soloi|Eunostos]], married Eirene, daughter of [[e:ptolemy-i-soter|Ptolemy I]], and the kingdom was absorbed into Ptolemaic [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]] c. 312 BCE. Soloi remained a city into Roman and early Christian times.

kingdom-of-gianyar.t: Central Balinese kingdom that chose Dutch protection in 1900 and whose princes at Ubud fostered Bali's modern arts.
kingdom-of-gianyar.o: Gianyar was founded around 1770 by a branch of the Dewa Manggis family, nobles linked to the senior court of the [[s:kingdom-of-klungkung|Kingdom of Klungkung]], who established a palace at Gianyar in the fertile valleys between the [[e:ayung-river|Ayung]] and Pakerisan rivers. The kingdom expanded through the 18th and 19th centuries at the expense of its neighbours.
kingdom-of-gianyar.r: Gianyar was densely populated and rich in irrigated [[e:rice|rice]] land, temples and craftsmen. Power was shared with branch lineages such as the princes of [[e:ubud|Ubud]] and Peliatan. In the 1880s it was shattered by wars with [[s:kingdom-of-klungkung|Klungkung]] and other courts, and its raja was briefly held captive by Klungkung before the kingdom was restored.
kingdom-of-gianyar.e: Seeking security, Gianyar accepted [[e:dutch|Dutch]] protection in 1900, retaining its dynasty as regents. Under colonial rule [[e:ubud|Ubud]] became the centre of a famous artistic revival, and Gianyar royals, including [[e:ide-anak-agung-gde-agung|Ide Anak Agung Gde Agung]], became Indonesian statesmen. It is now a regency of [[e:bali|Bali]].

komancza-republic.t: A tiny Ukrainian-oriented republic of Lemko villages in the Carpathians, which lasted from November 1918 to January 1919.
komancza-republic.o: When Austro-Hungarian rule collapsed in November 1918, Ukrainian-minded [[e:lemkos|Lemkos]] in about thirty villages around Komancza, in the eastern Lemko region of [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Galicia]], set up their own commissariat. Unlike the pro-Russian [[s:lemko-rusyn-republic|Lemko-Rusyn Republic]] further west, they aimed to join the [[s:west-ukrainian-peoples-republic|West Ukrainian People's Republic]].
komancza-republic.r: The republic was a local self-government led by a council and the Greek Catholic priest [[e:pantaleimon-shpylka|Pantaleimon Shpylka]], with a small militia to keep order and guard against Polish units. It had little territory and no resources of its own, and it existed mainly to hold the area until it could be united with the Ukrainian state.
komancza-republic.e: In January 1919 Polish troops entered the area during the [[e:polish-ukrainian-war|Polish-Ukrainian War]] and dissolved the republic. Its villages became part of the [[s:second-polish-republic|Second Polish Republic]], and their [[e:lemkos|Lemko]] inhabitants were deported in 1947.

kokura-domain.t: The domain guarding the Kanmon Straits in northern Kyushu, held by the Hosokawa and then by the Ogasawara, and defeated by Choshu in 1866.
kokura-domain.o: After [[e:battle-of-sekigahara|Sekigahara]], [[e:hosokawa-tadaoki|Hosokawa Tadaoki]] received [[e:buzen-province|Buzen]] province and built [[e:kokura|Kokura]] castle from 1602 on the southern shore of the [[e:kanmon-straits|Kanmon Straits]]. In 1632 the Hosokawa were moved to [[e:kumamoto|Kumamoto]], and [[e:ogasawara-tadazane|Ogasawara Tadazane]], a relative of the Tokugawa, took over Kokura with 150,000 koku.
kokura-domain.r: The [[e:ogasawara-clan|Ogasawara]], a hereditary [[e:vassal|vassal]] family, ruled until the end of the period with a mission to watch over the outside lords of [[e:kyushu|Kyushu]] and the sea route between [[e:honshu|Honshu]] and Kyushu. [[e:kokura|Kokura]] lay at the end of the [[e:nagasaki|Nagasaki]] road, where [[e:dutch|Dutch]] missions travelling to [[e:edo-tokyo|Edo]] crossed the straits to Honshu.
kokura-domain.e: In the second [[e:shogun|shogunate]] expedition against [[e:choshu-domain|Choshu]] in 1866, Choshu forces under [[e:takasugi-shinsaku|Takasugi Shinsaku]] crossed the straits; [[e:kokura|Kokura]] burned its castle and withdrew inland to Kawara. After abolition in 1871 the area became part of [[e:fukuoka-prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]].
