kazallu.t: An Amorite-era city-kingdom of northern Babylonia, an early rival of Babylon whose walls were torn down by Sumu-la-El.
kazallu.o: Kazallu lay in northern [[e:babylonia|Babylonia]], near [[e:marad|Marad]] and [[s:kish|Kish]]; its site has not been found. Under the [[s:neo-sumerian-empire|Neo-Sumerian Empire]] it was a province, and its governor Puzur-Numushda defied [[e:ibbi-sin|Ibbi-Sin]] in the last years of Ur. In the 19th century BCE it became the seat of an independent kingdom tied to the Amorite Mutiabal tribe.
kazallu.r: Kazallu is known mainly through the year names and inscriptions of its neighbours, which record wars and alliances with [[s:larsa|Larsa]], [[s:isin|Isin]], [[s:uruk|Uruk]] and the new Amorite dynasty of [[e:babylon|Babylon]]. Kings such as Yahzir-El briefly controlled the region, and the city's position on the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]] canals gave it influence over northern [[e:babylonia|Babylonia's]] grain lands. Its own institutions are almost undocumented.
kazallu.e: [[e:sumu-la-el|Sumu-la-El]] of [[e:babylon|Babylon]] defeated Kazallu and destroyed its walls in the early 19th century BCE, and it was absorbed by Babylon. Its Mutiabal population later rose against [[e:hammurabi|Hammurabi]], but by about 1800 BCE the kingdom had ceased to exist.

kingdom-of-kalinga.t: The ancient kingdom of the Odisha coast, whose bloody conquest by Ashoka in 261 BCE turned the Maurya emperor towards Buddhism.
kingdom-of-kalinga.o: [[e:kalinga|Kalinga]], the coastal plain between the [[e:mahanadi|Mahanadi]] and Godavari rivers, appears in the [[e:mahabharata|Mahabharata]] and in Buddhist texts, which name [[e:dantapura|Dantapura]] as an early capital. Its people controlled harbours facing the [[e:bay-of-bengal|Bay of Bengal]]. According to the later [[e:hathigumpha-inscription|Hathigumpha inscription]], a [[e:nanda-dynasty|Nanda]] king took a [[e:jainism|Jain]] image from Kalinga, which suggests a period of Magadhan control in the 4th century BCE.
kingdom-of-kalinga.r: [[e:kalinga|Kalinga's]] strength lay in maritime trade with [[s:sri-lanka|Sri Lanka]] and [[e:southeast-asia|Southeast Asia]], [[e:rice|rice]] farming in the [[e:mahanadi|Mahanadi]] delta and a large army; Greek sources reported that its king kept many [[e:war-elephant|war elephants]]. [[e:jainism|Jainism]] had a strong following there. Little is known of its rulers, and the government was probably a monarchy centred on [[e:tosali|Tosali]], near modern [[e:bhubaneswar|Bhubaneswar]].
kingdom-of-kalinga.e: Around 261 BCE the Maurya emperor [[e:ashoka|Ashoka]] conquered [[e:kalinga|Kalinga]]. His [[e:edicts-of-ashoka|Rock Edict XIII]] records 100,000 killed and 150,000 deported and expresses his remorse, a turning point in his commitment to dhamma. Kalinga regained independence after the [[e:maurya-empire|Mauryas]] under the [[s:mahameghavahana-dynasty|Mahameghavahana dynasty]].

kingdom-of-wuli.t: Mandinka kingdom of the upper Gambia river, visited by Mungo Park on his journey into the interior in 1795.
kingdom-of-wuli.o: Wuli was one of the [[e:mandinka|Mandinka]] kingdoms founded along the [[e:the-gambia|Gambia]] river as the influence of the [[s:mali-empire|Mali Empire]] spread westward. It occupied the north bank of the upper river and is traditionally dated to around the 16th century.
kingdom-of-wuli.r: The [[e:mansa|mansa]] of Wuli ruled from [[e:medina|Medina]] with a council of lineage heads and Muslim clerics. Wuli controlled [[e:caravan-trade|caravan routes]] between the [[e:the-gambia|Gambia]] and the upper [[e:senegal|Senegal]] and [[e:niger-river|Niger]], through which slaves, gold and cloth passed. [[e:mungo-park|Mungo Park]] stopped there in 1795, and the king gave him permission to continue east.
kingdom-of-wuli.e: In the 19th century Wuli was disrupted by wars between Muslim reformers and traditional rulers. The Anglo-French boundary agreement of 1889 divided the area, and Wuli became a district of the [[s:gambia-colony-and-protectorate|Gambia Colony and Protectorate]].

kingdom-of-carchemish.t: Neo-Hittite Carchemish, the leading Iron Age kingdom on the Euphrates, heir to Hittite royal tradition and famed for its sculpted walls.
kingdom-of-carchemish.o: When the [[s:hittite-empire|Hittite Empire]] fell c. 1180 BCE, the [[s:viceroyalty-of-carchemish|Viceroyalty of Carchemish]] survived, and King [[e:kuzi-teshub|Kuzi-Teshub]] took the title great king. His descendants and their successors ruled a kingdom astride the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]] crossing, in what is now the Turkish-Syrian border.
kingdom-of-carchemish.r: Kings of the house of Suhi, and later Astiru and the regent [[e:yariri|Yariri]], recorded their deeds in Luwian hieroglyphs on basalt reliefs lining [[e:processional-way|processional ways]], the Long Wall of Sculpture. Carchemish grew rich on river trade and textiles. [[e:british-museum|British Museum]] excavations from 1911, with [[e:leonard-woolley|Leonard Woolley]] and [[e:t-e-lawrence|T. E. Lawrence]], uncovered much of the city.
kingdom-of-carchemish.e: The kingdom paid tribute to the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]] from the 9th century BCE. In 717 BCE [[e:sargon-ii|Sargon II]] deposed King [[e:pisiri|Pisiri]] for plotting with [[s:kingdom-of-phrygia|Phrygia]] and turned Carchemish into a province. In 605 BCE the city saw [[e:nebuchadnezzar-ii|Nebuchadnezzar's]] victory over [[e:egypt|Egypt]].

kantoli.t: A Sumatran trading kingdom known only from Chinese records of its 5th- and 6th-century embassies, often seen as a forerunner of Srivijaya.
kantoli.o: Known only from Chinese dynastic histories, Kantoli sent envoys to the southern Chinese courts in 441, 455, 502, 518 and 563. Historians usually place it in southern [[e:sumatra|Sumatra]], around Jambi or [[e:palembang|Palembang]], though its exact site is unknown.
kantoli.r: Chinese texts describe a Buddhist king who exported [[e:cotton|cotton]] cloth, areca nut and aromatic woods. In 502 a king called [[e:gautama-subhadra|Gautama Subhadra]] sent tribute, followed by his son Vijayavarman. The embassies suggest a ruler eager for Chinese recognition to attract merchants to his port on the route between [[e:india|India]] and [[e:china|China]].
kantoli.e: Kantoli disappears from the records after 563. Its role as a Sumatran gateway to [[e:china|China]] passed to the [[s:melayu-kingdom|Melayu Kingdom]] and above all to [[e:srivijaya|Srivijaya]], which rose at [[e:palembang|Palembang]] in the late 7th century.

katyuri-kingdom.t: An early medieval kingdom of the Kumaon and Garhwal hills, builders of the temples of Jageshwar and Baijnath.
katyuri-kingdom.o: The Katyuris emerged in the central [[e:himalayas|Himalaya]], modern [[e:uttarakhand|Uttarakhand]], around the 7th or 8th century, perhaps after the decline of the [[s:kuninda-kingdom|Kuninda Kingdom]] and other hill states. Tradition places their first seat at [[e:joshimath|Joshimath]]; their capital Kartikeyapura is usually identified with [[e:baijnath-uttarakhand|Baijnath]] in the Katyur valley.
katyuri-kingdom.r: The dynasty is known from a handful of [[e:copper|copper]]-plate inscriptions of kings such as Lalitashuradeva, written in [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]], and from local tradition. The kings were [[e:shaivism|Shaivas]], and the temple groups at [[e:jageshwar|Jageshwar]] and [[e:baijnath-uttarakhand|Baijnath]] are associated with their rule. They controlled routes into [[s:tibet-1912-1951|Tibet]] and the pilgrimage centres of the upper [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges]].
katyuri-kingdom.e: From around the 11th century the kingdom fragmented into local principalities ruled by Katyuri branches. The [[s:kumaon-kingdom|Chand dynasty]] took over [[e:kumaon|Kumaon]], and the Parmar kings united [[e:garhwal|Garhwal]]. Katyuri chiefs survived as local rulers, notably at [[e:askot|Askot]].

kingdom-of-majorca.t: A Christian kingdom created after James I's conquest of Majorca, independent under its own dynasty from 1276 to 1344 and a realm of Aragon thereafter.
kingdom-of-majorca.o: [[e:james-i-of-aragon|James I of Aragon]] conquered [[e:mallorca|Majorca]] from the [[e:almohad-caliphate|Almohads]] in 1229, then [[s:ebusus|Ibiza]] in 1235, and established a separate kingdom. On his death in 1276 he left Majorca, [[e:roussillon|Roussillon]], [[e:cerdanya|Cerdanya]] and [[s:lordship-of-montpellier|Montpellier]] to his younger son [[e:james-ii-of-majorca|James II]], creating an independent dynasty.
kingdom-of-majorca.r: The kingdom was a [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]] trading state, with [[e:palma|Palma]] and [[e:perpignan|Perpignan]] as royal seats, merchant fleets reaching [[e:north-africa|North Africa]] and a famed school of cartographers who made the [[e:catalan-atlas|Catalan Atlas]]. [[e:ramon-llull|Ramon Llull]], philosopher and missionary, was its most famous son. Its kings were forced to accept [[e:vassal|vassalage]] to the [[s:crown-of-aragon|Crown of Aragon]].
kingdom-of-majorca.e: [[e:peter-iv-of-aragon|Peter IV of Aragon]] seized the kingdom in 1343-1344, and [[e:james-iii-of-majorca|James III]] was killed at [[e:battle-of-llucmajor|Llucmajor]] in 1349 trying to retake it. [[e:mallorca|Majorca]] remained a separate realm within the Crown until the [[e:nueva-planta-decrees|Nueva Planta]] decree of 1715.

kingdom-of-huahine.t: A kingdom of the Leeward Society Islands that defeated a French landing in 1846 and stayed independent until the 1890s.
kingdom-of-huahine.o: [[e:huahine|Huahine]], two islands joined by a narrow channel in the [[e:leeward-islands-society-islands|Leeward group]] of the Society Islands, was settled by [[e:polynesians|Polynesians]] perhaps a thousand years ago. Around Lake Fauna Nui at [[e:maeva|Maeva]], its chiefly families built one of the largest concentrations of marae in [[e:polynesia|Polynesia]]. By the 18th century the island and nearby [[e:maiao|Maiao]] were ruled by a single royal line.
kingdom-of-huahine.r: [[e:huahine|Huahine's]] ruling family was closely tied by marriage to the [[s:kingdom-of-tahiti|Kingdom of Tahiti]]; [[e:teriitaria-ii|Teriitaria II]], queen from 1815, was also a wife of [[e:pomare-ii|Pōmare II]]. [[e:james-cook|James Cook]] visited in 1769 and in 1777 left the traveller Mai, who had been to [[e:england|England]], settled there. The [[e:london-missionary-society|London Missionary Society]] arrived in 1818 and most islanders became Protestant. Islanders lived from breadfruit, taro, fishing and provisioning ships.
kingdom-of-huahine.e: In 1846 [[e:huahine|Huahine's]] warriors defeated French marines who tried to impose a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]], and the [[e:jarnac-convention|Jarnac Convention]] of 1847 recognised its independence. [[e:france|France]] proclaimed annexation of the [[e:leeward-islands-society-islands|Leeward Islands]] in 1888, completed on Huahine in 1895, and it is now part of [[s:french-polynesia|French Polynesia]].

kurume-domain.t: The Arima domain of Chikugo in northern Kyushu, known for its indigo kasuri cloth and a scholar lord who wrote on mathematics.
kurume-domain.o: After the Tanaka family who held [[e:chikugo-province|Chikugo]] died out, the [[e:shogun|shogunate]] divided the province, and in 1621 [[e:arima-toyouji|Arima Toyouji]], who had fought for [[e:tokugawa-ieyasu|Tokugawa Ieyasu]], received [[e:kurume|Kurume]] with about 210,000 koku.
kurume-domain.r: The Arima ruled until 1871 from [[e:kurume|Kurume]] castle on the [[e:chikugo-province|Chikugo]] river. Kurume kasuri, a dyed [[e:cotton|cotton]] fabric, became a famous product in the 19th century, and the domain promoted [[e:rice|rice]] and wax. In the 18th century [[e:arima-yoriyuki|Arima Yoriyuki]] published works on Japanese mathematics. Heavy taxes provoked a large peasant uprising in 1754. In the 1860s the Suitengu priest [[e:maki-izumi|Maki Izumi]] became a leading loyalist.
kurume-domain.e: [[e:kurume|Kurume]] joined the imperial side in 1868. Radical retainers involved in anti-government plots were purged in 1871, the year the domain was abolished; it became part of [[e:fukuoka-prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]].

kingdom-of-hanover.t: North German kingdom tied to the British crown until 1837, then ruled by its own kings until Prussia annexed it in 1866.
kingdom-of-hanover.o: The [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] raised the [[s:electorate-of-hanover|Electorate of Hanover]] to a kingdom in 1814, with [[e:george-iii|George III]] as king, and enlarged it with [[e:east-frisia|East Frisia]], [[e:hildesheim|Hildesheim]] and [[s:county-of-lingen|Lingen]]. It continued in personal union with [[s:kingdom-of-great-britain|Great Britain]] under George III, [[e:george-iv-of-the-united-kingdom|George IV]] and [[e:william-iv-of-the-united-kingdom|William IV]], governed by a [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]].
kingdom-of-hanover.r: When [[s:colony-of-victoria|Victoria]] became British queen in 1837, [[e:salic-law|Salic law]] excluded her and her uncle [[e:ernest-augustus-king-of-hanover|Ernest Augustus]] became King of [[e:hanover|Hanover]]. He revoked the liberal constitution of 1833, and seven [[e:gottingen|Göttingen]] professors who protested, including the [[e:brothers-grimm|Grimm brothers]], were dismissed. The kingdom was largely agrarian, though railways and the port of [[e:harburg-hamburg|Harburg]] developed. [[e:george-v-of-hanover|George V]], blind from youth, became king in 1851.
kingdom-of-hanover.e: [[e:george-v-of-hanover|George V]] sided with [[e:austria|Austria]] in 1866. His army won at [[e:battle-of-langensalza-1866|Langensalza]] but surrendered two days later. [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] annexed [[e:hanover|Hanover]] as a province, and the Guelph party long campaigned for restoration.

kingdom-of-illyria.t: Austrian crown land formed from the former French Illyrian Provinces, uniting Slovene and Adriatic lands under one title for three decades.
kingdom-of-illyria.o: When [[e:austria|Austria]] recovered [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] [[s:illyrian-provinces|Illyrian Provinces]], it kept the name and in 1816 created the [[s:illyrian-kingdom|Kingdom of Illyria]] as a crown land of the [[s:austrian-empire|Austrian Empire]]. It comprised [[e:carniola|Carniola]], [[e:carinthia|Carinthia]], [[s:county-of-gorizia|Gorizia and Gradisca]], [[s:histria|Istria]] and [[e:trieste|Trieste]], and for a few years Civil [[e:croatia|Croatia]] south of the [[e:sava|Sava]], which returned to [[e:hungary|Hungary]] in 1822.
kingdom-of-illyria.r: The kingdom was mainly an administrative label: it was divided into two [[e:governorate|governorates]], at [[e:ljubljana|Laibach]] and [[e:trieste|Trieste]], each run by Austrian officials under the system of [[e:klemens-von-metternich|Metternich]], with provincial estates of little power. Laibach hosted the congress of 1821 on revolutions in [[e:italy|Italy]]. Slovene cultural life grew, with the poet [[e:france-preseren|France Prešeren]] writing in Laibach in the 1830s and 1840s.
kingdom-of-illyria.e: After the revolutions of 1848, the 1849 constitution dissolved the kingdom into separate crown lands: [[e:carniola|Carniola]], [[e:carinthia|Carinthia]] and the [[e:austrian-littoral|Austrian Littoral]]. The emperor kept the title King of [[e:illyria|Illyria]] until 1918.

kingdom-of-thessalonica.t: Crusader kingdom created for Boniface of Montferrat after the Fourth Crusade, which lasted only twenty years before falling to Epirus.
kingdom-of-thessalonica.o: [[e:boniface-i-marquis-of-montferrat|Boniface of Montferrat]], leader of the [[e:fourth-crusade|Fourth Crusade]], lost the election for [[e:latin|Latin]] emperor in 1204 but received [[e:thessaloniki|Thessalonica]] and much of Macedonia and [[e:thessaly|Thessaly]]. He married Margaret of [[e:hungary|Hungary]], widow of [[e:isaac-ii-angelos|Isaac II]], and invaded central and southern [[e:greece|Greece]], granting fiefs such as the [[s:duchy-of-athens|Duchy of Athens]] and the [[s:marquisate-of-bodonitsa|Marquisate of Bodonitsa]] to his followers.
kingdom-of-thessalonica.r: The kingdom was ruled by [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] nobles from northern [[e:italy|Italy]] over a Greek population, under nominal homage to the [[s:latin-empire|Latin Empire]]. A [[e:latin|Latin]] archbishop replaced the [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] metropolitan. [[e:boniface-i-marquis-of-montferrat|Boniface]] was killed by the [[e:bulgarians|Bulgarians]] of [[e:kaloyan-of-bulgaria|Kaloyan]] in 1207, leaving his infant son Demetrius under a regency; the Lombard barons' revolt of 1208-1209 was suppressed by [[e:henry-of-flanders|Emperor Henry]].
kingdom-of-thessalonica.e: Weakened by internal divisions and Bulgarian attacks, the kingdom was gradually conquered by [[e:theodore-komnenos-doukas|Theodore Komnenos Doukas]] of [[e:epirus|Epirus]], who took [[e:thessaloniki|Thessalonica]] itself in 1224 and founded the [[s:empire-of-thessalonica|Empire of Thessalonica]]. The title survived among Western claimants.

kingdom-of-deira.t: The Anglian kingdom of the Yorkshire Wolds and York, whose boys in a Roman slave market are said to have inspired Pope Gregory's mission to the English.
kingdom-of-deira.o: Deira developed from Anglian settlement in east [[e:yorkshire|Yorkshire]], perhaps taking over a British territory whose name it kept. The [[e:anglo-saxon-chronicle|Anglo-Saxon Chronicle]] names [[e:aelle-of-deira|Aelle]] as its first king from 560. [[e:bede|Bede]] tells how [[e:pope-gregory-i|Gregory the Great]], seeing Deiran slave boys in [[e:rome|Rome]], punned that they were not [[e:angles|Angles]] but angels.
kingdom-of-deira.r: Deira's centre lay around [[e:york|York]] and the [[e:yorkshire-wolds|Wolds]]. [[e:edwin-of-northumbria|Edwin]], son of [[e:aelle-of-deira|Aelle]], ruled all [[s:kingdom-of-northumbria|Northumbria]] from 616, accepted baptism from [[e:paulinus-of-york|Paulinus]] at York in 627 and built the first church on the site of [[e:york-minster|York Minster]]. After his death in 633 Deira had its own kings again, including Oswine, killed on the orders of [[e:oswiu|Oswiu]] in 651.
kingdom-of-deira.e: Bernician kings repeatedly dominated Deira. Its sub-king [[e:oethelwald-of-deira|Oethelwald]], son of [[e:oswald-of-northumbria|Oswald]], supported [[e:penda-of-mercia|Penda]] against [[e:oswiu|Oswiu]] and disappeared after the [[e:battle-of-the-winwaed|Winwaed]] in 655; Oswiu's son [[e:alhfrith|Alhfrith]] then ruled Deira under his father. Deira became the southern half of the [[s:kingdom-of-northumbria|Kingdom of Northumbria]], its name surviving in later sources.

kingdom-of-the-iberians.t: The kingdom of the Georgian Bagratids in Tao-Klarjeti, a land of great monasteries whose rulers prepared the unification of Georgia.
kingdom-of-the-iberians.o: Early in the 9th century the [[e:bagrationi-dynasty|Bagratid]] prince Ashot I moved from [[s:kingdom-of-iberia|Kartli]] to the south-western borderland of [[e:klarjeti|Klarjeti]], where he rebuilt [[e:artanuji|Artanuji]] and the family won Byzantine titles. In 888 his descendant [[e:adarnase-iv-of-iberia|Adarnase IV]] took the title king of the [[e:iberians|Iberians]], restoring the royal title in [[s:georgia|Georgia]] after three centuries.
kingdom-of-the-iberians.r: Several [[e:bagrationi-dynasty|Bagratid]] branches shared rule over Tao, [[e:klarjeti|Klarjeti]] and [[e:shavsheti|Shavsheti]], with titles granted by the [[s:byzantine-empire|Byzantine Empire]]. Monks led by [[e:grigol-of-khandzta|Grigol of Khandzta]] founded monasteries, and great churches rose at [[e:oshki|Oshki]], [[e:ishkhani|Ishkhani]] and [[e:khakhuli-monastery|Khakhuli]], centres of Georgian learning. [[e:david-iii-kuropalates|David III Kouropalates]] of Tao made the region powerful and helped [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] against the rebel [[e:bardas-skleros|Bardas Skleros]].
kingdom-of-the-iberians.e: When [[e:david|David]] III died in 1000, [[e:basil-ii|Basil II]] annexed his lands of Tao to [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]]. The remaining [[e:bagrationi-dynasty|Bagratid]] holdings passed to [[e:bagrat-iii-of-georgia|Bagrat III]], who in 1008 united them with [[s:principality-of-abkhazia|Abkhazia]] and [[s:kingdom-of-iberia|Kartli]] in the [[s:kingdom-of-georgia|Kingdom of Georgia]].

kingdom-of-the-lombards.t: Germanic kingdom that ruled most of Italy from 568 until Charlemagne's conquest in 774, shaping its regions and its law.
kingdom-of-the-lombards.o: The [[e:lombards|Lombards]], a Germanic people settled in [[e:pannonia|Pannonia]], crossed into [[e:italy|Italy]] under [[e:alboin|King Alboin]] in 568, just after the Gothic Wars had exhausted the peninsula. They overran the north and much of the centre and south, took [[s:commune-of-pavia|Pavia]] in 572 after a long siege and made it their capital, leaving the [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]] with [[s:lordship-of-ravenna|Ravenna]], [[e:rome|Rome]] and the coasts.
kingdom-of-the-lombards.r: The king ruled with powerful dukes, some nearly independent, such as those of [[e:spoleto|Spoleto]] and [[e:benevento|Benevento]]. Under Queen [[e:theodelinda|Theodelinda]] the [[e:lombards|Lombards]] began to move from Arian to Catholic [[e:christianity|Christianity]]. Rothari issued a written law code, the [[e:edict-of-rothari|Edict of Rothari]], in 643. [[e:liutprand-king-of-the-lombards|Liutprand]] strengthened royal power and in 728 gave [[e:sutri|Sutri]] to the Pope, a step towards the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]]. Lombard art survives at [[e:cividale-del-friuli|Cividale]].
kingdom-of-the-lombards.e: When [[e:aistulf|Aistulf]] took [[s:lordship-of-ravenna|Ravenna]] in 751 and threatened [[e:rome|Rome]], the popes turned to the [[s:franks|Franks]]. [[e:pepin-the-short|Pepin the Short]] defeated Aistulf, and [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]] besieged [[s:commune-of-pavia|Pavia]] and captured King [[e:desiderius|Desiderius]] in 774, taking the title [[e:king-of-the-lombards|King of the Lombards]]. The region of [[e:lombardy|Lombardy]] keeps their name.

kalachuris-of-mahishmati.t: A short-lived but wide-ruling dynasty of western India whose silver coins circulated across the Deccan and whose era lasted for centuries.
kalachuris-of-mahishmati.o: The Early Kalachuris rose in the mid-6th century in [[e:malwa|Malwa]] and the northern [[e:deccan|Deccan]] as the [[s:gupta-empire|Gupta Empire]] and the [[s:vakataka-dynasty|Vakataka dynasty]] faded. Their kingdom centred on [[e:mahishmati|Mahishmati]] on the [[e:narmada-river|Narmada]] and stretched over [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]], Malwa, the Konkan and northern [[e:maharashtra|Maharashtra]]. They used the era of 248 later called the [[e:kalachuri-chedi-era|Kalachuri-Chedi era]].
kalachuris-of-mahishmati.r: Three kings are known: [[e:krishnaraja-kalachuri|Krishnaraja]], whose [[e:silver|silver]] coins circulated widely, his son [[e:shankaragana|Shankaragana]] and grandson [[e:buddharaja|Buddharaja]]. They were devotees of [[e:shiva|Shiva]] in the [[e:pashupata-shaivism|Pashupata]] tradition. Some historians attribute the great Shiva cave at [[e:elephanta-caves|Elephanta]] and early caves at [[e:ellora-caves|Ellora]] to their patronage, though this is debated.
kalachuris-of-mahishmati.e: Around 600 to 610 [[e:buddharaja|Buddharaja]] was defeated by [[e:mangalesha|Mangalesha]] of the [[s:chalukyas-of-badami|Chalukyas of Badami]], and [[e:pulakeshin-ii|Pulakeshin II]] completed the conquest of the Kalachuri lands. Later dynasties, notably the [[s:kalachuris-of-tripuri|Kalachuris of Tripuri]], claimed descent from them.

kachchhapaghata-dynasty.t: A Rajput dynasty that held the fortress of Gwalior and built its Sas-Bahu temple in the 11th century.
kachchhapaghata-dynasty.o: The Kachchhapaghatas emerged in the 10th century in the region of [[s:gwalior-state|Gwalior]], [[e:narwar|Narwar]] and [[e:dubkund|Dubkund]] in northern [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]], probably as feudatories of the [[s:gurjara-pratihara|Gurjara-Pratihara]] or the [[s:chandela-dynasty|Chandela dynasty]]. According to a Gwalior inscription, Vajradaman took the fort of [[e:gwalior-fort|Gopadri]], Gwalior, from the Pratiharas around 977.
kachchhapaghata-dynasty.r: Several branches of the family ruled from [[s:gwalior-state|Gwalior]], [[e:narwar|Narwar]] and [[e:dubkund|Dubkund]]. They were often [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the Chandelas and fought the [[s:paramara-dynasty|Paramara dynasty]]; Kirttiraja is said to have defeated an army from [[e:malwa|Malwa]]. Mahipala completed the great [[e:sas-bahu-temple|Sas-Bahu]] temple at Gwalior fort in 1093, and the Dubkund branch built Jain temples, showing patronage of both faiths.
kachchhapaghata-dynasty.e: In the 12th century the Kachchhapaghatas lost [[s:gwalior-state|Gwalior]] to a Pratihara family, and the region was later taken by [[e:iltutmish|Iltutmish]] of the [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]] in 1232. Later [[e:kachhwaha|Kachhwaha Rajputs]] of [[s:jaipur-state|Amber]] claimed descent from them.

kingdom-of-vannius.t: A Roman client kingdom of the Quadi north of the Danube, set up to house the followers of the fallen kings Maroboduus and Catualda.
kingdom-of-vannius.o: After [[e:maroboduus|Maroboduus]] and his successor [[e:catualda|Catualda]] were driven out in 19, their followers were settled by [[e:rome|Rome]] north of the [[e:danube|Danube]] between the March ([[e:morava-river|Morava]]) and Váh rivers. [[e:drusus-the-younger|Drusus the Younger]] installed [[e:vannius|Vannius]], of the [[s:quadi|Quadi]], as their king, creating a buffer state opposite the Roman frontier in [[e:pannonia|Pannonia]] and [[s:kingdom-of-noricum|Noricum]].
kingdom-of-vannius.r: [[e:vannius|Vannius]] ruled for some thirty years as a client of [[e:rome|Rome]]. [[e:tacitus|Tacitus]] says he was at first respected, then grew arrogant, enriching himself through raiding and tolls on traders. The kingdom grew wealthy on commerce along the [[s:jaipur-state|Amber]] Road between the Baltic and [[e:carnuntum|Carnuntum]], and Roman goods reached its elite graves.
kingdom-of-vannius.e: In 50 [[e:vannius|Vannius]] was overthrown by his nephews [[e:vangio|Vangio]] and [[e:sido|Sido]] with the help of the [[s:hermunduri|Hermunduri]] and [[e:lugii|Lugii]]. Emperor [[e:claudius|Claudius]] refused to intervene but gave him refuge in [[e:pannonia|Pannonia]]. The nephews divided the kingdom and stayed loyal to [[e:rome|Rome]]; Sido fought for Vespasian in 69.

kingdom-of-lesotho.t: The independent mountain kingdom of the Basotho, entirely surrounded by South Africa, since 1966.
kingdom-of-lesotho.o: [[s:basutoland|Basutoland]] became independent on 4 October 1966 as the Kingdom of [[s:basotho-kingdom|Lesotho]], a [[e:constitutional-monarchy|constitutional monarchy]] within the [[e:commonwealth-of-nations|Commonwealth]] with [[e:moshoeshoe-ii|Moshoeshoe II]], a descendant of [[e:moshoeshoe-i|Moshoeshoe I]] of the Basotho Kingdom, as king and [[e:leabua-jonathan|Leabua Jonathan]] of the [[e:basotho-national-party|Basotho National Party]] as prime minister.
kingdom-of-lesotho.r: Jonathan annulled the 1970 election he was losing and ruled by decree until a military coup in 1986. [[e:moshoeshoe-ii|Moshoeshoe II]] was exiled in 1990 and replaced by his son [[e:letsie-iii|Letsie III]], then briefly restored before his death in 1996. The economy relies on mine wages from [[s:republic-of-south-africa|South Africa]], textiles and the [[s:basotho-kingdom|Lesotho]] Highlands Water Project, which sells water to [[e:gauteng|Gauteng]].
kingdom-of-lesotho.e: A disputed election in 1998 led to rioting and intervention by South African and [[e:botswana|Botswana]] troops under [[e:southern-african-development-community|SADC]]. Since 2002 [[s:basotho-kingdom|Lesotho]] has held regular elections under a mixed electoral system, with [[e:letsie-iii|Letsie III]] as king.

kingdom-of-strathclyde.t: British kingdom of the Clyde, first centred on Dumbarton Rock and later at Govan, which outlasted the other northern Brittonic realms until absorbed into Scotland.
kingdom-of-strathclyde.o: The kingdom grew from the British people of the [[e:river-clyde|Clyde]], descendants of the [[s:damnonii|Damnonii]], after Roman influence ended. Its early king [[e:ceretic-guletic|Ceretic]], probably the Coroticus whom St Patrick rebuked for slave-raiding in the 5th century, ruled from Alt Clut, the fortress on [[e:dumbarton-rock|Dumbarton Rock]].
kingdom-of-strathclyde.r: [[e:rhydderch-hael|Rhydderch Hael]], a king of the late 6th century, appears in the lives of [[e:columba|Columba]] and [[e:saint-kentigern|Kentigern]], the patron saint of [[e:glasgow|Glasgow]]. In 642 Owain son of Beli defeated and killed [[e:domnall-brecc|Domnall Brecc]] of [[s:dal-riata|Dál Riata]] at [[e:battle-of-strathcarron|Strathcarron]]. Society rested on [[e:cattle|cattle]] farming, and its people spoke [[e:cumbric|Cumbric]], a northern form of Brittonic. After 870 the royal centre moved to [[e:govan|Govan]], where a fine collection of carved stones survives.
kingdom-of-strathclyde.e: In 870 [[e:vikings|Viking]] kings from [[e:dublin|Dublin]] took [[e:dumbarton-rock|Dumbarton]] after a four-month siege. The renewed kingdom, often called [[e:cumbria|Cumbria]], expanded south into Cumbria in the 10th century. Its last known king, [[e:owain-the-bald|Owain the Bald]], may have died around 1018, and it was absorbed into the kingdom of [[e:scotland|Scotland]] during the 11th century.

kingdom-of-asebu.t: Fante coastal kingdom that invited the Dutch to the Gold Coast, sending envoys to the Netherlands in 1611.
kingdom-of-asebu.o: Asebu was a small [[e:fante|Fante]] kingdom on the coast east of [[e:cape-coast|Cape Coast]], with its port at [[e:moree|Moree]]. It existed by the time Portuguese traders arrived in the late 15th century and resented Portuguese control of the [[e:gold-trade|gold trade]] from [[e:elmina|Elmina]].
kingdom-of-asebu.r: Seeking new partners, Asebu's ruler sent envoys to the [[s:dutch-republic|Dutch Republic]] in 1611, and in 1612 the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] built [[e:fort-nassau-gold-coast|Fort Nassau]] at [[e:moree|Moree]], their first fort on the [[s:gold-coast-colony|Gold Coast]]. Asebu then grew rich on gold and later the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]], while competing with neighbouring Fetu and the [[e:fante|Fante]] states.
kingdom-of-asebu.e: Asebu was absorbed into the wider [[e:fante|Fante]] group of states in the 18th century and joined the alliances against the [[s:ashanti-empire|Ashanti Empire]]. It came under British rule with the creation of the [[s:gold-coast-colony|Gold Coast Colony]] in 1874 and remains a traditional area in Ghana.

kingdom-of-phrygia.t: Phrygia, the Iron Age kingdom of Gordion in central Anatolia, home of King Midas and the Gordian knot.
kingdom-of-phrygia.o: The [[e:phrygians|Phrygians]], probably migrants from the [[e:balkans|Balkans]] after the [[e:late-bronze-age-collapse|Late Bronze Age collapse]], settled the plateau west of the [[e:kizilirmak|Kızılırmak]]. By the 9th century BCE they had built a fortified capital at [[e:gordion|Gordion]] on the [[e:sakarya-river|Sakarya]] river, with a citadel of megaron halls. Assyrian texts call the people Mushki.
kingdom-of-phrygia.r: Phrygian kings ruled from [[e:gordion|Gordion]] and built huge burial mounds; Tumulus MM held a king with bronze vessels and fine wooden furniture. [[e:midas|Midas]], the [[e:mita|Mita]] of Assyrian records, was a rival of [[e:sargon-ii|Sargon II]] and sent gifts to [[s:delphi|Delphi]]. The [[e:phrygians|Phrygians]] wrote in an alphabet adapted from Greek and worshipped the mother goddess [[e:cybele|Matar]], later Cybele.
kingdom-of-phrygia.e: According to Greek tradition, Cimmerian invaders overran [[e:phrygia|Phrygia]] in the early 7th century BCE and [[e:midas|Midas]] killed himself; the great destruction of [[e:gordion|Gordion]] itself is now dated c. 800 BCE. Phrygia then fell under the [[s:kingdom-of-lydia|Kingdom of Lydia]] and the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]], though its language and cults survived for centuries.

kelantan-sultanate.t: North-east Malay sultanate, long a tributary of Siam, now a state of Malaysia known for its strong Malay and Islamic identity.
kelantan-sultanate.o: Kelantan had been ruled by various local princes for centuries, often under the influence of [[s:pattani-kingdom|Pattani]] and Siam. In 1762 [[e:long-yunus|Long Yunus]], of a Pattani-linked family, unified the territory and founded the line of rulers that still holds the throne, and in the early 19th century his successors adopted the title of sultan.
kelantan-sultanate.r: Kelantan was a populous [[e:rice|rice]]-growing state on the delta of the Kelantan river, with fishing, weaving and metalwork. Its rulers sent the bunga mas to Siam while keeping internal autonomy, and [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:muhammad-ii-of-kelantan|Muhammad II]] strengthened royal power from [[e:kota-bharu|Kota Bharu]] in the mid 19th century. Wayang kulit, kite flying and Islamic schools were prominent.
kelantan-sultanate.e: The [[e:anglo-siamese-treaty-of-1909|Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909]] placed Kelantan under British protection as one of the [[s:unfederated-malay-states|Unfederated Malay States]]. After Japanese and Thai occupation it joined the [[s:federation-of-malaya|Federation of Malaya]], and today it is a state of [[s:malaysia|Malaysia]] whose sultan, [[e:muhammad-v-of-kelantan|Muhammad V]], served as king from 2016 to 2019.

kong-empire.t: A Dyula Muslim trading state in northern Ivory Coast, built by Seku Wattara around the city of Kong, a centre of commerce and Islamic learning.
kong-empire.o: [[e:kong-cote-divoire|Kong]] was already a [[e:wangara|Dyula]] market town when, around 1710, [[e:seku-wattara|Seku Wattara]] seized power from its earlier rulers and launched campaigns that extended its influence north towards the [[e:black-volta|Black Volta]] and the middle [[e:niger-river|Niger]]. The Wattara (Ouattara) family became the ruling dynasty, and their armies relied on cavalry and imported firearms.
kong-empire.r: [[e:kong-cote-divoire|Kong]] was more a commercial network than a centralised empire. [[e:wangara|Dyula]] merchants traded gold, [[e:kola-nut|kola nuts]], cloth and slaves between the forest and the [[e:sahel|Sahel]], and the town had mosques and [[e:quran|Qur'anic]] schools of wide reputation. The warrior estate, the Sonangi, did the fighting while Muslim scholars and traders ran the city. After [[e:seku-wattara|Seku]]'s death about 1745 the realm fragmented and his relative Famagan founded the [[s:kingdom-of-gwiriko|Kingdom of Gwiriko]].
kong-empire.e: [[e:kong-cote-divoire|Kong]] declined into a regional trading town. The French explorer [[e:louis-gustave-binger|Louis-Gustave Binger]] arrived in 1888, and a French treaty followed in 1889. [[e:samori-ture|Samori Toure]] sacked and burned Kong in 1897, and the area was absorbed into the [[s:french-ivory-coast|French Ivory Coast]].

kingdom-of-atholl.t: A Pictish kingdom in the central Highlands whose name, 'New Ireland', hints at Gaelic influence, later a Scottish earldom.
kingdom-of-atholl.o: [[e:atholl|Atholl]], Athfotla, appears in Irish annals from the 8th century, when a king of Atholl was drowned by [[e:oengus-i-of-the-picts|Oengus son of Fergus]], king of the [[e:picts|Picts]], in 739. The name is usually interpreted as 'New Ireland', suggesting Gaelic settlement or influence in the Pictish highlands of [[e:perthshire|Perthshire]]. Fotla is also one of the seven Pictish provinces.
kingdom-of-atholl.r: [[e:atholl|Atholl]] seems to have had its own kings within the Pictish overkingship. Its lands in the valleys of the [[e:river-tay|Tay]], [[e:river-tummel|Tummel]] and [[e:river-garry-perthshire|Garry]] were pastoral and thinly peopled. [[e:dunkeld|Dunkeld]], on its edge, became a major church centre in the 9th century.
kingdom-of-atholl.e: [[e:atholl|Atholl]] was absorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-scotland|Kingdom of Scotland]] as a mormaerdom and later an earldom. [[e:crinan-of-dunkeld|Crinan]], abbot of [[e:dunkeld|Dunkeld]] and father of King [[e:duncan-i-of-scotland|Duncan I]], is sometimes linked with Atholl, and its later earls descended from Duncan's family.

kingdom-of-henan.t: A short-lived kingdom around Luoyang, one of Xiang Yu's Eighteen Kingdoms, whose king Shen Yang surrendered to Liu Bang in 205 BCE.
kingdom-of-henan.o: In [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu's]] settlement of 206 BCE, [[e:shen-yang|Shen Yang]], a former official of Zhao and associate of [[e:zhang-er|Zhang Er]], was rewarded for welcoming Chu forces at the [[e:yellow-river|Yellow River]] by being made King of [[e:henan|Henan]], with his capital at [[e:luoyang|Luoyang]].
kingdom-of-henan.r: The kingdom held the strategic [[e:luoyang|Luoyang]] basin, the gateway between the [[e:guanzhong|Guanzhong]] region and the eastern plain. It lasted too briefly for any distinctive government to develop.
kingdom-of-henan.e: When [[e:liu-bang|Liu Bang]] emerged from the west in 205 BCE, [[e:shen-yang|Shen Yang]] surrendered without a fight, and his kingdom became [[e:henan|Henan]] [[e:commandery|Commandery]]. Its loss opened the route east for Liu Bang's ill-fated march on [[e:xuzhou|Pengcheng]], capital of [[s:western-chu|Western Chu]].

kingdom-of-seisyllwg.t: A Welsh kingdom of Ceredigion and Ystrad Tywi, named after King Seisyll, which merged with Dyfed to form Deheubarth.
kingdom-of-seisyllwg.o: Seisyllwg was created when [[e:seisyll-ap-clydog|Seisyll ap Clydog]] of [[s:kingdom-of-ceredigion|Ceredigion]] added [[s:kingdom-of-ystrad-tywi|Ystrad Tywi]], the Tywi valley, to his realm in the 8th century. The new territory was named after him. Little else is known of its early rulers beyond genealogies.
kingdom-of-seisyllwg.r: The kingdom covered much of later [[e:cardiganshire|Cardiganshire]] and [[e:carmarthenshire|Carmarthenshire]], a land of upland pasture and coastal farms with important churches such as [[e:llanbadarn-fawr|Llanbadarn Fawr]]. Its last native king, [[e:gwgon-ap-meurig|Gwgon]], drowned in 871, and it passed by marriage to [[e:rhodri-the-great|Rhodri the Great]] of [[s:kingdom-of-gwynedd|Gwynedd]], whose son Cadell inherited it.
kingdom-of-seisyllwg.e: Cadell's son [[e:hywel-dda|Hywel Dda]] united Seisyllwg with [[s:kingdom-of-dyfed|Dyfed]] around 920, creating the [[s:kingdom-of-deheubarth|Kingdom of Deheubarth]]. The name Seisyllwg fell out of use, though [[s:kingdom-of-ceredigion|Ceredigion]] persists as a county.

kingdom-of-morgannwg.t: A south-east Welsh kingdom formed by the union of Glywysing and Gwent, whose name survives in Glamorgan.
kingdom-of-morgannwg.o: Morgannwg, 'Morgan's land', is traditionally named after [[e:morgan-ab-owain|Morgan Hen]] ab Owain, who united the older kingdoms of [[s:kingdom-of-glywysing|Glywysing]] and [[s:kingdom-of-gwent|Gwent]] around 942. Earlier rulers of the region are known from the charters of the [[e:book-of-llandaff|Book of Llandaff]].
kingdom-of-morgannwg.r: The kingdom covered the fertile vale and uplands between the Tywi and the [[e:river-wye|Wye]], with churches such as [[e:llandaff|Llandaff]] and [[e:llancarfan|Llancarfan]]. Its kings dealt with English rulers, and [[e:morgan-ab-owain|Morgan Hen]] attended Aethelstan's court. After his death in 974 [[s:kingdom-of-gwent|Gwent]] and [[s:kingdom-of-glywysing|Glywysing]] separated again at times, and the kingdom was later ruled by [[e:gruffydd-ap-llywelyn|Gruffydd ap Llywelyn]] and then [[e:caradog-ap-gruffydd|Caradog ap Gruffydd]].
kingdom-of-morgannwg.e: [[e:iestyn-ap-gwrgant|Iestyn ap Gwrgant]], the last native ruler, was overthrown around 1090 by the Norman [[e:robert-fitzhamon|Robert Fitzhamon]], who created the [[s:lordship-of-glamorgan|Lordship of Glamorgan]]. The name survives in the counties of Glamorgan.

kingdom-of-gwrtheyrnion.t: Tiny Welsh kingdom between the Wye and the Ithon whose rulers claimed descent from Vortigern, the British ruler blamed for inviting the Saxons.
kingdom-of-gwrtheyrnion.o: Gwrtheyrnion means 'the land of [[e:vortigern|Gwrtheyrn]]', the Welsh form of Vortigern. The [[e:historia-brittonum|Historia Brittonum]], written in 829 or 830, says that after Vortigern's fall his son Pascent was granted [[s:kingdom-of-buellt|Buellt]] and Gwrtheyrnion by [[e:ambrosius-aurelianus|Ambrosius]], and that its ruler in the author's day, [[e:fernmail|Fernmail]], descended from him. The territory lay around [[e:rhayader|Rhayader]] in what became [[e:radnorshire|Radnorshire]].
kingdom-of-gwrtheyrnion.r: Almost nothing is known of its government beyond this genealogy. It was a small upland territory of river valleys and hill pasture, often ruled together with the neighbouring [[s:kingdom-of-buellt|Kingdom of Buellt]], and its dynasty used its link with [[e:vortigern|Vortigern]], whatever its truth, to assert ancient legitimacy.
kingdom-of-gwrtheyrnion.e: Gwrtheyrnion was absorbed by more powerful Welsh kingdoms, probably in the 10th century, and later formed a cantref of the Middle March between [[e:river-wye|Wye]] and [[e:river-severn|Severn]], held by Welsh and [[e:anglo-normans|Anglo-Norman]] lords such as the [[e:house-of-mortimer|Mortimers]].

kingdom-of-capsus.t: A Berber principality of southern Tunisia under Antalas, who fought the Vandals, allied with Byzantium and then turned against it.
kingdom-of-capsus.o: In the early 6th century, as the [[s:vandal-kingdom|Vandal Kingdom]] lost control of the interior, [[e:berbers|Berber]] chiefs of the Frexes and neighbouring tribes built a power base in southern [[s:byzacena|Byzacena]] around [[e:gafsa|Capsa]] (Gafsa). Its best-known leader, [[e:antalas|Antalas]], son of Guenfan, defeated a Vandal army sent by King [[e:hilderic|Hilderic]] around 530.
kingdom-of-capsus.r: What is known comes from [[e:procopius|Procopius]] and [[e:corippus|Corippus]]. [[e:antalas|Antalas]] led a tribal confederation of herders and oasis farmers on the desert edge. He sided with the [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]] after their conquest of 533 to 534, receiving [[e:subsidy|subsidies]], but rebelled in 544 after the general [[e:solomon|Solomon]] executed his brother. That year his forces killed Solomon at [[e:cillium|Cillium]], and he briefly allied with the Byzantine mutineer [[e:stotzas|Stotzas]].
kingdom-of-capsus.e: [[e:antalas|Antalas]] was defeated by [[e:john-troglita|John Troglita]], the general of the [[s:praetorian-prefecture-of-africa|Praetorian Prefecture of Africa]], and submitted around 546 to 548, fighting thereafter as a Byzantine ally against the [[s:laguatan|Laguatan]]. His principality then disappears from the record.

kingdom-of-hejaz-and-nejd.t: The dual kingdom of Ibn Saud, uniting the holy cities with Najd, and the immediate forerunner of Saudi Arabia.
kingdom-of-hejaz-and-nejd.o: After conquering the [[s:kingdom-of-hejaz|Kingdom of Hejaz]], [[e:ibn-saud|Abd al-Aziz ibn Saud]] was proclaimed King of the [[e:hejaz|Hejaz]] in [[e:mecca|Mecca]] in January 1926 while remaining [[e:sultan|Sultan]] of [[e:najd|Nejd]]. In 1927 Nejd was also raised to a kingdom, and the two realms were ruled in personal union.
kingdom-of-hejaz-and-nejd.r: The [[s:kingdom-of-hejaz|Hejaz]] kept its own administration and consultative council under [[e:ibn-saud|Ibn Saud's]] son Faisal as [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]], while [[e:najd|Najd]] was ruled directly. The [[e:treaty-of-jeddah-1927|Treaty of Jeddah]] in 1927 brought British recognition of full independence. The Ikhwan, angry at modern innovations and limits on raiding, rebelled; Ibn Saud defeated them at the [[e:battle-of-sabilla|Battle of Sabilla]] in 1929 and crushed the revolt by 1930.
kingdom-of-hejaz-and-nejd.e: On 23 September 1932 a royal decree unified the dual kingdom as the [[s:saudi-arabia|Kingdom of Saudi Arabia]], named after the ruling family.

kingdom-of-the-magonsaete.t: A small Anglian sub-kingdom on the Welsh border in Herefordshire and Shropshire, ruled by Merewalh's dynasty under Mercia.
kingdom-of-the-magonsaete.o: The Magonsaete, perhaps named after [[e:magnis|Magnis]] (Kenchester), emerged in the mid 7th century in the borderlands west of the [[e:river-severn|Severn]]. Their first known ruler was [[e:merewalh|Merewalh]], whom later tradition made a son of [[e:penda-of-mercia|Penda]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-mercia|Kingdom of Mercia]], though this is uncertain.
kingdom-of-the-magonsaete.r: [[e:merewalh|Merewalh's]] family was noted for piety: his daughter [[e:mildburh|Mildburh]] founded the abbey of [[e:much-wenlock|Much Wenlock]], and other children became saints. A bishopric at [[e:hereford|Hereford]] served the people. The rulers were sub-kings under Mercian overlordship, and the population included many [[e:britons-celtic-people|Britons]].
kingdom-of-the-magonsaete.e: The dynasty disappears from record in the 8th century, and the territory was absorbed directly into [[s:kingdom-of-mercia|Mercia]]. Its outline survived as the diocese of [[e:hereford|Hereford]].

kingdom-of-limerick.t: A Norse town-kingdom on the Shannon estuary whose fall to the Dal Cais opened the way for Brian Boru's rise.
kingdom-of-limerick.o: [[e:vikings|Vikings]] had raided the [[e:river-shannon|Shannon]] since the 9th century, and in 922 [[e:tomrair-mac-ailchi|Tomrair mac Ailchi]] established a permanent fleet base at [[e:limerick|Limerick]], Hlymrekr. The settlement competed with the [[s:kingdom-of-dublin|Kingdom of Dublin]] for control of the [[e:irish-sea|Irish Sea]] trade and raided deep into [[s:kingdom-of-connacht|Connacht]] and [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Munster]].
kingdom-of-limerick.r: [[e:limerick|Limerick]] was a fortified trading port on an island in the [[e:river-shannon|Shannon]], dealing in slaves and plunder. Its kings were rivals of [[e:dublin|Dublin]]'s dynasty, losing a war with them in 937. In the 960s [[e:ivar-of-limerick|Ivar of Limerick]] allied with Irish kings of [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Munster]] against the rising [[e:dal-cais|Dal Cais]].
kingdom-of-limerick.e: [[e:mathgamain-mac-cennetig|Mathgamain]] and [[e:brian-boru|Brian Boru]] of the [[e:dal-cais|Dal Cais]] defeated the Norse at [[e:battle-of-sulcoit|Sulcoit]] in 967 and sacked the town. Brian killed [[e:ivar-of-limerick|Ivar]] and his sons on [[e:scattery-island|Scattery Island]] in 977. [[e:limerick|Limerick]] became the [[e:obrien-dynasty|O'Brien]] capital and later the seat of the [[s:kingdom-of-thomond|Kingdom of Thomond]].

kuban-peoples-republic.t: A Cossack republic on the Kuban, proclaimed in 1918, that sought union with Ukraine and fought the Bolsheviks while quarrelling with the Whites.
kuban-peoples-republic.o: After the [[e:russian-revolution|Russian Revolution]] the [[s:kuban-cossack-host|Kuban Cossack Host]], descended partly from the [[s:black-sea-cossack-host|Black Sea Cossack Host]], set up its own [[e:kuban-rada|Rada]] in [[e:krasnodar|Yekaterinodar]]. In January 1918 the [[e:radaa|Rada]] proclaimed an independent Kuban People's Republic, with a population split between Ukrainian-speaking [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] [[e:cossacks|Cossacks]], Russian line Cossacks and non-Cossack settlers.
kuban-peoples-republic.r: The Bolsheviks took [[e:krasnodar|Yekaterinodar]] in March 1918, and the government retreated with the [[e:volunteer-army|Volunteer Army]], which recaptured the city in August. The republic had its own ataman, [[e:alexander-filimonov|Alexander Filimonov]], and a [[e:kuban-rada|Rada]] in which a Ukrainian-minded faction under [[e:mykola-ryabovol|Mykola Ryabovol]] and [[e:luka-bych|Luka Bych]] pushed for federation with [[e:ukraine|Ukraine]]. This brought conflict with General [[e:anton-denikin|Denikin]], who wanted a united [[e:russia|Russia]].
kuban-peoples-republic.e: [[e:mykola-ryabovol|Ryabovol]] was assassinated in 1919, and in November [[e:anton-denikin|Denikin]] had the [[e:kuban-rada|Rada]] member [[e:alexei-kulabukhov|Kulabukhov]] hanged and the [[e:radaa|Rada]] purged. Demoralised Kuban units deserted, and the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] took [[e:krasnodar|Yekaterinodar]] in March 1920, ending the republic.

kingdom-of-vientiane.t: The central Lao kingdom formed when Lan Xang split in 1707, destroyed by Siam after King Anouvong's revolt of 1826 to 1828.
kingdom-of-vientiane.o: When [[s:lan-xang|Lan Xang]]'s succession dispute erupted, [[e:setthathirath-ii|Setthathirath II]], with Vietnamese backing, took power at Vientiane around 1707, while [[s:kingdom-of-luang-phrabang|Luang Prabang]] broke away. Vientiane kept the old capital and much of the Lan Xang heritage, including the [[e:emerald-buddha|Emerald Buddha]].
kingdom-of-vientiane.r: The kingdom ruled the central [[e:mekong-river|Mekong]] valley and much of the [[e:khorat-plateau|Khorat plateau]], but it was weakened by wars with [[s:kingdom-of-luang-phrabang|Luang Prabang]]. In 1779 the [[s:thonburi-kingdom|Thonburi Kingdom]] captured Vientiane and carried off the [[e:emerald-buddha|Emerald Buddha]] to [[e:bangkok|Bangkok]], and Vientiane became a Siamese [[e:vassal|vassal]]. King [[e:anouvong|Anouvong]] built [[e:wat-si-saket|Wat Si Saket]] and tried to restore Lao power.
kingdom-of-vientiane.e: In 1826 [[e:anouvong|Anouvong]] rebelled against the [[s:rattanakosin-kingdom|Rattanakosin Kingdom]] and marched toward [[e:bangkok|Bangkok]], but was defeated. In 1828 Siamese armies razed Vientiane, deported much of its population to the [[e:khorat-plateau|Khorat plateau]]; Anouvong was captured and died in captivity in Bangkok. The kingdom was abolished, and Vientiane was refounded under French rule.

keonjhar-state.t: A Bhanja dynasty state in the forested hills of northern Odisha, known for the Bhuyan risings of 1868 and 1891 against its Raja.
keonjhar-state.o: Tradition holds that [[e:kendujhar|Keonjhar]] was founded in the 12th century by a younger brother of the ruler of [[s:mayurbhanj-state|Mayurbhanj]], so that both states were ruled by branches of the [[e:bhanja-dynasty|Bhanja dynasty]]. The capital was Keonjhargarh.
keonjhar-state.r: [[e:kendujhar|Keonjhar]] was hilly and wooded, with a large population of [[e:bhuyan|Bhuyan]] and [[e:juang|Juang peoples]], whose obligations to the Raja caused tension. Disputed successions and harsh exactions led to Bhuyan revolts in 1868 and 1891, the second led by [[e:dharanidhar-naik|Dharanidhar Naik]], both suppressed with British help. The state was later known for its iron ore.
keonjhar-state.e: [[e:kendujhar|Keonjhar]] merged into [[e:odisha|Orissa]] on 1 January 1948 and is now a district of Odisha.

kingdom-of-cambodia-1953-1970.t: Independent Cambodia under Norodom Sihanouk, who kept the kingdom neutral and peaceful through the 1950s and 1960s while war raged next door.
kingdom-of-cambodia-1953-1970.o: [[e:norodom-of-cambodia|King Norodom]] [[e:norodom-sihanouk|Sihanouk]]'s campaign against French rule won full independence on 9 November 1953, confirmed by the [[s:republic-of-geneva|Geneva]] conference in 1954. In 1955 he abdicated in favour of his father [[e:norodom-suramarit|Norodom Suramarit]] to enter politics, founding the [[e:sangkum-reastr-niyum|Sangkum Reastr Niyum]] movement, which won every seat in the national assembly.
kingdom-of-cambodia-1953-1970.r: [[e:norodom-sihanouk|Sihanouk]] dominated politics as prime minister and, after his father's death in 1960, head of state. The [[e:sangkum-reastr-niyum|Sangkum]] promoted Buddhist socialism, built schools, hospitals and modern buildings in [[e:phnom-penh|Phnom Penh]], and pursued neutrality in the [[e:cold-war|Cold War]]. In 1965 Sihanouk broke with the [[s:united-states|United States]] and tacitly allowed North Vietnamese forces to use Cambodian territory, while repressing the left.
kingdom-of-cambodia-1953-1970.e: A deteriorating economy, a peasant revolt at [[e:samlaut-uprising|Samlaut]] in 1967 and growing hostility from the right weakened him. On 18 March 1970, while [[e:norodom-sihanouk|Sihanouk]] was abroad, the national assembly deposed him, and [[e:lon-nol|Lon Nol]] proclaimed the [[s:khmer-republic|Khmer Republic]].

kingdom-of-brittany.t: Breton kingdom forged in the 9th century by Nominoe and his successors, who won independence from the Carolingian Franks.
kingdom-of-brittany.o: [[e:louis-the-pious|Louis the Pious]] appointed the Breton noble [[e:nominoe|Nominoe]] as his representative in [[s:duchy-of-brittany|Brittany]] in 831. After Louis's death Nominoe broke with [[e:charles-the-bald|Charles the Bald]], defeating him at [[e:battle-of-ballon|Ballon]] in 845. His son [[e:erispoe|Erispoe]] won again at [[e:battle-of-jengland|Jengland]] in 851, and the [[e:treaty-of-angers-851|Treaty of Angers]] recognised him as king with [[e:rennes|Rennes]], [[e:nantes|Nantes]] and the [[e:pays-de-retz|Pays de Retz]].
kingdom-of-brittany.r: The kingdom united [[s:domnonee|Domnonée]], [[s:cornouaille|Cornouaille]] and [[s:broerec|Broërec]] with the Frankish marches. [[e:salomon-of-brittany|Salomon]], who killed [[e:erispoe|Erispoe]] and took the throne in 857, gained the Cotentin and [[e:avranchin|Avranchin]] in 867. The kings ruled through local machtierns and monasteries such as [[e:redon-abbey|Redon]], and set up a Breton church province at [[e:dol-de-bretagne|Dol]].
kingdom-of-brittany.e: After internal conflict [[e:alan-i-king-of-brittany|Alan the Great]] defeated the [[e:vikings|Vikings]] at [[e:battle-of-questembert|Questembert]] around 888, but after his death in 907 Vikings overran [[s:duchy-of-brittany|Brittany]]. [[e:alan-ii-duke-of-brittany|Alan Barbetorte]] returned from [[e:england|England]] in 936 and expelled them by 939, ruling as duke and founding the Duchy of Brittany.

kerma.t: The first great kingdom of Nubia, centred on Kerma at the Third Cataract and for centuries a rival to pharaonic Egypt.
kerma.o: Kerma culture developed in [[e:upper-nubia|Upper Nubia]] from about 2500 BCE, with its centre at Kerma near the [[e:nile-cataracts|Third Cataract]] of the [[e:nile|Nile]]. The town grew from a farming and [[e:cattle|cattle]]-herding settlement into the capital of a kingdom that Egyptian texts called Kush, controlling the river trade in gold, [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]], [[e:ebony|ebony]] and cattle.
kerma.r: The rulers lived in a walled city dominated by the [[e:western-deffufa|Western Deffufa]], a massive mud-brick temple. Kings were buried under huge circular tumuli, some with hundreds of sacrificed attendants. Kerma potters made distinctive polished black-topped red ware. At its height, in the 17th century BCE, Kerma raided as far as [[e:elkab|Elkab]] in [[e:egypt|Egypt]], and the [[s:fifteenth-dynasty-of-egypt|Hyksos]] of the Fifteenth Dynasty of Egypt sought its alliance against [[s:thebes|Thebes]].
kerma.e: The [[e:new-kingdom-of-egypt|New Kingdom]] [[e:pharaoh|pharaohs]] struck back. [[e:thutmose-i|Thutmose I]] sacked Kerma around 1500 BCE, and [[e:egypt|Egypt]] annexed [[e:nubia|Nubia]] as the [[s:viceroyalty-of-kush|Viceroyalty of Kush]]. Kerma traditions survived beneath Egyptian rule and fed into the later [[e:kushite-empire|Kushite Empire of Napata]] and [[e:meroe|Meroë]].

kothi-state.t: A small Baghel Rajput principality of Baghelkhand said by family tradition to have branched off from the Sohawal ruling family.
kothi-state.o: Kothi was held by [[e:baghel|Baghel Rajputs]] and, according to family tradition, emerged as a separate holding from [[s:sohawal-state|Sohawal State]], itself a cadet branch of the Baghel house of Rewa. The register dates it from 1600, but the details of its separation are known mainly from family tradition.
kothi-state.r: The Raja ruled a few dozen villages in the upland country west of Rewa. In the British period Kothi was a non-salute state under the [[e:baghelkhand-agency|Baghelkhand Agency]] of Central [[e:india|India]], and little else of its internal history is widely recorded.
kothi-state.e: Kothi was merged into [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]] in 1948, which became part of [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]] in 1956. Its lands lie in today's [[e:satna-district|Satna district]].

kingdom-of-barwe.t: A Shona kingdom of central Mozambique whose rulers, the Makombe, resisted Portuguese conquest into the 20th century.
kingdom-of-barwe.o: Barwe emerged around 1500 between the [[e:mutapa-empire|Mutapa]] lands and the [[s:kingdom-of-manyika|Kingdom of Manyika]], ruled by a dynasty related to the Mutapa house. Its rulers, titled Makombe, controlled routes between the [[e:zambezi|Zambezi]] and the gold-bearing highlands.
kingdom-of-barwe.r: The Makombe was a sacred king whose installation required ritual approval, including holy water sent from the [[s:kingdom-of-uteve|Kingdom of Uteve]], and [[e:spirit-medium|spirit mediums]] held great influence. The kingdom traded with Portuguese posts at [[e:sena-mozambique|Sena]] and [[e:tete|Tete]] and frequently fought Afro-Portuguese prazo holders and neighbouring states. In the 19th century it fought off the [[e:gaza-empire|Gaza Nguni]] and the warlords of the [[e:zambezi|Zambezi]].
kingdom-of-barwe.e: After repeated campaigns, Portuguese forces occupied Barwe in 1902, ending its independence. A major rising in 1917, led by Barwe nobles and [[e:spirit-medium|spirit mediums]], was crushed, and the area was absorbed into [[s:portuguese-mozambique|Portuguese Mozambique]].

kingdom-of-fiji.t: A short-lived constitutional monarchy under Seru Cakobau that briefly united Fiji before debt and disorder led to cession to Britain.
kingdom-of-fiji.o: [[e:seru-epenisa-cakobau|Seru Epenisa Cakobau]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-bau|Kingdom of Bau]] claimed the title [[e:tui-viti|Tui Viti]], king of [[e:fiji|Fiji]], but faced rivals such as [[e:enele-maafu|Enele Maʻafu]] of the [[s:tovata-confederacy|Tovata Confederacy]] and American debt claims. A [[e:cotton|cotton]] boom during the [[e:american-civil-war|American Civil War]] brought hundreds of European planters to Fiji, and in 1871 settlers at [[e:levuka|Levuka]] helped Cakobau form a national government with a constitution.
kingdom-of-fiji.r: The kingdom had a cabinet dominated by Europeans, among them [[e:john-bates-thurston|John Bates Thurston]], and a legislature in which settlers held great influence. [[e:enele-maafu|Maʻafu]] joined as [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]] for [[e:lau-islands|Lau]], uniting the main chiefly powers. The government struggled to tax settlers, who often refused to recognise its authority, and to control the brutal labour trade that brought Pacific Islanders to the plantations.
kingdom-of-fiji.e: Bankrupt and unable to keep order, [[e:seru-epenisa-cakobau|Cakobau]] and the leading chiefs offered [[e:fiji|Fiji]] to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]]. The [[e:deed-of-cession-fiji|Deed of Cession]] was signed on 10 October 1874, creating the [[s:colony-of-fiji|Colony of Fiji]]. Cakobau's war club was later returned to Fiji as the mace of its parliament.

kasepuhan-sultanate.t: Senior branch of the divided Cirebon Sultanate in West Java, whose palace preserves one of the oldest royal compounds on Java.
kasepuhan-sultanate.o: When [[e:panembahan-girilaya|Panembahan Girilaya]] of [[e:cirebon|Cirebon]] died as a hostage at the [[s:mataram-sultanate|Mataram]] court in 1662, his sons were freed in 1677 with help from the rebel [[e:trunajaya|Trunajaya]] and the [[s:banten-sultanate|Banten Sultanate]]. [[e:sultan-ageng-tirtayasa|Sultan Ageng Tirtayasa]] of [[e:banten|Banten]] divided Cirebon among them, making the elder, [[e:pangeran-martawijaya|Pangeran Martawijaya]], [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Sepuh, the senior sultan, of Kasepuhan.
kasepuhan-sultanate.r: Kasepuhan held the old Pakungwati palace founded by [[e:sunan-gunung-jati|Sunan Gunung Jati]], whose shrine made [[e:cirebon|Cirebon]] a centre of Javanese [[e:islam|Islam]]. The sultan shared Cirebon with the [[s:kanoman-sultanate|Kanoman Sultanate]], and from 1681 both accepted [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] protection. Court culture blended Javanese, Sundanese, Chinese and Islamic elements, visible in batik and mask dance.
kasepuhan-sultanate.e: [[e:herman-willem-daendels|Herman Willem Daendels]] and then the British during [[s:british-java|British Java]] stripped the [[e:cirebon|Cirebon]] sultans of governing power, and by 1815 they had become pensioned nobles. The [[e:keraton-kasepuhan|Keraton Kasepuhan]] remains the seat of a ceremonial sultan and a major heritage site.

koch-kingdom.t: The Koch kingdom of Biswa Singha and Nara Narayan, which briefly dominated north-east India in the 16th century before splitting into Koch Bihar and Koch Hajo.
koch-kingdom.o: After the [[s:bengal-sultanate|Bengal Sultanate]] destroyed the [[s:kamata-kingdom|Kamata Kingdom]] around 1498, [[e:biswa-singha|Biswa Singha]], a leader of the Koch people, united the local chiefs and founded a new state around 1515, centred on the [[s:cooch-behar-state|Cooch Behar]] area. He adopted [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] kingship and [[e:brahmins|Brahmin]] rituals.
koch-kingdom.r: Under [[e:nara-narayan|Nara Narayan]] (r. 1540–1587) and his brother and general [[e:chilarai|Chilarai]], the Koch defeated the [[s:ahom-kingdom|Ahom kingdom]] and, according to later chronicles, forced tribute from the [[s:kachari-kingdom|Kachari kingdom]], Jaintia, [[s:kingdom-of-manipur|Manipur]] and [[e:tripura|Tripura]]. [[e:nara|Nara]] Narayan rebuilt the [[e:kamakhya-temple|Kamakhya]] temple and patronised the [[e:vaishnavism|Vaishnava]] saint [[e:srimanta-sankardev|Sankardev]] and Assamese and [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] literature.
koch-kingdom.e: In 1581 [[e:nara-narayan|Nara Narayan]] divided the kingdom with his nephew [[e:raghudev-narayan|Raghudev]], creating [[s:cooch-behar-state|Koch Bihar]] in the west and [[s:koch-hajo|Koch Hajo]] in the east. Koch [[e:bihar|Bihar]] continued as Cooch Behar State; Koch [[e:hajo|Hajo]] was later absorbed by the [[e:mughal-empire|Mughals]] and the [[e:ahom-people|Ahoms]].

kalabhra-dynasty.t: Rulers of the Tamil country during a poorly documented period between the Sangam age and the rise of the Pallavas and Pandyas.
kalabhra-dynasty.o: The Kalabhras are known mainly from later sources hostile to them. The 8th-century Velvikudi [[e:copper|copper]] plates of the [[s:later-pandyan-empire|Pandyas]] say a Kalabhra king overthrew the Tamil kings and seized the land, ending the rule of the [[s:early-pandyas|Early Pandyas]], [[s:early-cholas|Early Cholas]] and [[s:early-cheras|Early Cheras]] around the 3rd century. Their origins are unknown; they may have come from the hill country to the north.
kalabhra-dynasty.r: Very little is known about their rule. Later [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] sources accuse them of suppressing [[e:brahmins|Brahmin]] grants, which may reflect patronage of [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] and [[e:jainism|Jainism]]; the Buddhist writer [[e:buddhadatta|Buddhadatta]] mentions a king [[e:accuta-vikkanta|Accuta Vikkanta]] of the Kalabhra family in the Kaveri region. Much Tamil ethical literature, possibly including parts of the [[e:tirukkural|Tirukkural]] tradition, is often dated to this period.
kalabhra-dynasty.e: In the late 6th century the [[e:pandya-dynasty|Pandya]] king [[e:kadungon|Kadungon]] and the Pallava king [[e:simhavishnu|Simhavishnu]] expelled the Kalabhras, founding the [[s:first-pandyan-empire|First Pandyan Empire]] and expanding the [[s:pallava-dynasty|Pallava dynasty]].

kingdom-of-new-galicia.t: The Spanish kingdom of western Mexico, centred on Guadalajara, created by a brutal conquest and enriched by the silver of Zacatecas.
kingdom-of-new-galicia.o: [[e:nuno-de-guzman|Nuño de Guzmán]] led a notoriously violent campaign through western [[s:mexico|Mexico]] in 1529-31, founding towns and naming the territory Nueva [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Galicia]]. [[e:guadalajara-mexico|Guadalajara]] was founded in 1532 and, after several moves, settled at its present site in 1542.
kingdom-of-new-galicia.r: [[e:west-galicia|New Galicia]] had its own audiencia from 1548, seated in [[e:guadalajara-mexico|Guadalajara]] from 1560, giving it a degree of autonomy within [[s:new-spain|New Spain]]. The [[e:mixton-war|Mixtón War]] of 1540-42, a major indigenous uprising, nearly ended Spanish rule there. From 1546 the [[e:silver|silver]] mines of [[e:zacatecas|Zacatecas]] made the region rich and drew settlers north. Ranching and agriculture fed the mining towns.
kingdom-of-new-galicia.e: In 1786 the kingdom became the [[e:intendancy-of-guadalajara|Intendancy of Guadalajara]]. With independence in 1821 it passed to the [[s:first-mexican-empire|First Mexican Empire]], and its territory became the states of [[e:jalisco|Jalisco]], [[e:nayarit|Nayarit]], [[e:aguascalientes|Aguascalientes]] and parts of others.

kingdom-of-ruhuna.t: The southern kingdom of ancient Sri Lanka, base of rebels and liberators, from which Dutugemunu and Vijayabahu I set out to reunite the island.
kingdom-of-ruhuna.o: According to the [[e:mahavamsa|Mahavamsa]], Ruhuna was founded in the 3rd century BCE by [[e:mahanaga|Mahanaga]], a brother of [[e:devanampiya-tissa|Devanampiya Tissa]] of the [[s:anuradhapura-kingdom|Anuradhapura Kingdom]], who settled in the south-east of the island and built [[e:tissamaharama|Mahagama]], modern Tissamaharama. Its rulers formed a branch of the Sinhalese royal line, sometimes independent, sometimes subordinate to [[e:anuradhapura|Anuradhapura]].
kingdom-of-ruhuna.r: Ruhuna's dry south-east depended on [[e:reservoir|reservoirs]] such as [[e:tissa-wewa|Tissa Wewa]], while ports like [[e:godavaya|Godavaya]] linked it to [[e:indian-ocean-trade|Indian Ocean trade]]. Its kings patronised Buddhist monasteries, and the shrine at [[e:kataragama|Kataragama]] made it a pilgrimage region. Rugged and distant from the capital, it served for centuries as a refuge for princes and resistance against invaders; King [[e:kavan-tissa|Kavantissa]] ruled there, and his son [[e:dutugemunu|Dutugemunu]] marched north to defeat [[e:ellalan|Elara]] around 161 BCE.
kingdom-of-ruhuna.e: When the [[s:chola-empire|Chola Empire]] occupied northern [[s:sri-lanka|Sri Lanka]] in the 11th century, Ruhuna became the centre of Sinhalese resistance. Its prince [[e:vijayabahu-i|Vijayabahu I]] drove out the [[e:chola-empire|Cholas]] in 1070 and founded the [[s:polonnaruwa-kingdom|Polonnaruwa Kingdom]], which reabsorbed Ruhuna, though it rebelled again in the 12th century.

kurin-khanate.t: A khanate created by Russia in the Lezgin lands of southern Dagestan, which lasted until the end of the Caucasian War.
kurin-khanate.o: In 1812 the Russian authorities formed the Kurin Khanate from [[e:lezgins|Lezgin]] communities in the [[e:samur-river|Samur]] river area of southern [[e:dagestan|Dagestan]], which had been free societies. They placed it under [[e:aslan-khan-of-kazikumukh|Aslan Khan]], a member of the Kazikumukh ruling family, as a Russian ally, with its seat at Kurakh.
kurin-khanate.r: The khanate governed [[e:lezgins|Lezgin]] villages of farmers and herders under Russian supervision. Its khans held Russian military rank and pensions, collected taxes and supplied troops. [[e:aslan-khan-of-kazikumukh|Aslan Khan]] also gained the [[s:kazikumukh-khanate|Kazikumukh Khanate]], and the two were often ruled together. Kurakh had a Russian fort, and the khanate remained loyal during the wars with the [[s:caucasian-imamate|Caucasian Imamate]].
kurin-khanate.e: After the defeat of [[e:imam-shamil|Shamil]] and the stabilisation of [[e:dagestan|Dagestan]], the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] abolished the khanate in 1864 and incorporated it into the Kyurin district of the [[e:dagestan-oblast|Dagestan Oblast]]. The area remains the heartland of the [[e:lezgins|Lezgin people]] in southern Dagestan.

kanyok-kingdom.t: A Luba-related kingdom of the southern Kasai, long a rival of the Luba Empire, whose history is known mainly from oral tradition.
kanyok-kingdom.o: The Kanyok lived between the [[e:lubilash-river|Lubilash]] and [[e:mbuji-mayi-river|Mbuji-Mayi]] rivers in the southern [[e:kasai|Kasai]] and shared many institutions and origin stories with their [[e:luba-empire|Luba]] neighbours. A centralised kingship under the Mwen a Kanyok had formed by the 17th century, according to oral traditions.
kanyok-kingdom.r: The Mwen a Kanyok was a sacred ruler who governed through titled officials and village chiefs. Kanyok traditions recall repeated wars with the [[s:luba-empire|Luba Empire]], sometimes as rival and sometimes as tributary. In the 19th century the kingdom was drawn into regional trade and raiding linked to the [[e:chokwe|Chokwe]] and other slave traders.
kanyok-kingdom.e: The [[s:congo-free-state|Congo Free State]] extended its authority over the Kanyok in the 1890s, ending the kingdom's independence. Its history has been reconstructed by historians largely from oral traditions collected in the 20th century.

kingdom-of-mema.t: Soninke kingdom on the western edge of the inland Niger delta, a successor to the Ghana Empire that sheltered the young Sundiata Keita.
kingdom-of-mema.o: [[e:mema|Mema]] lay west of [[e:lake-debo|Lake Debo]] in present-day [[e:mali|Mali]], a region of lakes and pasture once far wetter than today. It was a province of the [[s:ghana-empire|Ghana Empire]] and emerged as an independent kingdom as [[e:ghana|Ghana]] declined after the 11th century. Archaeological survey around Akumbu shows a dense cluster of settlements and iron-smelting sites.
kingdom-of-mema.r: Little is recorded of its government. In the [[e:sundiata-keita|Sundiata]] epic, the exiled [[e:mande-peoples|Mande]] prince found refuge with the king of [[e:mema|Mema]], who gave him horsemen for his campaign against the [[s:sosso-kingdom|Sosso kingdom]]. Mema's [[e:soninke|Soninke]] elite traded along the [[e:niger-river|Niger]] and kept horses, a source of military strength.
kingdom-of-mema.e: [[e:mema|Mema]] became a province of the [[s:mali-empire|Mali Empire]] in the 13th century and was later absorbed by the [[s:songhai-empire|Songhai Empire]], around the middle of the 15th century. A drying climate drove much of its population away, and the region is now sparsely inhabited.

kingdom-of-kotte.t: The last Sinhalese kingdom to unite all of Sri Lanka, under Parakramabahu VI, before its kings became clients of the Portuguese.
kingdom-of-kotte.o: [[e:parakramabahu-vi|Parakramabahu VI]] took power in 1412 after the fall of the [[e:alagakkonara-family|Alakeshvara]] family of the [[s:kingdom-of-gampola|Kingdom of Gampola]], possibly with Chinese backing following [[e:zheng-he|Zheng He's]] intervention. He moved the capital to the fortified town of [[e:sri-jayawardenepura-kotte|Kotte]] near [[e:colombo|Colombo]], which the Alakeshvaras had built as a defence against the [[s:jaffna-kingdom|Jaffna Kingdom]].
kingdom-of-kotte.r: [[e:parakramabahu-vi|Parakramabahu VI]] reigned for over five decades and briefly unified the island, conquering the [[s:jaffna-kingdom|Jaffna Kingdom]] and subduing the [[s:vanni-chieftaincies|Vanni chieftaincies]]. His reign was a golden age of [[e:sinhala-language|Sinhala]] poetry, with the monk-poet [[e:thotagamuwe-sri-rahula-thera|Sri Rahula]]. [[e:sri-jayawardenepura-kotte|Kotte]] controlled the [[e:cinnamon|cinnamon]]-growing west coast, whose trade attracted the Portuguese, who arrived in 1505 and soon built a fort at [[e:colombo|Colombo]].
kingdom-of-kotte.e: In 1521 the kingdom split into [[e:sri-jayawardenepura-kotte|Kotte]], the [[s:kingdom-of-sitawaka|Kingdom of Sitawaka]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-raigama|Kingdom of Raigama]]. Kotte's king [[e:dharmapala-of-kotte|Dharmapala]] converted to [[e:christianity|Christianity]] and in 1580 bequeathed his realm to the King of Portugal; on his death in 1597 it became part of [[s:portuguese-ceylon|Portuguese Ceylon]].

kingdom-of-bugabo.t: A small Haya kingdom on the western shore of Lake Victoria, formed when Kyamutwara split around 1800.
kingdom-of-bugabo.o: Bugabo emerged around 1800 from the division of the [[s:kingdom-of-kyamutwara|Kingdom of Kyamutwara]] in the [[e:kagera-region|Kagera region]] of north-western [[s:tanzania|Tanzania]], one of several small [[e:haya-people|Haya]] states created by succession disputes among royal lines.
kingdom-of-bugabo.r: Little is recorded of its history. Like its neighbours it was a banana and [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]] farming kingdom ruled by a mukama with chiefs and royal rituals.
kingdom-of-bugabo.e: Bugabo became a native authority under [[s:german-east-africa|German East Africa]] and later [[e:tanganyika-territory|British Tanganyika Territory]]. Its chieftaincy was abolished in 1963.

kazikumukh-shamkhalate.t: The leading Muslim state of medieval Dagestan, ruled by shamkhals from the Lak village of Kumukh, which later divided into Tarki and Kazikumukh.
kazikumukh-shamkhalate.o: The [[e:lak|Laks]] of [[e:kumukh|Kumukh]] were among the first peoples of mountainous [[e:dagestan|Dagestan]] to adopt [[e:islam|Islam]], and their village became a religious centre. By the 14th century a ruler with the title shamkhal, claiming descent from early Arab commanders, headed a state there that spread its authority over neighbouring communities and the [[e:kumyks|Kumyk]] plain.
kazikumukh-shamkhalate.r: The shamkhals ruled with [[e:lak|Lak]] and [[e:kumyks|Kumyk]] nobles, promoting [[e:islam|Islam]] among neighbours and leading campaigns against Georgian and Circassian lands. The state lived from herding, crafts and trade and was tributary to the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]] before [[e:timur|Timur's]] invasion of 1395. In the 16th century it was the strongest power in [[e:dagestan|Dagestan]], courted by the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] and [[s:safavid-empire|Safavid Empire]].
kazikumukh-shamkhalate.e: Internal quarrels and pressure from [[e:persia|Persia]] weakened it, and by about 1642 the shamkhals had moved their seat to [[e:tarki|Tarki]] on the Caspian coast, founding the [[s:shamkhalate-of-tarki|Shamkhalate of Tarki]], while [[e:kumukh|Kumukh]] itself became the [[s:kazikumukh-khanate|Kazikumukh Khanate]].

kingdom-of-ireland.t: The kingdom created when Henry VIII took the title King of Ireland in 1542, ruled by English monarchs until the Act of Union of 1800.
kingdom-of-ireland.o: The [[e:crown-of-ireland-act-1542|Crown of Ireland Act]] of 1542, passed by the [[e:parliament-of-ireland|Irish Parliament]], replaced the [[s:lordship-of-ireland|Lordship of Ireland]] with a kingdom. [[e:henry-viii-of-england|Henry VIII]] pursued 'surrender and regrant', converting Gaelic chiefs into earls, while the [[e:house-of-tudor|Tudor]] and [[e:house-of-stuart|Stuart]] conquests extended English authority across the island.
kingdom-of-ireland.r: Ireland was governed by a lord deputy or lord lieutenant at [[e:dublin-castle|Dublin Castle]] and its own Parliament. Plantations in [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Munster]] and [[s:northern-ireland|Ulster]] settled English and Scottish Protestants. After the Williamite war of 1689 to 1691, the Penal Laws excluded Catholics from land and office, creating the Protestant Ascendancy. [[e:grattans-parliament|Grattan's Parliament]] gained legislative independence in 1782.
kingdom-of-ireland.e: After the [[e:society-of-united-irishmen|United Irishmen]] rebellion of 1798, the Acts of Union of 1800 merged Ireland into the [[s:united-kingdom-of-great-britain-and-ireland|United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland]] from 1 January 1801.
kingdom-of-ireland.re: Christianity; Catholic majority, Anglican established church
