kutlehr-state.t: A tiny Rajput hill state in the lower Himalaya near Kangra, one of the minor principalities absorbed by the Sikh Empire in the early 19th century.
kutlehr-state.o: The ruling family claimed descent from [[e:brahmins|Brahmins]] who became [[e:rajputs|Rajputs]] and came from the plains; tradition places the foundation around 750. Its seat was the fort of Kot Kutlehr, between the [[e:beas|Beas]] and the [[e:sutlej-river|Sutlej]].
kutlehr-state.r: Kutlehr was one of the smallest of the [[s:kangra-state|Kangra]] group of hill states, a few villages and forts under a Raja who was often a dependant of Kangra State or other larger neighbours. Few records of its internal history survive.
kutlehr-state.e: [[e:ranjit-singh|Ranjit Singh's]] [[s:sikh-empire|Sikh Empire]] annexed the state in 1825, leaving the family a [[e:jagir|jagir]]. After 1846 the British confirmed the family in a smaller jagir. The territory is now in [[e:himachal-pradesh|Himachal Pradesh]].

kingdom-of-cappadocia.t: Cappadocia, a Hellenistic kingdom of the central Anatolian plateau ruled by Iranian-descended kings who became loyal allies of Rome.
kingdom-of-cappadocia.o: [[e:ariarathes-i-of-cappadocia|Ariarathes]], the Persian [[e:satrapy|satrap]], defied Alexander's successors until [[e:perdiccas|Perdiccas]] killed him in 322 BCE. His adopted son [[e:ariarathes-ii-of-cappadocia|Ariarathes II]] regained the land c. 301 BCE, and his heirs took the title king, ruling the plateau from [[e:kayseri|Mazaca]] beneath [[e:mount-erciyes|Mount Argaeus]].
kingdom-of-cappadocia.r: The [[e:ariarathid-dynasty|Ariarathid]] kings ruled a rural country of large estates and temple domains, such as the shrine of the goddess Ma at [[e:comana-cappadocia|Comana]]. Iranian traditions mixed with Greek culture; [[e:ariarathes-v-of-cappadocia|Ariarathes V]] was a patron of philosophers. The kingdom supplied horses, slaves and grain and allied with [[e:rome|Rome]] against the [[s:seleucid-empire|Seleucid Empire]].
kingdom-of-cappadocia.e: After Pontic interference, [[e:rome|Rome]] installed [[e:ariobarzanes-i-of-cappadocia|Ariobarzanes I]] in 95 BCE. The last king, [[e:archelaus-of-cappadocia|Archelaus]], was summoned to Rome by [[e:tiberius|Tiberius]] and died there in 17 CE, and Cappadocia became a Roman province.

kingdom-of-karasahr.t: The oasis kingdom of Agni on the northern Silk Road, one of the homes of the Tocharian languages and of Central Asian Buddhism.
kingdom-of-karasahr.o: [[e:karashahr|Karasahr]], called Yanqi in Chinese and Agni in its own documents, grew around the [[e:bosten-lake|Bosten Lake]] oasis on the north-eastern edge of the [[e:tarim-basin|Tarim Basin]]. It enters Chinese records in the 2nd century BCE as one of the city-states of the [[e:western-regions|Western Regions]], alternating between [[e:xiongnu-empire|Xiongnu]] and Han control.
kingdom-of-karasahr.r: Its people spoke Tocharian A, an [[e:indo-european-languages|Indo-European]] language preserved in Buddhist [[e:manuscript|manuscripts]]. Ruled by its own kings, [[e:karashahr|Karasahr]] lived from irrigated farming, fishing, salt and [[e:silk-road|Silk Road]] trade, and its monasteries at Shikshin followed the [[e:sarvastivada|Sarvastivada]] school. The pilgrim [[e:xuanzang|Xuanzang]] passed through in 630. The Han general [[e:ban-chao|Ban Chao]] subdued it in 94, and the [[s:tang-dynasty|Tang Dynasty]] conquered it in 644 and made it one of the [[e:four-garrisons-of-anxi|Four Garrisons of Anxi]].
kingdom-of-karasahr.e: After [[s:later-tang|Tang]] power in the [[e:tarim-basin|Tarim]] faded in the late 8th century, [[e:karashahr|Karasahr]] passed under Tibetan and [[e:uyghurs|Uyghur]] influence. Uyghurs fleeing the fall of the [[s:uyghur-khaganate|Uyghur Khaganate]] in 840 settled there, and the region became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-qocho|Kingdom of Qocho]], where Tocharian gave way to [[e:old-uyghur-language|Old Uyghur]].

kingdom-of-gwiriko.t: A Dyula-ruled kingdom around Bobo-Dioulasso in western Burkina Faso, founded by a branch of the Wattara family of Kong.
kingdom-of-gwiriko.o: Gwiriko was created around 1714 by [[e:famagan-wattara|Famagan Wattara]], a kinsman of [[e:seku-wattara|Seku Wattara]] of the [[s:kong-empire|Kong Empire]], who led [[e:wangara|Dyula]] warriors into the region of the upper [[e:black-volta|Black Volta]]. He established his rule over the [[e:bobo-people|Bobo]], [[e:bwa-people|Bwa]] and other farming peoples, with [[e:bobo-dioulasso|Sya]], later Bobo-Dioulasso, as the main centre. After Seku's death it became independent of Kong.
kingdom-of-gwiriko.r: The Wattara and their [[e:wangara|Dyula]] allies formed a Muslim ruling and trading class over largely non-Muslim farming villages, collecting tribute and controlling trade in kola, salt, gold and slaves. After Famagan's reign the kingdom fragmented into rival branches, and in the 19th century it was weakened by revolts of subject peoples and wars with [[s:kenedougou-kingdom|Kenedougou]].
kingdom-of-gwiriko.e: By the 1890s Gwiriko was a loose collection of chiefdoms. [[e:samori-ture|Samori Toure]]'s armies passed through the region, and in 1897 the French occupied [[e:bobo-dioulasso|Bobo-Dioulasso]]. The area became part of [[s:french-sudan|French Sudan]] and later [[s:french-upper-volta|French Upper Volta]].

kamta-rajaula-state.t: A small Chaube jagir of Bundelkhand, one of the estates granted to the former Brahmin governors of Kalinjar in 1812.
kamta-rajaula-state.o: Kamta-Rajaula was created in 1812 as one of the shares given to the Chaube family, who had held the fort of [[e:kalinjar-fort|Kalinjar]] for the rulers of [[s:panna-state|Panna]], in return for surrendering it to the British.
kamta-rajaula-state.r: The estate covered a few villages near Kamta, the hill sacred to [[e:rama|Rama]] at [[e:chitrakoot|Chitrakoot]], under the [[e:bundelkhand-agency|Bundelkhand Agency]]. Little else of its history is recorded.
kamta-rajaula-state.e: After independence Kamta-Rajaula was merged into [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]] with the other [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]] states and absorbed by 1950.

kingdom-of-undi.t: The western Chewa kingdom of the Undi, an offshoot of Maravi whose lands held gold mines worked by Portuguese traders.
kingdom-of-undi.o: The Undi dynasty was founded in the 17th century by a member of the Phiri ruling clan of the [[s:kingdom-of-maravi|Kingdom of Maravi]] who, according to tradition, quarrelled with the Kalonga and led followers west. He established his capital at Mano near the Kapoche river, on the borderlands of present-day [[s:portuguese-mozambique|Mozambique]], [[e:zambia|Zambia]] and [[e:malawi|Malawi]].
kingdom-of-undi.r: The Undi ruled through kin and territorial chiefs who sent tribute and recognised his ritual primacy, including over rain shrines. The kingdom traded [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and cloth with the Portuguese at [[e:tete|Tete]] and [[e:zumbo|Zumbo]], and in the 18th century Portuguese and Goan miners worked gold deposits in Undi territory under licence. [[e:chewa|Chewa]] culture, including the [[e:nyau|Nyau]] masked societies, flourished.
kingdom-of-undi.e: Decline set in during the 19th century as Afro-Portuguese warlords and, from the 1830s, [[e:ngoni|Ngoni]] invaders raided its lands. By around 1880 central authority had collapsed. The Undi title survives as a [[e:chewa|Chewa]] paramount chieftaincy in [[e:zambia|Zambia]].

kingdom-of-yauri.t: Small kingdom on the middle Niger, among the 'outer' Hausa states, that survived the 19th century jihad with its dynasty intact.
kingdom-of-yauri.o: Yauri grew up along the [[e:niger-river|Niger]] above the [[s:kingdom-of-bussa|Bussa]] rapids among the Reshe and other river peoples, with a ruling house that adopted [[e:hausa|Hausa]] language and institutions. It was counted among the [[e:banza-bakwai|Banza Bakwai]] and is traditionally dated to around the 15th century.
kingdom-of-yauri.r: Yauri controlled river crossings and trade between [[s:hausa-kingdoms|Hausaland]], [[e:borgu|Borgu]] and [[e:nupe-kingdom|Nupe]]. It was frequently subject to stronger neighbours, including the [[s:kingdom-of-kebbi|Kingdom of Kebbi]] and the [[s:songhai-empire|Songhai Empire]], and adopted [[e:islam|Islam]] at court. After the [[e:jihad|jihad]] of the early 19th century its rulers accepted the suzerainty of the [[s:gwandu-emirate|Gwandu Emirate]] within the [[s:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto Caliphate]].
kingdom-of-yauri.e: Internal disputes led to the founding of a new capital at [[e:yelwa|Yelwa]] in the 1880s. Yauri came under the [[s:protectorate-of-northern-nigeria|Protectorate of Northern Nigeria]] around 1901 and survives as the Yauri [[e:emirate|Emirate]] in [[s:kingdom-of-kebbi|Kebbi]] State.

kingdom-of-the-ouarsenis.t: An obscure Berber kingdom of the Ouarsenis mountains in Algeria, known mainly from its monumental Djedar tombs.
kingdom-of-the-ouarsenis.o: After Roman and Vandal authority faded in the interior of [[s:mauretania-caesariensis|Mauretania Caesariensis]] in the late 5th century, a [[e:berbers|Berber]] kingdom emerged in the [[e:ouarsenis|Ouarsenis]] mountains and high plains around [[e:tiaret|Tiaret]]. [[e:procopius|Procopius]] mentions a ruler named Mastigas who, in the 530s, held most of [[s:kingdom-of-mauretania|Mauretania]] except the coastal city of [[s:lordship-of-caesarea|Caesarea]].
kingdom-of-the-ouarsenis.r: Very little is known of its government. The [[e:djedars|Djedars]], thirteen great stepped pyramid tombs near Frenda and [[e:tiaret|Tiaret]], built between the 5th and 7th centuries, are attributed to its rulers. Their [[e:latin|Latin]] inscriptions and Christian symbols show a Romanised, Christian [[e:berbers|Berber]] elite ruling over pastoral and farming tribes.
kingdom-of-the-ouarsenis.e: The kingdom disappears from the record by the late 6th century, and its lands later came under the Arab conquerors and [[e:berbers|Berber]] Islamic states such as the [[s:rustamid-imamate|Rustamid imamate]], whose capital [[e:tiaret|Tahert]] lay close by.

kingdom-of-hungary-1920-1946.t: Interwar Hungarian kingdom without a king, ruled by Regent Miklós Horthy, which sought to undo the Treaty of Trianon and was drawn into the Second World War.
kingdom-of-hungary-1920-1946.o: After the fall of the [[s:hungarian-soviet-republic|Hungarian Soviet Republic]], a national assembly restored the monarchy in 1920 but, with the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] barred, elected Admiral [[e:miklos-horthy|Miklós Horthy]] regent on 1 March. The [[e:treaty-of-trianon|Treaty of Trianon]] in June 1920 took two-thirds of the former [[s:kingdom-of-hungary-1867-1918|Kingdom of Hungary]] (1867-1918). Former king Charles IV twice tried to return in 1921 and failed.
kingdom-of-hungary-1920-1946.r: Prime Minister [[e:istvan-bethlen|István Bethlen]] stabilised the conservative regime in the 1920s, with restricted voting and dominance of landowners. Revision of Trianon was the central aim, and through the [[e:vienna-awards|Vienna Awards]] of 1938 and 1940 [[e:hungary|Hungary]] regained southern [[e:slovakia|Slovakia]] and northern [[s:principality-of-transylvania|Transylvania]] with German and Italian support. Antisemitic laws began with the numerus clausus of 1920 and tightened from 1938.
kingdom-of-hungary-1920-1946.e: [[e:hungary|Hungary]] joined the war against the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] in 1941. [[e:germany|Germany]] occupied it in March 1944, and around 437,000 [[e:jews|Jews]] were deported, most to [[e:auschwitz-concentration-camp|Auschwitz]]. [[e:miklos-horthy|Horthy]]'s attempt to leave the war in October 1944 led to [[e:ferenc-szalasi|Ferenc Szálasi's]] [[s:government-of-national-unity|Government of National Unity]]. The monarchy was abolished in February 1946.

kingdom-of-elymais.t: A semi-independent kingdom of Khuzestan and the Zagros under Parthian rule, known for its rock reliefs and for killing the Seleucid king Antiochus III.
kingdom-of-elymais.o: Elymais (from [[e:elam|Elam]]) covered the mountains of eastern [[e:khuzestan|Khuzestan]] and, at times, the plain of [[e:susa|Susa]]. Its people resisted the [[s:seleucid-empire|Seleucid Empire]]: [[e:antiochus-iii-the-great|Antiochus III]] was killed in 187 BCE while plundering a temple of [[e:bel-god|Bel]] there. Around 147 BCE a local ruler, [[e:kamnaskires-i|Kamnaskires I]], took Susa and issued coins as king.
kingdom-of-elymais.r: Elymais mixed Iranian, Mesopotamian and Greek traditions, worshipping [[e:bel-god|Bel]], [[e:nanaya|Nanaya]] and [[e:artemis|Artemis]] at rich temples. Its kings, often called [[e:kamnaskires-i|Kamnaskires]] or later Orodes, minted bronze coins and ruled as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[s:parthian-empire|Parthian Empire]], sometimes in revolt. Rock reliefs at [[e:hung-e-azhdar|Hung-e Azhdar]], [[e:tang-e-sarvak|Tang-e Sarvak]] and Hung-e Kamalvand show rulers and nobles in Parthian dress, and the bronze statue from Shami belongs to this world.
kingdom-of-elymais.e: [[e:ardashir-i|Ardashir I]] of the [[s:sasanian-empire|Sasanian Empire]] conquered Elymais around 221 CE, ending the dynasty. Its lands became part of the Sasanian province of [[e:khuzestan|Khuzestan]].

kingdom-of-cyrene.t: The Greek kingdom of the Battiad dynasty in eastern Libya, enriched by silphium, horses and grain.
kingdom-of-cyrene.o: According to [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]], colonists from the island of [[s:thera|Thera]], sent by the oracle of [[s:delphi|Delphi]], founded [[s:republic-of-cyrene|Cyrene]] around 631 BCE under a leader who became King [[e:battus-i-of-cyrene|Battus I]]. The site, on a fertile plateau above the coast of [[e:cyrenaica|Cyrenaica]], was shown to them by local [[s:libu|Libyans]], with whom the settlers intermarried.
kingdom-of-cyrene.r: Eight kings, alternately named [[e:battus-i-of-cyrene|Battus]] and Arcesilaus, ruled for nearly two centuries. [[e:battus-ii-of-cyrene|Battus II]] brought new settlers and defeated an Egyptian army sent by [[e:apries|Apries]] at [[e:battle-of-irasa|Irasa]] around 570 BCE, and the reformer [[e:demonax-of-mantinea|Demonax of Mantinea]] later limited royal power. The economy rested on silphium, a medicinal plant shown on the city's coins, and on horses and grain. [[s:republic-of-cyrene|Cyrene]] paid tribute to the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]] from 525 BCE.
kingdom-of-cyrene.e: Royal power provoked repeated conflict, including Barca's secession. [[e:arcesilaus-iv|Arcesilaus IV]], whose [[e:chariot|chariot]] victory at [[s:delphi|Delphi]] in 462 BCE was celebrated by [[e:pindar|Pindar]], was overthrown around 440 BCE, and the monarchy gave way to the [[s:republic-of-cyrene|Republic of Cyrene]].

kingdom-of-moray.t: A powerful northern Scottish realm whose rulers, styled kings or mormaers, contested the Scottish throne, most famously through Macbeth.
kingdom-of-moray.o: Moray emerged in the 10th century in the lands around the [[e:moray-firth|Moray Firth]] after the decline of the Pictish kingdom of [[s:kingdom-of-fortriu|Fortriu]]. Its ruling family, probably from [[s:cenel-loairn|Cenel Loairn]] by later genealogies, sometimes appear in Irish annals as kings of Alba, reflecting their claims to the [[s:kingdom-of-scotland|Kingdom of Scotland]].
kingdom-of-moray.r: Moray's rulers commanded a rich coastal plain and highland hinterland. [[e:macbeth-king-of-scotland|Macbeth]], mormaer of Moray, killed [[e:duncan-i-of-scotland|Duncan I]] in 1040 and ruled [[e:scotland|Scotland]] until 1057, making a pilgrimage to [[e:rome|Rome]]. His stepson [[e:lulach|Lulach]] briefly succeeded him. The house of Moray clashed repeatedly with Norse earls of [[e:orkney|Orkney]] and with the line of [[e:malcolm-iii-of-scotland|Malcolm III]].
kingdom-of-moray.e: After [[e:angus-of-moray|Angus of Moray]] died in battle at [[e:battle-of-stracathro|Stracathro]] in 1130, [[e:david|David]] I annexed the province, planting burghs and Flemish settlers. Revolts by [[e:meic-uilleim|MacWilliam]] claimants continued into the 13th century.

kingdom-of-hadramawt.t: The frankincense kingdom of south Arabia, ruling the Wadi Hadramawt from Shabwa and controlling the Dhofar groves and the port of Qana.
kingdom-of-hadramawt.o: Hadramawt is named in Sabaean inscriptions of the 7th century BCE, when it was first an ally and then a rival of the [[s:kingdom-of-saba|Kingdom of Saba]]. Its kings ruled the long [[e:wadi-hadhramaut|Wadi Hadramawt]] and its tributaries from [[e:shabwa|Shabwa]], a walled town where all [[e:incense|incense]] had to be brought for taxing before caravans set off west.
kingdom-of-hadramawt.r: Its wealth came from frankincense, gathered in [[e:dhofar|Dhofar]] where Hadramawt founded the port of [[e:sumhuram|Sumhuram]] (Khor Rori), and shipped through [[e:qana-yemen|Qana]] on the [[e:indian-ocean|Indian Ocean]] coast, a port described in the [[e:periplus-of-the-erythraean-sea|Periplus of the Erythraean Sea]]. The kingdom worshipped the moon god [[e:sayin|Sayin]] and wrote [[e:hadramautic-language|Hadramitic]], a south Arabian language. It absorbed much of the [[s:kingdom-of-qataban|Kingdom of Qataban]] in the 2nd century CE.
kingdom-of-hadramawt.e: In the early 3rd century CE Saba sacked [[e:shabwa|Shabwa]], and around 300 CE the [[s:himyarite-kingdom|Himyarite Kingdom]] under [[e:shammar-yahrish|Shammar Yahrish]] conquered Hadramawt outright. The name survived as a region, and the valley's later sultanates, such as the [[s:kathiri-sultanate|Kathiri Sultanate]] and the [[s:quaiti-sultanate|Qu'aiti Sultanate]], inherited it.

kotah-state.t: A Hada Chauhan Rajput state on the Chambal river, separated from Bundi under Shah Jahan and famed for its school of painting.
kotah-state.o: Kota was separated from [[s:bundi-state|Bundi State]] in 1631, when the Mughal emperor [[e:shah-jahan|Shah Jahan]] granted it to [[e:madho-singh-of-kota|Madho Singh]], a son of Rao [[e:ratan-singh-of-bundi|Ratan Singh of Bundi]], as a reward for service. The [[e:hada-chauhans|Hada]] rulers continued as Mughal mansabdars.
kotah-state.r: The Maharaos ruled the fertile [[e:chambal-river|Chambal]] valley. In the late 18th century the regent [[e:zalim-singh-jhala|Zalim Singh Jhala]] dominated the state, and in 1838 the British created [[s:jhalawar-state|Jhalawar]] for his descendants out of Kota lands. The court fostered the Kota school of painting, noted for its hunting scenes. It was a seventeen-gun salute state.
kotah-state.e: Kota joined the [[e:rajasthan|Rajasthan]] union in 1948, and Maharao [[e:bhim-singh-ii-of-kotah|Bhim Singh II]] became its [[e:rajpramukh|Rajpramukh]]. Kota is now a major city of Rajasthan.

kingdom-of-jembrana.t: Small, thinly peopled kingdom of western Bali, notable for its Bugis Muslim settlers and its position facing Java.
kingdom-of-jembrana.o: Jembrana occupied the forested western tip of [[e:bali|Bali]], facing [[e:java|Java]] across the [[e:bali-strait|Bali Strait]]. Its early history is poorly documented: a local dynasty emerged around 1700, and the area was repeatedly dominated by its more powerful neighbours, especially the [[s:kingdom-of-buleleng|Kingdom of Buleleng]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-badung|Kingdom of Badung]].
kingdom-of-jembrana.r: With little irrigated land, Jembrana was poorer than the southern Balinese kingdoms. [[e:bugis|Bugis]] seafarers from [[e:sulawesi|Sulawesi]] settled at Loloan near [[e:negara-bali|Negara]] in the 17th and 18th centuries, adding a Muslim trading community to the [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] Balinese population and linking the kingdom to the shipping routes of the [[e:java-sea|Java Sea]].
kingdom-of-jembrana.e: Jembrana came under [[e:dutch|Dutch]] control together with [[s:kingdom-of-buleleng|Buleleng]] after the 1849 expedition and was placed under direct colonial administration in 1882. It later became a regency of [[e:bali|Bali]] province in [[s:indonesia|Indonesia]].

koti-state.t: A small Rajput hill state just north of Shimla, a feudatory of Keonthal and one of the Simla Hill States.
koti-state.o: The ruling family claimed [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] descent, and tradition dates the state to around 1500. Little is reliably known about its origins.
koti-state.r: Koti was a small mountain state near [[e:mashobra|Mashobra]] and was a feudatory of [[s:keonthal-state|Keonthal State]]. Like its neighbours it was occupied by [[e:gurkhas|Gurkhas]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Kingdom of Nepal]] in the early 19th century and restored under British protection after 1815. Little detail of its history is recorded.
koti-state.e: Koti merged into [[e:himachal-pradesh|Himachal Pradesh]] in April 1948 and is now part of [[e:shimla|Shimla]] district.

kingdom-of-the-moors-and-romans.t: A post-Roman Berber kingdom in western Algeria whose king Masuna called himself ruler of both Moors and Romans.
kingdom-of-the-moors-and-romans.o: As Vandal control of the interior weakened in the late 5th century, [[e:berbers|Berber]] leaders in the former [[s:mauretania-caesariensis|Mauretania Caesariensis]] set up their own states. An inscription at [[e:altava|Altava]] (Ouled Mimoun) dated 508 names [[e:masuna|Masuna]] as 'king of the peoples of the Moors and [[e:roman-empire|Romans]]', the best evidence for this kingdom, which probably arose in the 470s or 480s.
kingdom-of-the-moors-and-romans.r: The kingdom combined [[e:berbers|Berber]] tribal leadership with surviving Roman towns, [[e:latin|Latin]] inscriptions and Christian communities, and kept Roman provincial dating. [[e:procopius|Procopius]] records that a Moorish ruler named [[e:masuna|Massonas]], probably the same Masuna, allied with the Byzantine general [[e:solomon|Solomon]] against other Berber rulers in 535. Its exact borders are unknown, but it was centred on the [[e:tlemcen|Tlemcen]] region and the [[e:oran|Oran]] plain.
kingdom-of-the-moors-and-romans.e: [[e:garmul|Garmul]], a later king, attacked [[s:praetorian-prefecture-of-africa|Byzantine Africa]] in the 570s and was killed by the general [[e:gennadius-exarch-of-africa|Gennadius]] in 578. Power in the region then passed to the [[s:kingdom-of-altava|Kingdom of Altava]], which survived until the Arab conquest.

kingdom-of-mustang.t: The small Tibetan Buddhist kingdom of Lo in the high valleys of northern Nepal, whose walled capital Lo Manthang survives intact.
kingdom-of-mustang.o: [[e:ame-pal|Ame Pal]], a Tibetan warrior, unified the upper [[e:kali-gandaki-river|Kali Gandaki]] valley around 1380 and founded the walled city of Lo Manthang as his capital. The kingdom of Lo controlled one of the main trade routes between the Tibetan plateau and the [[e:indian-subcontinent|Indian subcontinent]].
kingdom-of-mustang.r: Lo prospered from the trade in salt from [[s:tibet-1912-1951|Tibet]] and grain from the south, and its kings built great monasteries such as [[e:thubchen-monastery|Thubchen]] and [[e:jampa-lhakhang|Jampa]] in Lo Manthang, whose murals are among the finest in the Tibetan world. The [[s:sakya-regime|Sakya]] school of [[e:tibetan-buddhism|Tibetan Buddhism]] predominated. Lo paid tribute in turn to western Tibetan rulers, the [[s:kingdom-of-jumla|Kingdom of Jumla]] and later [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Nepal]].
kingdom-of-mustang.e: After the [[s:gorkha-kingdom|Gorkha]] conquests in the late 18th century, Lo became a tributary of the [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Kingdom of Nepal]] while keeping its own king. The monarchy lost its status when the [[s:federal-democratic-republic-of-nepal|Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal]] abolished royal titles in 2008. The last king, [[e:jigme-dorje-palbar-bista|Jigme Dorje Palbar Bista]], died in 2016.

kathrota-state.t: A minor chiefship of the Kathiawar peninsula, one of its many small estates.
kathrota-state.o: Kathrota was a small estate in [[e:kathiawar|Kathiawar]] held by a local chiefly family from around 1700. Its origins are poorly documented.
kathrota-state.r: The ruler held a handful of villages and, after 1807, came under British supervision in the [[e:kathiawar-agency|Kathiawar Agency]]. Standard references record little else.
kathrota-state.e: Kathrota merged into the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960.

kingdom-of-boussouma.t: Mossi kingdom east of Ouagadougou, one of the smaller independent Mossi states of the Burkina Faso plateau.
kingdom-of-boussouma.o: Known mainly from [[e:mossi|Mossi]] oral tradition. Boussouma was founded by a branch of the Mossi royal family, probably in the 17th century, on lands east of the [[s:kingdom-of-ouagadougou|Kingdom of Ouagadougou]], and its rulers bore the title Dima.
kingdom-of-boussouma.r: The Dima of Boussouma ruled with ministers and village chiefs over [[e:mossi|Mossi]] farming communities, with local earth-priests keeping the rites of land. The kingdom kept its independence from [[s:kingdom-of-ouagadougou|Ouagadougou]] and was a frequent rival of the [[e:mogho-naba|Mogho Naaba]].
kingdom-of-boussouma.e: Boussouma came under French control in 1896 and became part of [[s:french-west-africa|French West Africa]], later [[s:french-upper-volta|French Upper Volta]]. The Dima of Boussouma remains a traditional ruler in [[e:burkina-faso|Burkina Faso]].

kingdom-of-lithuania-1918.t: A short-lived monarchy declared by the Council of Lithuania in 1918, which elected a German prince as King Mindaugas II.
kingdom-of-lithuania-1918.o: [[e:germany|Germany]] recognised Lithuanian independence in March 1918 on condition of close ties with the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]], and plans circulated to unite the crown with [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] or [[e:saxony|Saxony]]. To avoid this, the [[e:council-of-lithuania|Council of Lithuania]] on 11 July 1918 proclaimed a [[e:constitutional-monarchy|constitutional monarchy]] and invited [[e:wilhelm-karl-duke-of-urach|Prince Wilhelm of Urach]], a Catholic from Wurttemberg, to be king.
kingdom-of-lithuania-1918.r: Wilhelm accepted and took the name [[e:wilhelm-karl-duke-of-urach|Mindaugas II]], after the medieval king of the [[s:kingdom-of-lithuania|Kingdom of Lithuania]], but he never came to [[s:republic-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] and the German authorities did not recognise his election. In practice the country remained under German military occupation, while the council prepared Lithuanian institutions.
kingdom-of-lithuania-1918.e: As [[e:germany|Germany's]] defeat approached, the Council revoked the election on 2 November 1918 and adopted provisional republican principles. The state continued as the [[s:republic-of-lithuania-1918-1940|Republic of Lithuania]] (1918-1940). Wilhelm never set foot in the country, and the episode is remembered as a curiosity of Lithuanian state-building.

kingdom-of-galicia-volhynia.t: The leading western Rus' state after the Mongol invasion, whose ruler Daniel was crowned King of Rus' and founded the city of Lviv.
kingdom-of-galicia-volhynia.o: In 1199 [[e:roman-the-great|Roman Mstislavich]] of the [[s:principality-of-volhynia|Principality of Volhynia]] took [[s:principality-of-galicia|Halych]] and united it with his own lands. After his death in battle in 1205 [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Galicia]] fell into decades of strife involving [[e:hungary|Hungary]] and [[e:poland|Poland]]. His son Daniel won back both lands by 1238 and made the state one of the most powerful in [[e:eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]].
kingdom-of-galicia-volhynia.r: Daniel submitted to [[e:batu-khan|Batu Khan]] in 1245 but looked to the West for help, and in 1253 he was crowned King of Rus' by a papal legate at [[e:drohiczyn|Dorohychyn]]. He founded [[e:chelm|Kholm]] and [[e:lviv|Lviv]], which he named after his son Leo, and welcomed German, Armenian and Jewish settlers to the towns. [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]], Catholic and steppe influences met in its court.
kingdom-of-galicia-volhynia.e: The direct dynasty ended in 1323, and [[e:yuri-ii-boleslav|Yuri II Boleslaw]], a Masovian Piast, was poisoned by boyars in 1340. [[e:poland|Poland]] and [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] then divided the kingdom, with [[e:casimir-iii-the-great|Casimir III]] taking [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Galicia]] by 1349 and the [[s:duchy-of-volhynia|Duchy of Volhynia]] going to [[e:lithuania|Lithuania]].

kingdom-of-spain.t: Spain's present parliamentary monarchy, built through the peaceful transition from Franco's dictatorship to democracy.
kingdom-of-spain.o: Two days after [[e:francisco-franco|Franco]]'s death, [[e:juan-carlos-i|Juan Carlos I]] was proclaimed king on 22 November 1975, ending [[s:francoist-spain|Francoist Spain]]. With Prime Minister [[e:adolfo-suarez|Adolfo Suárez]] he dismantled the dictatorship: the Law for Political Reform of 1976, free elections in June 1977 and the Constitution of 1978, approved by referendum.
kingdom-of-spain.r: [[e:spain|Spain]] became a parliamentary monarchy divided into 17 autonomous communities, recognising Catalan, Basque and Galician identities. The king's stand against the coup attempt of 23 February 1981 secured democracy. [[e:felipe-gonzalez|Felipe González's]] Socialists governed from 1982 to 1996, joining the [[e:european-economic-community|European Economic Community]] in 1986 and keeping Spain in [[e:nato|NATO]], which it had joined in 1982, after a referendum that year. The 1992 [[e:1992-summer-olympics|Barcelona Olympics]] and [[e:expo-92|Seville Expo]] marked modernisation.
kingdom-of-spain.e: [[e:spain|Spain]] remains a parliamentary monarchy. ETA declared an end to violence in 2011, [[e:felipe-vi-of-spain|Felipe VI]] succeeded his father in 2014, and the Catalan independence crisis of 2017 tested the constitutional order.

kingdom-of-kebbi.t: Hausa kingdom founded by the rebel Songhai general Kanta, which briefly dominated Hausaland in the 16th century.
kingdom-of-kebbi.o: Around 1516 [[e:muhammadu-kanta|Muhammadu Kanta]], a commander serving the [[s:songhai-empire|Songhai Empire]] under [[e:askia-muhammad|Askia Muhammad]], quarrelled over the spoils of a campaign against [[s:sultanate-of-agadez|Agadez]] and rebelled. He established an independent kingdom in the Kebbi region of north-western [[s:hausa-kingdoms|Hausaland]] and built fortified capitals at [[e:surame|Surame]] and later [[e:birnin-kebbi|Birnin Kebbi]].
kingdom-of-kebbi.r: [[e:muhammadu-kanta|Kanta]] defeated [[e:songhai-empire|Songhai]] and the [[s:kanem-bornu-empire|Kanem-Bornu Empire]] and made Kebbi the dominant power in western [[s:hausa-kingdoms|Hausaland]], taking tribute from [[s:katsina-kingdom|Katsina]], [[s:kingdom-of-zamfara|Zamfara]] and others. After his death Kebbi lost much of its empire but remained a strong military state, a member of the [[e:banza-bakwai|Banza Bakwai]]. Its people, the Kebbawa, are farmers and fishermen of the [[e:rima-river|Rima]] and [[e:niger-river|Niger]] valleys.
kingdom-of-kebbi.e: In 1805 jihadists of the [[s:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto Caliphate]] took [[e:birnin-kebbi|Birnin Kebbi]]. The Kebbi dynasty fought on from the marshes and in 1831 established the [[s:argungu-emirate|Argungu Emirate]], which resisted [[e:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto]] until British rule. The name lives on in Kebbi State.

kushan-empire.t: An empire of Yuezhi origin stretching from the Amu Darya to the Ganges, a crossroads of Rome, China and India that carried Buddhism into Central Asia.
kushan-empire.o: [[e:kujula-kadphises|Kujula Kadphises]], chief of the Kushan branch of the [[s:yuezhi|Yuezhi]], united the five [[e:yuezhi|Yuezhi]] chiefdoms of [[s:greco-bactrian-kingdom|Bactria]] in the 1st century CE and pushed south across the [[e:hindu-kush|Hindu Kush]], taking lands from the [[s:indo-parthian-kingdom|Indo-Parthians]] and [[s:indo-greek-kingdom|Indo-Greeks]]. His successors [[e:vima-takto|Vima Takto]] and [[e:vima-kadphises|Vima Kadphises]] extended rule deep into northern [[e:india|India]].
kushan-empire.r: Under [[e:kanishka|Kanishka the Great]] in the 2nd century, the empire was ruled from [[e:peshawar|Purushapura]] (Peshawar) and [[e:mathura|Mathura]], using Bactrian written in Greek script. Gold coins showed Greek, Iranian and Indian gods side by side. The Kushans controlled [[e:silk-road|Silk Road]] trade between [[e:han-dynasty|Han China]], [[e:parthia|Parthia]] and [[e:rome|Rome]], and patronised [[e:gandhara-art|Gandharan]] and Mathuran art, which produced some of the earliest images of the [[e:gautama-buddha|Buddha]]. [[e:mahayana-buddhism|Mahayana Buddhism]] spread northward under their rule.
kushan-empire.e: In the 3rd century the [[e:sasanian-empire|Sasanians]] conquered the western lands, creating the [[s:kushano-sasanian-kingdom|Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom]], while the [[s:gupta-empire|Gupta Empire]] and local rulers took the Indian territories. Small Kushan kingdoms lingered in [[s:kingdom-of-gandhara|Gandhara]] and [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]] until overrun by the [[s:kidarite-kingdom|Kidarite Kingdom]] in the 4th century.

kingdom-of-sanwi.t: An Anyi kingdom on the Aby lagoon in south-eastern Ivory Coast, ruled from Krinjabo, which was among the first states on that coast to sign a treaty with France.
kingdom-of-sanwi.o: Sanwi was founded around 1740 by Anyi migrants from [[s:aowin|Aowin]], who left their [[e:bantustan|homeland]] after the [[s:ashanti-empire|Ashanti Empire]] overran it. Under their leader Amon Ndoufou I they settled around [[e:krinjabo|Krinjabo]] and the [[e:aby-lagoon|Aby]] lagoon, subjecting the Eotile and Essouma peoples of the coast, including those of the trading town of [[e:assinie|Assinie]].
kingdom-of-sanwi.r: Sanwi followed [[e:akan|Akan]] forms of rule, with a king from a royal matrilineage, a court of chiefs and an elaborate regalia of gold and royal stools. The economy rested on gold, farming and trade with Europeans at [[e:assinie|Assinie]], where French and other merchants exchanged guns, cloth and spirits for gold, [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and slaves.
kingdom-of-sanwi.e: In 1843 Sanwi's rulers signed a treaty with the French naval officer [[e:louis-edouard-bouet-willaumez|Louis Edouard Bouet-Willaumez]], and [[e:assinie|Assinie]] became a French post. Sanwi was absorbed into the [[s:french-ivory-coast|French Ivory Coast]], though its kings remained and in 1959 attempted a brief secession.

kingdom-of-ergyng.t: A small British kingdom in the Wye valley around the Roman town of Ariconium, whose name survives in Archenfield, a Welsh-speaking district of Herefordshire.
kingdom-of-ergyng.o: Ergyng emerged after Roman rule ended, its name derived from [[e:ariconium|Ariconium]], an [[e:iron-working|iron-working]] town near [[e:ross-on-wye|Ross-on-Wye]]. It appears in the 6th and 7th centuries in the charters of the [[e:book-of-llandaff|Book of Llandaff]], which name local kings such as Peibio, associated in legend with the birth of [[e:dubricius|Saint Dubricius]].
kingdom-of-ergyng.r: Ergyng was a Christian British kingdom in which churches and monasteries, many linked to [[e:dubricius|Dubricius]], held land through royal grants. Its rulers were at times linked to the dynasties of [[s:kingdom-of-gwent|Gwent]] and [[s:kingdom-of-glywysing|Glywysing]]. Little else is reliably known of its government.
kingdom-of-ergyng.e: From the 7th century the kingdom was absorbed by [[s:kingdom-of-gwent|Gwent]], and English settlement from [[s:kingdom-of-mercia|Mercia]] advanced into the area. By the 10th century it was the district of Archenfield, under English lordship but still Welsh in law and speech; [[e:domesday-book|Domesday Book]] recorded its Welsh customs.
